proficiencies.toolsDB: Tinker's Tools and one other tool

1.name: Arcane Tinkerer
description: You have a knack for understanding the inner workings of magic items. Starting at 1st level, you can use a set of tools to cast both Mending and the ritual version of Identify, requiring no material components.
When you do so, the tools act as your spellcasting focus, and you use your Intelligence as your spellcasting ability.

1.name: Infusions
description: At 1st level, you learn to imbue objects with your signature magic, which allows you to produce magic items and spells.

subFeatures.name: Infusions Known
description: You know three Infusions of your choice.  As you gain levels, you learn more infusions, as shown in the Infusions Known column of the Artificer table.

At the end of each long rest, as long as you have access to a set of tools, you can replace one infusion you know with another infusion of your choice, so long as you meet the prerequisite for that infusion.

subFeatures.name: Arcane Charges
description: Your ability to craft and create magic objects is represented by a pool of arcane charges.  You have a number of arcane charges equal to twice your artificer level, and you regain all of your expended charges when you finish a long rest.  You can choose infusions to not end during a long rest, for which you do not regain the arcane charges.

subFeatures.name: Infusing an Object
description: Over the course of an hour, which can be during the course of a short or long rest, you can use a set of tools to imbue an infusion you know into a nonmagical object.  To do so, you must touch the object with your tools and expend the number of arcane charges equal to or greater than the infusion's degree.

Some infusions, like Minor Spellstoring Item, allow you to expend multiple arcane charges to grant that object multiple uses.  However, the maximum number of arcane charges an object bearing one of your infusions can hold at any one time is equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

If the infusion requires attunement, you can attune to the object the instant you infuse it, or you can forgo attunement so another creature can attune to it.  To attune to the infused item later, you must follow the normal attunement process.

The Infusion remains in an item indefinitely. If you die, the Infusion vanishes after a number of days have passed equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 day). Infusions vanish immediately if you give up your knowledge of one to learn another or imbue the infusion into another object.
So long as you have enoguh arcane charges to do so, you can imbue any infusion you know into multiple objects.

subFeatures.name: Infusing Ability
description: If one of your infusions allows the user to make a spell attack roll or forces a creature to make a saving throw, the infusion save DC and infusion attack modifier are calculated as follows:
Infusion save DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus
Infusion attack modifier =your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus

2.name: Arcane Recharge
description: You have learned to quickly refresh the arcane power of your infusions.  Starting at 2nd level, when you finish a short rest, you can use a set of tools to touch an object bearing one of your infusions and restore a number of expended arcane charges equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

6.name: Adjustable Inventions
description: Beginning at 6th level, you can alter your infusions on the fly.  When you finish a short rest, you can use a set of tools to remove an infusion from one item you touch, and instantly regain any arcane charges you used in that item's creation, so long as those charges have not been expended.
You must then use these arcane charges to immediately imbue one of your infusions into another item you touch.

6.name: Tool Expertise
description: There are few who can match an artificer's innate talent with their tools of choice.  Starting at 6th level, whenever you make an ability check that uses a tool with which you are proficient, you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.

7.name: Flash of Genius
description: Beginning at 7th level, your analytical mind can offer potent insights and suggestions at a moment's notice. As a reaction, when you, or another creature you can see within 30 feet, makes an ability check or a saving throw, you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the result of the roll.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

7.name: Inventive Adept
description: Your skills in craft and creation in regards to magical objects have greatly increased.  Beginning at 7th level, the maximum amount of arcane charges an object bearing your infusions can hold at any one time is equal to twice your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 2).
Moreover, it now takes you 10 minutes to imbue an object with an infusion you know.

10.name: Magic Item Mastery
description: You have gained a deep understanding of the inner workings and creation of magic items.  Beginning at 10th level, you can attune to up to four magic items at once, and for you, crafting a magic item with a rarity of common or uncommon takes a quarter of the normal time and costs half the normal gold. When you reach 20th level, this bonus also applies to rare and very rare magic items.
The number of magic items you can attune to at one time increases at 14th level (5 items) and at 18th level (6 items).

11.name: Arcane Breakthrough
description: Beginning at 11th level, your expert understanding of magic items allow you to attune to and use any magic item regardless of any alignment, class, race, spell, or level requirements.

20.name: Soul of Artifice
description: You imbue a spark of your own essence in the magic items you bear. At 20th level, you gain a +1 bonus to all saving throws for each magic item you are attuned to. In addition, if you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can choose to end your attunement to one magic item or infusion, causing you to drop to 1 hit point instead of 0.
Moreover, if you are killed, any object that bears one of your infusions counts as part of your body for the purposes of any spell that would bring you back to life.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.

The most dangerous Specialization an artificer can pursue is that of the Aeronaut. Constantly carrying out dangerous trials in their pursuit of mechanical flight, these pioneering minds will risk anything to complete the perfect flying machine. No setback or injury can dampen the spirits of a true Aeronaut.
subclasses.name: Aeronaut Specialization

1.name: Aeronaut Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stFeatherweight Weapon
5thBoots of the Wind
9thBoots of the Winding Path

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with weaver's tools. If you are already proficient with weaver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Aeronaut's Harness
description: When you adopt this Specialization at 1st level,, you craft for yourself the signature safety harness of an Aeronaut. You learn the Skyfall Harness Infusion, it doesn't count against your total number of  Infusions Known, and you can ignore its level prerequisite.
However, until you reach 5th level in this class, only you can don the skyfall harness you create with this Infusion. For all other creatures, this Infusion fails to function.

subFeatures.name: Skyfall Harness
description: Item: a cloak, vest, or harness
This magic harness automatically sizes to fit the wearer and can be worn over clothing or light armor. It has wing-like fins between its limbs that slow falls and allow wearers to glide.
When the wearer falls and isn't incapacitated, it subtracts up to 100 feet from its fall when calculating falling damage, and it can glide 2 feet horizontally every 1 foot that it falls.

3.name: Flying Machine
description: By 3rd level, you have constructed the signature invention of an Aeronaut, the Flying Machine. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use weaver's tools to craft a Flying Machine. Some Flying Machines include wings made of canvas, rotating blades, or even elemental engines. You can only maintain one Flying Machine, and creating a second one causes the magic of any others to dispel.
Your Flying Machine can only be used by you and can be attached to your skyfall harness. It also grants you a flying speed of 20 feet, and you can hover.
At certain Artificer levels, this flying speed increases: at 5th level (30 feet), at 9th level (40 feet), and at 15th level (60 feet).

5.name: Airborne Assault
description: At 5th level, your Flying Machine allows you to attack foes from unorthodox positions and catch enemies unaware. When you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground, your attacks deal an additional 1d8 bonus damage on hit.
At 15th level, this bonus damage becomes 2d8.

9.name: Aerial Maneuvers
description: At 9th level, you have greatly improved the maneuverability of your Flying Machine. While you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground with your Flying Machine, you gain the following benefits:

• You can use your bonus action to Dash.
  • You gain a bonus to your Dexterity ability checks and saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

15.name: Master Aeronaut
description: By 15th level, you have become a master Aeronaut. While you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground in your Flying Machine, and are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail.

Alchemy is a delicate art, tip the ratio of ingredients too far out of line and the effects could be disastrous. Those that study the magic of arcane potions and brews are known as Alchemists. They are experts at combining exotic reagents to produce a variety of materials and effects. From healing droughts that can mend a wound in moments, to sticky goo that explodes when it comes in contact with open flame. With careful preparation, and a bit of luck, Alchemists are masters of both giving life and leeching it away.
subclasses.name: Alchemist Specialization

1.name: Alchemist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stArm Launcher
5thMany-Handed Pouch
9thVampiric Weapon

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you are already proficient with weaver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of alchemist's supplies of your choice.

1.name: Alchemical Expert
description: Starting at 1st level, you are an expert of all things alchemical.  Over the course of a long rest, you can produce a single Common item that can be crafted with Alchemy without requiring any materials.  This item functions as it normally would, but turns to ash when you finish your next long rest.
At 9th level, you can create a Common or Uncommon item.

3.name: Alchemical Elixirs
description: Beginning at 3rd level, at the end of each long rest, you can use your alchemist's supplies produce an Elixir in an empty flask you touch. At creation, you choose the Elixir's effect from one of the tables below, some of which include your proficiency bonus (PB). The effect of an Elixir is triggered when someone drinks the Elixir for Enhancing Elixirs, or when the Elixir hits a creature for Astringent Elixirs. As a bonus action, a creature can drink a Enhancing Elixir or administer it to a creature within 5 feet. As an attack, a creature can throw an Astringent Elixir at a target within 15 feet, making a thrown improvised weapon attack. You have proficiency with attacks made with your Elixirs. A creature can only be under the effects of one Elixir at a time, and coming under the effects of another immediately ends any other Elixir effects.
Any Elixir you create through this feature lasts until it is used, or until the end of your next long rest.
As an action on your turn, you can expend an arcane charge to create an Elixir in an empty flask you touch. You can use the Elixir as part of the same action.
At certain levels in this class, you can make more Elixirs at the end of a long rest: at 6th level (two), and 15th level (three).

subFeatures.name: Astringent Elixirs
description:
ElixirEffect
BlazingThe target takes fire damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is set alight. The target takes an additional 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns while alight. A creature can use an action to extinguish itself or a willing creature within 5 feet of it. This fire does not go out when exposed to water.
CorrosiveThe target takes acid damage equal to 2d4 + PB and has their AC reduced by 1 for 1 minute.
LuminousThe target takes radiant damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is blinded for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Constitution saving throw against your Infusion save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
SappingThe target takes necrotic damage equal to 2d4 + PB and has their hit point maximum reduced by an equal amount until they finish a long rest.
StickyThe target is considered grappled for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Strength saving throw against your Infusion save DC as an action, ending the effect on a success.
ToxicThe target takes poison damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is poisoned for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Constitution saving throw against your Infusion save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

subFeatures.name: Enhancing Elixirs
description:
ElixirEffect
Alteration The drinker is transformed as if by the Alter Self spell. They determine the effect of the spell, which lasts for 10 minutes.
Boldness The drinker can add 1d4 to any attack rolls and saving throws they make for 1 minute.
Flight The drinker gains a flying speed equal to 5 times your PB in feet for 10 minutes.
Healing The drinker regains a number of hit points equal to PB(d4) + your Intelligence Modifier.
Resilience The drinker gains a bonus to their Armor Class equal to half your PB for 10 minutes.
Swiftness The drinker's speed increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times your PB for 1 hour.

5.name: Alchemical Savant
description: Starting at 5th level, when a spell you cast, one of your Elixirs, or one of your Infusions deals acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage, or restores hit points, you gain a bonus to the damage, or healing, roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

9.name: Restorative Reagents
description: Beginning at 9th level, whenever a creature drinks one of your Enhancing Elixirs, they gain temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier, in addition to the Elixir's effect.
Also, you can cast Lesser Restoration, provided you use your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus.
You can cast the spell in this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Master Alchemist
description: By 15th level, you have become a master Alchemist. You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, immunity to the poisoned condition, and you no longer age unless you wish to.
In addition, you can cast both Greater Restoration and Heal, without providing the material component, provided you use your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus.
You can cast each of these spells once with this feature, and you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

For centuries chroniclers have sought the best way to store vast amounts of information. While most were satisfied with scrolls, the Archivists looked for something greater. In their research, they learned to store libraries worth of information in objects, awakening the first Artificial Minds. Working with these wondrous Minds, Archivists wield the limitless power of these arcane intelligences to drive their research forward.
subclasses.name: Archivist Specialization

1.name: Archivist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stGoggles of Clearsight
5thMind Sharpener
9thHelm of Awareness

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies. If you are already proficient with calligrapher's supplies, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you learn to speak, read, and write two langauges of your choice.

1.name: Artificial Mind
description: At 1st level, you learn to awaken mundane objects. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use calligrapher's supplies to awaken an Artificial Mind in a Tiny nonmagical object you touch. While the object is awakened, it is a magical item that requires your attunement.
Should you awaken a second Artificial Mind, any previous Artificial Minds are instantly dispelled. While attuned to the awakened Artificial Mind, you gain the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Skill Proficiencies
description: Depending on the material of the object you awaken, you gain proficiency in two skills of your choice determined by the material your artificial mind is constructed from.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from an animal, such as parchment, leather, or bone.  You can choose from Animal Handling, Insight, Perception, and Survival.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from the earth, such as gems, glass, metal, or stone.  You can choose from Deception, Intimidation, Performance, and Persuasion.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from a plant, such as paper, wood, or vegetable matter.  You can choose from Arcana, History, Nature, and Religion.

subFeatures.name: Information Overload
description: Your Artificial Mind can bombard other minds with psychic information. As an action, you can force a creature you can see within 30 feet to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it takes 1d8 psychic damage and has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn.
As you gain artificer levels, the psychic damage increases: at 5th level (2d8), at 11th level (3d8), and at 17th level (4d8).

3.name: Magical Telephony
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can communicate telepathically with any creature carrying one of your infused items within a 1-mile radius. The creature can also respond telepathically.

5.name: Acute Overload
description: At 5th level, the power of your Artificial Mind has increased. Whenever a creature fails its save against Information Overload you can expend arcane charges to increase the psychic damage. The damage increases by 2d8 for 1 charge, and by an additional 1d8 for each additional charge you expend, to a maximum of 6d8.
In addition, when you deal psychic damage while attuned to your Artificial Mind, you gain a bonus to the damage roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

9.name: Improved Consciousness
description: Starting at 9th level, when you are forced to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration on a spell while you are attuned to your Artificial Mind, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).
Moreover, your Artificial Mind doesn't count against the total number of magical objects you can be attuned to.

15.name: Infoportation
description: By 15th level, you have become a master of Archivist artifice. As an action on your turn, you can transform into pure information and teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 60 feet, or an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a creature or object bearing one of your artificer infusions.

Of all the Specializations that an artificer can pursue, that of the Armorer is the most defensively-minded. With a focus on becoming a bastion of magics and metal, Armorers modify a set of armor to function as their second skin. They focus their signature magic through this armor to unleash potent attacks and generate formidable arcane defenses. An Armorer views their armor as an extension of their body, and as they refine their magical abilities, artificer and armor become one.
subclasses.name: Armorer Specialization

1.name: Armorer Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Defense
5thInfiltrator Armor
9thArmor of Magical Strength

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

1.name: Arcane Gauntlet
description: Starting at 1st level, you can forge for yourself a wondrous weapon of war known as an Arcane Gauntlet. At the end of a long rest, you can use blacksmith's tools to create an Arcane Gauntlet, choosing for it to have one of the following weapons. It is a simple weapon only usable by you, and you use your Intelligence, in place of Strength or Dexterity, for its attack and damage rolls.
You can only have one Arcane Gauntlet at a time. Creating a second causes the magic of the first to immediately dispel.

traits.name: Blaze Gauntlet
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 fire damage.  Additionally, if a target starts its turn grappled by you, it takes 1d6 fire damage.

traits.name: Chain Hook
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 60 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 piercing damage.  Any target hit by your Chain Hook can't move further than 60 feet away from you until they use an action to detach the chain from themselves.

traits.name: Lightning Launcer
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 120 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 lightning damage.  Once per turn, when you hit with an attack with your Lightning Launcher, you can cause it to deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage.

traits.name: Razor Edge
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 slashing damage.  You score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 for attacks with your Razor Edge.

traits.name: Sub-Zero Slammer
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 cold damage.  Any target hit by your Sub-Zero Slammer has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Thunder Fist
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 thunder damage.  Any target hit by your Thunder Fist has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Wrecking Ball
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon with a reach of 10 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage.  If you hit a creature that your size or smaller with your Wrecking Ball, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward yourself.

3.name: Arcane Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, you expand the magic of your Arcane Gauntlet to encompass a full suit of armor. At the end of a long rest, you can use your blacksmith's tools to transform a set of armor into Arcane Armor. This armor incorporates your Arcane Gauntlet, is only usable by you, and while wearing it you gain the following benefits:

• If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, your arcane armor lacks this requirement for you.
  • Your arcane armor attaches to you and can't be removed against your will. It expands to cover your entire body, and functionally replaces any missing limbs or body parts.
  • You can don or doff your arcane armor as an action, and can retract or deploy the helmet as a bonus action.
  • You can use a bonus action to grant yourself temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

5.name: Armorer Adept
description: At 5th level, you can use magical armor as Arcane Armor. Though, any innate magical bonuses to Armor Class from magic armor, Infusions, or other features don't stack. You must choose one.
Finally, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Modular Armor
description: Starting at 9th level, your Arcane Armor counts as multiple items for the purpose of your infusions: armor (the chest piece), boots, helmet, and the gauntlets (weapon), and each item can bear one infusion.
Also, your number of Infusions Known increases by 2, but these extra infusions must be applied to your arcane armor.
When you create an infusion using your arcane armor as the target item, the number of arcane charges you must expend to create the infusion is reduced to 0.

15.name: Master Armorer
description: By 15th level, you have become a master of Armorer artifice. You gain the benefits listed below while wearing your Arcane Armor:

• You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
  • You adjust your Arcane Armor so that you have access to two weapons.
  • Each of your weapons now deal an additional die of damage.

traits.name: Blaze Gauntlet
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 fire damage.  Additionally, if a target starts its turn grappled by you, it takes 1d6 fire damage.

traits.name: Chain Hook
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 60 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 piercing damage.  Any target hit by your Chain Hook can't move further than 60 feet away from you until they use an action to detach the chain from themselves.
