description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 slashing damage.  You score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 for attacks with your Razor Edge.

traits.name: Sub-Zero Slammer
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 cold damage.  Any target hit by your Sub-Zero Slammer has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Thunder Fist
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 thunder damage.  Any target hit by your Thunder Fist has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Wrecking Ball
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon with a reach of 10 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage.  If you hit a creature that your size or smaller with your Wrecking Ball, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward yourself.

An Artillerist specializes in using magic to hurl energy, projectiles, and explosions on a battlefield. This destructive power is valued by armies in the wars on many different worlds. And when war passes, some members of this specialization seek to build a more peaceful world by using their powers to fight the resurgence of strife. The world-hopping gnome artificer Vi has been especially vocal about making things right: "It's about time we fixed things instead of blowing them all to hell."
subclasses.name: Artillerist Specialization

1.name: Artillerist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
2ndArm Launcher
5thRepulsion Gauntlets
9thSplintershot Weapon

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you are already proficient with woodcarver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Arcane Cannon
description: Also at 1st level, you've learned how to create a magical cannon. Using woodcarver's tools, you can take an action to magically create a Small arcane cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of you. An arcane cannon occupies its space. Once you create a cannon, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or until you expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one cannon at a time and can't create one while your cannon is present.

The cannon is a magical object. It has an AC of 18 and a number of hit points equal to five times your artificer level. It is immune to poison damage and psychic damage. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). If the Mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. It disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points or after 1 hour. You can dismiss it early as an action.

When you create the cannon, you determine its appearance and whether it has legs. You also decide which type it is, choosing from the options on the Arcane Cannons table. On each of your turns, you can take a bonus action to cause the cannon to activate if you are within 60 feet of it. As part of the same bonus action, you can direct the cannon to walk or climb up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space, provided it has legs.

Most cannons require an attack roll or saving throw, for which Intelligence is your ability. Your attack modifier for their effects and your saving throw DC are the same as your Infusion attack modifier and saving throw DC.

CannonEffect
Acid SpitterThe cannon belches acid in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 acid damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The acid instantly dissolves any nonmagical, organic objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
BolterThe cannon fires a simple projectile at high speed. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 120 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes magical piercing damage equal to 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier.
ChainswordThe cannon lashes out with a blade resembling that of a chainsaw. Make a melee attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 magical slashing damage. The cannon deals a critical hit with this attack on a roll of 19 or 20.
FlamethrowerThe cannon shoots flames in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 fire damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The flames ignite any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
Force BallistaThe cannon launches a bolt of magical energy. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 60 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 force damage and is pushed up to 5 feet away from the cannon.
Freeze RayThe cannon fires a bolt of energy that drains away heat. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 60 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 cold damage and if the target is a creature, its speed is reduced by 10 feet.
Grenade LauncherThe cannon lobs an explosive at a point within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 magical bludgeoning damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The explosive deals double damage to objects and structures.
Mental DisruptorThe cannon emits a cloud of confusion-inducing gas. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make an Intelligence saving throw, taking 2d8 psychic damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also stunned until the start of its next turn or until it takes damage.
ProtectorThe cannon emits a burst of positive energy that grants itself and each creature of your choice within 10 feet of it a number of temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier.
Sanguine DrainerThe cannon saps away life energy. Make a melee spell attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 necrotic damage and it cannot regain hit points by any means short of the Wish spell until the start of its next turn.
Solar FlareThe cannon shines blinding light in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also blinded until the end of its next turn.
Tesla CoilThe cannon launches lightning in an adjacent 40-foot long, 5-foot wide line that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 lightning damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The lightning ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
Ultrasonic GeneratorThe cannon emits deafening sound. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 thunder damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also deafened until the end of its next turn.
Viral DispenserThe cannon emits a cloud of disease. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 poison damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also poisoned until the end of its next turn.

3.name: Spell-Storing Cannon
description: Starting at 3rd level, your Arcane Cannon can serve as the material for a Minor Spellstoring Item, and you can choose to cast the stored spell instead of causing the cannon's effect when you activate it.
Starting at 9th level, it can also serve as the material for a Greater Spellstoring Item.

5.name: Versatile Artillery
description: At 5th level, when you create an arcane cannon, you can choose two effects, rather than one, though you can only activate one effect of your choice with your bonus action.
At 15th level, you can instead choose three effects.

9.name: Explosive Cannon
description: Starting at 9th level, every arcane cannon you create is more destructive:

• The cannon's damage rolls all increase by 1d8.
  • As an action, you can command the cannon to detonate if you are within 60 feet of it. Doing so destroys the cannon and forces each creature within 20 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

15.name: Fortified Position
description: By 15th level, you're a master at forming well-defended emplacements using Arcane Cannon:

• You and your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of a cannon you create with Arcane Cannon, as a result of a shimmering field of magical protection that the cannon emits.
  • You can now have two cannons at the same time. You can create two with the same action, and you can activate both of them with the same bonus action. You determine whether the cannons are identical to each other or different. You can't create a third cannon while you have two.

A combination of protector and medic, Battle Smith artificers are experts at defending others and repairing both material and personnel. To aid in their work, Battle Smiths construct and modify their Steel Defender, a one-of-a-kind companion.
subclasses.name: Battle Smith

1.name: Battle Smith Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Weapon
5thRepulsion Shield
9thBoots of Earthquakes

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you gain proficiency in heavy armor.

1.name: Steel Defender
description: At 1st level, you have created for yourself a faithful construct, known as a Steel Defender. It is friendly to you and your allies and obeys your orders. Your Steel Defender's game statistics are found in the Steel Defender stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in multiple places.

In combat, your Steel Defender acts during your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it only uses the Dodge action on its turn unless you use your bonus action to order it to take an action in its stat block, or another action. If you are incapacitated, your Steel Defender acts on its own.
If your Steel Defender has died within the last hour, you can touch it with your blacksmith's tools and expend an arcane charge to return it to life with its maximum hit points.
At the end of a long rest, you can magically create a new Steel Defender with your blacksmith's tools. When you do so, any previous Steel Defenders are immediately rendered inert.
Upon its creation, you choose the shape of your Steel Defender, which can affect its abilities in and out of combat.

Steel Defender
Medium or Large construct
Armor Class: 12 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 2 + your Intelligence modifier + 5 times your artificer level
Speed: 30 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
16 (+3)12 (+1)14 (+2)4 (-3)10 (0)6 (-2)
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: charmed, dominated, exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10 + PB
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Proficiency Bonus (PB): equals your bonus
Might of the Master. You add your PB to any ability check or saving throw the Steel Defender makes.
Vigilant. The defender can't be surprised.
Actions
Rend. Melee Weapon Attack: your Intelligence modifier + PB to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d8 + PB force damage.
Repair. The magical mechanisms inside the defender restore 1d10 + PB hit points to itself or to one construct or object within 5 feet of it.
Your Steel Defender is the size of a Medium humanoid creature. It is proficient with shields, and it has humanoid hands that it can use to perform basic tasks.
Your Steel Defender resembles a Large beast of your choice. Its speed increases by 10 feet, and it can be ridden as a mount by you as if it was a trained mount.
Specific version of the Humanoid Steel Defender for Neelo.

3.name: Battle Ready
description: At 3rd level, you have trained to stand alongside your Steel Defender in battle. You can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls you make with magic weapons, or any weapon that bears one of your Infusions.

5.name: Infusion Bearer
description: At 5th level, you have designed your Steel Defender to bear your most potent infusions. Your Steel Defender can bear any infusion that is meant for boots, cloaks, gauntlets, helms, or suits of armor. However, it can only bear one Infusion at a time.

5.name: Minor Upgrade
description: Also at 5th level, you have improved the offensive capabilities of your Steel Defender. Choose one of the Minor Upgrades below:

The damage of your Steel Defender's Rend becomes 1d10, and when you command it to take the Rend action it can make two Rend attacks instead of one. It can replace either Rend attack with a grapple or shove.

You imbue your Steel Defender with a 1st-level spell with a casting time of one action. As a bonus action, you can order your Steel Defender to cast the imbued spell at 1st-level, using your Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.
Your Steel Defender has a number of charges of the spell equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1), and it regains all expended charges when you finish a long rest.

9.name: Adjustable Upgrades
description: Starting at 9th level, you can adjust your Steel Defender's Upgrades to face the challenges at hand. Each time you finish a long rest, you can use your blacksmith's tools to replace one of your Steel Defender's Upgrades with another Upgrade gained at the same level.

9.name: Greater Upgrade
description: Also at 9th level, you can imbue your Steel Defender with wondrous abilities and features. Choose one of the Greater Upgrades below:

You improve the cognitive abilities of your Steel Defender. Its Intelligence score becomes a 10. It also gains proficiency with a set of tools of your choice and learns to speak, read, and write two languages of your choice.
Your Steel Defender can bear up to two infusions, though the infusions must be meant for different types of objects.
You improve the structure of your Steel Defender. It gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from all non-magical attacks.

15.name: Masterwork Upgrade
description: At 15th level, you imbue your Steel Defender with wondrous abilities and powers. Choose one of the Masterwork Upgrades below:
Creatures of your choice within 15 feet of your Steel Defender are resistant to damage from spells.

You imbue your Steel Defender with a 3rd-level spell with a casting time of one action. As a bonus action, you can order your Steel Defender to cast the imbued spell at 3rd-level, using your Intelligence as its spellcasting ability.
Your Steel Defender has a number of charges of the spell equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1), and it regains all expended charges when you finish a long rest.

You embed a powerful arcane explosive in your Steel Defender. As a bonus action, you can order your Steel Defender to self-destruct, destroying itself and forcing creatures within 20 feet to make a Dexterity saving throw. Creatures take force damage equal to your Steel Defenders remaining Hit Dice on a failed save, or half as much damage on a success. Once this feature is used, your Steel Defender cannot be revived until the end of your next long rest.

Every adventuring party needs a safe place to rest. A Caravaneer is a master of hospitality who maintains and provides a smoking magical vehicle to act as a home away from home for any diligent traveler.
subclasses.name: Caravaneer Specialization

1.name: Caravaneer Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Tool Set
5thImmovable Boots
9thBoots of the Winding Path

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with mason's tools. If you are already proficient with mason's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Comforts of the Home
description: At 1st level, you can readily produce basic items that one might find in a typical home or village.  At the end of a long rest, you can produce a number of items of adventuring gear equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).  Each of these objects must be worth 10 gp or less. These objects appear as mundane versions of those objects but turn to ash at the end of your next long rest.
You can also craft the normal versions of such objects in one-quarter of the normal time.

3.name: Arcane Caravan
description: At 3rd level, you have constructed a mobile home known as an arcane caravan. See its game statistics in the Arcane Caravan stat block along with your 9th and 15th level features. You determine the arcane caravan's appearance and you can use an action to control it with a console inside.

Inside the arcane caravan is an extradimensional dwelling. It is warm and dry, regardless of conditions outside. You can create any floor plan you like with the space indicated in the stat block. The place is furnished and decorated as you choose, but it must include a fireplace that leads to the chimney outside, a console, and at least one door and window. Any equipment or furnishings conjured within the arcane caravan dissipate into smoke if removed from it. You can use an action with mason's tools to transform the layout when no creatures are inside it except yourself.

Once per round, if fire damage is dealt to the fireplace, the arcane caravan regains 2d4+2 hit points. If its hit points are reduced to zero, all creatures and objects within the extradimensional dwelling are expelled through the chimney and fall prone into the nearest open spaces, taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage plus any excess damage the arcane caravan took. No creatures can enter or recall the arcane caravan until it is revived. You can spend 1 hour working with mason's tools and expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to revive it with all of its hit points restored.
Using mason's tools, you can spend 8 hours to construct a new arcane caravan. If you already have an arcane caravan from this feature, the first one immediately perishes.

Arcane Caravan
Large or Huge vehicle (3000 or 9000 lbs)
Armor Class: 15 (natural armor)
Hit Points: 2 + your Intelligence modifier + 5 times your artificer level
Speed: 30 ft.
STRDEXCON
18 (+4)7 (-2)20 (+5)
Chimney Focus. If a spell that affects an area is cast within 5 feet of the fireplace, such as Burning Hands or Fog Cloud, the caster can choose to have it originated or centered on the caravan's chimney, affecting the area outside. This effect does not damage the caravan itself.
Extradimensional Dwelling. The dwelling inside the caravan can be up to 10 cubes, each cube being 10 feet on each side.
Recall Link. You can use an action to recall the caravan, making it travel to your location from up to 5 miles away.
Console Actions
Activate/Deactivate Headlight (Action). A piece of the caravan casts or snuffs a bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
Set Course (Action). The controller chooses a destination it can see or has seen and a rough route. The caravan automatically follows the route to the destination.
Use Periscope (Bonus Action). You can see outside as if you were in the caravan's space.

5.name: Zone of Hospitality
description: At 5th level, you can generate zones which act as small magical sanctuaries for your allies. When a creature restores hit points within 5 feet of an object which bears one of your infusions, it gains temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier plus double your proficiency bonus.

9.name: Improved Caravan
description: At 9th level, you improve your arcane caravan, causing it to gain the following benefits:

• Its speed increases to 50 ft.
  • The maximum space within the caravan expands to 100 cubes, each cube being 10 feet on a side.
  • You can spend 1 hour working with mason's tools to swap in a climbing or swimming speed to the caravan equal to its base speed.
  • The caravan's Recall Link trait works as long as it is on the same plane of existence as you.

15.name: Master Caravaneer
description: At 15th level, you perfect your arcane caravan, causing it to gain the following benefits:

• You can spend 1 hour working with mason's tools to swap in a flying speed to the caravan equal to its base speed.
  • As an action while at the console, you can cause the caravan to teleport to a destination it has been on the same plane of existence in the past 7 days. Once this is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

Behind every great musician, every standing ovation, every sold-out concert, there is most often Composer who put quill to parchment and penned the notes. These great minds are unlike other bards and entertainers, Composers take a more cerebral approach to music. They are masters of patterns and repetition, and when they apply their analytical mind to a problem it is only a matter of time before they find a solution.
subclasses.name: Composer Specialization

1.name: Composer Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Instrument
5thRepulsion Gauntlets
9thChameleon Armor

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you are already proficient with woodcarver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, if you spend at least 1 minute practicing with a musical instrument, you are considered proficient with that musical instrument until the end of your next long rest.

1.name: Musical Apparatus
description: At 1st level, you have designed a wondrous new musical instrument. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use woodcarver's tools to construct a Musical Apparatus of your own design. You are proficient with your Apparatus as a musical instrument, and whenever you make an ability check that uses your Musical Apparatus, you can add double your proficiency bonus to the result of your roll. You can only have one Musical Apparatus at a time. If you create a second, the previous Apparatus becomes unusable.
When you gain the Spellcasting feature at 2nd level your Musical Apparatus can be used as a spellcasting focus.

3.name: Weaponized Apparatus
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can modify your Musical Apparatus to be used for both entertainment and combat. When you create an Apparatus, it gains one of the following features of your choice:

traits.name: Raucous Blast
description: As an action, you can use your Apparatus to make an attack using your Intelligence modifier against a creature within 60 feet that can hear you. On hit, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage and is deafened until the beginning of your next turn.
This thunder damage increases by 1d8 at 5th level (2d8), and again at 11th level (3d8), and at 17th level (4d8).

traits.name: Ringing Strike
description: Your Apparatus is a simple weapon with the versatile property, that deals 1d8 (1d10) bludgeoning damage on hit. You are considered proficient with it, and you can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength, for attack and damage rolls with the Apparatus.
You also learn the Booming Blade cantrip.  Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it. When you cast booming blade, you must use your Apparatus as the spell's material component.

5.name: Thunderous Note
description: Starting at 5th level, when you use your Apparatus to deal thunder damage, you can expend any number of arcane charges to knock a Large or smaller creature back with a thunderous burst of sound. The target is knocked back 20 feet  for 1 charge, and by an additional 10 feet for each additional charge you expend.
Also, whenever you deal thunder damage you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage roll.

9.name: Resonant Frequency
description: Starting at 9th level, as an action, you can play a note on your Apparatus to cause a creature of your choice within 10 feet to resonate with undetectable vibrations for 1 hour. The next time it is hit with a melee attack, its attacker must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the attacker takes 2d8 thunder damage and cannot take reactions until the beginning of its next turn. On a successful save, the attacker takes half damage.
You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Master Composer
description: By 15th level, you have mastered the theory and applications of musical artifice, becoming a master. You gain the following benefits:

• You are immune to thunder damage and being deafened.
  • Your Musical Apparatus gains both the Raucous Blast and Ringing Strike attacks.
  • Your Thunderous Note feature can affect Huge or smaller creatures. Large or smaller creatures that fail the saving throw fall prone at the end of their forced movement.
  • The damage of Resonant Frequency becomes 4d8.

traits.name: Ringing Strike
description: Your Apparatus is a simple weapon with the versatile property, that deals 1d8 (1d10) bludgeoning damage on hit. You are considered proficient with it, and you can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength, for attack and damage rolls with the Apparatus.
You also learn the Booming Blade cantrip.  Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it. When you cast booming blade, you must use your Apparatus as the spell's material component.

traits.name: Raucous Blast
description: As an action, you can use your Apparatus to make an attack using your Intelligence modifier against a creature within 60 feet that can hear you. On hit, the creature takes 1d8 thunder damage and is deafened until the beginning of your next turn.
This thunder damage increases by 1d8 at 5th level (2d8), and again at 11th level (3d8), and at 17th level (4d8).

Where most artificers develop objects of wondrous power, those known as Enhanced bring their great intellect to bear by modifying their own bodies. They replace and improve their own limbs with arcane enhancements, forever striving to create a more perfect self. Enhanced artificers are known for their impressive, and deadly, combat Enhancements.
subclasses.name: Enhanced Specialization

1.name: Enhanced Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Weapon
5thImmovable Boots
9thArmor of Magical Strength

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

1.name: Blade Enhancement
description: Starting at 1st level, you modify one of your arms to bear a hidden blade. It is a simple melee weapon with the finesse property that deals 1d8 slashing damage on hit and has the following abilities:

• It is completely concealed within your arm unless you use a bonus action to activate or retract your blade.
  • It can bear one Infusion meant for a melee weapon.
  • You can use your Intelligence, in place of your Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls of your blade.

3.name: Enhancements
description: At 3rd level, you begin to modify your body with mechanical augmentations.  You gain one Enhancement of your choice. They can be attached in place of a missing body part, or over a body part.
When you gain an artificer level you can replace your Enhancement with another Enhancement of your choice.
As you gain artificer levels, your body can bear additional Enhancements at one time: at 5th level (2), 9th level (3), and at 15th level (4).

5.name: Combat Enhancement
description: At 5th level, you have improved your modifications to further augment your combat abilities. You gain the following benefits:

• You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
  • Each of your Enhancements can bear a single Infusion usually meant for the following objects: Mobility (boots), Nimble (gauntlets), Power (armor), Visual (helm, goggles).
  • Your Blade counts as magical for the sake of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks.

9.name: Improved Enhancements
description: Starting at 9th level, your number of Infusions Known increases by 1, but this additional Infusion must be applied to an Enhancement.
When you create an infusion using one of your enhancements as the target item, the number of arcane charges you must expend to create the infusion is reduced to 0.
In addition, the damage of your blade attacks becomes 2d10.

15.name: Master Enhanced
description: By 15th level, choose one of your Enhancements to become a Masterwork Enhancement, granting you the additional benefits below.
Each time you finish a long rest, you can replace your Masterwork Enhancement with another of your choice.
Your Blade Enhancement weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
When you take the Dash action you are immune to opportunity attacks and you can move along vertical surfaces and liquids without falling during the move.
When you make a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
When you make a Strength check with your modified arm, you treat a roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
When you make a check that relies on your sense of sight, you treat a roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

While most artificers are primarily tinkers that take up a life of adventure to test experiments in the field, those known as Forgewrights seek out battle for its own sake. Reveling in the thrill of combat, they combine their innovation with their skill as warriors to forge their signature Arcane Armament.
subclasses.name: Forgewright Specialization

1.name: Forgewright Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Weapon
5thLight Blade
9thTelescoping Weapon

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

1.name: Arcane Armament
description: At 1st level, you can create a wondrous weapon known as an Arcane Armament.  Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use your blacksmith's tools to transform one melee weapon you touch into your Arcane Armament. While you wield your Arcane Armament, you gain the benefits below.
You can only have one Arcane Armament at a time, and enchanting a second causes the magic of the first to end.

• You can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength or Dexterity, for attack and damage rolls with the weapon. The weapon gains both the Thrown (20/60) and Returning properties. After you make a thrown weapon attack with your Arcane Armament, it instantly returns to your hand.
  • It counts as a magical weapon if it was not already.

3.name: Forge of War
description: At 3rd level, your signature artifice enhances the power of your weapon. Any weapon attacks you make with your Arcane Armament score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
Also, your total number of Infusions Known increases by 1. However, this bonus infusion must be applied to your Arcane Armament, and can be applied even if it was a magic weapon.
When you create an infusion using your arcane armament as the target item, the number of arcane charges you must expend to create the infusion is reduced to 0.

5.name: Arcane Jolt
description: At 5th level, when you hit a creature with your arcane armament you can expend arcane charges to deal additional force damage. The damage increases by 2d6 for 1 charge, and by an additional 1d6 for each additional charge you expend, to a maximum of 6d6.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Also at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, when you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Improved Arcane Jolt
description: Starting at 9th level, the magic of your Arcane Armament empowers its strikes. Each time you hit a creature with a weapon attack with your Arcane Armament you deal an additional 1d6 force damage.
This force damage does not count against the maximum amount of damage you can deal with your Arcane Jolt feature.

15.name: Master Forgewright
description: By 15th level, you have become a master among Forgewright artificers and can extend the power within your Arcane Armament to allies. As an action, you can hold aloft your Arcane Armament and, choose a number of weapons equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) within 30 feet, one of which can be your Arcane Armament. For the next minute these weapons deal an additional 1d6 force damage on hit.
Once you use this feature you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses of this feature left, you can expend 3 arcane charges to use this feature again.

These Artificers focus their magic on harnessing the strength of stone and earth. As master masons, they infuse their magic into stone to create a Terrain Manipulator. They utilise these unique magical constructs as a tool to alter the field of battle.
subclasses.name: Geologist Specialization

1.name: Geologist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stEnhanced Defense
5thImmovable Boots
9thBoots of Earthquakes

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with mason's tools. If you are already proficient with mason's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Terrain Manipulator
description: At 2nd level, you have constructed the signature invention of a Geologist, the Terrain Manipulator. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use mason's tools to craft a Terrain Manipulator. It is a small, magical object, made of a single block of magically enhanced stone or clay, that appears as a geometric shape of your choice.

Your Terrain Manipulator hovers off the ground and follows you if not directed otherwise. You can direct it to attach itself to you (no action required), occupying the same space as you and moving with you.

On each of your turns, you can take a bonus action to cause the Terrain Manipulator to activate one of the abilities below if you are within 60 feet of it. As part of the same bonus action, you can direct it to move up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space. If you die, it crumbles and becomes permanently inactive.

The Terrain Manipulator has an AC of 10 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier and a number of Hit Points equal to 10 times your Artificer level.  As an action, you can touch it and expend any number of arcane charges, restoring a number of hit points equal to five times the number of expended charges.
If it is forced to make an ability check or saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 + your proficiency bonus.
You can only maintain one Terrain Manipulator, and creating a second one causes the magic of any others to dispel.

subFeatures.name: Manipulate
description: You choose a portion of dirt or stone that you can see within range and that fits within a 5-foot cube. It is manipulated in one of the following ways:

• If you target an area of loose earth, you can instantaneously excavate it, move it along the ground, and deposit it up to 5 feet away. This movement doesn't have enough force to cause damage.
  • You cause shapes, colors, or both to appear on the dirt or stone, spelling out words, creating images, or shaping patterns. The changes last for 1 hour.
  • If the dirt or stone you target is on the ground, you cause it to become difficult terrain. Alternatively, you can cause the ground to become normal terrain if it is already difficult terrain. This change lasts for 1 hour.
If you use this feature multiple times, you can have no more than two of its non-instantaneous effects active at a time, and you can dismiss such an effect as a bonus action.

3.name: Advanced Manipulation
description: At 3rd level, your Terrain Manipulator gains the following additional functions.

subFeatures.name: Displace
description: The Terrain Manipulator attempts to push a creature within 5 feet of it with a swell of dirt, forcing it to make a Strength saving throw against your Infusion save DC. On a failed save, the creature is pushed up to 15 feet in a straight line.

subFeatures.name: Stone Barrier
description: The Terrain Manipulator shifts itself into a barrier of solid stone. Starting at its current location, the barrier must be in a straight line up to 10 feet wide, 5 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The barrier cannot be extended through the space of a structure or creature. While the barrier is active, the Terrain Manipulator cannot move or be moved. When the Terrain Manipulator's hit points fall to zero or as a bonus action, it shifts back into its original form. When Stone Barrier is deactivated, it can only be activated again on your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Upheval
description: The Terrain Manipulator creates a tremor in a 10 foot radius around itself. The area becomes difficult terrain until the start of your next turn.

5.name: Earthen Eruption
description: At 5th level, your focus on studying the magic of earth and stone allows you to infuse all of your magic with its power.
Once per turn, when a creature is affected by one of your class features, you can choose one of the affected creatures and activate one of the following effects on it in addition.

subFeatures.name: Explosive Eruption
description: Any number of creatures of your choice within 5 feet of the affected creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Infusion save DC or take bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

subFeatures.name: Implosive Eruption
description: The affected creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Infusion save DC or take bludgeoning damage equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

9.name: Bolstered Manipulation
description: At 9th level, You infuse additional magic into your Terrain Manipulator, enhancing its abilities.
The Displace, Stone Barrier, and Upheaval abilities of your Terrain Manipulator change as described below.

subFeatures.name: Displace
description: The affected creature can now be pushed up to 20 feet.

subFeatures.name: Stone Barrier
description: The Stone Barrier can now be up to 20 feet wide and 10 feet high.

subFeatures.name: Upheval
description: The affected area now has a radius of 15 feet.

15.name: Focused Manipulation
description: By 15th level, you refine the magic invoking glyphs carved into your Terrain Manipulator, adding additional utility to its abilities.
The Stone Barrier, Displace, and Upheaval abilities of your Terrain Manipulator gain the following features.

subFeatures.name: Displace
description: When a creature is pushed by Displace, it is also restrained until the end of its next turn.

subFeatures.name: Stone Barrier
description: When Stone Barrier is used, the Terrain Manipulator becomes immune to all damage until the end of your next turn and resistant to all damage types for each turn after that as long as Stone Barrier is active.

subFeatures.name: Upheval
description: When Upheaval is used, you can force one creature in the affected area to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Infusion save DC. On a failed save, it is knocked prone.

A Lapidist specializes in the creation of magical gemstones and prisms. These crystals focus and split their spells, and allow them to easily expand or focus their magic. The crystals that lapidists create can be used by them or their allies, which makes them wonderful support for any variety of offensive spellcaster.
subclasses.name: Lapidist Specialization

1.name: Lapidist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stGoggles of Clearsight
5thRadiant Weapon
9thChameleon Armor

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with jeweler's tools. If you are already proficient with jeweler's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Runic Crystal
description: At 1st level, you forge a runic crystal, an iridescent and enscorcelled crystal, through which to channel spells. When you finish a long rest, you can magically produce a Runic Crystal, provided you have jeweler's tools in hand. Your Runic Crystal is a Tiny object with a flying speed of 30 feet and the ability to hover.

You can create additional Runic Crystals by expending an arcane charge for each one. In any case, you can have a maximum number of crystals equal to your proficiency bonus. If you attempt to exceed the limit, the oldest existing crystal becomes inert.
As a bonus action on your turn, you can move your Runic Crystal up to its speed. You can cast spells from your location or from the location of your Runic Crystal.

When you reach certain levels in this class, you can make more crystals at the end of a long rest: two at 6th level and three at 15th level. The crystals function identically, and you can move one or multiple with a bonus action.

3.name: Redirection
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can redirect your spells through your Runic Crystal, reflecting the spell in a different direction.

If you or a friendly creature causes an effect that affects an area of effect in a line, if you or your Runic Crystal is within the effect's area of effect, you can choose to redirect the effect's area of effect. If you do so, the line goes until you or the crystal and then turns in a direction of your choice and goes the remaining distance. A target can only be affected by a given effect once. For example, a lightning bolt spell could move 20 feet towards a crystal, turn, and then move another 80 feet in a new direction.
When a target redirects a effect, it is unaffected by the effect.

If you redirect an effect that does not have a duration of Instantaneous, the redirection ends if you or one of the crystals exits its area. You can change how crystals redirect an effect as part of the same bonus action you use to move them.
Effects that qualify for this feature include line spells, a dragonborn's breath weapon (if they choose for it to be a line), or anything else that has a line area of effect.

5.name: Focused Point
description: Starting at 5th level, you can reroll the damage of any spell you cast or redirect through a Runic Crystal and take either total.

9.name: Splitting Redirection
description: Starting at 9th level, when you use your Redirection feature, you can choose to split the effect into multiple lines. If you do so, each line that you split the effect into has a range equal to the remaining range divided by the number of lines (rounding down to the nearest amount of 5 feet). For example, a lightning bolt spell could move 20 feet towards a crystal, and then be expelled as two 40-foot lines or four 20-foot lines.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Refraction
description: Starting at 15th level, your Runic Crystals can function as magical prisms, refracting spells into cones of destructive force. When you use your Redirection feature, you can instead choose to have the Runic Crystal expel the spell as a cone with a size equal to half its remaining range (minimum of 5 feet). For example, a lightning bolt spell could move 20 feet towards a crystal, turn, and then be expelled as a 40-foot cone.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so once you finish a long rest.

While some artificers spend their lives perfecting one solitary creation, Machinist artificer value quantity over quality. They are known for creating their signature Automatons, small clockwork men that are created for a single, but temporary purpose. Armed with their tools, and an army of strange and wondrous servants, Machinists are ready for any challenge.
subclasses.name: Machinist Specialization

1.name: Machinist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stArcane Firearm
5thMany-Handed Pouch
9thHorseless Carriage

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Automatons
description: At 1st level, you learned to craft unique mechanical servants known as Automatons. At the end of each long rest, you can use your smith's tools to craft a Small Automaton in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

Automatons are magical constructs with an Armor Class equal to 12 + your Intelligence modifier and hit points equal to your artificer level + your Intelligence modifier. When they make an ability check or a saving throw, its ability scores are 10 (0). If the Mending spell is cast on one, it regains 2d6 hit points. It disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points or after 1 hour.

In order to create an additional Automaton before the end of your next long rest, you must expend an arcane charge to create one. You can only have a single operational Automaton at any one time. Creating a second Automaton causes any previous ones to instantly fall apart.

Your Automatons can do nothing on their own. However, you can use a bonus action on your turn to activate one of your Automatons so long as you are within 60 feet of it. As part of this bonus action, you can also cause your Automation to move up to 25 feet.
Whenever you create an Automaton, choose one of the Automaton models below:

subFeatures.name: Agent Automaton
description: When activated, you see and hear through the Automaton, so long as you are within 100 feet of it. You are deaf and blind to your senses until you end this link as a bonus action.

subFeatures.name: Artisan Automaton
description: This Automaton is proficient with one set of tools, and when activated, it makes an ability check with its tool set, and adds your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to its roll.

3.name: Innovative Models
description: Starting at 3rd level, you learn to create the following additional models of automaton:

subFeatures.name: Anchor Automaton
description: When activated, the Automaton latches onto a target within 5 feet, reducing the target's speed by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 5 feet).

subFeatures.name: Armor Automaton
description: When activated, the Automaton attaches itself to a willing creature within 5 feet. While attached, that creature's Armor Class cannot be less than 13 + your Intelligence modifier.

subFeatures.name: Assault Automaton
description: When activated, the Automaton makes a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet. On hit, it deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Intelligence modifier.

5.name: Arcane Conduit
description: At 5th level, you can channel your signature artificer magic through your Automatons. When you cast a spell, you can choose for the spell to originate from an Automaton of your choice, instead of yourself, so long as you are within 60 feet of it.

5.name: Automated Army
description: Also at 5th level, you now create two Automatons of your choice at the end of each long rest without expending any arcane charges, and you can activate up to two Automatons with the same bonus action.
At 15th level, you can create and control up to three.

9.name: Efficient Artifice
description: Starting at 9th level, whenever you expend arcane charges to create an Automaton, you create a number of Automatons equal to the number of charges expended. You cannot use this feature to exceed the maximum number of Automatons you can control.

15.name: Master Machinist
description: By 15th level, you have become a master of Machinist artifice. When you are forced to make a saving throw or are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to switch places with one of your Automatons within 60 feet. The Automaton then becomes the target of the attack or saving throw.

Mutagenists are Artificers who have subjected themselves to radical experiments in physical augmentation, making use of alchemical mutagens. As a result, they now harbor two selves - a brilliant master of mutagenics, and a savage, muscular alter-ego. This internal duality is both a source of power and a personal struggle.
subclasses.name: Mutagenist Specialization

1.name: Mutagenist Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stArm Launcher
5thSwift Ring
9thAdrenaline Armor

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you are already proficient with alchemist's supplies, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Mutagenic Shot
description: When you adopt this Specialization at 1st level, you learn to craft alchemical mutagens that can enhance the physical abilities of creatures. While you have your alchemist's supplies, you can expend an arcane charge as a bonus action to touch a creature within 5 feet of you and briefly enhance its capabilities. Choose between Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution. The target has advantage on all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws using the chosen ability score until the start of your next turn.

3.name: Brutish Transformation
description: Starting at 3rd level, the mutagens in your body have altered your body and mind to create a monstrous alter-ego within you. As a bonus action, you can expend an arcane charge to surrender your keen mind and give way to this brute. Being in your brute from imparts the following effects on you for 10 minutes, until you become incapacitated, or until you take a bonus action to end them early.

subFeatures.name: Hulking Constitution
description: You gain temporary hit points equal to three times your Artificer level. If you have any of these temporary hit points remaining when this effect ends, they are lost.

subFeatures.name: Brutish Strength
description: You can use your Intelligence modifier in place of your Strength modifier when making ability checks, saving throws, and attack or damage rolls using Strength. However, when you make an Intelligence ability check or saving throw, you don't add your Intelligence modifier to the roll.
Additionally, you ignore the Heavy property of weapons, and you can use the larger dice of a Massive weapon without a penalty to your attack roll.

subFeatures.name: Smashing Strikes
description: When you hit with an unarmed strike, it deals bludgeoning damage equal to 1d8 + your Strength or Intelligence modifier. Once per turn when you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can deal an additional 1d8 damage of the same type.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with improvised weapons.

subFeatures.name: Savage Mind
description: You can only cast or concentrate on a spell, or use a feature that expends any number of arcane charges, if it targets only yourself.

5.name: Enhanced Assault
description: At 5th level, your knowledge of mutagens grows. You gain the following benefits.

subFeatures.name: Extra Attack
entries: While you're in your Brute Form, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

subFeatures.name: Strike Enhancement
entries: While not in your Brute Form, you can administer special mutagens to enhance the strikes of others. Whenever you use your Mutagenic Shot, the first time the target deals damage before the start of your next turn, it can add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll.

9.name: Mutagenic Expertise
description: At 9th level, your experience with mutagens allows you to shape your Brute Form and your allies to be tougher, faster, or larger. Select one of the following options. You can change your selection whenever you finish a long rest.

traits.name: Thunderous Charge
description: While you are in your Brute Form, your speed increases by 10 feet and you have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. When you deal the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you can move up to 10 feet without expending movement or provoking opportunity attacks.

traits.name: Swiftstep
description: When you use your Mutagenic Shot, the target moves swiftly. Until the start of your next turn, its speed is doubled and it can make one additional attak when it takes the Attack action.

traits.name: Ironclad Endurance
description: While you are in your Brute form, you gain resistance to two damage types of your choice. When you deal the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you gain temporary hit points equal to the roll of the extra 1d8.

traits.name: Ironskin
description: When you use your Mutagenic Shot, the target gains temporary hit points equal to your Artificer level. Until the start of your next turn, it gains resistance to two damage types of your choice.

traits.name: Hulking Size
description: While you are in your Brute Form, if you are smaller than Large, you become Large, and the damage die for your unarmed strikes increases to 1d10. If there isn;t enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesn't change. When you deal the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you can push the target 15 feet away from your in a straight line.

traits.name: Muscular Expansion
description: When you use your Mutagenic Shot, the target's muscles swell. Until the start of your next turn, its reach is increased by 5 feet, and it deals an extra 1d6 damage when it hits with a melee weapon attack.

15.name: Master of Two Minds
description: By 15th level, you and your brutish self have reached a point of equilibrium, and can work in synergy.

subFeatures.name: Adept Augment
description: You can change the choice of your Mutagenic Expertise whenever you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Devastating Smash
description: The extra damage of your Smashing Strikes increases to 2d8.

subFeatures.name: Free Transformation
description: You can remain in your Brute Form indefinitely. Additionally, you can transform into your Brute Form without expending an arcane charge.

subFeatures.name: Supercharged Shot
description: When you use your Mutagenic Shot, you can expend 2 extra arcane charges to extend its benefits to last for 1 minute.

Focusing their inventive mind on training their domesticated ooze, Ooze Ranchers never go anywhere without their loyal pets. Using their signature Ooze Containment Unit, they can harvest the Essence of other creatures and use these strange concentrates to modify their Domesticated Ooze, granting it the powers of any monster they can slay and harvest.
subclasses.name: Ooze Rancher

1.name: Ooze Rancher Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stPower Whip
5thRepulsion Shield
9thChameleon Armor

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you are already proficient with alchemist's supplies, you instead gain proficiency with another set of alchemist's supplies of your choice.

1.name: Ooze Containment Unit
description: At 1st level, you have created a strange invention that creates and holds your Domesticated Oozes. This Unit is a Small item which can be worn as a backpack or carried with two hands.

While you wear this item and your Domesticated Ooze is within 10 feet, you can use a bonus action to cause the Ooze to instantly become stored within the Unit. You can also use a bonus action to eject your Ooze into an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of you. While it is within the Unit, your Ooze cannot take damage or be targeted. Your Unit can only hold one Domesticated Ooze at at time.
If your Ooze is killed, you can use your action to expend an arcane charge, fueling the Unit and creating another Ooze within your Unit.

At the end of each long rest, you can create a new Ooze in your Containment Unit without expending an arcane charge. You can only have one Ooze at a time, and creating a new Ooze causes any previous Oozes to instantly dissolve into goo.
If your Ooze Containment Unit is destroyed you can craft another from spare parts over the course of a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Domesticated Ooze
description: You have captured, bred, or created a Domesticated Ooze to serve you. Your Ooze uses the Domesticated Ooze stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) and save DC.

Your Domesticated Ooze is friendly to you and your allies and it obeys your commands. In combat, it acts on your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it only takes the Dodge action on its turn unless you use a bonus action to order it to take an action from its stat block or another action.

Also, whenever you take the attack action, you can forgo one of your attacks to order your Ooze to attack. If you are incapacitated, your Domesticated Ooze can act on its own, and it will defend itself and you to the best of its ability.

3.name: Essence Harvester
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can extract the very Essence of the creatures you slay, synthesizing it into upgrades for your Oozes. As an action, you can touch your Ooze Containment Unit to one creature that has died within the last minute and harvest its Essence.
Your Containment Unit can hold a number of Essences equal to your Artificer level. If you harvest an Essence while you are at your maximum, choose one Essence to replace.

While an Ooze is within the Unit, you can use an action to infuse it with an Essence, granting your Ooze the benefits of the Essence . An Essence is expended when it is infused into one of your Oozes.

Your Domesticated Ooze can benefit from one Essence at a time. At certain Artificer levels, it can be infused with multiple Essences, gaining all their benefits: at 5th level (2 Essences), 9th level (3 Essences), and finally at 15th level (4 Essences).

5.name: Extra Attack
description: At 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, when you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, once per turn when you order your Ooze to attack, it can make two attacks.

9.name: Ooze Adept
description: At 9th level, your work with Oozes has granted you a special resistance to their toxins. You gain resistance to acid and poison damage.
Moreover, when you infuse your Domesticated Ooze with one of your Essences, the Essence is no longer expended.

15.name: Master Rancher
description: By 15th level, your experiments with Oozes have increased the power and ability of the Oozes you control. Whenever you use your Ooze Containment Unit to create an Ooze, you choose whether the Ooze is Tiny, Small, Medium, or Large.

Known as pilots, these artificers specialize in the creation and construction of exoskeletons.  These arcane constructs enhance their own physical abilities, and eventually grow to become massive suit sof mechanical armor that its pilot can ride inside of.  Towering over their enemies on the battlefield, a pilot and their exoskeleton is a force to be reckoned with.
subclasses.name: Pilot Specialization

1.name: Pilot Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stAdaptation Armor
5thWar Gauntlet
9thShoulder-Mounted Weapon

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Arcane Exoskeleton
description: At 1st level, you have crafted an exoskeleton that enhances your movements.  Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use your blacksmith's tools to create an Arcane Exoskeleton, which can only be used by you.
You can wear your exoskeleton over a set of light armor, and while you wear it you gain the following benefits:

• You can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength, to calculate your jumping distance.
  • You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.
  • Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 magical bludgeoning damage on a hit, and you can use your Intelligence, in place of Strength, for attack and damage rolls with unarmed strikes.
For the purposes of infusions, your exoskeleton is considered a suit of armor.

3.name: Empowered Exoskeleton
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can empower your exoskeleton to grow into a suit of wonderous mechanical armor that covers your whole body and gives you the benefits listed below:

• Your size increases to Medium, if it wasn't already larger.
  • Your Armor Class equals 13 + your Intelligence modifier
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
  • Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
  • You can add your Intelligence modifier to Athletics and Perception checks.
  • The damage of your unarmed strikes increases to 1d8.
  • Your attacks deal the maximum possible damage against nonmagical objects and structures.
  • You gain temporary hit points equal to your Artificer level. While you have these temporary hit points, you are considered a construct for the purposes of spells and abilities. If any temporary hit points remain when this transformation ends, they are lost.
  • As an action, you can fire a grappling hook at a target within 30 feet of you. If the target is an object, you instantly pull yourself to that object, or you can pull a Medium or smaller object to yourself. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pulled to a space within 5 feet of you of your choice.

Your exoskeleton remains empowered for 1 minute or until you end it as a bonus action.  You can empower your exoskeleton once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest.  When you have no uses left, you can expend 2 arcane charges to empower your exoskeleton again.

5.name: Pilot Adept
description: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Enhanced Reflexes
description: At 9th level, your arcane exoskeleton improves your physical abilities even further.  You gain a bonus to initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier.
In addition, whenever you are forced to make a Dexterity saving throw while your exoskeleton is empowered, you have advantage on the roll.

15.name: Master Pilot
description: By 15th level, your exoskeleton serves as an extension of your very body. If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
In addition, when you empower your exoskeleton, you can choose for your size to increase to Large, so long as there is room for you to do so.

Portaleers are artificers that specialize in conjuration magic. More specifically, they specialize in the portion of conjuration magic that deals with teleportation and planar travel. Powerful portaleers can traverse planes and teleport an object or creature across vast distances.
subclasses.name: Portaleer Specialization

1.name: Portaleer Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stAdaptation Armor
5thMany-Handed Pouch
9thBoots of the Winding Path

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with cartographer's tools. If you are already proficient with cartographer's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Ethereal Portals
description: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to create magical portals that allow quick travel between two nearby places. As an action, you can create two linked portals at grounded points of your choice within 120 feet. You choose the appearance of the portals, but they must still function as gateways. Thereafter, as a bonus action, you can move either of the portals to a point of your choice within 120 feet. You must concentrate to keep your portals active (as if concentrating on a spell), and they are destroyed if your concentration is lost.

Portals are large enough to accomodate a medium creature without squeezing, and a creature or object in the space of one portal is simultaneously in the space of the corresponding portal. A creature that willingly enters a portal can choose to exit either portal's space, but an object not being worn or carried by a creature or a creature forced into a portal always exits the opposite portal's space. Portals also extend onto the Ethereal Plane, where they function identically.

Portals have a maximum range of 300 feet, and are destroyed if you are farther than 500 feet from them. Portals cannot be created within an area of antimagic, and are destroyed if targeted by dispel magic. A portal without a pair is useless.

3.name: Reactive Teleport
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can quickly teleport yourself out of harm's way. As a reaction when you are hit by an attack, you can teleport to the space of any of your active portals.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

5.name: Inertial Manipulation
description: Starting at 5th level, you can alter the inertia of objects that pass through your portals.  When a ranged attack is made that travels through your portal, you can increase or decrease the damage (your choice) by an amount equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

5.name: Planar Expert
description: Also at 5th level, your knowledge of planes other than the material improves. You have advantage on checks made to recall information about planes other than the material and their inhabitants.
In addition, as an action, you can pinpoint the location of the nearest planar portal.

9.name: Planeswalker
description: Starting at 9th level, you can cast the Plane Shift spell once without the need for material components, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
When cast in this way, the spell takes ten minutes to cast, and cannot teleport unwilling creatures.

15.name: Master Portaleer
description: Starting at 15th level, your control of teleportation magic improves enough that you can sustain multiple portals at a time. You can now sustain two extra sets of portals, both of which are separately linked.
In addition, your portals no longer require concentration, though you can only have a maximum of three sets of portals active at any given time.

Though all artificers have their quirks, Puppeteers tend to be the strangest subset of artificers. They dedicate their research and intellect towards mastery of manipulation and control of other creatures through the use of their Marionette Strings. Often found literally pulling the strings from behind the scenes, these strange artificers prefer to empower their allies rather than risk their own lives on the front lines.
subclasses.name: Puppeteer Specialization

1.name: Puppeteer Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stPower Whip
5thMany-Handed Pouch
9thHorseless Carriage

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with weaver's tools. If you are already proficient with weaver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Arcane Threads
description: At 1st level, you have constructed for yourself arcane threads that you can manipulate with magic. You learn the Thorn Whip cantrip.  Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.  When you cast thorn whip it has the following changes:

• You must use weaver's tools as the spellcasting focus.
  • You can choose for the spell not to damage a creature.
  • You can target objects and creatures. If the object is smaller than you and is not being worn or carried, it is pulled up to 30 feet to you. If the object is larger than you, you can pull yourself up to 30 feet toward the object.

3.name: Marionette Strings
description: At 3rd level, you can use your strange artifice to help and control. While holding weaver's tools, you can use an action to cause your Strings to fly and attach to a willing creature within 30 feet.

While a creature is attached to your Strings, you gain the features listed below. Your Marionette Strings detach after 1 minute, if you use a bonus action to detach them, or if you and the attached creature are ever more than 30 feet apart.

subFeatures.name: Channel Spell
description: As an action on your turn, you can cast a spell as if it originated from the attached creature. If the spell requires concentration, you must concentrate on it.

subFeatures.name: Corrected Strike
description: When the attached creature makes a melee attack, you can use your reaction to have them re-roll their attack roll, and they must use the new roll. You must use this reaction before you know if the attack hits or misses.

subFeatures.name: Strands of Guidance
description: When the attached creature makes an ability check using a skill that you are proficient in, they add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to their roll.

subFeatures.name: Strange Movement
description: As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the attached creature a number of feet equal to 5 times your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 5 feet). This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

5.name: Strange Strikes
description: At 5th level, the control you can exert through your Strings grows. As a reaction when the creature attached to your Strings makes an attack, you can cause them to make one additional attack.

9.name: Nimble Fingers
description: Starting at 9th level, you can have up to two creatures attached to your Strings at one time. You must have a free hand to control each creature. The two creatures can be any distance apart from each other, so long as they remain within the range of your Strings.
In addition, the length of your Marionette Strings, and the range of all of your Puppeteer abilities increases to 60 feet.

15.name: Master of Puppets
description: By 15th level, you have become a master Puppeteer. As an action, you can use your weaver's tools to cast Otto's Irresistible Dance, without requiring concentration. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it. However, you can only have once instance of this spell active at a time, and the spell requires one of your free hands to maintain.
Once you cast the spell in this way, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.

Most artificers focus their creativity on mechanical or arcane inventions, but those known as Reanimators use their unique abilities to raise their defeated enemies as thralls.  Instead of improving themselves, they put everything into utilizing the abilities that their thralls had in life, now in undeath.
subclasses.name: Reanimator Specialization

1.name: Reanimator Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stHomonculus Servant (Fleshy)
5thRepulsion Shield
9thHorseless Carriage

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with leatherworker's tools. If you are already proficient with leatherworker's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, any construct you create is a construct undead (corporeal).

1.name: Reanimated Thrall
description: Starting when you choose this specialization at 1st level, you can restore a facsimile of life into your slain foes.  Over the course of 1 minute, you can perform a special ritual where you use leatherworker's tools on one creature you can touch that has died within the last minute.  At the end of this ritual, the target rises as a thrall as if it had completed a long rest.

The maximum CR of creatures you can reanimate as thralls is limited by your Artificer level, as shown in the Max Thrall CR column of the Reanimator table.  You can reanimate Beasts and Humanoids, and you learn to reanimate other creature types as you gain levels in this class.

Your thrall uses the stat block it had in life, but it gains the Undead creature type in addition to its original type, it cannot speak, its Intelligence score becomes 2 (-4) unless it was already lower, it has no Hit Dice, and it gains no benefits from short or long rests.

Your thrall is mindless and obeys your orders completely to the best of its abilities.  In combat, it acts on your turn.  It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it will only take the Dodge action on its turn unless you use your bonus action to command it to take an action from its stat block or another combat action.  If you are incapacitated, your thrall will act on its own to defend itself, but it will take no further actions.
Once your thrall is slain, it cannot be raised as a thrall again.  If you raise a second thrall, your previous thrall falls to 0 hit points and dies.

3.name: Greater Reanimations
description: At 3rd level, your knowledge of reanimation grows, and you learn to create thralls from more diverse and powerful creatures.  Choose a creature type from Elemental, Ooze, Plant, and Undead, which you can renaimate as a thrall as part of your Reanimated Thrall feature.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Moreover, whenever you take the Attack action, you can command your thrall to make one attack from its stat block in place of one of your attacks.

9.name: Empowered Thrall
description: At 9th level, you have weaved magic into your thrall, allowing it to bear your most potent infusions. Your thrall can bear any infusion that is meant for boots, cloaks, gauntlets, helms, or suits of armor. However, it can only bear one Infusion at a time.

9.name: Advanced Reanimations
description: At 9th level, you can raise some of hte most powerful mortal creatures in existence to serve you as thralls.  Choose a creature type from Aberration, Dragon, Elemental, Giant, Ooze, Plant, and Undead, which you can renaimate as a thrall as part of your Reanimated Thrall feature.

15.name: Magnum Opus
description: Starting at 15th level, you can keep your thrall alive so long as your power lasts.  When your thrall is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can use a reaction to expend any number of arcane charges, and grant your thrall a number of hit points equal to 10 times the number of charges you expend.

15.name: Superior Reanimations
description: Also at 15th level, you can raise even immortals to be your thralls if you manage to slay them.  Choose a creature type from Aberration, Celestial, Dragon, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Ooze, Plant, and Undead, which you can renaimate as a thrall as part of your Reanimated Thrall feature.

Spellsmiths are artificers who devote themselves to studying the workings of arcane magic. Even moreso than other artificers, they are true masters of spellstoring items. Spellsmiths excel when their inventions can be used by a wide variety of allies, allowing them to spread their magical trinkets far and wide.
subclasses.name: Spellsmith Specialization

1.name: Spellsmith Infusions
description: You learn certain infusions at the levels noted in the table below.  They don't count against your number of infusions known, and they cannot be replaced with other infusions.

LevelInfusion
1stMinor Spellstoring Item
5thGreater Spellstoring Item
9thAdvanced Spellstoring Item

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with one set of artisan's tools of your choice. Additionally, you add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to all ability checks you make with artisan's tools that you lack proficiency with.

1.name: Spellstoring Item Adept
description: At 1st level, your specialization in the creation of spellstoring items grants you insights into how to create them more efficiently. When you expend arcane charges to imbue one of your Spellstoring Item infusions, you can choose to not expend any arcane charges if you would expend a number of arcane charges less than or equal to your proficiency bonus.

You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. Any infusions created using this feature automatically end when you finish a long rest, and you can't choose for them to not end.

3.name: Altered Formulas
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you create a Spellstoring Item, you can expend additional arcane charges to modify the spell in any of the following ways:

subFeatures.name: Area of Effect Type
description: Cost: 3 arcane charges
You change the area of effect type of the spell, using the table below to convert its size.

New AoE Type

Cone-SizeRadius: Size

subFeatures.name: Damage Type
description: Cost: 1 arcane charge
