3.name: Radiant Ascension
description: Also at 3rd level, you can draw upon the power of the celestial magic within your blood, if only for a short time.  As a bonus action, you can transform into a Radiant Form which resembles the celestial from which you draw your divine blood magic.  While you are in your radiant form, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your blood hunter level.
  • Whenever you make an attack on your turn, you can instead produce a Radiant Bolt from an empty hand. Make a ranged spell attack against a target you can see within 60 feet, using your Charisma as the spellcasting modifier. On a hit, the target takes radiant damage equal to 1d8 + your Charisma modifier.
  • When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction to add one roll of your Rite Die to the result of the roll.
This transformation lasts for 1 minute.  It ends early if you are incapacitated, or you choose to end it as a bonus action.
Once you transform, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  If you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to transform again.

3.name: Heavenly Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your divine blasphemy also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a celestial, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Luminous Warrior
description: At 7th level, you are able to draw out a greater amount of the divine power within your blood.  When in your Radiant Form, you gain the following additional benefits:

• You gain resistance to necrotic damage, and to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
  • When you use a Blood Rite that deals necrotic damage, you can choose for it to deal radiant damage instead.
  • Once per turn when you hit a target with your Radiant Bolt, you deal bonus radiant damage equal to a roll of your Rite Die.

13.name: Divine Ascent
description: Starting at 13th level, your mortal flesh can withstand a wonderous amount of divine magic. Your transformation into your Radiant Form lasts for 10 minutes, and while you are in your Radiant Form, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
In addition, you can make Radiant Bolt attacks even when you are not in your Radiant Form.

18.name: Anointed Slayer
description: By 18th level, you wield divine power rivaling that of the champions of celestial courts.  You can transform into your Radiant Form at will, without needing to make a Vital Sacrifice to do so, and your Radiant Form transformation lasts indefinitely.

In addition, once per turn when you hit a creature with your Radiant Bolt attack, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw.  On a failed saving throw, the target is blinded until the start of your next turn.

subclasses.name: Order of Ascension

description: The Order of the Cosmic Veil is an unnatural one.  These Blood Hunters, tainted by the influence of the Far Realm, fight against the ungodly, aberrant invaders of this realm.  They use powerful illusions to disguise the influence of the Far Realm, trying to prevent anyone from ever seeing beyond the veil.

3.name: Close the Veil
description: Starting at 3rd level, your skill at hiding the true nature of aberrations grants you expertise in illusion magics.  You know the Minor Illusion cantrip.  Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for it.
In addition, whenever you make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or Charisma (Deception) check, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

3.name: Aberrant Slayer
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your blood magic is especially potent when used against aberrations.  Your learn the Rite of the Spark if you don't already know it, and when you use it with your Crimson Rite feature, you gain the following additional benefits:

• The normal damage of the weapon is changed to force damage.
  • While you hold the weapon you have resistance to psychic damage and your mind cannot be read through magic.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Spark
description: Your rite damage type is force damage.

3.name: Cosmic Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your awareness of the Veil also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an aberration or astral creature, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Mental Block
description: Starting at 7th level, as an action, you can force an aberration you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Charisma saving throw against your Rite save DC.  On a failed saving throw, the target is unable to target other creatures with harmful mental effects for 1 minute.  An affected target can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

13.name: Sentinel of Reality
description: Starting at 13th level, you remain ever vigilant for the attacks of the Far Realm, gaining the following benefits:

• You can add one roll of your Rite Die to your initiative rolls.
  • A creature under the effects of your Mental Block feature subtracts a roll of your Rite Die from their damage whenever they deal psychic damage.

18.name: Dark Curtain
description: Starting at 18th level, you can alter the minds of others to protect them from the knowledge of the Far Realm.  You can cast the Modify Memory spell, for which Intelligence is your spellcasting ability.
Once you cast the spell using this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

subclasses.name: Order of the Cosmic Veil

description: The Order of the Everlasting Rose isn't one of hunters, or at least, not in the traditional sense. Scattered across the whole world, these knights are in a quest to find the absolute, pure flame that will burn the rose that gives them name and powers.
Moved by devotion and honor, they are often found in the track of a dragon, be it for battle or diplomacy.
The knights of this order are not only trained in the ways of the blade and spears, but also taught to wield their blood to conjure the rose and it's aspects in the form of deadly curses.

3.name: Knight Instruction
description: When you join the Order of the Everlasting Rose at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor. Furthermore, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track dragons, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about such creatures.

3.name: Imbued Curses
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you learn a Rose Curse, which is considered a Blood Rite.
You learn one additional Rose Curse of your choice at 7th, 11th, and 15th level. Rose Curses don't count against the number of Blood Rites you know.

3.name: Draconic Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your use of Rose Curses also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a dragon, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Unburning Blood
description: From 7th level and on, your connection with the everlasting rose has become stronger. You gain resistance to fire damage. Furthermore, if you have taken an amount of fire damage or have lost an amount of hit points from making a Vital Sacrifice equal or higher than your Constitution modifier within the last minute, you can use a bonus action to release the heat you've gathered in your body in a blast, forcing creatures within 10 feet of you to make a Dexterity saving throw. Creatures take fire damage equal to your Blood Hunter level + a roll of your Rite die on a failed saving throw, or half as much on a success.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

13.name: Wyrm's Blood
description: Upon reaching 15th level, you learn a powerful way to use the heat you release when you use your Unburning Blood feature. Whenever you use it, you cause this effect instead of the normal one. Choose one of the following features to learn.  Once you have used it, you can't do it again until you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Fiery Wings
description: Wings of petals or wings of fire erupt from your back. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute.

subFeatures.name: Great Conflagration
description: A massive fire in the shape of a rose erupts around you. Creatures within 20 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to twice your Blood Hunter level + two rolls of your Rite die, or half as much on a success. The flames ignite flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.

subFeatures.name: Indomitable Scales
description: You cover yourself in crimson, searing scales. You gain immunity to fire damage and gain a +2 bonus to your AC for 1 minute.

18.name: Heart's Demise
description: Starting at 18th level, your connection to the rose has increased your burning fury.  You can use your Unburning Blood feature an unlimited number of times.  In addition, your conection to the rose has also granted you part of it's everlasting gift. For every 2 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.

subclasses.name: Order of the Everlasting Rose

description: Making the ultimate sacrifice to fight against the forces of evil, Blood Hunters of the Order of Hellfire sell their eternal souls in an infernal bargain for power.  Infused with the power of Hell itself, these dark avengers use their infernal abilities to bring judgement upon all those who harm the innocent.

3.name: Infernal Bargain
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have entered into an infernal pact, imbuing you with the powers of darkness at the cost of your eternal soul.  You learn to speak, read, and write Infernal, and whenever you make a Charisma check to interact with fiends, or an Intelligence check to recall information about fiends, you add one roll of your Rite Die to the ability check.
Finally, you learn the Rite of the Flame if you don't already know it.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Flame
description: Your rite damage type is fire damage.

3.name: Hellfire Form
description: Also at 3rd level, you can infuse your body with the powers of Hell to transform, if only for a short time.  As a bonus action, you can transform into a Hellfire Form. While you are in your hellfire form, you gain the following benefits:

• You are wreathed in hellfire and terrifying to behold.
  • Your creature type changes to Fiend.
  • You gain resistance to fire, poison, and necrotic damage.
  • You manifest a flaming whip or chain in a free hand. You are considered proficient with this weapon, which has a reach of 10 feet and deals magical slashing damage equal to 1d10 + your Strength modifier on a hit.
  • When you manifest your flaming whip or chain, you can invoke a Rite of the Flame or Rite of the Dead on it without performing a Vital Sacrifice.
This transformation lasts for 1 minute.  It ends early if you are incapacitated, or you choose to end it as a bonus action.
Once you transform, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  If you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to transform again.

3.name: Infernal Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your infernal pact also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a fiend, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Penance Stare
description: At 7th level, the power granted to you by your pact with Hell allows you to peer into the souls of your foes. As an action, you can force one creature within 30 feet that can see you to look into your eyes, seeing the weight of its sins and making a Wisdom saving throw against your Rite save DC.  On a failed save, the creature takes psychic damage equal to five rolls of your Rite Die, and half as much on a success.
If you force a creature of evil alignment to make this saving throw, you can make a Vital Sacrifice as part of this action to force it to make the saving throw at disadvantage.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  If you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use it again.

13.name: Hellish Empowerment
description: Starting at 13th level, the hellfire that burns in your veins infuses you with a dark and sinister resilience.  Whenever you start your turn in your Hellfire Form, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution modifier.
In addition, while in your Hellfire Form, your walking speed is increased by 10 feet, and you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical sources.

18.name: Spirit of Vengeance
description: By 18th level, you have mastered the infernal magic of your Order.  You can transform into your Hellfire Form at will, without needing to make a Vital Sacrifice to do so, and your Hellfire Form transformation lasts indefinitely.
In addition, while you are in your Hellfire Form, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action, so long as you end your movement closer to a hostile creature you can see.

subclasses.name: Order of Hellfire

description: Excommunicated from their religious orders, the founders of the Order of Heretics were holy priests who desired to utilize forbidden rites to combat darkness. Branded heretics, these conduits of divine power supplemented their holy knowledge with blood magic. Now, this Order of priestly Blood Hunters works to combat wayward divine entities, both good and evil.

3.name: Blasphemous Prayer
description: Starting at 3rd level, you are able to channel divine energies despite your status as a heretic. You gain two Channel Divinity options: Censure the Divine, which is detailed below, and one Channel Divinity of your choice. For the second, you use your Blood Hunter level in place of any mentions of Cleric level and your Rite save DC.
You can use each of your Channel Divinities once, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use either of your Channel Divinity options again.

subFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Censure the Divine
description: You utter blasphemies painful for divine entities to hear. Any celestials, fiends, or creatures capable of divine magic of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed a Charisma saving throw against your Rite save DC or be incapacitated and restrained for 1 minute.
Creatures repeat this saving throw at the end of their turns and when they take damage, ending this effect on a success.

3.name: Heretical Knowledge
description: Despite your beliefs, you understand the traditional religious practices, rites, and prayers. Also starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in Religion. If you already have proficiency in Religion, your proficiency bonus is doubled for that skill.
In addition, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Divine spell list.  Constitution is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

3.name: Heretical Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your religious past also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a celestial or fiend, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Unholy Restoration
description: Starting at 7th level, you can draw life from one creature and transfer it to another in a dark mockery of the divine. As an action, you can force a creature you can see within 30 feet to make a Constitution saving throw against your Rite save DC. On a failure, it takes necrotic damage equal to four rolls of your Rite Die, and half as much necrotic damage on a success. It has disadvantage on its saving throw if you touch it as part of this action.
As part of the action, a creature you can see within 30 feet regains hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all uses when you finish a long rest. When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

13.name: Divine Anathema
description: Starting at 13th level, when you use Censure the Divine you can empower it with a Vital Sacrifice, forcing creatures of your choice within 30 feet must make on a Constitution saving throw against your Rite save DC, in place of its normal effects. On a failed save, creatures have their speed reduced by 10 feet.

Creatures repeat this saving throw at the end of each of their turns. On a failure, their speed is further reduced by 10 feet, and on a success they regain 10 feet of speed. This effect ends when a creature's speed becomes 0, at which point it is petrified, or when a creature's speed returns to normal.
Celestials and fiends have disadvantage on saving throws to resist this feature. Once a creature succeeds against this feature it is immune to its effect until the following dawn.

18.name: Utmost Transgression
description: Starting at 18th level, you use your occult knowledge to bind denizens of heaven. As an action, you can cast summon celestial, using Constitution as its spellcasting modifier. The celestial is bound against its will by unholy blood magic, allowing you to ignore the material component of the spell, but the duration of the spell is reduced to 1 minute.
Once you cast this spell you must finish a short or long rest before you can cast it this way again.

subclasses.name: Order of Heretics

description: To the mind of some paladins, their oaths and religious orders do not fight hard enough against the forces of the Nine Hells.  These paladins sometimes end up becoming Hellriders, holy Blood Hunters that recklessly venture into Avernus itself to drive back the devils there.

3.name: Hunter's Smite
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the magic of your blood to incinerate dark creatures in holy fire.  When you hit a creature with a weapon empowered by your Crimson Rite feature, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to deal bonus radiant damage to the target equal to two rolls of your Rite Die.
In addition, you learn the Rite of the Dawn if you don't already know it.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Dawn
description: Your rite damage type is radiant damage.

3.name: Consecrated Blood
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your blood itself is consecrated with divine magic.  You have immunity to disease, resistance to poison damage, and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.

3.name: Hellrider's Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your fervor also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a celestial or fiend, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Ride Into Hell
description: Starting at 7th level, you call upon a spirit to serve as your noble steed.  You learn the Find Steed spell, and can cast it by making a Vital Sacrifice.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

13.name: Relentless Hunter
description: Starting at 13th level, when you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack and as part of the same reaction. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
In addition, you learn the Find Greater Steed spell, and can cast it by making a Vital Sacrifice.

18.name: Divine Sangromancy
description: Starting at 18th level, the divine energy in your blood permeates into every attack.  When you deal damage to a creature, you can deal bonus radiant damage equal to a roll of your Rite Die.

subclasses.name: Order of the Hellrider

description: While every Blood Hunter must undergo the Hunter's Bane, postulants of the Order of Ichor endure the most painful and transformative version of this sinister ritual.  Through ancient dark arts, their blood is infected with sentient ooze, giving it a life of its own, and a primal desire for control over its host.

3.name: Living Blood
description: Starting at 3rd level, the primal sentience in your blood enhances both your resilience and physical ability.  You gain resistance to poison damage, and whenever you make a Strength (Athletics) check, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to a roll of your Rite Die.

3.name: Symbiotic Defense
description: Also starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can draw out the ichor within your blood to cover yourself in a protective, ooze-like coating.  For 1 minute, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Wisdom modifier, unless it was already higher.  Also, once per turn while this effect is active, you can reduce one instance of damage you take by an amount equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

While your Symbiotic Defense is active, you are hideous and terrifying to behold, and you have disadvantage on any Charisma checks you make that are not Charisma (Intimidation) checks.  You can only end this feature early by making a Vital Sacrifice as a bonus action.

3.name: Symbiotic Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your sentient blood also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an ooze, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Adaptable Form
description: Starting at 7th level, you have learned to bend the alien mind within your blood to your will.  Each time you activate Symbiotic Defense, you gain one of the following features of your choice for the duration:

subFeatures.name: Aberrant Form
description: You gain a climbing speed equal to yoru walking speed, and you can liquefy yourself to move through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing.

subFeatures.name: Alien Resilience
description: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Blood Hunter level and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage not dealt by silvered weapons.

subFeatures.name: Living Liquid
description: You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and you can hold your breath indefinitely underwater.

7.name: Symbiotic Weapon
description: Also at 7th level, your strange blood can enhance the power of your weapons.  You learn the Rite of the Vitriol if you didn't already know it, and you can choose to empower it further.  When you do so, the weapon merges with your ichor, and any hands you use the wield the weapon become unusable.  However, the damage die of the wepaon becomes a d8 if it wasn't already higher, and you can use your Constitution, in place of Strength or Dexterity, for your attack and damage rolls with it.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Vitriol
description: Your rite damage type is acid damage.

13.name: Sanguine Rebuke
description: Starting at 13th level, the sentience of your blood can defend you even when you havce not called upon it to do so.  When a creature within 10 feet of you that you can see damages you, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Dexterity saving throw.  On a failed save, the target takes acid damage equal to two rolls of your Rite Die.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.  When you have no uses of this feature left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.
Finally, when you activate your Symbiotic Defense feature, you gain two benefits from Adaptable Form, rather than one.

18.name: Symbiotic Mastery
description: Starting at 18th level, you and the alien presence within your blood are of one mind and goal.  When you activate your Symbiotic Defense feature, you gain all three benefits from Adaptable Form, and you can choose to have your transformation last for 1 hour.

Finally, when a creature fails its saving throw against your Sanguine Rebuke feature while your Symbiotic Defense is active, you can choose for the creature to also be blinded, poisoned, or have its speed reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn.

subclasses.name: Order of Ichor

description: Lycanthropy is an ancient curse that changes those afflicted into mindless beasts with a wild hunger for flesh.  However, there are Orders of Blood Hunters who purposefully contract this curse.  Willing to give themselves over so that they may use this feral power to rid the world of other lycanthropes.

3.name: Beast Form
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can control your lycanthropy, allowing you to shift your form at will.  Choose a beast of CR 1 or lower that represents the animal your curse is based on.  Common Beast Forms include boars, brown bears, dire wolves, tigers, and rats.
As an action, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to shift into the Beast Form of your lycanthropy.
While you are transformed, the following rules apply:

• Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.
  • When you transform, you retain your current and maximum hit points, and you gain temporary hit points equal to twice your level.
  • You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your beast form. Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as Call Lightning, that you've already cast.
  • You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. However, you can't use any of your special senses, such as darkvision, unless your new form also has that sense.
  • You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.
If you make a Vital Sacrifice while in Beast Form, you reduce the maximum hit points of both your Beast Form and your normal form, but only the current hit points of your Beast Form.

You remain in your Beast Form for 1 hour.  You revert to your normal form if you are reduced to 0 hit points or use an action to do so.  You can make a Vital Sacrifice at any time (no action required) to extend the duration of your transformation by 1 hour.

3.name: Hybrid Form
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you can use the dark magic of your blood to draw out the power of your inner beast.  As a bonus action, you can enter a Hybrid Form, a fusion between your Beast Form and your natural shape.  While in your Hybrid Form, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.
  • Your fingers and teeth become claws and fangs. On a hit, they deal slashing or piercing damage equal to two rolls of your Rite Die + your Strength modifier.
  • Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
You can remain in your Hybrid Form for up to 1 minute.  You revert to your normal form early if you are reduced to 0 hit points or you use a bonus action on your turn to do so.
Once you transform into your Hybrid Form, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  If you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to transform again.

3.name: Feral Senses
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your lycanthropy enhances your primal senses.  When you make a Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Survival) check that is based on your sense of hearing, sight, or smell, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

3.name: Bestial Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your lycanthropy also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a beast or shapechanger, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Lycan Warrior
description: Starting at 7th level, you are able to draw out more power from your curse.  While you are in Beast Form or Hybrid Form, you gain the following benefits:

• Your natural weapon attacks are considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical damage.
  • You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered.

13.name: Feral Prowess
description: Starting at 13th level, your curse fuels your bloodlust and allows you to shrug off minor wounds.  At the start of each of your turns while you are in Beast Form or Hybrid Form, you regain hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1), so long as you have at least 1 hit point and less than half of your maximum hit points.
In addition, while you are in Beast Form or Hybrid Form, you have advantage on your attack rolls against creatures marked by your Crimson Brand.

18.name: Howl of Primal Fury
description: Starting at 18th level, as an action on your turn, you can let forth a bloodcurdling howl.  Creatures of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Rite save DC or be frightened of you for 1 minute.  Creatures can repeat their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on themselves on a success.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

18.name: Transformation Mastery
description: Also at 18th level, you have mastered the lycanthropic curse that flows in your veins.  You can transform into your Hybrid Form at will.
In addition, your Beast Form and Hybrid Form transformations now last until you choose to end them.

subclasses.name: Order of the Pale Moon

description: Those who have taken to the Order of the Profane Soul are driven by an overwhelming desire to destroy the great evils of the world.  Those especially dedicated, those willing to give up anything, are often approached by Eldritch Powers, beings of otherworldly might.  These benefactors offer power in return for a fraction of the warrior's soul or unquestioning fealty.

3.name: Pact Magic
description: When you reach 3rd level, you can augment your combat techniques with the ability to cast spells as a warlock does.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Occult spell list. You learn an additional Occult cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Profane Soul Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have. The table also shows what the level of those slots is; all of your spell slots are the same level. To cast one of your Occult spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: At 3rd level, you know three 1st-level spells of your choice from the Occult spell list. The Spells Known column of the Profane Soul table shows when you learn more Occult spells of your choice of 1st level and higher. A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. Additionally, when you gain a level in this class and order, you can choose one of the Occult spells you know and replace it with another spell from the Occult spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Occult spells.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

3.name: Crimson Smite
description: Starting at 3rd level, magic seeps into the blood you sacrifice to empower your weapons.  You can use any weapon empowered by your Crimson Rite feature as a spellcasting focus for your Occult spells.

In addition, when you hit a target with a weapon empowered by your Crimson Rite feature, you can expend one of your spell slots to deal bonus damage of your Crimson Rite damage type to the target.  This bonus damage is two rolls of your Rite Die for a 1st-level spell slot, plus one more roll of your Rite Die for each spell level higher than 1st.

3.name: Profane Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your dark bargain also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a creature of the same type as your patron, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Sanguine Warrior
description: Starting at 7th level, you seamlessly weave minor spells with weapon attacks. If you use your action to cast a spell, or activate a spell you are concentrating on, you can make a weapon attack as a bonus action on that turn.

Moreover, when you cast a spell while you are holding a weapon empowered by Crimson Rite, you can cause the spell to deal the damage type of your Crimson Rite in place of the normal damage of that spell.

13.name: Bewitched Strikes
description: Starting at 13th level, the eldritch magic within your blood seeps into your weapon strikes.  When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

18.name: Profane Sacrifice
description: At 18th level, you can offer the death of your foes to your Eldritch Power for enhanced abilities.  When a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to regain one of your expended Pact Magic spell slots, or temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Rite Die + your spellcasting ability modifier.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.

subclasses.name: Order of the Profane Soul

description: Legends say the Order of the Reaper was founded by an ancient death cult to serve as their champions. Though their origins are lost to time, Blood Hunters who join this Order are given powers associated with death and destruction. By sacrificing their own vitality, these warriors channel the power of death.

3.name: Reaper's Mark
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can infuse your strikes with dark magic to mark your foes for death. When you hit a creature with a Crimson Offering attack, you can place a Mark on it as part of your attack.

This Mark lasts for 1 minute, and you must concentrate on it as if were concentrating on a spell. The Mark ends early if you lose concentration, if you mark another creature, or if it is dispelled by a spell like lesser restoration or remove curse.
Once per turn, when a creature Marked in this way makes an ability check or saving throw, it suffers a penalty to its roll equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

3.name: Cultist of Death
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your blood magic saps at life and vitality.  Your learn the Rite of the Dead if you don't already know it, and when you use it with your Crimson Rite feature, you gain the following additional benefits:

• The normal damage of the weapon is changed to necrotic damage.
  • You have resistance to necrotic and poison damage.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Dead
description: Your rite damage type is necrotic damage.

3.name: One With Death
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you have undergone an ancient and sinister ritual that has bonded you with death itself. Whenever you make a death saving throw, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to one roll of your Rite Die. Also, when a spellcaster targets you with a spell that restores you to life (but not undeath) such as raise dead, they do not need the normal material components.

3.name: Deathly Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your special relationship with death also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an undead, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Reaper's Bond
description: Starting at 7th level, you can bind yourself to a foe with deathly magic. When you Mark a creature with Reaper's Mark, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to bond yourselves together. While bonded in this way, both you and your Mark suffer the following effects:

• Your concentration on this feature cannot be broken unless you choose to break it or you are incapacitated.
  • When either you or your Mark takes damage, the other takes necrotic damage equal to half the damage taken.
  • If you or your Mark is reduced to 0 hit points, the other gains temporary hit points equal to your level.

13.name: Shadow of Death
description: Starting at 13th level, your connection to the magic of death has greatly increased. As a bonus action, you can exude an aura of death magic that extends from, and moves with you, in a 15-foot radius. This aura lasts for 1 minute, and it ends early if you use a bonus action to end it, or if you become incapacitated.
Creatures of your choice within this radius cannot regain hit points, any damage immunities they have are treated as resistance, and any damage resistances are ignored.
Once you use this feature you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. When you have no uses remaining, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

18.name: Archreaper
description: Starting at 18th level, you have mastered the dark magic of your Order, and to you death is an ally. When you use Shadow of Death, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
In addition, you can have multiple creature's Marked with your Reaper's Mark at one time, up to a maximum of 1 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2) creatures at once.

subclasses.name: Order of the Reaper

description: Since the dawn of time, the ancient Order of Salt and Iron has produced exorcists that protect the living from the undead.  Willing to sacrifice everything, they taint their soul with spectral power.  Once mastered, they use this dark power to drive back the night itself.  These resolute warriors work tirelessly to prevent the tide of undeath from overwhelming the world of the living.

3.name: Spectral Nature
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have tainted your soul with ghastly power. You require half the amount of sleep, food, and drink for the average member of your race.

Also, you can use a bonus action to enter a temporary Spectral State, which lasts until the end of your current turn. While in this state, you are resistant to all bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from non-magical attacks that aren't silvered, and you can move through solid objects and creatures as if they were difficult terrain. If you end your movement inside a creature or object, you are instantly shunted to the nearest unoccupied space, taking 1d10 force damage for every 5 feet you were shunted.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all uses when you finish a long rest. You can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feautre again.
At certain levels in this class, the duration of this Spectral State increases: at 7th-level (1 minute), 13th-level (1 hour), and at 18th level (indefinite). You can end this state as a bonus action.

3.name: Warrior of the Dawn
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your blood magic is especially potent when used against undead.  Your learn the Rite of the Dawn if you don't already know it, and when you use it with your Crimson Rite feature, you gain the following additional benefits:

• The normal damage of the weapon is changed to radiant damage.
  • While you hold the weapon you have resistance to necrotic damage.
  • The weapon sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius, and dim light an additional 20 feet beyond that.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Dawn
description: Your rite damage type is radiant damage.

3.name: Spectral Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your spectral nature also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an undead or incorporeal creature, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Curse Specialist
description: Starting at 7th level, your knowledge and experience with undead enhances the power of your blood magic. You can target any creature with your Blood Rites, even if it does not have blood in its veins.
In addition, at the end of each long rest you can choose one Blood Rite you know. You can invoke that Rite one additional time before you must make a Vital Sacrifice to use it again.

13.name: Warrior Exorcist
description: Starting at 13th level, you use the power of blood magic to drive out the influence of extraplanar creatures. As a bonus action on your turn, you can choose one willing creature within 30 feet that can hear you that is currently charmed, frightened, or being magically controlled, and instantly end one of the above effects on it.

If the creature that inflicted this condition is also within 30 feet, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Rite save DC. On a failure it takes radiant damage equal to four rolls of your Rite Die, and half damage on a success.
Once you use this feature you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

18.name: Sacrificial Offering
description: You can sacrifice your own vitality to resist the grasp of death. Starting at 18th level, when you would fall to 0 hit points but are not killed outright, you can choose to reduce your maximum hit points by one roll of your Rite Die, and fall to 1 hit point instead.

18.name: Spectral Mastery
description: Also at 18th level, you walk between the land of the living and the dead. For every 10 years that pass, you age 1 year, and you no longer need to sleep, eat, or drink. You gain the benefits of a long rest when you spend 6 hours performing only light activity.
Moreover, when you are in your Spectral State, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover.

subclasses.name: Order of Salt and Iron

description: Though all Blood Hunters learn to hunt and fight, no others can match the wilderness prowess of the Silver Blades.  These experts of the sword and of the compass often support other Blood Hunters with their excellent tracking abilities.

3.name: Hunter's Exploits
description: You have studied and learned various advanced martial techniques. At 3rd level, you gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: You have two d4 Exploit Dice. To use an Exploit you must expend one of these dice, and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: You know the Crippling Strike and Feral Senses exploits.  You can use each of these exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die.  Starting at 17th level, you also gain the Suppressing Strike exploit as a Mastered Exploit.

subFeatures.name: Wild Exploits
description: You learn two Exploits of your choice from the list of Wild Exploits. You can only use one Exploit per ability check or attack. When you gain a level, you can replace an Exploit you know with another of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: Some of your Exploits require your target to make a saving throw to resist your Marital Exploit's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

3.name: Hunter's Eye
description: Also at 3rd level, whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze a creature, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Stand Against Darkness
description: Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on saving throws against the characteristic innate abilities of fey, fiends, shapechangers, and undead, such as a lich's Paralyzing Touch or a pit fiend's Fear Aura, but not against spells they cast.

13.name: Improved Crimson Brand
description: Starting at 13th level, your Crimson Brand becomes more powerful, gaining the following benefits:

• You always know which plane of existence the target is on, and if it is not your own, you know the direction to the nearest planar portal that will take you there.
  • If you kill a creature under the effects of your Crimson Brand and deal damage to another creature on the same turn, you can Brand them without making a Vital Sacrifice.

18.name: Piercing Eye
description: At 18th level, your eye can see through any illusion.  You gain 60 feet of truesight.  Though, your truesight from this feature cannot see into the Ethereal Plane.
In addition, you cannot have disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures under the effects of your Crimson Brand feature.

subclasses.name: Order of the Silver Blade

description: Experts at hunting dangerous creatures and practitioners of foul magicks, Blood Hunters that join the Order of Thaumaturgy combine their blood magic and martial abilities with Thaumaturge's Signs. Wielding these minor magics, they are able to combat creatures and spellcasters many times their superior.

3.name: Thaumaturge's Signs
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to conjure minor magical effects, known as Thaumaturge's Signs to augment your combat abilities:

subFeatures.name: Signs
description: At 3rd level, you learn two Signs of your choice.

Once you use a Sign you know, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use that Sign again. When you have no uses of a Sign remaining, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use that Sign again.
You learn an additional Sign of your choice when you reach 7th, 13th, and 18th level. Moreover, whenever you learn a new Sign, you can replace one Sign you know with another Sign of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Somatic Components
description: When casting a Sign, you must have one hand free to perform the somatic components of that Sign. Signs used by this Occult Order require no other verbal or material components.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: If a Sign requires a creature to make a saving throw, its DC is calculated as follows:
Thaumaturge's Sign save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

3.name: Scholar of Miracles
description: Also at 3rd level, you have spent much time studying the basics of magic and its applications in combat. You gain proficiency in Arcana, and whenever you make an Intelligence (Arcana) check that relates to a spell of 3rd-level or lower (or an effect of similar scope), you treat a roll of 7 or lower on the d20 as an 8.

3.name: Arcane Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your miraculous magic also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an aberration, dragon, or ooze, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Battlemage
description: Starting at 7th level, you have gained great skill in using your Signs in combat. When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can cast one of your Signs in place of one attack.

13.name: Potent Magicks
description: Starting at 13th level, your willpower enhances the potency of your Signs. Whenever you use a Sign, you add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage roll.

18.name: Signature Sign
description: Starting at 18th level, your magicks have become second nature to you. Choose a Sign you know to be your Signature Sign. You can cast it a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), before you must make a Vital Sacrifice.
You regain all expended uses of your Signature Sign when you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Order of Thaumaturgy

description: Legends speak of an ancient vampire who came to regret the many atrocities he committed when driven by thirst.  He gathered to himself a group of vampire hunters, and after they vowed to scour the curse of vampirism from the world, passed his curse to them and instructed them in the power of ancient blood magic.  Known as the Order of Undying Thirst, these blood hunters work tirelessly to carry out their founding vow to destroy all vampires.

3.name: Blood Magic Specialist
description: Starting when you choose this order at 3rd level, your curse grants you increased control over your blood magic.  You learn an additional Blood Rite, but it doesn't count against your total number of Blood Rites known.
Also, your Rite Die increases in size to a d6.  At certain levels, the Rite Die increases again: at 5th level (d8), 11th level (d10), and 17th level (d12).
Finally, you learn the Rite of the Dead if you don't already know it.

subFeatures.name: Rite of the Dead
description: Your rite damage type is necrotic damage.

3.name: Vampiric Nature
description: Also starting at 3rd level, the ancient disease of your Order has irreparably changed you physiology.  Your teeth elongate into fangs which you can use for unarmed strikes. On a hit, they deal piercing damage equal to one roll of your Rite Die + your Strength modifier.

3.name: Sanguine Awareness
description: Also at 3rd level, your partially vampiric nature also empowers your blood magic. Whenever you use Hunter's Bane to analyze an undead or shapechanger, you gain a bonus to your ability check equal to one roll of your Rite Die.

7.name: Essence Drain
description: Starting at 7th level, you can drain the very life-essence from your foes. When you hit a creature with a fang attack, you can restore a number of your maximum hit points equal to the piercing damage dealt. Piercing damage from your fang attacks ignores resistances and immunities to non-magical damage.
Once you use this feature to restore maximum hit points must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

7.name: Sinister Resilience
description: Also at 7th level, your vampiric power waxes in the darkness and wanes in the light of the sun.  When you deal necrotic damage to a creature, you gain temporary hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt.

While you have temporary hit points from this feature, you are resistant to necrotic, poison, and bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons, and you are immune to disease and the poisoned condition.
However, if you take any amount of radiant damage, all of the temporary hit points from this feature are immediately lost, and the radiant damage is applied to your normal hit points.

13.name: Misty Escape
description: Starting at 13th level, your sinister power allows you to evade your foes.  When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to turn into a cloud of swirling mist.  The triggering attack automatically misses, and you instantly reappear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  When you have no uses left, you can make a Vital Sacrifice to use this feature again.

18.name: Crimson Lord
description: By 18th level, you have mastered the ancient power of your curse, and your abilities rival vampire lords.  You gain the following benefits:

• You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
  • When you hit a creature with a fang attack, it has disadvantage on saving throws to resist the effects of your Blood Rites until the end of your next turn.
  • For every 10 years that pass, your body only ages 1 year.

subclasses.name: Order of Undying Thirst

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Iron Physique
description: You have learned to take a hit better than most and prefer to absorb blows rather then dodge. Starting at 1st level, you can use your Constitution modifier, in place of Dexterity, when calculating your Armor Class in light and medium armor.
If you are not wearing any armor or wielding a shield your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier.

1.name: Contender
description: You have forged your body into a deadly weapon and can fight with nearly anything. For the purposes of your Brawler class features, Brawler attacks are attacks with unarmed strikes, grapples, shoves, improvised weapons, and simple melee or thrown weapons.
Beginning at 1st level, so long as you are not wearing heavy armor, wielding a shield, or wielding a weapon with the heavy property, your Brawler attacks gain the benefits listed below:

• Whenever you make a Brawler attack you can roll your Contender die in place of the normal damage die for that weapon. This die starts out as a d6 and changes as you gain brawler levels, as indicated in the Contender column of the Brawler table above.
  • When you take the Attack action on your turn and make only Brawler attacks, you can use a bonus action on that turn to make a grapple, shove, or unarmed strike attack.

2.name: Brutal Exploits
description: At 2nd level, you have picked up hand-to-hand techniques to enhance your combat skill, both on and off the field of battle.

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: The Brawler table shows how many Exploit Dice you have to perform your Brutal Exploits. To use an Exploit, you must expend one of these Dice. You can only use one Exploit per attack, ability check, or saving throw and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.
Your Exploit Dice begin as d4s, and increase in size as you gain levels in this class, as indicated in the Brawler table.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: At 2nd level, choose two Brutal Exploits of 1st-degree. These become your Mastered Exploits. You gain more Mastered Exploits as you gain levels in this class, as shown on the Brawler table. When you gain new Mastered Exploits, they must be of a degree less than or equal to half of your Degree Limit (rounded up, minimum of 1st-degree). This limit can be seen in parentheses next to your Degree Limit on the Brawler table.

You can use each of your Mastered Exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can choose to exchange one of your Mastered Exploits with a different Brutal Exploit for which you meet the requirements.

subFeatures.name: Exploits Prepared
description: At 2nd level, when you finish a long rest, you can prepare a number of Brutal Exploits equal to your exploit modifier + half your Brawler level (minimum 1). To prepare an Exploit it must be of a degree less than or equal to your Degree Limit.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: If an Exploit requires a creature to make a saving throw, your Exploit saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

2.name: Sterner Stuff
description: You may get knocked down, but you will never give up when a physical contest is on the line. Starting at 2nd level, whenever you fail a Strength or Dexterity ability check or saving throw, you can add your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1) to the result of your roll, possibly turning failure into success.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. When you have no uses left, you can expend an Exploit Die to use it again.

5.name: Martial Superiority
description: At 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Moreover, you can take the Dash or Disengage action in place of one of those attacks.

6.name: Furious Fists
description: Determination empowers your blows. Beginning at 6th level, your Brawler attacks count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks.

7.name: Sturdy Frame
description: Beginning at 7th level, your resilient frame lets you shrug off the brunt of certain effects, such as a green dragon's poison breath or a cone of cold spell. Whenever you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

9.name: Steel Physique
description: Your physique has been purified in the fires of battle. Starting at 9th level, when you take damage you can expend one use of Sterner Stuff to gain resistance to that instance of damage.
Also, whenever you make a Strength or a Dexterity ability check, you can use Sterner Stuff without expending a use.

11.name: Prizefighter
description: At 11th level, your ruthless style of brawling becomes second nature to you. Once on your turn, you can use one 1st-degree Brutal Exploit you know that can be used as part of an attack, without expending an Exploit Die.
At 15th level, you can use 2nd-degree Brutal Exploits you know in this way, following the same restrictions. Though, you can only use one Brutal Exploit per turn in this way.

13.name: Battle Forged
description: You are always prepared to stand and fight. At 13th level, you gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws. Also, when you roll initiative you regain one expended use of Sterner Stuff.

14.name: Mercurial Mind
description: Beginning at 14th level, if you are charmed, dominated, frightened, paralyzed, or stunned at the start of your turn, you can expend one of your Exploit Dice to immediately end one of those conditions for yourself.

18.name: Diamond Physique
description: Your ruthless determination allows you to survive strikes that would be deadly to weaker warriors. Beginning at 18th level, when you use Steel Physique to gain damage resistance, you gain temporary hit points equal to any damage you took.

20.name: Adamantine Fists
description: At 20th level, your blows send even the most dauntless of foes reeling. When you hit a creature with a Brawler attack it has disadvantage on the first ability check or saving throw that it is forced to make before the beginning of your next turn.

Champions forgo all other forms of improvement to focus on enhancing their raw physical might. These immense figures strive to maintain peak physical condition through relentless training. In battle, Champions perform supernatural feats of athleticism and overwhelm their foes with their raw power.
subclasses.name: Champion

3.name: Mighty Warrior
description: Starting at 3rd level, the raw physical might that you have cultivated has greatly enhanced your prowess in battle. Your Brawler attacks now score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
At 17th level, this range increases again and your Brawler attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

6.name: Remarkable Athlete
description: Starting at 6th level, you can regularly perform feats of athleticism that would be impossible for most. Feat of Strength and Mighty Leap become Mastered Exploits for you.

10.name: Brutal Critical
description: Starting at 10th level, the force of your strikes sends foes reeling. When you score a critical hit with a Brawler attack you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage.
This increases to two additional damage dice at 17th level.

17.name: Legendary Champion
description: Starting at 17th level, you are a nearly perfect specimen of physical vigor, and have become exceedingly hard to kill. When you start your turn with half of your hit points or less remaining, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier.
You do not regain any hit points if you are at 0 hit points.

Often found in the ranks of thieves' guilds and other criminal organizations, Enforcers are Brawlers who use their physical prowess to control others. To an Enforcer, no tactics are too dirty or dishonorable, all that matters is achieving their goal.
subclasses.name: Enforcer

3.name: Rough 'Em Up
description: Starting at 3rd level, you are adept at using your strength to goad and overwhelm others. When you hit a creature with a Brawler attack it has disadvantage on all attacks against creatures other than you until the beginning of your next turn.

3.name: The Wrong Crowd
description: Also at 3rd level, you find yourself at home in the seedy underbelly of any city. If you spend a night carousing in a settlement of any size, you have advantage on ability checks to gather information on that settlement, its culture, factions, and important figures.
You also learn to speak, read, write, and decipher Thieves' Cant, the secret code and jargon of thieves and criminals

6.name: Imposing Glance
description: Starting at 6th level, your ruthless style of fighting inspires fear in your enemies. Once per turn, If you hit a creature with two or more Brawler attacks on your turn, you can force that creature, or another creature that can see you within 30 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Exploit save DC. On a failed save, it is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

10.name: Ruthless Pursuit
description: Starting at 10th level, once you have a foe in your sights it is rare that they escape your grasp. You have advantage on any Strength (Athletics) checks you make to grapple creatures that are frightened of you, and you have advantage on Brawler attack rolls against creatures that are frightened of you or grappled by you.

10.name: Nerves of Steel
description: Fear is a weapon to be used against cowards and the weakwilled, you do not succumb to such base emotions. Starting at 10th level, you gain immunity to the frightened condition.

17.name: No Mercy
description: Starting at 17th level, you have no qualms about exploiting the weaknesses of foes and you make sure to target them whenever you can. When you force a creature that is frightened of you or grappled by you to make a saving throw to resist the effects of a Brutal Exploit, it has disadvantage on its saving throw.

Gentleman, ladies, and other noble folks are often held in high regard due to their honor.  Brawlers called Esteemed Boxers are those that hold this honor, along with usually holding some form of title.  They eschew dirty fighting techniques, and engage their opponents in a fair, even competition of strength.
subclasses.name: Esteemed Boxer

3.name: Elegant Bearing
description: Starting at 3rd level, you possess the bearing of a noble.  You gain the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency in two of the following skills: Insight, Intimidation, Persuasion, or Society.
  • If you are not wearing any armor or wielding a shield your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Charisma modifier.
  • You can replicate the effects of the Compelled Duel spell by expending an Exploit die. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

3.name: Fisticuffs
description: Also at 3rd level, when you are struck you strike back in turn. When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to move with the momentum of the blow, decreasing the damage dealt by an amount equal to a roll of your Exploit die + your Brawler level.
If you reduce the incoming damage to 0, you can make an unarmed strike against the attacker as part of the same reaction.

You can make this attack a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.  If you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can expend an Exploit die to use it again.

6.name: Honorable Presence
description: Starting at 6th level, your honorable nature seems to compel others to act more honorably in your presence. When a creature of your choice starts its turn within 10 feet of you or moves there for the first time on a turn, you can force them to make a Charisma saving throw against your Exploit save DC. On a failed saving throw, the target cannot knowingly and willingly tell a lie or use poison until the start of their next turn.

10.name: Enforced Chivalry
description: Starting at 10th level, others are made to reciprocate your manners in one way or another:

• You gain resistance to psychic damage.
  • Creatures hidden from you have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
  • When you finish a short or long rest, you gain the benefits of the Sanctuary spell. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

17.name: Knockout
description: Starting at 17th level, you can knock an enemy senseless with a single blow.  Once per turn when you reduce a creature to a number of hit points less than or equal to your Brawler level, you can immediately reduce the creature's hit points to 0 non-lethally and knock them unconscious.
Additionally, you can make attacks with your Fisticuffs feature an unlimited number of times, without expending an Exploit die.
Finally, the range of your Honorable Presence feature increases to 30 feet.

Inferno souls can channel the heat and energy naturally produced by their bodies to create waves of heat and destruction. They believe that anything is possible, even rebirth, if they put enough drive and passion into it.
subclasses.name: Inferno Soul

3.name: Heated Body
description: Starting at 3rd level, you gain the ability to store heat within your body for later use. You gain resistance to fire damage, and whenever you take fire damage, you gain twice as many Heat charges, which remain for 1 hour. You can have a number of Heat charges up to three times your Brawler level. If you would take any amount of non-fire damage, it is dealt to your Heat charges first, and any remaining damage is dealt to you as normal.
Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can expend all of your Heat charges to deal additional fire damage equal to your total number of Heat charges.

3.name: Ignition
description: Also at 3rd level, you can tap into the heat within you to strengthen your fight. As a bonus action on your turn, you can expend a use of your Sterner Stuff to set yourself on fire for the next 10 minutes and enter a state of Ignition. For the duration you gain the following benefits:

• At the start of your turn you gain Heat charges equal to a roll of your Contender die.
  • Creatures you are grappling or grappled by begin burning (1d10) at the start of each of their turns.
  • When you hit with an unarmed strike, you can choose for it to deal fire damage, instead of whichever damage type it would normally deal.
  • Whenever you score a critical hit or expend an Exploit Die, your Contender die increases by one step until the end of your turn.

6.name: Flickering Flame
description: Starting at 6th level, you have learned how to dance like the flames of a candle. When a creature hits you with an attack while you are in Ignition, you can expend an Exploit Die and roll it as a reaction, subtracting the result from the attack roll. If the attack misses, the attacker also takes fire damage equal to the result.

10.name: Flare Up
description: Starting at 10th level, the fire within your soul begins to flare up. If you would be reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright, if you have any amount of Heat charges, you instead drop to 1 hit point and 0 Heat charges.
Additionally, when you use your Flickering Flame featuer to cause an attack to miss, you gain Heat charges equal to the roll.

17.name: Heat-Sync
description: Starting at 17th level, you have become one with the heat within you and around you. While in Ignition you are immune to fire damage, but you still gain Heat charges as though you weren't.
Additionally, when you roll the highest result on your Contender Die when rolling damage, you can roll an Exploit Die an add it to the total.
Finally, fire damage you deals ignores resistance to fire damage and treats immunity as resistance.
Immovable objects are experts at holding ground and forming impassable walls, utilizing their bodies strategically to control areas.
subclasses.name: Immovable Object

3.name: Hold Your Ground
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action you can expend a use of Sterner Stuff to gain the following properties until the start of your next turn:

• Your speed is reduced to 0.
  • You can't be forcefully moved or knocked prone.
  • Your Armor Class increases by 2.
  • When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.

3.name: Large Body
description: Also at 3rd level, whenever you would make a Dexterity saving throw, you may instead make a Constitution saving throw. Benefits that apply only to Dexterity saving throws, such as the Evasion feature, still apply when you use this feature.

6.name: Human Shield
description: Starting at 6th level, when a creature within 5 feet of you fails a Strength or Dexterity ability check or saving throw, you can expend a use of Sterner Stuff to add your Constitution modifier to the roll, potentially turning it into a success.

10.name: Weaponized Mass
description: Starting at 10th level, friendly creatures of your size or smaller can use you to gain the benefits of three-quarters cover.
Additionally, hostile creatures treat the area within 5 feet of you as difficult terrain.

17.name: No Way Out
description: Starting at 17th level, when you use your Hold Your Ground feature, you gain the following additional benefits:

• You gain a special reaction that you can take once during every turn, but you can only use this special reaction for an opportunity attack.
  • Other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter your reach.
  • When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature must make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (target's choice) against your exploit save DC or be knocked prone.

Lucha libre is a discipline marked by high-flying acrobatics and a deep, spiritual connection to an assumed identity, a persona embodied by the Luchador's signature mask and expressed through combat.  Luchadors often have a strong sense of showmanship, and there is very little they won't do to win a fight or wow a crowd.
subclasses.name: Luchador

3.name: High-Flying Strikes
description: Starting at 3rd level, whenever you make an unarmed strike, you can leap up to 10 feet before or after making the attack without expending any movement.
When you make a successful unarmed strike against a creature that you started your turn at least 10 feet away from, you can deal additional damage equal to a roll of your Exploit Die.

3.name: Persona Mask
description: Also at 3rd level, you create or otherwise acquire a mask that represents some inner facet of your fighting spirit. Choose three powers for your mask. If your mask is removed by force, it forever loses its powers.
You can create a new mask over the course of a week, choosing new powers for it. If you create or acquire a new mask, your old mask loses its powers.

6.name: Build Heat
description: Starting at 6th level, as bonus action in combat, you can attempt to rile up onlookers, drawing fighting spirit from their attention and enthusiasm whether it is directed for or against you.

When you do, choose either enemies or allies to rile, then make a Performance (Charisma) check with DC equal to 10 plus the number of creatures of the chosen type within 30 feet that can see or hear you.
On a success, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the number of creatures affected.

6.name: Slip and Roll
description: Also at 6th level, your speed increases by 10 feet, and opportunity attacks made against you have disadvantage.

10.name: Undeniable Appeal
description: Starting at 10th level, you gain proficiency in Performance.  If you already have proficiency in it, you double your proficiency bonus for checks made with it.
Additionally, when you use your Build Heat feature, you can affect both allies and enemies instead of choosing.
Finally, your mask gains two additional mask powers.

17.name: Aura of Stardom
description: Starting at 17th level, while you have any temporary hit points, you are wreathed in the adoration or hatred of the masses, warding you against harm. The first attack made against you each turn has disadvantage, and you have advantage on all saving throws.
Additionally, you can attack three times whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

While most Brawlers focus only on their physical perfection, Martial Artists also pursue inner enlightenment. Tempering rigorous training with meditation and study, these wise ones strive for complete mastery over their body, mind, and spirit.
subclasses.name: Martial Artist

3.name: Practiced Strikes
description: Starting at 3rd level, you practice your chosen techniques over and over until they become second nature to you. When you hit a creature with a Brawler attack, you can use one Brutal Exploit you know, that can be used when you hit with a melee weapon attack or an unarmed strike, without expending an Exploit Die. When you do so, you must roll a d4 in place of your Exploit Die.
You can use a Brutal Exploit in this way a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses each time you finish a long rest.

3.name: Warrior Sage
description: Also at 3rd level, your training not only hones your body, but also your mind and soul. You gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice and one set of artisan's tools of your choice.
Whenever you make an ability check that uses either of the proficiencies you gained from this feature you gain a bonus to your roll equal to one roll of your Exploit Die.

6.name: Ebb and Flow
description: Starting at 6th level, you use your foes' momentum against them. When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Exploit Save DC. On a failure, it suffers one of the following effects:

• It is knocked prone and loses its remaining movement.
  • You move it 10 feet away from you in a straight line.
  • You can make a single Brawler attack against it.

10.name: Spirit of Serenity
description: By 10th level, you have honed your spirit alongside your physical abilities. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

17.name: Enlightenment
description: Starting at 17th level, you have become an unparalleled master of your style of martial arts and are able to strike with both overwhelming power and wondrous speed. You gain the benefits below:

• When you make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, you can make two unarmed strikes instead of the normal one.
  • You gain one additional reaction per round, but it can only be used for Ebb and Flow or an opportunity attack.

Whether by ritual, birth, or happenstance, the Brawlers of the Ghostly Hand have been imbued with the esoteric powers of ethereal undead. Combining this strange power with their mastery of unarmed combat, they are a true terror to behold.
subclasses.name: Ghostly Hand

3.name: Incorporeal Jaunt
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can draw on the otherworldly power you wield to become temporarily incorporeal. Until the end of your current turn, you can move through solid creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain.
If you end your movement inside a solid creature or object, you are instantly shunted to the nearest unoccupied space, taking 1d10 force damage for every 5 feet you traveled.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. When you have no uses left, you can expend an Exploit Die to use it again.

3.name: Unsettling Visage
description: Also at 3rd level, the power that dwells within you unsettles other creatures. You gain proficiency in Intimidation.

6.name: Otherworldly Resistance
description: Starting at 6th level, the supernatural power that permeates your body and style of combat hardens your body. You gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage and immunity to disease and the poisoned condition.
Moreover, whenever you make a Death saving throw, you can expend an Exploit Die, roll it, and add it to your roll.
