description: You can move an object or a creature with your mind. As an action, you target one loose object that is Large or smaller or one willing creature, other than yourself. If you can see the target and it is within 30 feet of you, you can move it up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, if it is a Tiny object, you can move it to or from your hand. Either way, you can move the target horizontally, vertically, or both. Once you take this action, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend a Psionic Energy die to take it again.

7.name: Telekinetic Adept
description: By the 7th level, You have mastered new ways to use your telekinetic abilities, detailed below.

subFeatures.name: Psi-Powered Leap
description: As a bonus action, you can propel your body with your mind. You gain a flying speed equal to twice your walking speed until the end of the current turn. Once you take this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend a Psionic Energy die to take it again.

subFeatures.name: Telekinetic Thrust
description: When you deal damage to a target with your Psionic Strike, you can force the target to make a Strength saving throw against a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. If the save fails, you can knock the target prone or move it up to 10 feet in any direction horizontally.

10.name: Guarded Mind
description: Starting at 10th level, the psionic energy flowing through you has bolstered your mind. You have resistance to psychic damage. Moreover, if you start your turn charmed or frightened, you can expend a Psionic Energy die and end every effect on yourself subjecting you to those conditions.

15.name: Bulwark of Force
description: At 15th level, you can shield yourself and others with telekinetic force. As a bonus action, you can choose creatures, which can include you, that you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of the chosen creatures is protected by half cover for 1 minute or until you're incapacitated.
Once you take this bonus action, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Psionic Energy die to take it again.

18.name: Telekinetic Master
description: By 18th level, your ability to move creatures and objects with your mind is matched by few. You can cast the Telekinesis spell, requiring no components, and your spellcasting ability for the spell is Intelligence. On each of your turns while you concentrate on the spell, including the turn when you cast it, you can make one attack with a weapon as a bonus action.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a Psionic Energy die to cast it again.

subclasses.name: Psi Warrior

description: While all Fighters are deadly with their chosen weapons, the warriors known as Opportunists can turn any object, into a deadly weapon. Always ready to scrap, these unconventional Fighters often grow up on the streets, where every day is a fight for their lives. When each day is a struggle, you learn to find success even in the most unfavorable conditions.

3.name: Improvised Adept
description: Beginning when you choose this subclass at 3rd level, to a  true opportunist, anything can be a weapon. You gain proficiency with improvised weapons. Whenever you make an attack with an improvised weapon, the object's damage die is equal to your Exploit Die if it was not already larger.
Moreover, when you use an improvised weapon, you can treat it as if it has the Finesse, Heavy, or Thrown (20/60) property.

3.name: Jack of All Trades
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you can add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to any ability check you make that doesn't already include your proficiency bonus.

7.name: Wondrous Determination
description: Starting at 7th level, you always find a way to make things work, no matter how unlikely your success might seem. Your improvised weapon attacks count as magical for overcoming resistances and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Also, you can use any creature that is equal to your size or smaller as an improvised weapon while you are grappling it. When you hit with an improvised attack using a grappled creature, the grappled creature also takes damage equal to one roll of your Exploit Die.

10.name: Cunning Defense
description: Starting at 10th level, you can make use of your surroundings for defense. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to grab an object that is not being worn or carried to intercept the attack. If there is an object you can grab with a free hand, you reduce the damage of the triggering attack by one roll of your Exploit Die + your Strength or your Dexterity modifier. When you do so, the object is destroyed.

15.name: Improvised Expert
description: Starting at 15th level, you can crush your improvised weapons to make use of your martial skill. When you hit with an improvised weapon attack using an object, you can choose to instantly destroy the object to use one Martial Exploit you know without expending an Exploit Die. The Exploit you use must be able to be used as part of a weapon attack.

18.name: Legendary Opportunist
description: Starting at 18th level, to you, anything is a deadly weapon. When you pick up an object to use it as an improvised weapon, you can expend one Exploit Die to infuse it with mythical power. For the 1 minute, that object gains one of the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Brutal Power
description: If the object deals bludgeoning damage, once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Exploit save DC or be stunned until the beginning of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Critical Point
description: If the object deals piercing damage, your attacks with it score a critical on a roll of 17-20 on the d20.

subFeatures.name: Honed Edge
description: If the object deals slashing damage, it gains a +3 bonus to its attack and damage rolls when you use it.

subclasses.name: Opportunist

description: Pugilists live by their fists, bare-knuckle warriors who do not hesitate to throw hands if the situation demands it. They know the intense, close, violent intimacy of melee, and they operate unapologetically in that space. Whether in fighting pits by the docks to make some extra coin, in the king's grand arena as champions of quarreling nobles, or in the employ of local merchants in need of seemingly weaponless guards, pugilists can be found in all rungs of society. Pugilists take pleasure in a battle hard won and thrill in the energy of the fight rather than in a kill. They can often be found celebrating or having drinks with a former opponent hours after the fight, regardless of the bout's winner.

3.name: Bare Knuckle Brawler
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn to use your fists, knees, elbows, head, and feet to attack your opponents. You gain the following benefits while you are not wearing heavy armor and while you are not wielding weapons or a shield:

Your unarmed strikes deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d8 + your Strength modifier on a hit. Your unarmed strike damage increases as you reach higher levels. The d8 becomes a d10 at 10th level and a d12 at 18th level.
  • When you use the Attack action to make one or more unarmed strikes, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action.

3.name: Resilient
description: Starting at 3rd level, you learn to endure great amounts of physical punishment. You add your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) to any death saving throw you make. In addition, you can use Second Wind a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

7.name: Uncanny Fortitude
description: Beginning at 7th level, if damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you can make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is from a critical hit. On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
In addition, when you use Second Wind, you now regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level + your Constitution modifier

10.name: Debilitating Blow
description: At 10th level, when you hit one target with two unarmed strikes in the same turn, you can use a bonus action to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failure, the target has disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

15.name: Withstand Death
description: At 15th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use Second Wind as a reaction, provided you have uses of Second Wind remaining. You can decide to use this reaction before or after your Uncanny Fortitude feature triggers.
In addition, when you make a death saving throw and roll a 1 on the d20, it counts as one failure instead of two.

18.name: Opportunisitc
description: Starting at 18th level, you might not look for a fight around every corner, but you're ready in case one happens. You have advantage on initiative rolls.

In addition, when a creature you can see enters a space within 5 feet of you, you can make one opportunity attack against the creature. This opportunity attack must be made with an unarmed strike. You have a number of reactions each turn equal to your proficiency bonus, but these reactions can be used only to perform opportunity attacks.

subclasses.name: Pugilist

description: Every successful adventurer knows the value of teamwork, but none value it more then those known as Quartermasters. These supportive warriors strive to help their allies reach their full potential. Constantly putting the needs of their companions before their own, Quartermasters keep their team in top condition with a fresh Ration and a helping hand.

3.name: Cook's Expertise
description: Starting when you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you are able to prepare potent morsels of food that keep your allies in peak condition. At the end of each long rest, you can prepare a number of these Rations equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

As a bonus action, you can eat a prepared Ration, or feed a Ration to a creature within 5 feet. Consuming a Ration ends any current Ration effects on that creature. Any Rations you have prepared become inert at the end of your next long rest.
As an action, you can expend an Exploit Die to prepare an additional Ration of your choice. You can eat a Ration or feed it to a creature as part of the same action used to create it.

subFeatures.name: Fortifying Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature chooses either Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution. For the next minute, the creature can add your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1) to any ability check or saving throw for the chosen ability score.
At 10th level the duration of the effect increases to 1 hour.

subFeatures.name: Invigorating Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature regains hit points equal to 1d10 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1).
Starting at 10th level, this Ration restores an additional 1d10 hit points, and any hit points they regain that exceed their hit point maximum become temporary hit points.

subFeatures.name: Revitalizing Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature ends one of the following conditions currently affecting it: blindness, deafness, poison, or they reduce their exhaustion level by 1.
Starting at 10th level, this Ration can also cure the charmed, frightened, paralyzed, and stunned conditions.

subFeatures.name: Stimulating Ration
description: This Ration must be consumed as part of a short rest. Upon consumption, the creature gains advantage on the roll for any Hit Dice they choose to expend during that short rest.
Starting at 10th level, consuming this Ration allows the creature to treat any Hit Dice they expend during the short rest as their maximum possible result instead of rolling.

3.name: Down to Earth
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with cook's utensils, land vehicles, and in Animal Handling. Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of the proficiencies you gained through this feature, you a bonus to your roll equal to your Exploit Die.

7.name: Dependable
description: Starting at 7th level, you are always there to lend a helping hand to your allies. You can take the following special actions as a bonus action:

subFeatures.name: Arm
description: You give a weapon, item, or any ammunition you are carrying to a creature within 5 feet. The creature can then equip the given item, and stow one item as a free action.

subFeatures.name: Encourage
description: You take the Help action, targeting a creature of your choice within 10 feet that can see or hear you.

subFeatures.name: Wrangle
description: You make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) or a land vehicles check to control a mount or cart you are riding.

7.name: Enhanced Rations
description: Also starting at 7th level, you learn how to produce the following additional Rations.

subFeatures.name: Heightening Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature chooses either Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. For the next minute, the creature can add your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1) to any ability check or saving throw for the chosen ability score.
At 10th level the duration of the effect increases to 1 hour.

subFeatures.name: Limbering Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature's speed increases by 10 feet for the next minute.
At 14th level the creature's speed increases by 20 feet.

subFeatures.name: Thickening Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature gains resistance to either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (their choice) for the next minute.
Starting at 10th level consuming this Ration grants resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subFeatures.name: Warding Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature gains resistance to acid, cold, fire, poison, lightning, or thunder damage (their choice) for the next minute.
At 10th level the duration of the effect increases to 1 hour, and the creature can choose from force, necrotic, psychic, or radiant damage in addition to the other damage types.

10.name: Improved Rations
description: By 10th level, you have greatly improved the speed at which you prepare Rations. You can use a bonus action on your turn to create a Ration of your choice, eating it or feeding it to a creature within 5 feet of youas part of that same bonus action.

15.name: Ever Ready
description: At 15th level, you are always ready to support your companions. When you roll initiative, so long as you are not surprised, you prepare one Ration of your choice without expending an Exploit Die.
In addition, you learn how to produce the following additional Rations.

subFeatures.name: Berserker Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature does not fall unconscious when it is reduced to 0 hit points for the next hour. However, it still makes death saving throws as normal, dying upon failing three.

subFeatures.name: Rejuvenating Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature gains all the benefits of a short rest, including the ability to expend its Hit Dice as part of consuming the Ration. At the end of its current turn, the creature gains 1 level of exhaustion. After a creature eats this Ration, it must finish a long rest before it can gain the benefits of any other Ration you prepare.

subFeatures.name: Tenacious Ration
description: Upon consumption, the creature gains immunity to one of the following conditions (their choice): blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, poisoned, paralyzed, or stunned for the next hour.

18.name: Iron Stomach
description: By 18th level, your experiments with new Ration formulas have toughened your body and hardened your stomach. Your Constitution score, and maximum Constitution score, increase by 2, and you are immune to the poisoned condition.

In addition, you are always under the effects of one Ration of your choice with a duration of at least 1 minute. It does not need to be a Ration that you prepared, and you can change the Ration effect at the end of each short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Quartermaster

description: Rune Knights enhance their martial prowess using the supernatural power of runes, an ancient practice that originated with giants. Rune cutters can be found among any family of giants, and you likely learned your methods first or second hand from such a mystical artisan. Whether you found the giant's work carved into a hill or cave, learned of the runes from a sage, or met the giant in person, you studied the giant's craft and learned how to apply magic runes to empower your equipment.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with whitesmith's tools, and you learn to speak, read, and write Jiganti.

3.name: Rune Carver
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use magic runes to enhance your gear. You learn two runes of your choice, from among the runes described below, and each time you gain a level in this class, you can replace one rune you know with a different one from this feature. You learn additional runes at 7th, 10th, and 15th levels

Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch a number of objects equal to the number of runes you know, and you inscribe a different rune onto each of the objects. To be eligible, an object must be a weapon, a suit of armor, a shield, a piece of jewelry, or something else you can wear or hold in a hand. Your rune remains on an object until you finish a long rest, and an object can bear only one of your runes at a time

The following runes are available to you when you learn a rune. If a rune has a level requirement, you must be at least that level in this class to learn the rune. If a rune requires a saving throw, your Rune Magic save DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier.

3.name: Giant Might
description: At 3rd level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to transform and gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

• If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. If you lack the room to become Large in size, your size doesn't change.
  • You gain advantage on Strength ability checks and saving throws.
  • Once per turn, when you hit a target with a melee or thrown weapon attack, you can deal additional damage of the weapon's type equal to your Exploit Die on hit.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

7.name: Runic Shield
description: At 7th level, you learn to invoke your rune magic to protect your allies. When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to reroll the d20 and use the new roll
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

10.name: Great Stature
description: By 10th level, the magic of your runes permanently alters you. When you gain this feature, roll 3d4. You grow a number of inches in height equal to the roll
Moreover, the extra damage you deal with your Giant's Might feature increases to 1d6.

15.name: Master of Runes
description: At 15th level, you can invoke each rune you know from your Rune Carver feature twice, rather than once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

18.name: Runic Juggernaut
description: At 18th level, you learn how to amplify your rune-powered transformation. As a result, the extra damage you deal with the Giant's Might feature increases to 1d10. Moreover, when you use that feature, your size can increase to Huge, and while you are that size, your reach increases by 5 feet.

subclasses.name: Rune Knight

description: The Samurai is a fighter who draws on an implacable fighting spirit to overcome enemies. A samurai's resolve is nearly unbreakable, and the enemies in a samurai's path have two choices: yield or die fighting.

3.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Performance, Persuasion, or Society. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

3.name: Fighting Spirit
description: Starting at 3rd level, your intensity in battle can shield you and help you strike true. As a bonus action on your turn, you can give yourself advantage on all weapon attack rolls until the end of the current turn. When you do so, you also gain 5 temporary hit points. The number of hit points increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 10 at 10th level and 15 at 15th level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

7.name: Elegant Courtier
description: Starting at 7th level, your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations. Whenever you make a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier.

Your self-control also causes you to gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

10.name: Tireless Spirit
description: Starting at 10th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Fighting Spirit remaining, you regain one use.

15.name: Rapid Strike
description: Starting at 15th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

18.name: Strength Before Death
description: Starting at 18th level, your fighting spirit can delay the grasp of death. If you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to delay falling unconscious, and you can immediately take an extra turn. While you have 0 hit points during that extra turn, taking damage causes death saving throw failures as normal, and three death saving throw failures can still kill you. When the extra turn ends, you fall unconscious if you still have 0 hit points.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Samurai

description: An arcane focus is just another weapon utilizing the same deft precision required for ranged weaponry. Understanding this aspect of magic, spellslingers hone the simplest spells into becoming the deadly ammunition employed by their spellcasting implements.

3.name: Arcane Gunslinger
description: At 3rd level, when you choose this archetype, you gain proficiency in the Arcana skill and your choice of jeweler's tools or woodcarver's tools. You also learn four cantrips of your choice from the Arcane spell list. At 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level, you learn an additional cantrip of your choice. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of these cantrip with another from any spell list.

3.name: Spellslinging
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you learn to sling cantrips as ranged attacks. Any cantrip you cast that deals damage can use Dexterity as its spellcasting ability. At 18th level, any spell you can cast that deals damage gains this benefit.
Additionally, you treat an arcane focus as a simple ranged weapon with the following special property.

subFeatures.name: Spellshot
description: In place of the item's weapon attack, you can cast a cantrip with the following changes:

• The spell is also considered a weapon attack made using the item for the purpose of any features from your class, race, or other sources.
  • The spell is cast as if you are a 1st level character, gaining no benefits even if you have reached 5th level or higher.
  • You gain a bonus to one damage roll of the spell equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + half your proficiency bonus.

7.name: Esoteric Implements
description: Starting at 7th level, you ignore the class requirements of arcane foci you attempt to attune to and spell scrolls you attempt to read. Additionally, choose one of the following options to gain the benefits of:
You can use the spell attack bonus and spell save DC from any of your spellcasting abilities in place of any attack bonus or DC provided by a magic item you use
When you finish a long rest, you can replace one cantrip you know from your Arcane Gunslinger feature with another cantrip from the Arcane spell list.
You can treat any weapon as an arcane focus. Moreover, any arcane focus you're using benefits from its Spellshot property even when not used as a ranged weapon.

10.name: Arcane Resistance
description: Starting at 10th level, while holding a magical focus, you add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) to saving throws you make against spells. Moreover, the cantrips you cast is immune to anti-magic spells like counterspell, dispel magic, or antimagic field.

15.name: Piercing Incantation
description: Starting at 15th level, your shots can pierce through targets.  As an action, choose a cantrip you know and a point you can see within 60 feet of you. In a 10-foot wide line between you and the point, you can cast the chosen cantrip as a part of your Spellslinging feature against each creature in the area as if it is the target of or included in the area of effect of the spell.

18.name: Mystical Deadeye
description: Starting at 18th level, your magical shots always hit their mark.  The cantrips you cast ignore effects that grant immunity to magic, such as magic immunity or reflective carapace.

subclasses.name: Spellslinger

description: These fighters are a form of magic user called a half-spark. They are people who are talented in one specific area of magic: and their talent is in lightning. They benefit from a magical phenomenon that causes their body to be able to store a massive electric charge, and release it as easily as they would a breath of air. This makes them very dangerous fighters, and even lovers; because if they are not disciplined enough all it takes in small flare of emotion and the person standing closest to them may be struck by lightning.

3.name: Storm Surge
description: At 3rd, when you choose this archetype, your talent with lightning manifests. It gives you the ability to accelerate and enhance your body beyond what is normally possible using the energy you can create. As a bonus action, you can use this feature to gain one of the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

• Your walking speed increases by 15 feet
  • You gain advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws
  • Your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1), and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

7.name: Perfect Grounding
description: Starting at 7th level, you look forward to getting hit by lighting. You gain resistance to lighting damage.

Additionally, if you are forced make a Dexterity saving throw to avoid lightning damage from a spell or ability such as lightning bolt, you can use your reaction to consume the erupting electricity and cause the spell or ability to deal half damage to you, and any other creature who had to make the save. You regain one use of your Storm Surge feature if you take 15 or more lightning damage after using this feature.

10.name: Arcing Strikes
description: By 10th level, you have learned how to release your energy in a very precise manner, arcing it from one point to another. The first time you hit a creature on your turn after using your storm surge ability, you may deal lightning damage to another creature within 20 feet of the target equal to half of any bludgeoning, piercing, slashing and/or lightning damage you dealt with the attack.
At 18th level you may target two creatures with this feature instead of one.

15.name: Ride the Lightning
description: Starting at 15th level, you can use the power in your body in order to lift you off the ground. As an action, you can expend a use of your Storm Surge feature in order to gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 10 minutes. You can hover when flying this way.

18.name: Stormborn
description: At 18th level, you can use an action to expend a use of your Action Surge to cast the Chain Lightning spell without expending a spell slot. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

subclasses.name: Storm Heart

description: Swordsage, blade master, sword saints; expert warriors who dedicate their lives to the art of battle have had many names throughout history. Only drawing their weapon when they are prepared to kill, a Swordsage will only slay another creature when necessary. A master Swordsage will only take a single apprentice, teaching everything they know to a single warrior.

3.name: Battle Trance
description: Starting at 3rd level when you choose this Archetype, so long as you are not wearing heavy armor or a shield, you can use a bonus action to enter a Battle Trance. Your Battle Trance grants you the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You can take the Dash action as a bonus action.
  • You gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class.
  • You have advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.
  • Once per turn when you use a Swordsage Exploit, you can roll a d4 instead of expending one of your Exploit Dice.

Your Battle Trance ends early if you are incapacitated, or you don a shield or heavy armor. Once you enter your Battle Trance you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can expend an Exploit Die to enter a Battle Trance again.

3.name: Student of the Blade
description: Also starting at 3rd level, in your studies you have mastered other skills adjacent to swordplay. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Athletics, Acrobatics, Insight, Intimidation, Performance, Society.
Whenever you make an ability check with the chosen skill you gain a bonus to your roll equal to your Exploit Die.

7.name: Reflexes of the Sage
description: By 7th level, you have honed your reflexes to a point in pursuit of martial perfection. You gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws, and you add your proficiency bonus to your initiative rolls.
Also, while you are in your Battle Trance, the bonus to your Armor Class increases by 1, for a total bonus of +2.

10.name: Masterful Trance
description: By 10th level, you have mastered the Battle Trance of the Swordsage. When you roll initiative, so long as you are not surprised, you can enter a Battle Trance without expending any resources.

15.name: Legendary Swordsage
description: At 15th level, you become a whirlwind of deadly steel while in your Battle Trance. Once per turn while you are in a Battle Trance, you can use any Exploit that you know, rolling a d6 in place of expending one of your Exploit Dice.
At 18th level the d6 from this feature becomes a d8.

subclasses.name: Swordsage

description: There are warriors who move so quickly that they seem to stop time, then there are those who actually alter time with their attacks. The timeblade augments physical attacks by manipulating temporal powers and eventually learns to step outside time itself.

3.name: Temporal Strike
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to trigger one of the following effects. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Dislocative Step
description: You step outside of time and move to an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. At 10th level, you can move up to 30 feet.

subFeatures.name: Dislocative Shove
description: You push the target of your attack to an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you. You can move the target only horizontally, and before moving into damaging terrain, such as lava or a pit, the target can make a Strength saving throw against your Exploit save DC, ending the movement in an unoccupied space next to the damaging terrain on a success. At 10th level, you can move the target up to 30 feet.

7.name: Chronologic Echo
description: At 7th level, immediately after you use your Second Wind feature, you can trigger an echo in time, allowing you to use it twice. Roll separately for each use of Second Wind. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

10.name: Improved Temporal Strike
description: At 10th level, when you use your Temporal Strike feature, you can choose one of the following additional options:

subFeatures.name: Chronal Cleave
description: You immediately make a weapon attack against a different target within range.

subFeatures.name: Chronal Shield
description: You add your proficiency bonus to your Armor Class until the beginning of your next turn.

15.name: Continuity Rift
description: At 15th level, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can instantly open a rupture in space-time to swallow the target. The creature disappears and falls through a realm outside of reality.

At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. It takes 8d8 psychic damage as it grapples with the mind-breaking experience. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw against your Exploit save DC or it acts randomly for 1 minute as if under the effects of the Confusion spell. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

18.name: Temporal Warrior
description: Starting at 18th level, you can momentarily step outside of time to attack your foes. As an action, you can briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself. No time passes for other creatures, while you take 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, during which you can use actions and move as normal. This effect works like the Time Stop spell, except you can make one attack on each of your turns without ending the effect. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Timeblade

description: The fighters known as Tinker Knights seek an unorthodox form of martial skill. Rather than master martial techniques they look to augment their physical ability with mechanical inventions and innovative weaponry. Though they spend most of their time theorizing, tinkering, and experimenting with new Schematics, Tinker Knights and their inventive arsenals are a force to be reckoned with on the field of battle.

3.name: Inventive Arsenal
description: Starting when you choose this Archetype at 3rd level, you have come up with a cacophony of strange modifications for weapons and armor, known as Schematics. You know two Schematics. When you gain a level in this class, you can replace one Schematic you know with another Schematic of your choice.
As you gain levels in this class, your number of Schematics known grows; at 7th level (3), 10th level (4), and 15th level (5).

At the end of each a long rest, you can touch a number of objects equal to your number of Schematics Known and you modify each object with the features of one Schematic. These features last until the end of your next long rest. Each object can only be modified by one Schematic at a time, and it must meet the requirements in the Schematic description.
If a Schematic requires a saving throw, your Schematic save DC is calculated as follows:
Schematic save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

3.name: Analytical Mind
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with tinker's tools and whitesmith's tools. If you already proficient with these tools, you gain proficiency with another set of tools of your choice.
You also learn the Tinker's Intuition Exploit, but it doesn't count against your total number of Exploits Prepared.

7.name: Tinker's Expertise
description: Starting at 7th level, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check that uses your proficiency with tinker's tools or whitesmith's tools.
In addition, items modified by your Schematics count as magical for overcoming resistances and immunities, and you can apply Schematics to magic weapons and armor.

10.name: Mechanical Synergy
description: Starting at 10th level, your modifications can work in tandem with each other. You can apply two Schematics to one object, so long as the object meets the prerequisites for both Schematics.

15.name: Flexible Innovation
description: Starting at 15th level, your inventive arsenal can adjust to meet the challenges at hand. At the end of a short rest, you can transfer a Schematic from one object to another, so long as the new object meets the prerequisites. If a Schematic has a limited amount of charges, the number of expended charges remains the same.
In addition, you can apply up to three Schematics to one object, so long as it meets all the Schematic prerequisites.

18.name: Masterwork Inventions
description: Starting at 18th level, weapons modified by your Schematics gain a +1 bonus to its attack and damage rolls for each Schematic applied to it, and any set of armor modified by a Schematic gains a +1 bonus to its Armor Class for each of your Schematics applied to it.
Weapons and armor modified by your Schematics cannot gain a bonus greater then +3, regardless of any bonuses the item may have had before applying your Schematics.

subclasses.name: Tinker Knight

description: Those who walk the dark path of the Witch Knight are driven by an overwhelming desire to destroy the great evils of the world. Those especially dedicated, those willing to give up anything, are often approached by Eldritch Powers, beings of otherworldly might. These benefactors offer power in return for a fraction of the warrior's soul or unquestioning fealty.

3.name: Pact Magic
description: At 3rd level, the bargain you have struck with your Patron allows you to cast spells, much like a warlock does.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the Occult spell list. Upon reaching 10th level in this class you learn one additional Occult cantrip of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Witch Knight Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have, and the level of those spell slots. All of your spell slots from this feature are the same level. To cast one of your Occult spells of 1st-level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You learn two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Occult spell list. The Spells Known column of the Witch Knight Spellcasting table shows when you learn more Occult spells of 1st-level or higher. A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level.

When you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Occult spells you know and replace it with another spell of your choice from the Occult spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Occult spells.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

3.name: Sanguine Offering
description: You have learned to sacrifice your own vitality to your Patron for increased martial potency. Starting at 3rd level, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one of your fighter Hit Die as part of the attack to deal an additional 2d10 necrotic damage to the target, in addition to the normal damage of your weapon.

3.name: Eldritch Power
description: When you adopt this Archetype at 3rd level, you gain minor eldritch abilities that reflect the source of your power.
You gain one skill proficiency of your choice, and you learn one cantrip of your choice from any spell list. This cantrip doesn't count against your total number of Cantrips Known.

7.name: Otherworldly Step
description: Beginning at 7th level, you can draw upon the dark power gifted to you by your Patron to slip through cracks in reality. As an action, you can expend an Exploit Die to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. If you appear within 5 feet of a creature, you can make one melee weapon attack against them as part of the same action.

10.name: Enchanted Strikes
description: The eldritch magic within your blood seeps into your weapon strikes, undercutting resistance to spells. Starting at 10th level, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

15.name: Improved Sanguine Offering
description: You can restore your own vitality by inflicting pain on others. Beginning at 15th level, when you empower a weapon attack with your Sanguine Offering, you gain temporary hit points equal to the additional necrotic damage dealt to the creature.
Temporary hit points from this ability last for one minute, or until you gain temporary hit points from a different source.

18.name: Profane Sacrifice
description: Upon reaching 18th level, you can offer the death of your foes to your Eldritch Power in return for enhanced abilities. As a reaction when a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice:

• You have advantage on any weapon attack you make before the end of your next turn.
  • You regain 1d4 +1 expended Hit Dice.
  • You regain one expended Pact Magic spell slot.
You can use this ability a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Witch Knight

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Adrenaline Rush
description: Starting at 1st level, in battle your adrenaline increases your speed and your clarity. As a bonus action on your turn, you can enter an adrenaline rush. While in an adrenaline rush, you gain the following benefits:

• You have advantage on Dexterity ability checks and on saving throws against effects that you can see, such as traps and spells. To gain this benefit, you can't be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
  • Your movement speed increases by 5 feet. This bonus increases when you reach certain gunslinger levels, as shown in the Gunslinger table. If you are able to cast spells, you can only cast spells that deal damage while in an adrenaline rush.

Your Adrenaline Rush lasts for 1 minute. The adrenaline ends early if you are incapacitated, or if you end your turn and have not done one of the following since your last turn: attacked a creature, taken damage, used the Dash action to move as close as you can toward a hostile creature, or made a Strength or Dexterity check.

Once you have used your adrenaline rush the number of times shown for your gunslinger level in the Adrenaline Rushes column of the Gunslinger table, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

1.name: Expertise
description: You have come to master a specific set of skills and abilities. Also at 1st level, choose any two skill proficiencies, any two tool proficiencies, or one skill and one tool proficiency. If you were not already proficient, you gain proficiency with the two chosen skills or tools. If you were already proficient in those skills or tools, you can add double your proficiency bonus to any check you make with the chosen skills or tools.
If you already add double your proficiency bonus to a skill or tool, you cannot select it again for this feature.

1.name: Firearm Expert
description: Starting at 1st level, you know how to expertly use firearms.  You can reload or unjam any firearm as an object interaction.

1.name: Thieves' Cant
description: In pursuit of your skills you learned to speak, understand, and leave messages in the secret code of thieves. At 1st level, you learn Thieves' Cant. You can use this secret mix of dialect, jargon, and code, that allows you to hide messages in normal conversation, that can only be understood by other thieves.

You can also use your knowledge of Thieves' Cant to write and understand secret signs and symbols that convey short, simple messages. For example, you may use these symbols to mark an area as the territory of your thieves' guild, or to mark an inn as a haven for thieves or a place to sell illegal wares.

In addition, you can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.

2.name: Fighting Style
description: At 2nd level you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

2.name: Deadeye Exploits
description: Also at 2nd level, your quick hand and sharp eye grant you increased prowess in the use of firearms, represented by Deadeye Exploits.

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: The Gunslinger table shows how many Exploit Dice you have to perform the Exploits you know. To use your Exploits, you must expend one of your Exploit Dice. You can only use one Exploit per attack, ability check, or saving throw. You regain all expended Exploit Dice at the end of a short or long rest.
Your Exploit Dice begin as d4s and increase in size as you gain levels in this class, as indicated in the Gunslinger table.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: At 2nd level, choose two Deadeye Exploits of 1st-degree. These become your Mastered Exploits. You gain more Mastered Exploits as you gain levels in this class, as shown on the Gunslinger table. When you gain new Mastered Exploits, they must be of a degree less than or equal to half of your Degree Limit (rounded up, minimum of 1st-degree). This limit can be seen in parentheses next to your Degree Limit on the Gunslinger table.

You can use each of your Mastered Exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can choose to exchange one of your Mastered Exploits with a different Deadeye Exploit for which you meet the requirements.

subFeatures.name: Exploits Prepared
description: At 2nd level, when you finish a long rest, prepare a number of Deadeye Exploits equal to your exploit modifier + half your Gunslinger level (minimum 1). To prepare an Exploit it must be of a degree less than or equal to your Degree Limit.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: If one of your Exploits requires a creature to make a saving throw, your Exploit saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier

3.name: Enduring
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can move twice the normal amount of time (up to 16 hours) each day before being subject to the effect of a forced march (see "Travel Pace"in chapter 8 of the Player's Handbook).

5.name: Martial Superiority
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Moreover, you can take the Dash or Disengage action in place of one of those attacks.

6.name: Nimble Escape
description: Starting at 6th level, your training allows you react quickly to incoming strikes, reducing the damage you take. When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

9.name: Battle Readiness
description: Your resolve and fitness level help you push past fatigue. Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid exhuastion.
In addition, whenever you finish a short rest, your exhaustion level, if any, is decreased by 1.

11.name: Unwavering Loyalty
description: Starting at 11th level, your loyalty to your allies and your cause is unshakeable. You are immune to effects that would force you to act against your will, such as the charmed condition or the command spell.

13.name: Lingering Adrenaline Rush
description: Your adrenaline rush only ends early if you fall unconscious or you choose to end it early.
In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw.

14.name: Fortified Position
description: Starting at 14th level, you use your knowledge of battle to fortify your position against the enemy. During your adrenaline rush, you and allies within 10 feet gain the benefits of half cover and cannot be forecfully moved by non-magical means.

17.name: Adrenaline Surge
description: Starting at 17th level, while you are in an adrenaline rush, you can use your action to cause an adrenaline surge, further increasing your abilities.
When you cause an adrenaline surge, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute or until your adrenaline rush ends:

• Your speed is doubled
  • You gain a +2 bonus to your Armor Class
  • You have advantage on all Dexterity saving throws
  • You gain an additional action on each of your turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action
When this effect ends, you have disadvantage on ability checks until you finish a short rest.

20.name: Finish the Fight
description: At 20th level, you are determined to finish the fight, no matter the cost, and push yourself beyond your limits. When you are below half your hit point maximum, you can use your action to gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You have resistance to all damage.
  • If you are reduced to 0 hit points, you do not fall unconscious, but still make death saving throws and suffer the normal effects of taking damage at 0 hit points.
  • You are immune to being grappled, paralyzed, petrified, restrained, or stunned, and you can stand up from prone with no movement cost.
  • You can't be forcefully moved, your speed can't be reduced by any means, and you can move through another creature's space, though you can't end your turn there.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

Though most gunslingers see the explosive properties of black powder as a means to an end, demolitionists seek to harness this volatile potential directly, crafting deadly explosives and leaving the battlefield scarred with craters and blackened foliage.

3.name: Grenadier
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have been trained how to construct basic explosive grenades uisng your tinker's tools. When you gain this feature, you learn three how to make three types of Grenades of your choice. During a long rest, you can craft a number of grenades equal to your proficiency bonus.  You can only craft a single 4th-degree grenade at the end of a long rest.
A grenade can be thrown up to 60 feet as an action, where it detonates. Most grenades require a saving throw, which is made against your Exploit save DC.
The grenades you craft using this feature are unstable, and only last until you finish your next long rest.

You learn how to make two additional types of grenades of your choice at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn how to make new types of grenades, you can also replace one option you know with a different one.

7.name: Improved Explosives
description: At 7th level, you have gained access to higher quality explosives, improving the effect of your grenades. The damage dealt by explosives that you have crafted is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical damage. You also gain resisitance to fire damage due to your knowledge of how explosives work and how to best avoid injury.

10.name: Landmines
description: At 10th level, you have learned to craft landmines, traps with the effects of your explosives.  Over the course of one minute, you can plant a landmine in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you by expending one of your grenades.
Landmines are hidden, and require a Wisdom (Perception) check by a creature within 15 feet of it against your Exploit save DC in order to locate.

The next time a creature enters a landmine's space, the landmine detonates, causing the effects of the grenade used to craft it.  You can also detonate a landmine you can see as a bonus action on your turn.

15.name: Versatile Explosives
description: By 15th level, you have learned to modify your explosives quickly to produce different effects when needed.  Over the course of 1 hour, which can coincide with a short rest, you can change any number of grenades you have to a different grenade of equal or lesser degree.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

18.name: Master Grenadier
description: At 18th level, you have learned to craft explosives with more efficiency.  When you finish a long rest, you craft a number of grenades equal to twice your proficiency bonus.
In addition, you can now craft up to three 4th-degree grenades at a time.

subclasses.name: Demolitionist Teaching

description: Desperadoes are gunslingers who don't have any particularly special training in one field or another.  However, the accuracy and determination of a desperado is not to be underestimated, and they can hold out for far longer than any other gunslinger.

3.name: Fever Pitch
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you enter an adrenaline rush, you can choose to enter a fever pitch, a state of heightened battle awareness that is manifested through your fight-or-flight response.
While you are in a fever pitch, as a bonus action on your turn, you can take the Dash or Disengage action, or you can make one weapon attack.

3.name: Survivalist
description: Also at 3rd level, you have additional training in all aspects of adventuring. Chose any two skills and one type of tool you do not have proficiency in. You may add half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to checks made with the chosen skills and tool.

At 10th level, you can choose a third skill and a second tool. When you gain a level in this class, you can replace any of the proficiencies granted by this feature with another skill or tool of your choice.

7.name: Down But not Out
description: By 7th level, you have excellent physical conditioning, granting you the following benefits:

• Your walking speed is increased by 10 feet.
  • When you're prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.

10.name: Combat Veteran
description: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

15.name: Take Cover
description: At 15th level, your experience at fortifying your current position gives you insight on how to best defend yourself and your companions.

With 1 hour of work, which can coincide with a short or long rest, you can construct temporary fortifications from materials in your environment. The fortifications each are 5 ft x 5 ft in size, and you can construct a maximum number equal to 1 + your Dexterity modifier.

Fortifications constructed by this feature have an Armor Class equal to 10 + your proficiency bonus, and a number of hit points equal to twice your gunslinger level. The fortifications grant the benefits of half cover, and collapse naturally after 8 hours.
Starting at 18th level, the fortifications grant the benefits of three-quarters cover.

18.name: Posse
description: Starting at 18th level, you and your companions have formed a cohesive fighting unit together. You and friendly creatures within 20 feet of you gain a bonus to ranged attack rolls or Armor Class (your choice) equal to the number of creatures benefiting from your Take Cover feature.

subclasses.name: Desperado Teaching

description: Juggernauts are gunslingers who make use of both the fury of black powder and the strength of steel and armor.  A hearty bunch who enjoy a good fight, juggernauts are valuable for their incredible durability.

3.name: Hearty Physique
description: When you choose this teaching at 3rd level, your hit point maximum increases by 6 points, and it increases by 2 every time you gain a gunslinger level.

3.name: Powder and Iron
description: Also at 3rd level, you have mastered the art of using armor with black powder weapons, gaining the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency with heavy armor and one exotic weapon of your choice.
  • While you are wearing heavy armor, you can use your Constitution modifier in place of your Strength modifier for any Strength requirement the armor has.
  • While you are wearing light or medium armor, you can use your Constitution modifier in place of your Dexterity modifier when determining your Armor Class.

7.name: Strength of Steel
description: At 7th level, you gain proficiency in the Athletics skill. If you already have it, you gain proficiency in your choice of Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Medicine, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

In addition, your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks you make using your Athletics proficiency, and you can use your Constitution modifier in place of your Strength modifier for such ability checks.

10.name: Unyielding Devotion
description: Starting at 10th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can instead drop to a number of hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Once you use this feature you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

15.name: Living Fortress
description: Starting at 15th level, you can reduce all damage you take by an amount equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
In addition, allies of your size or smaller may use you to gain the benefits of three-quarters cover.

18.name: Steelskin
description: At 18th level, you know how to set your body to resist even the biggest of hits.  Any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit.

subclasses.name: Juggernaut Teaching

description: All gunslingers make use of firearms, but you have dedicated your life to the development of a one-of-a-kind weapon of war, the Bespoke Firearm. Marked by this signature weapon, you enter the fray with the swagger and guile only found in one kind of gunslinger, the Gunsmith.

3.name: Bespoke Firearm
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have crafted for yourself a unique, specialized firearm. At the end of a long rest, you can use tinker's tools to transform a firearm into a Bespoke Firearm. A crank gun, machine gun, or hand-cannon cannot be made into a Bespoke Firearm. You can only have one Bespoke Firearm at a time. Creating another Bespoke Firearm renders the special properties of the first inert.

Your Bespoke Firearm is modular so you can adjust it to best meet the challenges at hand. You learn two of these Upgrades. When you gain a Gunslinger level you can replace one Upgrade you know with another Upgrade of your choice.
Over the course of 10 minutes, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use tinker's tools to modify your Bespoke Firearm with the benefits of one Upgrade you know.
You learn one additional Upgrade of your choice when you reach 7th level, and again at 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

7.name: Advanced Tinker
description: At 7th level, you have done research to adopt more peculiar ideas for your prototype designs and combat style. You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice from Arcana, History, Nature, Religion, and Society.
Additionally, you can use your tinker's tools to replicate the effects of the Mending cantrip.
Finally, your Bespoke Firearm can be modified with two Upgrades at one time.

10.name: Overcharge
description: At 10th level, you can fire a shot from your Bespoke Firearm with additional black powder. When you make an attack with your Bespoke Firearm attack, you can cause that attack to deal bonus piercing damage to the target. This bonus piercing damage is equal to two rolls of your exploit die.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Quickdraw
description: Starting at 15th level, you always seem to shoot first. When you roll initiative, so long as you are not surprised, you can make a single attack with your Bespoke Firearm before any other creatures act.
Additionally, your Bespoke Firearm can be modified with three Upgrades at one time.
Finally, you can craft two one-handed firearms or one two-handed firearm into your Bespoke Firearm. If you choose to craft two one-handed Bespoke Firearms, they share all of the same Upgrades.

18.name: Magnum Opus
description: By 18th level, you have forged your Bespoke Firearm into a masterfully crafted weapon.  It can be modified with four Upgrades at one time, and you can swap out Upgrades over the course of 1 minute.
Additionally, attacks with your Bespoke Firearm score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

subclasses.name: Gunsmith Teaching

description: Gunslingers known as Hunters focus on hunting down information, objects, and most often, other creatures. Rivaling the great hunters of the wilderness, these gunslingers leverage their wondrous Seeking Sights in the pursuit of their current quarry.

3.name: Seeking Sight
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have crafted a wondrous creation to aid you in pursuing our foes. When wearing this object, most often over one or both eyes, you can use a bonus action to place an arcane Mark on a creature or object that you can see within 60 feet. The Mark grants you the following benefits against the Marked target:

• Whenever you make a Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Survival) check related to it you gain a bonus to the roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).
  • You always know the direction and distance to the target so long as you are on the same plane of existence.
  • You can add your Intelligence modifier to damage rolls against the target.

This Mark lasts for 1 hour, but ends early when you Mark another target or if you use your bonus action to end it. If the Mark is slain, you can use a reaction to Mark another target of your choice that you can see within range of this feature.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses each time you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can expend an exploit die to use this feature again.

3.name: Restraints
description: Also at 3rd level, you are adept at capturing your opponents alive. Once per turn when you hit your Mark with a weapon attack, you can force the target to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target is restrained, and your Mark instantly ends.

As an action, the target, or another creature within 5 feet of it, can make a Strength check against your Exploit save DC, ending the restrained condition on your target on a success. This condition also ends if the target takes any damage.

7.name: Enhanced Sight
description: By 7th level, your Seeking Sight grants you insights into the targets that you Mark. When you Mark a target you instantly learn one of the following characteristics of your choice: its highest ability score, lowest ability score, Armor Class, speed, creature type, or one special sense.

10.name: Defensive Maneuvers
description: At 10th level, your analysis of your chosen foe allows you to better defend yourself against them. You gain the following new reactions:

• When your Mark targets you with an attack that you can see, you can use your reaction to add your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class against that attack.
  • If you Mark misses you with a melee attack you can use your reaction to force it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Exploit save DC. On a failed save, it is knocked prone or grappled by you (your choice). You must have a free hand in order to grapple the target with this feature.

15.name: Predictive Instincts
description: Starting at 15th level, your sharp mind allows you to predict the actions of your enemies. Your Mark has disadvantage on any attack roll that it makes against you, and it has disadvantage on the first saving throw you force it to make on each of your turns.

18.name: Master Hunter
description: At 18th level, you can strike the most evasive of enemies, even those hiding behind obscured visibility or magical protection. Your attack rolls against your Mark cannot have disadvantage. You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't both blinded and deafened.

subclasses.name: Hunter Teaching

description: Marshalls are gunslingers with particular leadership expertise.  With their knowledge of the mechanics of battle, marshalls lead their compatriots to victory, but also know when it is time to fall back and regroup.

3.name: Leadership Style
description: At 3rd level, you choose a Leadership Style from the options below. Each choice determines the ability score you will use for your Leadership modifier:

traits.name: Strategist
description: You guide others with cunning and wit. You use Intelligence as your Leadership modifier.

traits.name: Mentor
description: You counsel others with wise insights. You use Wisdom as your Leadership modifier.

traits.name: Captain
description: You lead from the front with presence. You use Charisma as your Leadership modifier.

3.name: Tactical Exploits
description: You learn two Exploits of your choice from the list of Tactical Exploits.  You learn two additional tactical exploits at 7th level and again at 15th level.

3.name: Lead From the Front
description: You lead your companions from the front lines, fighting side by side with them. At 3rd level, you learn the Commander's Presence Exploit, and whenever you use it, you can roll a d4 in place of expending an Exploit Die.

7.name: Hold Fast
description: Your sheer determination serves to inspire your allies to fight on. Beginning at 7th level, when you use Nimble Escape, you can choose three creatures within 30 feet that can see or hear you to regain hit points equal to your Exploit Die + your proficiency bonus.

10.name: Heroic Charge
description: Beginning at 10th level, when you use Adrenaline Rush, choose a creature within 30 feet that can see or hear you. The creature can use its reaction to move its speed, without provoking any opportunity attacks, then it can make a single weapon attack.

15.name: Inspiring Presence
description: Your presence and leadership inspires an unshakeable loyalty in your companions to you. Beginning at 15th level, you and creatures within 10 feet of you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or against effects that would force you to act against your will.
At 18th level, the range of this feature increases to 30 feet.

18.name: Marshall's Fervor
description: Your ability to inspire others and lead allies into battle leads anyone to fight beyond their normal limits. Starting at 18th level, your Heroic Charge can affect up to two creatures of your choice within 30 feet that can see or hear you.

subclasses.name: Marshall Teaching

description: Medics are those who keep their allies alive and fighting. Armed with medicine and bandages they treat their friends' wounds in the midst of the battlefield while defending them from the enemy onslaught.

3.name: Field Medic
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have been trained in administering first aid in the midst of battle. You are gain proficiency in the Medicine skill if you don't already have it.

In addition, you gain the ability to heal a creature quickly in a pinch. As an action, you can touch a willing creature within 5 feet of you. The target regains hit points equal to a roll of your Exploit Die plus your Wisdom modifier.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

3.name: Close Quarters Training
description: Also at 3rd level, you have received extensive training in fighting at small distances. When you are wielding a ranged weapon, you do not suffer disadvantage as a result of being within 5 feet of a hostile creature.
In addition, when you make an opportunity attack, you can make a ranged weapon attack against the target.

7.name: Defend the Wounded
description: At 7th level, your devotion to the wounded gives you clarity in battle. When you use your Field Medic feature, you gain advantage on attack rolls until the end of your next turn.

10.name: Field Surgeon
description: Starting at 10th level, your experience in field medicine has built upon your knowledge. When you use your Field Medic feature, you can expend a number of uses up to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down), adding a roll of your Exploit Die to the healing for each use expended past the first.

15.name: Doctor's Fury
description: Starting at 15th level, while you benefit from advantage from your Defend the Wounded feature, each of your attacks deal extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.
In addition, if you use your Field Medic feature, you can make a ranged weapon attack as a bonus action.

18.name: Field Hospital
description: Starting at 18th level, you maximize your training and experience for the treatment of the injured. You gain the following benefits:

• You double your proficiency bonus for checks made with your Medicine proficiency.
  • When you use your Field Medic feature, you can add your proficiency bonus to the amount of hit points you restore.
  • You can expend a use of your Field Medic feature to end one disease or condition affecting the target instead of restoring hit points.

subclasses.name: Medic Teaching

description: Renegades are the most versatile of gunslingers.  Often considered a one-man army, they are masters of infiltration, assassination, and succeeding where others cannot through use of superior firepower and advanced training for nearly any situation.

3.name: Elite Fitness
description: When you choose this teaching at 3rd level, your hit point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 every time you gain a gunslinger level.
In addition, you are immune to disease.

3.name: Overwhelming Force
description: Also starting at 3rd level, once per turn when you hit a creature with a finesse or ranged weapon attack, you can deal a bonus 1d8 damage, so long as one of the following conditions are met:

• You are grappling the target.
  • You have advantage on your attack roll.
  • An enemy of your target (other than you) is within 5 feet of your target, and the other enemy isn't incapacitated.
You don't gain the benefits feature if you have disadvantage on your attack roll, even if the other conditions are met.
This bonus damage increases to 2d8 at 7th level, 3d8 at 10th, 4d8 at 15th, and 5d8 at 18th level.

7.name: Art of War
description: Starting at 7th level, you can use your Dexterity modifier, instead of Strength, for attack and damage rolls with all weapons that lack the Heavy property, as though they had the Finesse property.

10.name: Ambush
description: Starting at 10th level, you have mastered how to set up an effective ambush to surprise your enemies. You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in the combat yet.
In addition, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.

15.name: Hail of Shots
description: Starting at 15th level, you can fire a rapid stream of ranged attacks. You can use your action to make a number of ranged weapon attacks equal to your proficiency bonus.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

18.name: Last Stand
description: Starting at 18th level, when you know death is coming for you, you make one heroic last stand against your foes. When you are reduced to 0 hit points, but not killed outright, you can use your reaction to immediately take one extra turn, interrupting the current turn, during which none of the actions you take can heal you in any way. On this extra turn, you have advantage on all attack rolls. When the extra turn ends, you fall unconscious as normal.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Renegade Teaching

description: The sharpshooter teaching teaches stealth, precision, and accuracy.  Your strikes shouldn't be noticed, and they should come from far away to strike your enemies with unerring accuracy.  Sharpshooters are often cold, calculating, no-nonsense gunslingers who get their jobs done but don't have time for friends on the battlefield.

3.name: Long Range Training
description: By 3rd level, you have trained extensively at extremely long ranges, granting you the following benefits:

• You do not suffer disadvantage when making ranged attacks from a prone position.
  • While behind cover, you add your proficiency bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

3.name: Covering Fire
description: Also at 3rd level, you use your position to cover your allies.  While you are behind cover, when a creature you can see that is within the normal range of a ranged weapon you are holding attacks a friendly creature, you can use your reaction to make a ranged weapon attack against the attacker.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

7.name: Aim for the Heart
description: At 7th level, you are adept at finding weak points in the defenses of your targets.  Your ranged weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
At 18th level, your ranged weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

10.name: Expert Sharpshooter
description: At 10th level, you have perfected your ability to find the best place to set up for covering allies, granting you the following benefits:

• You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while behind cover.
  • Your ranged weapon attacks ignore the benefits of half cover.
  • As a bonus action, you give yourself advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this bonus action only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use the bonus action, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

15.name: Rapid Reload
description: At 15th level, you can ignore the loading propery of ranged weapons with which you are proficient, and you can reload any kind of firearm as an object interaction on your turn.

subclasses.name: Sharpshooter Teaching

description: Spies are gunslingers trained in stealth and magic.  Making use of arcane magic to hide themselves and go unnoticed, they are known to be able to sneak into anywhere.  Typically mysterious, spies eschew the company of people, preferring the company of machines.

3.name: Spellcasting
description: Starting at 3rd level, you've studied the workings of magic and how to cast spells, channeling the magic through objects. To observers, you don't appear to be casting spells in a conventional way; your spells manifest as various gadgets and items that you use.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Invention spell list. You learn an additional Invention cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
