description: The Spy Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You know three 1st level Invention spells of your choice. The Spells Known column of the Spy Spellcasting table shows when you can learn more Invention spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be an Evocation or Illusion spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the Invention spells you know with another spell of your choice from the Invention spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Invention spells, since you learn your spells through study and memorization.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

3.name: Espionage
description: Also at 3rd level, you are heavily trained in sneaking in and out of places and taking things from them unseen. You gain proficiency in the Stealth or Sleight of Hand skill (your choice).

You also craft a small drone to assist you in your endeavors. You determine the drone's appearance. The drone acts as a familliar that is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See this creature's game statistics in the Spy Drone stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

In combat, the drone shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the drone can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

The drone regains 2d6 hit points if the Mending spell is cast on it. If it has died within the last hour, you can use an action to revive it, provided you are within 5 feet of it and you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The drone returns to life after 1 minute with all its hit points restored.
At the end of a long rest, you can create a new droneu. If you already have a drone from this feature, the first one immediately perishes. The drone also perishes if you die.

Spy Drone
Tiny construct
Armor Class 12
Hit Points your Intelligence modifier + your gunslinger level
Speed 30 ft., fly 30 ft. (hover)
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
4 (-3)15 (+2)10 (0)10 (0)12 (+1)7 (-2)
Saving Throws: DEX +2 plus PB
Skills: Perception +1 plus PB x 2, Stealth +2 plus PB
Damage Immunities: poison, psychic
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 11 + (PB x 2)
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Flyby. The spy drone doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.
Keen Sensors. The spy drone has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or sight.
Relay Senses. As an action, you can see through your drone's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses that the drone has. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses.
Actions
Force Strike. Ranged Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, range 30 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d4 + PB force damage.

7.name: Stolen Secrets
description: At 7th level, you steal the secrets to crafting an upgrade to a piece of gear and how to cast some of your magic faster. You learn one Infusion available to artificers. Any time an infusion refers to your artificer level, use your gunslinger level instead.
You learn a second infusion of your choice at 18th level. You can replace either of these infusions with a different one that you meet the requirements for whenever you gain a gunslinger level.
In addition, when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can cast a cantrip in place of one of your attacks.

10.name: Master of the Shadows
description: At 10th level, you have mastered the ability to hide in and strike from the shadows. When in dim light or darkness you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and can hide when only lightly obscured or in dim light.
In addition, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

15.name: Master Spy
description: Starting at 15th level, you double your proficiency bonus for checks made with the skill chosen from your Espionage feature.
In addition, your drone gains the following additional benfits:

• As long as you are with 100 feet of your drone, you can cause your spells to originate from the drone instead of you.
  • The drone can see normally in heavily obscured areas and magical darkness.
  • If the drone is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails. It can't use this trait if it's incapacitated.

18.name: Arcane Agent
description: Starting at 18th level, when you take the Attack action on your turn, you can cast an Invention spell in place of one of your weapon attacks.

subclasses.name: Spy Teaching

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Apocalyptic
description: Starting at 1st level, you know Apocalyptic, the secret language of harbingers. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without magic.

1.name: Spellcasting
description: Drawing on the power of nature's wrath, you can cast spells that bend this primal force to your bidding.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the Primal spell list. You learn additional Primal cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Harbinger table.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Harbinger table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Primal spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these Primal spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Primal spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the Primal spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Primal spells equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + your harbinger level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can also change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Primal spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Primal spells, since your magic draws from primal forces.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a primal focus as a spellcasting focus for your Primal spells.

2.name: Entropic Attunement
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can call upon your special connection to entropy and the primordial forces of decay that it wields. As an action, you can activate Entropic Attunement. When you do so, choose two of the following magical options; you can choose the same option more than once.

On subsequent turns, you can use an action to use one of these options again. You have access to these options for 1 minute. Once this time passes, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.
While Entropic Attunement is active, you can expend a spell slot as an action to extend its duration by a number of minutes equal to the level of the spell slot expended.
At 5th level, you can use three options instead of two when you activate this feature, and two options instead of one as an action on one of your subsequent turns before Entropic Attunement ends.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Dark Void
description: You manifest the void at the end of it all in a 10-foot-cube area within 30 feet of you.  The area is shrouded in darkness until the start of your next turn.  A creature with darkvision can't see through this darkness, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.
If any of this effect's area overlaps with an area of light created by a spell of a level equal to or lower than your proficiency bonus, the spell that created the light is dispelled.

subFeatures.name: Destructive Wrath
description: You manifest the sheer destruction of a natural calamity, targeting a creature within 60 feet of you. It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take damage equal to your Harbinger level.
The damage type of this effect is determined by your Entropic Focus.

subFeatures.name: Entropy Shield
description: You create an aura of entropy around a creature within 60 feet of you, rapidly withering any magic or object that tries to come close to them.  The target gains a bonus to their Armor Class and saving throws they make until the start of your next turn.  This bonus equals your proficiency bonus.

subFeatures.name: Inescapable Doom
description: You manifest the inescapable nature of death, binding a creature with spectral chains that is within 60 feet of you and no more than 10 feet away from a solid surface, using your spell attack modifier to make a grapple attack.  On a success, the target is restrained until the start of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Rift to the End
description: You create a rift in the fabric of space-time into the endless, passionless void beyond at a point within 30 feet of you.  It is 5 feet wide and 15 feet long.  If a creature is standing in a space where the rift is torn, they are moved to the nearest unoccupied space.

Each 5-foot-cube section of the rift can be attacked and destroyed (AC equal to you spell save DC, 15 hp, vulnerability to radiant, resistance to necrotic and psychic damage; immunity to nonmagical damage).  A creature that touches the rift for the first time on a turn or starts their turn touching it takes necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
When you use Rift to the End, you can choose to target an existing rift to make it grow 5 feet wider or 15 feet longer.

subFeatures.name: Arcane Hunger (Requires 4th Level)
description: You manifest the end of all magic, creating a temporary field in yourself that draws in and devours arcane energies.  Until the start of your next turn, you gain the following benefits:

• Spellcasters within 30 feet of you must include you as at least one of the targets of each of their spells.
  • Spell attack rolls made against you are made at disadvantage.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
  • You have resistance to damage dealt by spells and other magical effects.

subFeatures.name: Repear's Assurance (Requires 8th Level)
description: You manifest the reaper itself to inch your enemies closer to death.  Creatures within 30 feet of you of your choice that do not have all of their hit points must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.  On a failed save, a creature has its maximum hit points reduced to an amount equal to its current hit points until they finish a long rest.

18.name: Living Inevitable
description: Starting at 18th level, the entropy of your magic is impossible to resist. Any spells or effects granted by your entropic focus ignore resistance to damage.

20.name: Apocalypse
description: At 20th level, you can use an option from Entropic Attunement as an action on any of your turns without needing it to be active and you can use your Entropic Attunement an unlimited number of times.
Blizzard harbingers control the chilled magics of snow and ice. Their magic can freeze their enemies solid. Blizzard harbingers are cold, calculating, and very unpersonable.

2.name: Icy Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals cold damage.

2.name: Arctic Wind
description: Starting at 2nd level, the winds of the north swirl within and around you.  As an action, you can blast a wind of sheer cold in a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide for the next minute.  The wind moves with you, and you can change the direction it blows as a bonus action on your turn.  You must concentrate on this effect as if concentrating on a spell.
Creatures within the wind have disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution ability checks, as well as on saving throws made to maintain concentration on a spell.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

2.name: Icy Countentance
description: Also at 2nd level, your body takes on some traits of ice and snow.  Your skin could be unnaturally pale and cool to the touch, your eyes could be milky white, or your hair could appear perpetually frozen.
In addition, you gain resistance to cold damage.

6.name: Gale Force
description: Starting at 6th level, the speed of the ice-cold wind you can summon increases significantly. Ranged attacks that target a point within or pass through your wind are made at disadvantage.

10.name: Glacial Tomb
description: Starting at 10th level, you can preserve creatures in a glacier-like form of ice.  As an action, you can target a creature or corpse within your wind.  The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.

On a failed save, a target becomes encased in a thick layer of magical ice until another creature uses an action to shatter the casing.  A willing creature can choose to fail the save, and a corpse fails the save automatically.  While a creature is encased, they have total cover and are considered petrified.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14.name: Frozen Solid
description: Starting at 14th level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with cold damage, you freeze the target solid into a statue of ice that radiates cold for the next minute, upon which time the statue thaws.
Creatures within 10 feet of an ice statue have disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution ability checks, as well as on saving throws made to maintain concentration on a spell.
Additionally, you can use your Arctic Wind feature an unlimited number of times.

subclasses.name: Blizzard Focus

description: The cosmos inspire wonders in humanity, but also terror. Any number of cosmic horrors and astronomical anomalies prowl the cosmos, things that could destroy humanity in an instant if they so desired. Some harbingers, instead of avoiding this topic, choose to study it instead.

2.name: Cosmic Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals psychic or radiant damage (your choice).

2.name: Cosmic Horror
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can manifest the horrors of the cosmos within yourself.  As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Entropic Attunement feature to undergo a transformation, twisting your flesh into a horrifying form and gaining the following benefits for the next minute:

• Your creature type changes to Aberration.
  • You have advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks and disadvantage on all other Charisma checks.
  • You have resistance to psychic damage.
  • Once per turn, when you deal psychic or radiant damage with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you until the start of your next turn.

2.name: Nebulous Aura
description: Also at 2nd level, you exude an aura of astral energies that appears as a nebula to outside viewers.  The area within 15 feet of you is considered lightly obscured to creatures of your choice, and can't be targeted by divination spells unless you allow it.

6.name: Galactic Aura
description: At 6th level, your nebulous aura grows into a galaxy.  Its range increases to 30 feet, and creatures of your choice within your aura can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action.

10.name: Maddening Horror
description: Starting at 10th level, your horrifying magic can cause madness simply by its existence.  While a creature is frightened of you as a result of your Cosmic Horror feature, they also suffer a random form of madness from the table below.

d8Effect
1The creature cannot speak or cast spells that have verbal components.
2The creature takes 1d8 psychic damage at the start of each of its turns.
3The creature is disoriented. It immediately falls prone and falls prone again at the end of each turn it moves 5 feet or more.
4The creature is distracted by visions and voices and has disadvantage on attack rolls and Wisdom (Perception) ability checks.
5The creature is unsure of itself. It can move or take an action on its turn but not both and it cannot use reactions.
6The creature is reckless. It has advantage on attack rolls and attack rolls against it have advantage.
7The creature is deafened and cannot see objects or creatures further than 30 feet away.
8The creature is charmed by you.
Additionally, if a creature remains frightened of you as a result of your Cosmic Horror feature for 1 minute or more, they suffer a random form of indefinite madness.

14.name: Twisted Wings
description: Starting at 14th level, you sprout mangled wings while in your Cosmic Horror form, granting you a flying speed equal to your walking speed and the ability to hover.

subclasses.name: Cosmological Focus

description: Among all harbingers, those of the disease focus are the most mysterious and unpersonable. Their magic is by far the most devastating, able to easily wipe out entire cities or even nations, even if it wouldn't seem as so at first glance.

2.name: Diseased Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals necrotic or poison damage (your choice).

2.name: Curse of Pestilence
description: Starting at 2nd level, your body becomes a vector for all manner of death, disease, and decay. Whenever you deal damage to a creature, you can curse it for 1 minute, causing flies to swarm forth from its wounds.
Whenever the cursed creature takes damage, it takes additional necrotic damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of 1).

2.name: Diseased Body
description: Also at 2nd level, the diseases spread through your body and soul grant you insights into disease and decay, represented by the following benefits:

• You are immune to disease.
  • You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being poisoned.
  • You have proficiency in the Medicine skill.

6.name: Incurable
description: Starting at 6th level, when you deal necrotic or poison damage to a creature, they cannot regain hit points until the start of your next turn.

6.name: Cursed Contagion
description: Also at 6th level, whenever a creature afflicted by your Curse of Pestilence is reduced to 0 hit points or dies, you can use your reaction to cause each creature of your choice within 20 feet of the target to become afflicted by your Curse of Pestilence.

10.name: Epidemic
description: Starting at 10th level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with necrotic or poison damage, you can immediately deal necrotic damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier to another creature within 10 feet of the target.  If you reduce this new target to 0 hit points as well, you can use this feature again as many times as you can keep reducing your targets to 0 hit points.

10.name: Greater Curse of Pestilence
description: Also at 10th level, at the start of each of your turns, you gain 5 temporary hit points for each creature within 30 feet of you that is afflicted with your Curse of Pestilence.

14.name: Become the Plague
description: At 14th level, the diseases are spread so far through your body and soul that you are more disease than harbinger, gaining the following benefits:

• You have immunity to poison damage and resistance to necrotic damage.
  • You can't be blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, or poisoned.
  • Your ability scores and hit point maximum can't be reduced.
  • Any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit.

subclasses.name: Disease Focus

description: Sometimes the gods wipe the world clean, using their divine power to destroy so that a new civilization can rise. Harbingers of this focus serve as arms of the gods' will to carry out their vengeance.

2.name: Divine Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals radiant damage.

2.name: Arm of Divinity
description: Starting at 2nd level, you are chosen as the champion of your god's vengeance.  You gain the following benefits:

• You can speak, read, and write Celestial.
  • You gain proficiency with martial weapons.

2.name: Chosen for Judgement
description: Also at 2nd level, you can use a bonus action to mark a creature you can see within 30 feet of you as the target of your god's judgement. The target is marked for 1 minute. The mark ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the mark ends, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain a bonus to damage rolls against the marked target. The bonus equals your proficiency bonus.
  • Any attack roll you make against the marked target is a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
  • The marked target can't benefit from being invisible or hidden, and you know if they tell a lie.
You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.  When you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can expend a spell slot to use it again.

6.name: Blade of the Gods
description: Starting at 6th level, you can empower your weapons to carry divine energies with them.  When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

If you use this feature on an attack targeting the creature marked by your Chosen for Judgement feature, they must additionally succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the start of your next turn.

10.name: Champion of Light
description: Starting at 10th level, your link to your god allows you to serve as a conduit for radiant energy that fills and emboldens you.  You have resistance to radiant damage and cannot be charmed, dominated, or frightened.

14.name: Divine Avenger
description: At 14th level, you are the manifestation of your god's wrath.  Using a bonus action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• Wings sprout from your back and grant you a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
  • You emanate an aura of menace in a 30-foot radius. When a hostile creature enters your aura for the first time on a turn or starts their turn there, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you for 1 minute or until they take any damage.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Divine Focus

description: Among all methods of apocalypse, none are more iconic than a meteor. Quick, clean, and simple.  These harbingers are the most direct of their kind, preferring to embody this destructive force themselves and bring it to the battlefield in dramatic fashion.

2.name: Meteoric Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals bludgeoning, fire, or thunder damage (your choice).

2.name: Primal Hammer
description: Starting at 2nd level, your magic carries with it the force of a meteor impact.  Once per turn, whenever you hit with a spell attack roll for a spell of 1st level or higher, or a creature fails its saving throw against a spell you cast of 1st level or higher, you can additionally move the target up to 10 feet in any direction or knock them prone.

2.name: Meteoric Magic
description: Also at 2nd level, whenever you would deal damage with a spell, you can choose to deal bludgeoning, fire, or thunder damage instead of the spell's original damage type or types.

6.name: Craterous Impact
description: Starting at 6th level, your magic leaves behind a mark on the battlefield.  When you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher that deals damage, you can choose to empower it with meteoric force.  This modifies the spell differently depending on whether it is targeted or has an area of effect.  For spells that have both targeted and area of effect portions, such as *ice knife*, you choose which effect to use.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.  If a spell has multiple targets or areas of effect, you must expend a use of this feature for each one you wish to affect.

subFeatures.name: Area of Effect
description: In an area with a size 10 feet larger in all dimensions than the spell's original area of effect, the ground is cracked by the magical energy coursing through it, causing it to become difficult terrain.  A 5-foot square of difficult terrain created by this feature can be cleared with one minute of work.

subFeatures.name: Targeted
description: Creatures within 5 feet of the target(s) must make saving throws against the spell, or Dexterity saving throws if the spell involves an attack roll instead, taking damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier on a failed save.  This damage is the same type as the triggering spell.  If the spell deals multiple types of damage, you choose the damage type from among the types the spell deals for each creature.

10.name: Meteoric Mastery
description: Starting at 10th level, you can use your Primal Hammer feature on cantrips as well as spells of 1st level or higher.

14.name: Cataclysmic Impact
description: Starting at 14th level, the meteoric force you can empower your magic with grows to staggering power.  When you use your Craterous Impact feature, the spell gains one of the following additional effects, once again depending on whether it is targeted or has an area of effect.

subFeatures.name: Area of Effect
description: Creatures standing on the affected ground must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone, and flying creatures without the ability to hover in the area of effect must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or begin falling.

subFeatures.name: Targeted
description: The range increases to 10 feet, the damage increases to twice your spellcasting ability modifier, and creatures take half as much damage if they succeed on their saving throws, instead of no damage.

subclasses.name: Meteoric Focus

description: Storms of the sky and sea are part of the oldest legends of the apocalypse. These harbingers can take on the power of these legends, using water, wind, and lightning to destroy their foes.

2.name: Electric Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals lightning or thunder damage (your choice).

2.name: Storm Surge
description: Starting at 2nd level, as a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Entropic Attunement to empower your physiology with the power of the storm, filling your body with the energy of lightning and gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

• Your walking speed increases by 15 feet.
  • You have advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws.
  • Your movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

2.name: Electric Blood
description: Also at 2nd level, your blood is filled with electricity and wild energy that begs to be let loose.  You gain resistance to lightning damage, and whenever you deal lightning damage you can reroll the damage dice once and take the higher total.

6.name: Terrible Tempest
description: Starting at 6th level, even the smallest the winds you summon bear the speed and fury of a storm.  When you cast a spell that involves wind while your Storm Surge is active, the area of effect of the spell is increased by 10 feet in all dimensions, and any forced movement caused by the spell is doubled.

10.name: Cascading Current
description: Starting at 10th level, when you deal lightning damage to a creature with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose to arc the lightning to an additional target within 30 feet of the first target.
The new target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking half as much damage as the original target on a failed save, and one quarter as much damage on a success.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14.name: Perfect Storm
description: Starting at 14th level, you have mastered the wild energy in your blood.  You can use your Storm Surge feature an unlimited number of times, without expending a use of your Entropic Attunement.
Additionally, while your Storm Surge is active, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
Finally, you gain immunity to lightning damage and resistance to thunder damage.

subclasses.name: Storm Focus

description: While most entropic foci entail active causes of the apocalypse, harbingers of the temporal focus study time. The relentless march of time can reduce even the grandest of cities to rubble eventually, and these harbingers are willing to sit back and wait.

2.name: Temporal Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals force, necrotic, or psychic damage (your choice).

2.name: Time Displacement
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can displace creatures and objects through the flow of time.  When a creature makes an attack roll or saving throw within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to roll a d20 and choose whether you want to replace their roll with the number you rolled.  You can make this decision after knowing what the roll is, but before you know if it succeeded or failed.
You can replace rolls a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

2.name: Temporal Awareness
description: Also at 2nd level, you have learned to see echoes of past events in the present. You gain proficiency in History, and whenever you make an Intelligence (History) check while in the location where the subject of your check took place, you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.

6.name: Psychometry
description: Starting at 6th level, you can understand the history of objects. As an action, you can touch an object and learn everything that happened to it within the last seven days. Starting at 14th level, you learn everything that happened to it within the last 30 days.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Split From Time
description: Your use of time magic has caused your physical form to be detached from the normal flow of time. Starting at 6th level, your age cannot be changed by spells or magical effects, and for every 10 years that pass, your physical body only ages 1 year.
At 14th level, you only age 1 year for every 100 years that pass, and at 20th level, your body stops aging completely.
Additionally, you can add your spellcasting ability modifier to your initiative rolls.

10.name: Distant Shift
description: Starting at 10th level, you can displace others further in time.  When you use your Time Displacement feature, you roll two d20s and can decide which d20 to replace the target's roll with.

14.name: Untethered Mind
description: Starting at 14th level, as a bonus action, you can completely untether yourself from the flow of time temporarily.  At the start of your next turn, you snap back to the normal flow of time, with all effects caused since you used this feature reversed, but with the knowledge of what happened still fixed in your mind and your mind only.

You cannot use this feature on two subsequent turns. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

subclasses.name: Temporal Focus

description: Harbingers of the volcanic focus draw upon fiery, volcanic magic. This magic is among the most uncontrollable of the harbinger foci, and unless a harbinger is careful they can easily destroy themselves.

But even as the volcano erupts, it grants its ashes to the soil, making fields fertile and green.  Harbingers of this focus know destruction to be a necessary evil, as they believe that to create you must first destroy.

2.name: Volcanic Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals fire or poison damage (your choice).

2.name: Volcanic Body
description: Starting at 1st level, the heat of a volcano burns within you, and you gain the ability to coat your skin in magma-like armor.  When you aren't wearing armor, your AC is 10 + your Constitution modifier + your spellcasting ability modifier. You can use your natural armor to determine your AC if the armor you wear would leave you with a lower AC. A shield's benefits apply as normal while you use your natural armor.
In addition, you gain resistance to fire damage and you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

6.name: Thermal Furnace
description: Starting at 6th level, your volcanic core heats up as if an entire magma chamber resided inside you.  The area within 10 feet of you is uncomfortably warm. Creatures of your choice within this range must make a Constitution saving throw at the start of each of their turns.  On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 fire damage and is unable to take the Dash or Disengage actions until the start of your next turn.
Additionally, whenever you use your action to cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

10.name: Obsidian Shell
description: Starting at 10th level, the outer layer of your magma armor hardens into volcanic glass.  When you are hit with a melee attack by a creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to deal slashing damage equal to 1d4 + your spellcasting ability modifier to the attacker.

14.name: Erupting Fury
description: At 14th level, you can channel your volcanic core into a mighty eruption as an action, gaining the following benefits for the next minute:

• The damage of your Thermal Furnace feature increases to 2d10, and creatures who fail their saving throws are additionally unable to make more than one attack when they take the Attack action.
  • Your Obsidian Shell feature deals fire damage equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier, and does not require your reaction to activate.
  • You are immune to fire damage, and have resistance to cold damage.
  • Metal objects within 10 feet of you are heated up to uncomfortable levels. Creatures holding metal weapons or wearing metal armor make attacks at disadvantage.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Volcanic Focus

description: The natural world has its plagues and its disasters, but few things cause as much damage as the ravages of man.  War and conflict are issues as ancient as the world, and leave death and destruction wherever they go.  Harbingers who channel the entropic energies left behind by war find themselves physically empowered, able to perform great feats of martial skill.

Some of these harbingers are warmongers themselves, but most are deeply scarred by the tragedies of war.  They absorb its energies in the hope that they can put a stop to conflict whenever they find it.

2.name: Warrior's Wrath
description: Your Destructive Wrath option for your Entropic Attunement feature deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage (your choice).

2.name: War Exploits
description: Starting at 2nd level, the entropic energies of combat empower your martial capabilities. At 3rd level, you gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Martial Exploits
description: You learn two Exploits of your choice from the list of Martial Exploits. You can only use one Exploit per ability check or attack. When you gain a level, you can replace an Exploit you know with another of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: You have two d4 Exploit Dice. To use an Exploit you must expend one of these dice, and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: Some of your Exploits require your target to make a saving throw to resist your Tactical Exploit's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

2.name: Warrior Spirits
description: Also starting at 2nd level, you can summon forth the spirits of warriors from past battles.  The spirits' game statistics are found in the Spirit Warrior stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus in multiple places.

In combat, the spirits act during your turn. They can move and use their reactions on their own, but they only use the Dodge action on their turns unless you use your bonus action to order them to take an action in their stat block, or another action. If you are incapacitated, the spirits do not act.

At the end of a long rest, you can summon a number of spirits equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down, minimum of one).  When you do so, any previously summoned spirits disappear.  When you summon a spirit, you must choose if it is a Soldier or Archer spirit, which determines which stat block you use.

6.name: Spiritual Commander
description: Starting at 6th level, whenever you use your action to cast a spell of 1st level or higher or to use an exploit, each of your spirits can make one attack as part of the action.

10.name: Empowered Spirits
description: Starting at 10th level, the spirits you can draw from the past grow stronger.  When they take the Attack action, they can make two attacks.  In addition, each gains an additional special action.  You can command a spirit to take this special action a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14.name: Warmaster
description: Starting at 14th level, once per turn when a spirit uses an exploit of 1st- or 2nd-degree, you can choose to not expend an exploit die and instead use a d4 as your exploit die.

subclasses.name: War Focus

proficiencies.toolsDB: Tinker's Tools and one other tool

1.name: Infusions
description: You have learned to imbue objects with your signature brand of magic in order to produce wondrous items. At 1st level, you learn two Infusions of your choice from the list at the end of this class. The Infusions Known column of the Inventor table shows when you learn more Infusions of your choice.
At the end of a long rest, as long as you have tinker's tools, you can replace one Infusion you know with another Infusion of your choice, so long as you meet all of its prerequisites.

subFeatures.name: Infusing an Object
description: Over the course of a long rest, you can use your tinker's tools to imbue an Infusion you know into a nonmagical object. To do so, you must be able to touch the object with your tools.

If the Infusion requires attunement, you can attune to the object the instant you infuse it, or you can forgo attunement so another creature can attune to it. To attune to the infused item later, you must follow the normal attunement process.

The Infusion remains in an item indefinitely. If you die, the Infusion vanishes after a number of days have passed equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 day). Infusions vanish immediately if you give up your knowledge of one to learn another or imbue the Infusion into another object.

You can infuse multiple objects at the end of each long rest, up to one for each Infusion you know. Each Infusion can be in only one object at a time, and no object can bear more than one Infusion. If you transfer an Infusion to a new object, any previous instance of that Infusion immediately ends.

subFeatures.name: Infusing Ability
description: If one of your infusions allows the user to make a spell attack roll or forces a creature to make a saving throw, the infusion save DC and infusion attack modifier are calculated as follows:
Infusion save DC = 8 + your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus
Infusion attack modifier =your Intelligence modifier + your proficiency bonus

subFeatures.name: Replicate Magic Item
description: You can also use your Infusions to replicate magic items that you have studied. Over the course of a long rest, you can use tinker's tools to examine a magic item you can touch. At the end of that long rest, you can replace one of your Infusions Known with the knowledge of this magic item. After which, you can infuse an object with the properties of that magic item, following all the rules for your other Infusions.

You can use this feature to replicate any item of Common rarity. As you gain Inventor levels you can use this feature to replicate items of increasing rarity: Uncommon at 5th level, Rare at 9th level, and finally Very Rare items at 13th level.

2.name: Spellcasting
description: At 2nd level, you can use your tools and your signature brand of magic to produce strange and wondrous spell effects from objects and tools that you imbue with arcane power.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: At 2nd level, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Invention spell list. You learn an additional Invention cantrip of your choice when you reach 4th level and again at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Inventor table shows how many spell slots you have to cast spells of 1st-level and higher. To cast one of your spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all of your expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Invention spell list. The Spells Known column of the Inventor table shows when you learn more Invention spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
When you gain a level, you can replace one of your Invention spells with another spell for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence is the spellcasting ability for your Invention spells, as you use your knowledge of the arcane to cast spells.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

subFeatures.name: Ritual Casting
description: You can cast any Invention spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You must use either your tinker's tools, a set of artisan's tools with which you are proficient, or an item bearing one of your Infusions as the spellcasting focus for your Invention spells.

While you have access to your tinker's tools, you know both the mending cantrip and identify, but they don't count against your number of Spells Known. You can use your tinker's tools to cast identify by spending a spell slot, or as a ritual spell.

6.name: Adjustable Inventions
description: Beginning at 6th level, you can alter your Infusions on the fly. Over the course of a short rest, you can use tinker's tools to replace one of your Infusions Known with another Infusion of your choice or to learn to replicate one magic item you can touch. At the end of the short rest, you can imbue your new Infusion in an object you touch. If it requires attunement, you can follow the normal rules for attuning to your Infusions.

6.name: Tool Expertise
description: There are few who can match an inventor's innate talent with their tools of choice.  Starting at 6th level, whenever you make an ability check that uses a tool with which you are proficient, you can add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.

7.name: Flash of Genius
description: Beginning at 7th level, your analytical mind can offer potent insights and suggestions at a moment's notice. As a reaction, when you, or another creature you can see within 30 feet, makes an ability check or a saving throw, you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the result of the roll.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

10.name: Magic Item Mastery
description: You have gained a deep understanding of the inner workings and creation of magic items.  Beginning at 10th level, you can attune to up to four magic items at once, and for you, crafting a magic item with a rarity of common or uncommon takes a quarter of the normal time and costs half the normal gold. When you reach 20th level, this bonus also applies to rare and very rare magic items.
The number of magic items you can attune to at one time increases at 14th level (5 items) and at 18th level (6 items).
Finally, for you, crafting a magic item with a rarity of Common or Uncommon takes a quarter of the normal time. When you reach 20th level, this bonus also applies to Rare and Very Rare magic items.

11.name: Arcane Breakthrough
description: Beginning at 11th level, your expert understanding of magic items allow you to attune to and use any magic item regardless of any alignment, class, race, spell, or level requirements.

20.name: Soul of Artifice
description: You imbue a spark of your own essence in the magic items you bear. At 20th level, you gain a +1 bonus to all saving throws for each magic item you are attuned to. In addition, if you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can choose to end your attunement to one magic item or infusion, causing you to drop to 1 hit point instead of 0.
Moreover, if you are killed, any object that bears one of your infusions counts as part of your body for the purposes of any spell that would bring you back to life.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

The most dangerous Specialization an inventor can pursue is that of the Aeronaut. Constantly carrying out dangerous trials in their pursuit of mechanical flight, these pioneering minds will risk anything to complete the perfect flying machine. No setback or injury can dampen the spirits of a true Aeronaut.
subclasses.name: Aeronaut Specialization

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with weaver's tools. If you are already proficient with weaver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Aeronaut's Harness
description: When you adopt this Specialization at 1st level, you craft for yourself the signature safety harness of an Aeronaut. You learn the Skyfall Harness Infusion, it doesn't count against your total number of  Infusions Known, and you can ignore its level prerequisite.
However, until you reach 5th level in this class, only you can don the skyfall harness you create with this Infusion. For all other creatures, this Infusion fails to function.

subFeatures.name: Skyfall Harness
description: Item: a cloak, vest, or harness
This magic harness automatically sizes to fit the wearer and can be worn over clothing or light armor. It has wing-like fins between its limbs that slow falls and allow wearers to glide.
When the wearer falls and isn't incapacitated, it subtracts up to 100 feet from its fall when calculating falling damage, and it can glide 2 feet horizontally every 1 foot that it falls.

2.name: Specialist Spells
description:
Inventor LevelSpells
2ndFog Cloud, Zephyr Strike
5thDust Devil, Warding Wind
9thFly, Wind Wall
13thAero Barrage, Suffocate
17thControl Winds, Tornado

3.name: Flying Machine
description: By 3rd level, you have constructed the signature invention of an Aeronaut, the Flying Machine. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use weaver's tools to craft a Flying Machine. Some Flying Machines include wings made of canvas, rotating blades, or even elemental engines. You can only maintain one Flying Machine, and creating a second one causes the magic of any others to dispel.

Your Flying Machine can only be used by you and can be attached to your skyfall harness. While you wear your Flying Machine, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for spells. It also grants you a flying speed of 20 feet, and you can hover.
At certain Inventor levels, this flying speed increases: at 5th level (30 feet), at 9th level (40 feet), and at 15th level (60 feet).

5.name: Airborne Assault
description: At 5th level, your Flying Machine allows you to attack foes from unorthodox positions and catch enemies unaware. When you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground, your attacks deal an additional 1d8 bonus damage on hit.
At 15th level, this bonus damage becomes 2d8.

9.name: Aerial Maneuvers
description: At 9th level, you have greatly improved the maneuverability of your Flying Machine. While you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground with your Flying Machine, you gain the following benefits:

• You can use your bonus action to Dash.
  • You gain a bonus to your Dexterity ability checks and saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

15.name: Master Aeronaut
description: By 15th level, you have become a master Aeronaut. While you are flying at least 5 feet off the ground in your Flying Machine, and are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed, and only half damage if you fail.

Alchemy is a delicate art, tip the ratio of ingredients too far out of line and the effects could be disastrous. Those that study the magic of arcane potions and brews are known as Alchemists. They are experts at combining exotic reagents to produce a variety of materials and effects. From healing droughts that can mend a wound in moments, to sticky goo that explodes when it comes in contact with open flame. With careful preparation, and a bit of luck, Alchemists are masters of both giving life and leeching it away.
subclasses.name: Alchemist Specialization

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you are already proficient with weaver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of alchemist's supplies of your choice.

1.name: Alchemical Expert
description: Starting at 1st level, you are an expert of all things alchemical.  Over the course of a long rest, you can produce a single Common item that can be crafted with Alchemy without requiring any materials.  This item functions as it normally would, but turns to ash when you finish your next long rest.
At 9th level, you can create a Common or Uncommon item.

3.name: Alchemical Elixirs
description: Beginning at 3rd level, at the end of each long rest, you can use your alchemist's supplies produce an Elixir in an empty flask you touch. At creation, you choose the Elixir's effect from one of the tables below, some of which include your proficiency bonus (PB). The effect of an Elixir is triggered when someone drinks the Elixir for Enhancing Elixirs, or when the Elixir hits a creature for Astringent Elixirs. As a bonus action, a creature can drink a Enhancing Elixir or administer it to a creature within 5 feet. As an attack, a creature can throw an Astringent Elixir at a target within 15 feet, making a thrown improvised weapon attack. You have proficiency with attacks made with your Elixirs. A creature can only be under the effects of one Elixir at a time, and coming under the effects of another immediately ends any other Elixir effects.
Any Elixir you create through this feature lasts until it is used, or until the end of your next long rest.
As an action on your turn, you can expend a spell slot to create an Elixir in an empty flask you touch. You can use the Elixir as part of the same action.
At certain levels in this class, you can make more Elixirs at the end of a long rest: at 6th level (two), and 15th level (three).

subFeatures.name: Astringent Elixirs
description:
ElixirEffect
BlazingThe target takes fire damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is set alight. The target takes an additional 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns while alight. A creature can use an action to extinguish itself or a willing creature within 5 feet of it. This fire does not go out when exposed to water.
CorrosiveThe target takes acid damage equal to 2d4 + PB and has their AC reduced by 1 for 1 minute.
LuminousThe target takes radiant damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is blinded for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Constitution saving throw against your Infusion save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
SappingThe target takes necrotic damage equal to 2d4 + PB and has their hit point maximum reduced by an equal amount until they finish a long rest.
StickyThe target is considered grappled for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Strength saving throw against your Infusion save DC as an action, ending the effect on a success.
ToxicThe target takes poison damage equal to 1d4 + PB and is poisoned for 1 minute. An affected target can make a Constitution saving throw against your Infusion save DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

subFeatures.name: Enhancing Elixirs
description:
ElixirEffect
Alteration The drinker is transformed as if by the Alter Self spell. They determine the effect of the spell, which lasts for 10 minutes.
Boldness The drinker can add 1d4 to any attack rolls and saving throws they make for 1 minute.
Flight The drinker gains a flying speed equal to 5 times your PB in feet for 10 minutes.
Healing The drinker regains a number of hit points equal to PB(d4) + your Intelligence Modifier.
Resilience The drinker gains a bonus to their Armor Class equal to half your PB for 10 minutes.
Swiftness The drinker's speed increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times your PB for 1 hour.

5.name: Alchemical Savant
description: Starting at 5th level, when a spell you cast, one of your Elixirs, or one of your Infusions deals acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage, or restores hit points, you gain a bonus to the damage, or healing, roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

9.name: Restorative Reagents
description: Beginning at 9th level, whenever a creature drinks one of your Enhancing Elixirs, they gain temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier, in addition to the Elixir's effect.
Also, you can cast Lesser Restoration, provided you use your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus.
You can cast the spell in this way a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Master Alchemist
description: By 15th level, you have become a master Alchemist. You gain resistance to acid and poison damage, immunity to the poisoned condition, and you no longer age unless you wish to.
In addition, you can cast both Greater Restoration and Heal, without providing the material component, provided you use your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus.
You can cast each of these spells once with this feature, and you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

For centuries chroniclers have sought the best way to store vast amounts of information. While most were satisfied with scrolls, the Archivists looked for something greater. In their research, they learned to store libraries worth of information in objects, awakening the first Artificial Minds. Working with these wondrous Minds, Archivists wield the limitless power of these arcane intelligences to drive their research forward.
subclasses.name: Archivist Specialization

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies. If you are already proficient with calligrapher's supplies, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you learn to speak, read, and write two langauges of your choice.

1.name: Artificial Mind
description: At 1st level, you learn to awaken mundane objects. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use calligrapher's supplies to awaken an Artificial Mind in a Tiny nonmagical object you touch. While the object is awakened, it is a magical item that requires your attunement.
Should you awaken a second Artificial Mind, any previous Artificial Minds are instantly dispelled. While attuned to the awakened Artificial Mind, you gain the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Skill Proficiencies
description: Depending on the material of the object you awaken, you gain proficiency in two skills of your choice determined by the material your artificial mind is constructed from.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from an animal, such as parchment, leather, or bone.  You can choose from Animal Handling, Insight, Perception, and Survival.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from the earth, such as gems, glass, metal, or stone.  You can choose from Deception, Intimidation, Performance, and Persuasion.
Your artificial mind is made of a material obtained from a plant, such as paper, wood, or vegetable matter.  You can choose from Arcana, History, Nature, and Religion.

subFeatures.name: Information Overload
description: Your Artificial Mind can bombard other minds with psychic information. As an action, you can force a creature you can see within 30 feet to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, it takes 1d8 psychic damage and has disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn.
As you gain inventor levels, the psychic damage increases: at 5th level (2d8), at 11th level (3d8), and at 17th level (4d8).

3.name: Magical Telephony
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can communicate telepathically with any creature carrying one of your infused items within a 1-mile radius. The creature can also respond telepathically.

5.name: Acute Overload
description: At 5th level, the power of your Artificial Mind has increased. Whenever a creature fails its save against Information Overload, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra psychic damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

9.name: Improved Consciousness
description: Starting at 9th level, when you are forced to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration on a spell while you are attuned to your Artificial Mind, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).
Moreover, your Artificial Mind doesn't count against the total number of magical objects you can be attuned to.

15.name: Infoportation
description: By 15th level, you have become a master of Archivist artifice. As an action on your turn, you can transform into pure information and teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 60 feet, or an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a creature or object bearing one of your infusions.

Of all the Specializations that an inventor can pursue, that of the Armorer is the most defensively-minded. With a focus on becoming a bastion of magics and metal, Armorers modify a set of armor to function as their second skin. They focus their signature magic through this armor to unleash potent attacks and generate formidable arcane defenses. An Armorer views their armor as an extension of their body, and as they refine their magical abilities, inventor and armor become one.
subclasses.name: Armorer Specialization

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools. If you are already proficient with blacksmith's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.
In addition, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

1.name: Arcane Gauntlet
description: Starting at 1st level, you can forge for yourself a wondrous weapon of war known as an Arcane Gauntlet. At the end of a long rest, you can use blacksmith's tools to create an Arcane Gauntlet, choosing for it to have one of the following weapons. It is a simple weapon only usable by you, and you use your Intelligence, in place of Strength or Dexterity, for its attack and damage rolls.
You can only have one Arcane Gauntlet at a time. Creating a second causes the magic of the first to immediately dispel.

traits.name: Blaze Gauntlet
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 fire damage.  Additionally, if a target starts its turn grappled by you, it takes 1d6 fire damage.

traits.name: Chain Hook
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 60 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 piercing damage.  Any target hit by your Chain Hook can't move further than 60 feet away from you until they use an action to detach the chain from themselves.

traits.name: Lightning Launcer
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 120 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 lightning damage.  Once per turn, when you hit with an attack with your Lightning Launcher, you can cause it to deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage.

traits.name: Razor Edge
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 slashing damage.  You score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 for attacks with your Razor Edge.

traits.name: Sub-Zero Slammer
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 cold damage.  Any target hit by your Sub-Zero Slammer has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Thunder Fist
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 thunder damage.  Any target hit by your Thunder Fist has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Wrecking Ball
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon with a reach of 10 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage.  If you hit a creature that your size or smaller with your Wrecking Ball, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward yourself.

3.name: Arcane Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, you expand the magic of your Arcane Gauntlet to encompass a full suit of armor. At the end of a long rest, you can use your blacksmith's tools to transform a set of armor into Arcane Armor. This armor incorporates your Arcane Gauntlet, is only usable by you, and while wearing it you gain the following benefits:

• If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, your arcane armor lacks this requirement for you.
  • Your arcane armor attaches to you and can't be removed against your will. It expands to cover your entire body, and functionally replaces any missing limbs or body parts.
  • You can don or doff your arcane armor as an action, and can retract or deploy the helmet as a bonus action.
  • You can use a bonus action to grant yourself temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1).

5.name: Armorer Adept
description: At 5th level, you can use magical armor as Arcane Armor. Though, any innate magical bonuses to Armor Class from magic armor, Infusions, or other features don't stack. You must choose one.
Finally, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Modular Armor
description: Starting at 9th level, your Arcane Armor counts as multiple items for the purpose of your infusions: armor (the chest piece), boots, helmet, and the gauntlets (weapon), and each item can bear one infusion.
Also, your number of Infusions Known increases by 2, but these extra infusions must be applied to your arcane armor.

15.name: Master Armorer
description: By 15th level, you have become a master of Armorer artifice. You gain the benefits listed below while wearing your Arcane Armor:

• You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed.
  • You adjust your Arcane Armor so that you have access to two weapons.
  • Each of your weapons now deal an additional die of damage.

traits.name: Blaze Gauntlet
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 fire damage.  Additionally, if a target starts its turn grappled by you, it takes 1d6 fire damage.

traits.name: Chain Hook
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 60 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 piercing damage.  Any target hit by your Chain Hook can't move further than 60 feet away from you until they use an action to detach the chain from themselves.

traits.name: Lightning Launcer
description: Your gauntlet is a ranged weapon with a range of 120 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d6 lightning damage.  Once per turn, when you hit with an attack with your Lightning Launcher, you can cause it to deal an additional 1d6 lightning damage.

traits.name: Razor Edge
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 slashing damage.  You score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 for attacks with your Razor Edge.

traits.name: Sub-Zero Slammer
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 cold damage.  Any target hit by your Sub-Zero Slammer has its speed reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Thunder Fist
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon.  On a hit, it deals 1d8 thunder damage.  Any target hit by your Thunder Fist has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

traits.name: Wrecking Ball
description: Your gauntlet is a melee weapon with a reach of 10 feet.  On a hit, it deals 1d10 bludgeoning damage.  If you hit a creature that your size or smaller with your Wrecking Ball, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward yourself.

An Artillerist specializes in using magic to hurl energy, projectiles, and explosions on a battlefield. This destructive power is valued by armies in the wars on many different worlds. And when war passes, some members of this specialization seek to build a more peaceful world by using their powers to fight the resurgence of strife.
subclasses.name: Artillerist Specialization

1.name: Tools of the Trade
description: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you are already proficient with woodcarver's tools, you instead gain proficiency with another set of artisan's tools of your choice.

1.name: Arcane Cannon
description: At 1st level, you've learned how to create a magical cannon. Using woodcarver's tools, you can take an action to magically create a Small arcane cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of you. An arcane cannon occupies its space. Once you create a cannon, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or until you expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one cannon at a time and can't create one while your cannon is present.

The cannon is a magical object. It has an AC of 18 and a number of hit points equal to five times your inventor level. It is immune to poison damage and psychic damage. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). If the Mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. It disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points or after 1 hour. You can dismiss it early as an action.

When you create the cannon, you determine its appearance and whether it has legs. You also decide which type it is, choosing from the options on the Arcane Cannons table. On each of your turns, you can take a bonus action to cause the cannon to activate if you are within 60 feet of it. As part of the same bonus action, you can direct the cannon to walk or climb up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space, provided it has legs.

Most cannons require an attack roll or saving throw, for which Intelligence is your ability. Your attack modifier for their effects and your saving throw DC are the same as your Infusion attack modifier and saving throw DC.

CannonEffect
Acid SpitterThe cannon belches acid in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 acid damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The acid instantly dissolves any nonmagical, organic objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
BolterThe cannon fires a simple projectile at high speed. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 120 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes magical piercing damage equal to 2d8 + your Intelligence modifier.
ChainswordThe cannon lashes out with a blade resembling that of a chainsaw. Make a melee attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 magical slashing damage. The cannon deals a critical hit with this attack on a roll of 19 or 20.
FlamethrowerThe cannon shoots flames in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 fire damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The flames ignite any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
Force BallistaThe cannon launches a bolt of magical energy. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 60 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 force damage and is pushed up to 5 feet away from the cannon.
Freeze RayThe cannon fires a bolt of energy that drains away heat. Make a ranged attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 60 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 cold damage and if the target is a creature, its speed is reduced by 10 feet.
Grenade LauncherThe cannon lobs an explosive at a point within 60 feet of it. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 magical bludgeoning damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The explosive deals double damage to objects and structures.
Mental DisruptorThe cannon emits a cloud of confusion-inducing gas. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make an Intelligence saving throw, taking 2d8 psychic damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also stunned until the start of its next turn or until it takes damage.
ProtectorThe cannon emits a burst of positive energy that grants itself and each creature of your choice within 10 feet of it a number of temporary hit points equal to 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier.
Sanguine DrainerThe cannon saps away life energy. Make a melee spell attack, originating from the cannon, at one creature or object within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 necrotic damage and it cannot regain hit points by any means short of the Wish spell until the start of its next turn.
Solar FlareThe cannon shines blinding light in an adjacent 15-foot cone that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 radiant damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also blinded until the end of its next turn.
Tesla CoilThe cannon launches lightning in an adjacent 40-foot long, 5-foot wide line that you designate. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 lightning damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. The lightning ignites any flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried.
Ultrasonic GeneratorThe cannon emits deafening sound. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 thunder damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also deafened until the end of its next turn.
Viral DispenserThe cannon emits a cloud of disease. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d8 poison damage on a failed saving throw and half as much on a successful one. A creature that fails its saving throw is also poisoned until the end of its next turn.

3.name: Spell Cannon
