description: You have become a master of the Order of Sacred Inks, and your celestial tattoos are a direct reflection of divine beauty. At 17th level, you can use an action to assume a celestial form. For the next minute you gain the following benefits:

• Your tattoos manifest angelic wings. You gain a flying speed equal to your movement speed and can hover.
  • When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike you can choose to deal radiant in place of bludgeoning damage.
  • Your attacks deal an additional 1d6 radiant damage on hit.
  • You gain access to all of your Divine Conduit features for the duration, and their Ki Point costs are reduced by 1.
Once you use this feature you must finish a long rest before you can use it again, unless you expend 6 Ki Points to use it.

subclasses.name: Way of the Sacred Inks

description: While most practitioners of martial arts place a high value on honorable conduct and combat, those who follow the Way of Shadow exploit every weakness possible. Assassins, spies, and infiltrators, Shadow monks use darkness to their advantage and strike only when their success is assured.

3.name: Shadow Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Slow Fall
5th Gentling Touch
9th Heavenly Step

3.name: Eyes of Night
description: When you join this Tradition at 3rd level, the darkness itself becomes your ally. You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, it increases by 30 feet. In addition, you have advantage on any Dexterity (Stealth) checks you make while you are in dim light or darkness.

3.name: Shadow Arts
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can draw forth inky tendrils of your shadowy Ki to reproduce the effects of certain spells. As an action, you can cast the following spells without providing a spell slot or their material components: Darkness, Darkvision, Pass Without Trace, or Silence. You can see through magical darkness produced by the effects of any spell you cast. You can cast each spell once, and you regain the ability to cast them when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can spend 2 Ki Points to cast one of these spells again.

6.name: Shadow Step
description: You move as an undetected shadow through the darkness. Beginning at 6th level, you can step from one shadow into another. When you are in dim light or darkness, you can use your bonus action to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. After teleporting in this way, you have advantage on the first Martial Arts attack you make before the end of that turn.

11.name: Cloak of Shadows
description: Starting at 11th level, you can become one with the darkness. When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use an action to become invisible. You remain invisible until you attack, cast a spell, or move into an area of bright light. Moreover, if you are invisible, you can make opportunity attacks as a reaction when a creature moves into your reach. Opportunity attacks only end your invisibility if you hit your target. If the opportunity attack misses, you remain invisible.

17.name: Grand Master of Shadows
description: You are an unrivaled practitioner of the Shadow Arts, and you have unlocked abilities that are only able to be used by a true Grand Master of Shadow. Upon reaching 17th level, your Way of the Shadow Arts features gain the following benefits:

• You can cast the spells you gained from Shadow Arts an unlimited amount of times without expending Ki Points.
  • The range of your Shadow Step increases to 120 feet.
  • You can use your Cloak of Shadows as a bonus action.
  • As an action, you can cast Greater Invisibility or Shadow of Moil, targeting only yourself, without expending a spell slot or material components. You can cast each spell once, and you regain the ability to cast it when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can spend 4 Ki Points to cast one of these spells again.

subclasses.name: Way of Shadow

description: Monks of the Way of the Soul Knife are monks who have learned to harnass and focus their ki, using their inner will and focus to control psionic powers - primarily into a blade of pure Psionic power: a Soul Knife.

3.name: Soul Knife Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Empowered Strike
5th Seeking Strike
9th Aura Sight

3.name: Soul Knife
description: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you've learned to focus your ki into a psionic blade. As a bonus action, you can create a blade of pure scintillating psionic energy. The blade you create this way most typically takes the form of a knife-like blade projecting from your fist, but you can shape it however you choose. You can choose to create multiple blades, but any blade you are not holding vanishes at the end of your turn and must be resummoned.
Regardless of the form it takes, the weapon is a monk weapon for you, deals 1d8 psychic damage, and has the light, finesse, and thrown (20/60) properties.

3.name: Telekinetic Force
description: Additionally at 3rd level, you learn the Mage Hand cantrip. You also gain the ability to smash a target creature or object you can see with your mental power. As an action, you can force a target within 60 feet to succeed on a Strength saving throw or take 1d10 bludgeoning damage and be knocked 5 feet in a direction of your choice or knocked prone.

You can spend 1 Ki Point to add any of the following modifiers to this attack. The points must be spent when choosing the target of the power. The number of Ki you may spend on one attack increase as you gain levels in this class. You may spend up to 2 ki points at 5th level, 3 ki points at 9th level, 4 ki points at 14th level, and 5 ki points at 17th level.

subFeatures.name: Hammering
description: You spend 1 or more ki points, and the target takes an additional 1d10 bludgeoning damage for each point spent.

subFeatures.name: Hurling
description: You spend 1 to 3 ki points, and the target is knocked an extra 10 feet in a direction of your choosing for each point spent.

subFeatures.name: Crushing
description: You spend 2 ki points, and the target is restrained until the end of its next turn.

subFeatures.name: Sweeping
description: You spend 3 ki points to target all creatures in a 10 foot radius of a point within range.

6.name: Art of the Soul Knife
description: Starting at 6th level, your expertise with the blade allows you to control it in unique and powerful ways.

subFeatures.name: Extended Knife
description: You can expend 1 ki point to give your weapon the Reach property until the end of your turn.

subFeatures.name: Psionic Flurry
description: When you make a Flurry of Blows, you can make the additional attacks with your Soul Knife.

subFeatures.name: Soul Strike
description: When you take the attack action, you can focus. Make a single attack using your action (forgoing any additional attacks gained from Extra Attack) to ignore all armor a creature has and treating its AC as 10 + its Dexterity modifier. On a hit, the creature takes additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

11.name: Power of the Mind
description: Starting at 11th level, your Psionic abilities manifest more completely, giving you greater control and power in your psionic abilities.

subFeatures.name: Consumptive Blade
description: Whenever you kill a creature with your Soul Knife that has an Intelligence of 6 or higher, you can can use your reaction draw in part of their Psionic essence. You regain 1d4 hit points and 1 expended ki point.

subFeatures.name: Ethereal Sweep
description: When you use Extended Knife, you can sweep or stab through multiple creatures with a single blow. Once per turn, when you make an attack with your Soul Knife, you can make a single additional weapon attack with your Soul Knife against another creature within range.

17.name: Transcendent Knife
description: Starting at 17th level, your Soul Knife becomes an peerless weapon. You can add a +1 to its attack and damage rolls. You can choose for your knife to effect inanimate material, causing it to gain the Siege property and deal force damage to it when you choose. Reactions that parry or block to add Armor Class against an attack are ineffective against attacks made with the Soul Knife.

Additionally, critical strikes from your weapon rends soul of the target. If a creature would have less than 50 hit points after taking damage from your critical strike, the creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On failure, its Charisma becomes zero and it dies.

subclasses.name: Way of the Soul Knife

description: Even now, millennia after their construction, the dusty tombs and forgotten crypts of the god-kings are still sacred locations. The monasteries of the sun have endured, safeguarding the tombs from harmful interlopers, with generation after generation of stalwart guardians, ensuring the pharaohs' rest is not disturbed. These monks are trained in the Way of the Sphinx, a fluid but aggressive style of martial arts, focused squarely on the use of khopeshes, and take a sacred oath to guard the tombs until their deaths. These monks leave the bounds of the desert only if one of their number has failed in their duties, and a sacred artifact from the tombs must be recovered.

3.name: Sphinx Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Arresting Strike
5th Divine Light
9th Indomitable Spirit

3.name: Flurry of Blades
description: When you choose this monastic tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with khopeshes, which count as monk weapons for you. In addition, khopeshes are considered light weapons for you.

In addition, when you engage in two-weapon fighting, you add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack. When you use your Flurry of Blows feature while wielding a monk weapon in each hand, you can use your weapons for the additional attacks.

3.name: Inscrutable
description: Also at 3rd level, you are immune to any magical effect that would sense your emotions or read your thoughts. Wisdom (Insight) checks made to ascertain your intentions or sincerity have disadvantage.

6.name: Divine Guardian
description: Starting at 6th level, your monastery teaches divine magic. Some of the spells they practice hamper their enemies, others help the caster survive in their harsh surroundings. You can spend ki points to cast the Create Or Destroy Water, Dust Devil, and Shield of Faith spells.

When you cast a spell in this way, you must expend a number of ki points equal to the spell's level. If the spell can be cast at higher levels, you can spend additional ki points to cast the spell at a higher level, at a cost of one additional ki point per spell level. You can expend ki points equal to no more than one third of your monk level (rounded down) on any spell granted by this feature.

6.name: Claws of the Sphinx
description: Also at 6th level, you are marked by the gods to defend the mortal world against the spirits of the dead and other unholy creatures. Attacks you make with a light monk weapon count as magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

11.name: Whirling Blades
description: Starting at 11th level, as an action while you hold a monk weapon in both hands, you can spend movement equal to your Unarmored Movement bonus to whirl around in a lethal flourish. When you do so, each creature within 10 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage equal to your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier, and is pushed 5 feet away from you in a straight line. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed away from you.

17.name: Pharaoh's Judgement
description: Starting at 17th level, your voice booms with divine authority, causing hostile creatures to freeze when you pass judgement upon them. As an action, you can spend a number of ki points up to your Wisdom modifier. You cast the Hold Monster spell, targeting a number of creatures equal to the number of ki points spent. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Way of the Sphinx

description: Legends tell of wandering sages that channel bursts of light from within their bodies. These students of the Sun Soul have such fine control over their spirit that they can assault others with radiant blasts of Ki. These luminous warriors travel the land promoting harmony and justice amongst all peoples.

3.name: Sun Soul Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Mystic Healing
5th Divine Light
9th Aura Sight

3.name: Radiant Bolt
description: When you join this Tradition at 3rd level, you can focus your Ki into bolts of searing light. When you make an unarmed strike, you can replace the attack with a Radiant Bolt.
Radiant Bolts are ranged (30/90) Martial Arts attacks that you are proficient in. On hit, they deal radiant damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier.
In addition, you learn the Light cantrip, and you use Wisdom as your spellcasting modifier for it.

6.name: Searing Blast
description: Starting at 6th level, you can create searing blasts of radiant Ki. As a bonus action, you can force creatures in an adjacent 15-foot cone to make a Dexterity saving throw. Creatures take radiant damage equal to three rolls of your Marital Arts die on a failed save, and half as much on a successful one.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can spend 1 Ki Point to use it again.

11.name: Luminous Burst
description: Your spirit brims with burning radiance that you can channel to purify the world. Beginning at 11th level, you can use your action to cast the fireball spell. When you use this feature to cast this spell it deals radiant damage instead of fire damage.
You can expend Ki Points as part of this action to empower your Luminous Burst. For each Ki Point you spend, up to a maximum of 3, it deals an additional 1d6 radiant damage.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can spend 3 Ki Points to use it again.

17.name: Master of Light
description: Your radiant spirit can stand against the greatest powers of darkness. At 17th level, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain a flying speed equal to your movement speed.
  • You become wreathed in light. You shed bright sunlight in a 30-foot radius and dim sunlight for 30 feet beyond that. You can extinguish or restore the light as a bonus action.
  • The radiant damage of your Radiant Bolt, Searing Blast, and Luminous Burst all count as true sunlight.
  • You are immune to radiant damage and being blinded, and you have resistance to necrotic damage.

subclasses.name: Way of the Sun Soul

description: Monks of the Twin Dragons are masters of fighting in tandem with a partner. However, their partner is a ki-based projection of themselves. This makes them dangerous to fight, and hard to keep track of, as the advantage created by their tandem style fighting means that every blind spot is struck and every opening is taken advantage of as four fists, two real, and two ethereal, strike joints nerves and weak points in a hundred different ways from a hundred different angles, pummeling an enemy into the ground.

3.name: Twin Dragon Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Whirling Strike
5th Stunning Strike
9th Commune with Self

3.name: Extended Self Technique
description: At 3rd level, when you choose this tradition, you summon a split, a ki projection of yourself that fights alongside you.

On your turn, you may move your split up to your movement speed, then, if you use flurry of blows, you can have your split attack as well, dealing your martial arts die in force damage and inflicting one of the following effects on the target until the start of your next turn.

• The targets movement speed is reduced by 10 feet.
  • The target has disadvantage on its next attack.
  • The target cannot use its reaction.

Your split uses your attack bonus to hit, but only deals your martial arts die in force damage. If you or an ally are not within 5 feet of the creature your split is attacking, its attack deal damage but does not have any other effect.

The split is also an illusion and cannot take damage or be dispelled. It cannot move through objects and creatures, and cannot be more than 60 ft away from you, and is moved with you if you move more than 60 feet away from it.

6.name: Twin Ox style
description: At 6th level, you begin to perfect the strange style of fighting aside your self. You've learned to time your's and your split's strikes in unison. Whenever you use a strike Technique and your split is adjacent to the creature you are attacking, you can force the creature roll a d4 and subtract that from their saving throw roll.

11.name: Twin Spirit Style
description: At 11th level, you have strengthened your split's projection and connection to you. Whenever you take the attack action, you can choose to attack a target that your split is adjacent to by switching places with your split with a quick teleportation

17.name: Twin Dragon Style
description: At 17th level, you have mastered combat alongside your split. Whenever you end your turn, you may spend 3 ki points to have your split copy every action, bonus action, and move action you made during your turn.

subclasses.name: Way of the Twin Dragons

description: The inner peace of contemplation, the artistry of focused breathing, and the calm awareness which leads to pinpoint accuracy all contribute to the Way of the Unerring Arrow. Some are dedicated soldiers, others walk the path of a wandering warrior-mendicant, but all of them hone their art of self-control, spirituality, and the martial arts, combining unarmed combat with archery.

3.name: Unerring Arrow Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Step of the Wind
5th Deflect Missiles
9th Aura Sight

3.name: Archery Training
description: When you choose this tradition at 3rd level, your particular martial arts training guides you to master the use of ranged weaponry. You gain proficiency with all martial ranged weapons, and ranged weapons with which you are proficient are considered monk weapons for you. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.

When you make an unarmed strike as a bonus action as part of your Martial Arts feature or as part of a Flurry of Blows, you can choose for the unarmed strike to deal piercing damage as you jab the target with an arrow.

6.name: Needle Eye of Insight
description: At 6th level, your attacks with ranged weapons with which you are proficient count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. In addition, when you make a ranged weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to cause your ranged attacks to ignore half cover and three-quarters cover until the start of your next turn.

6.name: Flurry of Deflection
description: Also at 6th level, you get additional reactions equal to your proficiency bonus, but these reactions can be used only for your Deflect Missiles feature. If you reduce the damage of the ranged weapon attack to 0 and the missile can be fired with a ranged weapon you have, you can spend 1 ki point to make a ranged attack with the weapon, using the missile you caught as ammunition.
At 9th level, when you use Deflect Missiles, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 2d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level

11.name: Steel Rain Blossom
description: At 11th level, you can fire arrows in a deadly rain. While wielding a ranged weapon with which you are proficient, you can use an action to fire an arcing shot at a point you can see within your weapon's normal range. As the shot descends onto the point, it magically replicates into dozens of shots. Each creature within 15 feet of that point must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take piercing damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die. A creature behind total cover automatically succeeds on this saving throw. You can increase the steel rain's damage by spending ki points. Each point you spend, to a maximum of 3, increases the damage by one Martial Arts die.
In addition, when you would make an unarmed strike as a bonus action as part of your Martial Arts feature or as part of a Flurry of Blows, you can choose to make a ranged weapon attack instead.

17.name: Improbable Shot
description: At 17th level, when you use your Needle Eye of Insight feature to ignore cover, you can spend 3 ki points to ignore all forms of cover instead. The shot even passes through solid barriers, provided you have seen the target within the past minute and it is within your weapon's normal range.

Alternatively, you can spend 5 ki points to strike a target you have seen within the past minute that is now on a different plane or in an extradimensional space, such as through the plane shift or rope trick spells or a phase spider' Ethereal Jaunt trait. If you do so, you can't use this feature in this way again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Way of the Unerring Arrow

description: While all monks strive for perfection in one way or another, monks of this Tradition stand as paragons of justice, liberty, and fair play. Lauded as heroes by some, and derided as extrajudicial criminals by others, Vigilante monks work to perform ever more impressive feats of heroism.

The signature mark of a Vigilante monk is their Heroic Persona, a mantle they create for themselves that protects their true identity. Vigilante monks almost always have a deeply personal reason for donning their Heroic Persona and working to thwart villains of all kinds. What is yours?

3.name: Vigilante Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Slow Fall
5th Unyielding Perseverance
9th Monastic Fortitude

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you adopt this Tradition at 3rd level, you gain the skills to succeed as a heroic Vigilante. You gain proficiency in your choice of either Intimidation or Performance.
You also gain proficiency with light armor, medium armor, and shields. When wearing armor or using a shield you still gain the benefits of Martial Arts and Unarmored Movement.

3.name: Heroic Persona
description: At 3rd level, you design your Heroic Persona, a lager than life identity usually marked by a thematic costume or flashy suit of armor. As a bonus action, so long as you cannot be seen, you can adopt your Heroic Persona, which can include a suit of light or medium armor and a shield. When you do so, you gain temporary hit points equal to your monk level, and while your Heroic Persona is active you gain the following benefits:

• As a bonus action, you can spend 1 Ki Point to gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier.
  • When you hit with a Martial Arts attack, you can spend 1 Ki Point to deal an additional 1d10 damage to the target.
  • You can use your Wisdom, in place of Dexterity, when calculating your Armor Class in light or medium armor.
  • Ability checks and divination spells that would discern your true identity automatically fail.

Your Heroic Persona lasts for 1 hour, and ends early if you use a bonus action to doff your Persona. Once you adopt your Heroic Persona you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest, unless you expend 3 Ki Points to use it again.

6.name: Valiant Action
description: As the reputation and power of your Heroic Persona grows, you gain enhanced physical abilities. At 6th level, you gain proficiency in your choice of either Acrobatics or Athletics.
Also, whenever you make a Strength (Athletics), Dexterity (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check while your Heroic Persona is active, you treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

11.name: Inspiring Presence
description: The presence of your Heroic Persona inspires confidence in those who fight alongside you. Beginning at 11th level, while your Heroic Persona is active, creatures of your choice within 15 feet that can see or hear you have advantage on saving throws to resist being charmed or frightened.
At 17th level, the radius of this ability increases to 30 feet.

17.name: Heroic Strike
description: Beginning at 17th level, you can channel all that you are into one devastating blow. As an action, you can touch a creature and spend 1 or more Ki Points, forcing it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it takes 1d10 bludgeoning damage and is knocked back 10 feet for each Ki Point you spent. On a success, it takes half that damage and is not moved.

17.name: Paragon of Virtue
description: Your true identity and your Heroic Persona have become one. Starting at 17th level, when you adopt your Heroic Persona, it lasts until you choose to dismiss it as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Way of the Vigilante

description: Monks that follow the traditions of the Way of the Void look to the spaces between the stars for inspiration in their techniques. Their training emphasizes emptiness of mind and body, and monks of this tradition spend long hours in fasting and meditation.

3.name: Void Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Empowered Strike
5th Deflect Missiles
9th Heavenly Step

3.name: Void Techniques
description: At 3rd level, you learn the techniques of the void. You gain the following abilities:

subFeatures.name: Endless Self
description: You do not need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, you do not require sleep and can choose to remain conscious during a long rest, though you must still refrain from strenuous activity to gain the benefit of the rest.

subFeatures.name: Vacuum Pull
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one ki point to create a vacuum centered on the target. Each creature other than you within 10 feet of the target must make a Strength saving throw or be pulled 5 feet toward the target and take bludgeoning damage equal to your Martial Arts die.

6.name: Empty Soul
description: At 6th level, you learn to fight without being weighed down by your own life energy. When you have no ki remaining, your movement speed increases by 10 feet and you gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns.

11.name: Empty Mind
description: At 11th level, you learn to remove your presence. You are always under the effects of a Nondetection spell. Additionally, you are immune to psychic damage.

17.name: Nothing
description: At 17th level, you can become so empty that not even magic can exist around you. You can use your action to spend 6 ki points to cast the Antimagic Field spell, without material components.

subclasses.name: Way of the Void

description: Within the walls of a temple, monks train to fight with only their fists and their wits. But someone has to protect the temple while the others train, and those that do have found that a good shield is not to be discounted. Adherents to the Way of the Walled Temple have adapted the teachings of their masters to incorporate defensive gear, and value vigilance and protection above all else.

Because these monks almost never leave their temples, it is unusual for one to become an adventurer, and when they do it is usually because something has gone wrong. Perhaps their temple was destroyed, and they seek retribution from those who did it. Maybe they failed to spot an intruding assassin, and have abandoned their post in shame. It's also possible that the monk feels confident their old temple is well guarded, and seeks a new shrine to watch over.

3.name: Walled Temple Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Patient Defense
5th Unyielding Perseverance
9th Monastic Fortitude

3.name: Temple's Shield
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have mastered using a shield alongside your martial arts, gaining the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Monk's Shield
description: You gain proficiency with shields, and wielding one does not prevent you from using your Martial Arts, Unarmored Movement, or Unarmored Defense features. A shield is also considered a monk weapon for you.

subFeatures.name: Deflect Strikes
description: While wielding a shield, you can expend 1 ki points to use your reaction to neutralize the force of an incoming melee weapon attack. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by an amount equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can immediately make a shove attempt against the attacker, substituting a shield attack roll for your Strength (Athletics) check. All other restrictions of making a shove still apply.

subFeatures.name: Ricochet Shot
description: While wielding a shield other than a tower shield, it gains theThrown (20/60) and Returning properties for you.

6.name: Watcher on the Wall
description: At 6th level, you learn a special meditation technique that expands your vision. After spending 1 minute in meditation, you can expend 2 ki points to enter a state of heightened awareness. For the next hour, you have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and initiative rolls, and you cannot be surprised.

11.name: Stoic Gatekeeper
description: Starting at 11th level, you can keep multiple assailants at bay. While wielding a shield, you can take two reactions intead of one.

17.name: Last Line of Defense
description: Starting at 17th level, you have the power to single-handedly protect your temple. Using an action, you can expend 6 ki points to cast the Wall of Force spell. When you cast the spell in this way, it does not require material components, and the wall is semi-visible, resembling the architechture of your home temple.

subclasses.name: Way of the Walled Temple

description: Wrestling is the ultimate contest of might, a bout where two enter a ring and only one remains within it moments later. The Way of Wrestler teaches its students to stand their ground and maintain perfect discipline and form to meet whatever challenge they face. In contrast to other monks, who are typically lithe and nimble, wrestlers are rippling with muscle, a necessity for grappling with the mightiest contenders of the sport without surrendering any ground.

3.name: Wrestler Techniques
description: You learn certain Techniques at the levels noted in the table below. They don't count against your number of Techniques Known and they cannot be switched upon gaining a level.

Monk Level Technique
3rd Improvised Strikes
5th Crushing Strike
9th Indomitable Spirit

3.name: Stout Defense
description: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Strength modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

3.name: Implacable Stance
description: At 3rd level, you are considered one size larger for the purposes of grappling and have advantage on all your Strength checks.

Additionally, if you move 5 feet or less on your turn, you can anchor your heels into the ground. Until the beginning of your next turn, you can't be moved against your will, and, for the duration, you can spend a ki point whenever you take damage to reduce the damage taken by 1d8.

6.name: Huge Presence
description: By 6th level, your enormous silhouette causes even hardened warriors to take pause. You gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill. If you already had proficiency in this skill, you can add twice your proficiency modifier to ability checks made using it.
Additionally, attacks made against you before you have taken a turn in combat have disadvantage.

11.name: Colossus Slam
description: Beginning at 11th level, you can drop your full weight on a foe like a falling meteorite. Once on each of your turns when you make a unarmed strike, you can deal twice the number of damage dice on a hit, but also knock yourself prone after the attack.

17.name: Yokozuna
description: By 17th level, you are a master of the art of wrestling, an unmovable titan. Whenever you take damage, you can expend any number of ki points to reduce the damage by 1d8 per ki point expended.

subclasses.name: Way of the Wrestler

description: Rather than focus inward, some monks attune themselves to the forces of nature. Known as Wu Jen, these primal sages augment their skills with the power of the eight elements; Aether, Air, Earth, Fire, Light, Shadow, Water, and Wood. Through meditation, they can learn to channel their Ki into displays of elemental power.

3.name: Disciple of the Elements
description: When you join this Monastic Tradition at 3rd level, you learn ancient monastic arts that allow you cast spells.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Wu Jen Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have, and the level of those slots. All of your spell slots are the same level. To cast an Elemental spell of 1st-level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You use the spell's casting time and other rules, but your body becomes the spellcasting focus for these spells, and you don't need to provide any material components. You regain all expended Wu Jen spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You learn three 1st-level spells of your choice from the Elemental spell list. The Spells Known column of the Wu Jen Spellcasting table shows when you learn more Elemental spells. A spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level.
When you gain a level, you can choose an Elemental spell you know and replace it with another spell from the Elemental spell list, which must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Elemental spells, so you use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability, when setting a saving throw DC, and when making a spell attack roll.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

3.name: Elemental Attunement
description: Also at 3rd level, you can learn to control the elements in minor ways. You know the Control the Elements cantrip.

6.name: Fist of the Elements
description: You can empower your fists with the elements. Starting at 6th level, when you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can choose for your unarmed strike to deal elemental damage that corresponds to the element of an Elemental spell you know, instead of bludgeoning damage: Aether (force), Air (lightning), Earth (acid), Fire (fire), Light (radiant), Shadow (necrotic), Water (cold), or Wood (poison).
Also, when you use your action to cast an Elemental spell, you can make one Martial Arts attack as a bonus action.

11.name: Spiritual Flow
description: You weave your martial arts with magic. Beginning at 11th level, when you cast an Elemental spell with a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 Ki Points to cast it as a bonus action.

17.name: Grand Master of the Elements
description: Beginning at 17th level, you can use an action to assume an Elemental Form for 1 minute. This form ends early if you are incapacitated or you use a bonus action to end it. Once you use this feature you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses remaining, you can expend 6 Ki Points to use your Elemental Form again.
While in your Elemental Form you gain the benefits listed below, so long as you know one Wu Jen spell of the corresponding element.

subFeatures.name: Aether
description: You have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

subFeatures.name: Air
description: You gain a flying speed of 60 feet.

subFeatures.name: Earth
description: You have resistance to all non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subFeatures.name: Fire
description: Any creature that hits you with a melee attack takes fire damage equal to your Martial Arts die.

subFeatures.name: Light
description: You gain truesight out to 30 feet.

subFeatures.name: Shadow
description: Bright light within 30 feet of you becomes dim light, and dim light within 30 feet of you becomes darkness.

subFeatures.name: Water
description: Critical hits against you become normal hits, and opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage.

subFeatures.name: Wood
description: You gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns.

subclasses.name: Way of the Wu Jen

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Psionic Awakening
description: At 1st level, your mind is awake to the psychic hum of the universe, giving you the power to influence your surroundings with a mere thought.  The raw strength of your mind is represented by your Psi Die, the starting size of which is a d4.  You roll the die when using a number of features gained through this class.

subFeatures.name: Changing the Die's Size
description: If you roll a 1 on your Psi Die, it decreases by one size after the roll, down to a minimum size of a d2.  This represents you losing clarity or focus.
Conversely, if you roll the highest number on your Psi Die, it increases by one die size after the roll, up to its starting size.  This represents you building momentum with your abilities.

Whenever you finish a long rest, your Psi Die resets to its starting size.  When you reach certain levels, the starting size of your Psi Die increases, as shown in the Psi Die column of the Mystic table.

subFeatures.name: Dull Thoughts
description: When you take damage from a creature within 60 feet of you and your Psi Die is larger than a d2, you can use your reaction to diminish the ambient willpower in their vicinity.  Your Psi Die decreases by one die size, and until the start of your next turn, any damage dice rolled by the creature (including those of the triggering effect) are decreased by one size as well, down to a minimum size of a d2.

subFeatures.name: Reorient Thoughts
description: As a bonus action, you can calm your mind for a moment and restore your Psi Die to its starting size.  You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Psionic Ability
description: Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice) is your Psionic Ability.  You use your chosen ability score when mystic features refer to your Psionic ability.
Psionic attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Psionic ability modifier
Psionic Save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Psionic ability modifier

1.name: Focus Field
description: Also at 1st level, you manifest your attention as a tactile influence upon the world: a focus field.  While you are not incapacitated and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a shield, the field exists as an invisible, Medium force with a flying speed of 40 feet and the ability to hover.  It is intangible and doesn't occupy its space.  The field has blindsight within 5 feet of its space, but no other senses.  You are telepathically aware of what it sees.

On your turn, the focus field can hover up to its speed to a space that you are aware of.  It can pass through creatures and objects.  If you take the Dash action, your focus field also gains the benefits of that action.
The field has a maximum range it can move away from you.  This range in feet equals 30 times your proficiency bonus.
If you recover from being incapacitated after losing your focus field, the field reforms within 10 feet of you within a space of your choice.
You can command the field in the following ways:

• When you take the Attack action, you can replace one or more of your attacks with a telekinetic attack made with your field against a target within 5 feet of it. You use your Psionic ability instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of this attack, which counts as a simple weapon attack that deals your choice of bludgeoning or psychic damage equal to one roll of your Psi Die.
  • As a bonus action, you can make one special shove attack through your focus field against a target within 5 feet of it. When you do so, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Psionic save DC or be moved 5 feet in a direction of your choice. A creature can willingly fail this save.
  • Your focus field can carry, push, drag, or lift objects not being worn or carried, with a carrying capacity in pounds equal to your Psionic ability score multiplied by 15. While carrying, pushing, dragging, or lifting any object that weighs more than your Psionic ability score in pounds, you must concentrate on the task as if concentrating on a spell. A creature attempting to wrest an object from the grip of the field must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against your Psionic save DC in order to do so.
  • You can manipulate objects with the field as if using the Mage Hand cantrip, or speak with a creature within 5 feet of it as if using the Message cantrip.
  • You learn if a creature within 5 feet of your field telepathically communicates, although not the contents of any such communication.

2.name: Ki
description: Starting at 2nd level, you learn to control the incredible power of your mind through the meditative energy of ki.  Your access to this energy is represented by a number of ki points.  You have a number of ki points equal to twice your Mystic level.

You can spend these points to fuel various ki features.  Chief among them are personal lessons, called Mantras, that help you to focus and structure your thoughts.  You start knowing three such mantras: Guarded Thoughts, Inner Peace, and Sentient Sense, as well as four expressive mantras of your choice.  You learn more ways to use ki as your gain levels in this class.

When you spend a ki point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or long rest, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself.  You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your ki points.
Some of your ki features requires the target to make a saving throw to resist the feature's effects.  The saving throw DC is equal to your Psionic save DC.

subFeatures.name: Guarded Thoughts
description: As a reaction when you take psychic damage or a creature attempts to read your mind, you can spend 1 ki point to gain resistance to psychic damage until the start of your next turn.  For the duration, your thoughts can't be read by any means short of the Wish spell.

subFeatures.name: Inner Peace
description: You can spend 1 ki point as a bonus action to gain advantage on Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws until the end of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Sentient Sense
description: As an action, you can spend 1 ki point to expand your awareness and scan for other thinking minds.  Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any creature within 60 feet of you that has an Intelligence score of 4 or higher.  You do not know the type of any being whose presence you sense.  Within the same radius, you also become aware of any creature that has the ability to communicate telepathically.

subFeatures.name: Expressive Mantras
description: When you gain this feature, choose four Expressive Mantras of your choice.  You learn additional mantras of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Mantras Known column of the mystic table.

3.name: Telepathy
description: At 3rd level, you have gained the ability to communicate with telepathy.  As an action, you can roll your Psi Die to create a telepathic link with a number of creatures up to the result rolled that are within 120 feet of you.  You can telepathically speak with linked creatures while they are within this range, and they can respond in kind.  You don't need to share a language with a creature for it to understand your telepathic messages, but it must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself.  An existing telepathic link ends if your fall unconscious or if you use this feature again.

7.name: Quietude of the Soul
description: Starting at 7th level, when you fail a saving throw that causes you to lose concentration, become subject to madness, or to become charmed or frightened, you can spend 1 ki point to reroll the saving throw.  If you do so, you must use the new roll.

10.name: Heightened Focus
description: Starting at 10th level, before you take an action or bonus action on your turn using your focus field, you can spend ki points to increase its size category by one for a number of minutes equal to the number of ki points spent.  Your focus field's carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, and lift is doubled for each size category above Medium it achieves, as if it was a creature.
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the size category of your focus field by two when you use this feature, for a cost of 1 additional ki point per minute.

18.name: Epiphany
description: At 18th level, a revelation close to the peak of enlightenment grants you proficiency in Charisma saving throws.
In addition, choose one mantra you know.  Any ki cost required by the mantra is reduced by 1.

While disciplining your psionic gift, you have meditated on the ways of war.  With keenly tempered tactical awareness, battleminds are able to observe and influence wide swaths of an engagement with keen insights and raw psychic strength.  Displaying galling confidence, they cut decisively forward to deliver a clean, clear victory.

3.name: Combat Acumen
description: Starting at 3rd level, your extensive study of warfare has grants you the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency with martial weapons and light armor. You can manifest your focus field even while wearing armor your are proficient with.
  • A focus field you manifest can wield a weapon that you are proficient with, and make attacks with the weapon in place of its normal telekinetic attacks. It can carry and use any ammunition required by the weapon.
  • Weapon attacks you make from within one of your focus fields use your Psionic ability modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.

3.name: Split Focus
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your preternatural awareness allows you to hold sway over multiple dominions of the battlefield at once.  As an action, you can split your focus field in two.  When split in this way, the focus fields cannot be any larger in size than Medium.  Each focus field has its own movement speed and can move independently of the other as your direct it on your turn.  When using your focus field as part of an action, bonus action, or reaction, you choose which of the fields to act through.
This effect ends early if you become incapacitated, or if you choose to end it early by dismissing one of the fields as a bonus action.

6.name: Extra Attack
description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

11.name: Iron Will
description: Starting at 11th level, you can now use your Quietude of the Soul feature to reroll a failed saving throw that would cause you to gain exhaustion to become paralyzed, poisoned, or stunned.

20.name: One Mind Army
description: At 20th level, your psionic war machine unfolds with terrifying grace.  When you hit with an attack made as part of the Attack action, you can immediately make up to two further weapon attacks.  Each of these attacks must originate from a different space to the original attack.

subclasses.name: Battlemind Discipline

description: Your mind and heart are open to all the woes, worries, merriments, and fears of sapient life.  More than other mystics, you have homed in on the underlying current of emotion tangled in a complex push and pull with the tides of all thought and action.  By extending your understanding - even to those who would call themselves your enemies - you offer the chance to dissolve and resolve conflicts in a way that few others could.  When an emotional storm is brewing, you can guide all parties to the calm at its center.

3.name: Detect Feelings
description: Starting at 3rd level, whenever you use your Sentient Sense feature, you can see the surface shape of emotions in creatures you detect.  The deeper truth of their thoughts is hidden from you, but you know whether a creature is feeling angry, afraid, happy, sad, or violent, for example, and gain a general sense of who or what, if anything, those emotions are being directed at if their subject is within 60 feet of you.

3.name: Soothe Ego
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you understand how to redirect feelings of shame or fear to more revitalizing pastures.  As a bonus action, you can grant temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Psi Die + your Psionic ability modifier (minimum of 1) to each creature of your choice within 5 feet of your focus field.  When you grant temporary hit points to a creature in this way, you can choose one effect of the Calm Emotions spell to affect the target.
You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your Psionic ability modifier, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Shared Pain
description: Starting at 6th level, once per turn when a creature within 5 feet of either you or your focus field deals damage to another creature, you can choose for it to take psychic damage equal to one roll of your Psi Die, as it is subjected to the psychic feedback of the pain it has caused.

11.name: Swelling Emotion
description: Starting at 11th level, when the size of your focus field increases using your Heightened Focus feature, creatures of your choice within 5 feet of the field must make a Charisma saving throw against your Psionic save DC.  A creature can willingly fail this saving throw.  On a failure, you choose one of the following effects to influence the creature:

subFeatures.name: Joy
description: Happiness fills every limb with warmth and energy.  Until the end of your next turn, the target's movement speed increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Psionic ability modifier, and it adds your Psionic ability modifier to attack rolls for the duration.

subFeatures.name: Misery
description: Dolorous fatigue bears down on every fibre.  The target is under the effects of the Slow spell until the end of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Panic
description: Rising fear gives way to chaotic flight.  The target must spend its turns trying to move as far away from all other creatures as it  can.  It also can't take reactions.  For its action, it can only use the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving.  If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the creature can use the Dodge action.

subFeatures.name: Pride
description: Hubris solidifies even an untenable position.  Until the end of your next turn, the target refuses to move.  If it had previously taken an action, it repeats this action on its next turn, regardless of its effectiveness.  If the action cannot be repeated, it does nothing.

subFeatures.name: Rage
description: Immense anger fuels a brief and hollowing blaze.  Until the end of your next turn, the target gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, and adds your Psionic ability modifier to the damage rolls of melee weapon attacks.  When the effect ends, the target gains one level of exhaustion.

20.name: Hearts and Minds
description: Starting at 20th level, you have advantage on all Wisdom (Insight) and Charisma (Persuasion) checks made against creatures within the maximum range of your focus field.

In addition, you can help inspiration flow between allies even when they are unable to express it themselves.  Once per turn when a creature you can currently speak with through your telepathic link makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can roll a number of Psi Dice equal to the number of other creatures in your link you can see within 60 feet of you.  The creature can add the highest number rolled to its ability check, attack roll, or saving throw.  Use the first die rolled to determine whether the size of your Psi Die changes after the triggering action is resolved.

subclasses.name: Empath Discipline

description: Mystics who discipline their minds and bodies as "Immortals"achieve incredible mastery and malleability over their physical form through the concentration of their psychic powers.  Their very flesh becomes akin to iron, stone, or wood: unphased by the winds of time or the swords and arrows of their enemies.  An Immortal walks softly into battle with unnerving calm, and walks out again just as unruffled.  The highest mystics of this order might remain secluded from outside knowledge for decades or even centuries, patinently waiting for the sign that they should once again enter the world to tread the bucking path of destiny.

3.name: Unflinching Flesh
description: At 3rd level, your hit point maximum increases by 3, and increases by 1 for each mystic level you gain after 1st.

3.name: Meditate Upon Eternity
description: Also starting at 3rd level, as an action while you are within 5 feet of your focus field, you can focus your psionic energy to augment your body against any assault.  You gain temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Psi Die + your mystic level + your Psionic ability modifier.  While you have these temporary hit points, you do not age, and you don't need to eat or drink.
You can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

6.name: Immortal Form
description: Starting at 6th level, when you gain temporary hit points through your Meditate Upon Eternity feature, you can transform your body into an enduring material of nature to become a living weapon or shield.  You are immune to any effect that would reduce your ability scores or hit point maximum while transformed.  In addition, choose one of the following effects, which lasts until you lose these temporary hit points, or until you use this feature again.

subFeatures.name: Changeless Crystal
description: You gain advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.  When you are subjected to a magical effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you can spend 1 ki point as a reaction to instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw.

subFeatures.name: Immutable Metal
description: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d8 damage and become magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical damage.  You gain a bonus to the damage rolls of your unarmed strikes equal to your Constitution modifier.  As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point to gain a damage threshold equal to one roll of your Psi Die + your mystic level until the start of your next turn.  You have immunity to all damage unless you take an amount of damage that equals or exceeds this threshold.

subFeatures.name: Proud Tree
description: At the start of each of your turns, you add temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Psi Die to your pool of temporary hit points.  You can spend 1 ki point to add additional temporary hit points to the result equal to your mystic level.  Temporary hit points you gain in this way cannot exceed a total equal to half of your hit point maximum.

subFeatures.name: Tenacious Stone
description: Your weight multiplies by ten, and you gain a bonus to your Armor Class equal to your Constitution modifier.  As a bonus action, you can spend 1 ki point, reducing your speed to 0 and gaining resistance to all damage until the end of your next turn.

11.name: Patience Neverending
description: Strating at 11th level, you no longer need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep, and you no longer age unless you wish to.  In addition, you can no longer lose concentration while you retain temporary hit points granted by your Meditate Upon Eternity feature.

20.name: Indestructible Spirit
description: At 20th level, whenever you are reduced to 0 hit points, roll your Psi Die.  On a roll of 3 or higher, you do not fall unconscious, and you immediately regain a number of hit points equal to twice the number rolled + your Psionic ability modifier.

subclasses.name: Immortal Discipline

description: Mystics of this discipline are diligent students of other minds, keeping their own open to inspiration from without as well as within.  Through highly attuned manipulation of their telekinetic powers, they also practice the mimicry of other lifeforms.  A Mirror Mind might use their mental abilities to imitate the swaying tentacles of an octopus, the breath of a young dragon, or the ferocity of a chimera.  To outside inspection, their own minds are highly polished surfaces that force interlopers to consider themselves, offering the Mirror Mind an opportunity to follow and learn.

3.name: Reflect Aspect
description: Starting at 3rd level, a combination of telepathic reconnaissance and telekinetic agility allows you to mimic the capabilities of other creatures with great accuracy.  As a bonus action, you can copy one action you have prior knowledge of from those available to a creature within 5 feet of your focus field.  The target must have a challenge rating equal to or lower than your mystic level divided by 3.

Once you have copied an action in this way, you can use it yourself as an action on your turn.  Attack rolls you make as a part of the copied action use your Psionic ability modifier and proficiency bonus, but any damage and additional effects of the action are resolved exactly as if performed by the target creature.  The action is copied exactly as it is available to the target creature when you use this bonus action.  For example, if you copy the breath weapon of a dragon while the breath weapon has yet to recharge, your copy of it must also recharge.  An action with a limited number of uses is coped with the current remaining number of uses available.
A copied action remains available to you until you use this bonus action again.

3.name: Reflect Visage
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you can expend 1 ki point to cast the Disguise Self spell, taking on the appearance of any target you currently have copied through your Reflect Aspect feature, so long as its appearance can be replicated within the limits of the spell.

3.name: Burnished Mind
description: Also starting at 3rd level, the telepathic glare of your psyche subconsciously distracts and disorients others.  When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Psionic ability modifier.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against effects that read your mind or emotional state, such as the Detect Thoughts spell or similar magic.

6.name: Dedicated Extrospection
description: Starting at 6th level, after extensive study, you can better mimic other beings.  You can now retain up to three copied actions using your Reflect Aspect feature, which can be curated from separate targets.  In place of one possible action, you can also choose to copy one bonus action or reaction available to a target.

If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside of combat, you can learn a number of actions, bonus actions, or reactions it can take up to your Psionic ability modifier, chosen from a list determined at the DM's discretion.
If you copy an action, bonus action, or reaction that would exceed your limit of copies, you must choose one of your current copied acitons, bonus actions, or reactions to forget.

11.name: Ardent Reflection
description: Starting at 11th level, to any being with the talent to see it, your psychic self is now a perfect, blazing mirror of metaphyiscal light.  You have advantage on saving throws against any spell that targets only you.  If you roll a 20 for the save against such a spell and the spell is 7th level or lower, the spell has no effect on you and instead targets another creature of your choice within the maximum range of your focus field, using the slot level, spell save DC, attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the caster.

20.name: Uncanny Imagery
description: At 20th level, your mastery of mental mirroring now creates perfect reflections.  The number of copied options you can retain using your Reflect Aspect feature and the maximum challenge rating of your targets increases to 7.

In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of your focus field takes an action, you can use your reaction to perfectly mirror it, regardless of the target's CR.  You can immediately take the same action as the creature, and you gain access to all actions, bonus actions, reactions, and saving throw modifiers available to it until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this reaction to mirror a creature, you must complete a short or long rest before you can do so again.

subclasses.name: Mirror Mind Discipline

description: As their name suggests, nomads live to travel.  The desire to collect knowledge and new experiences motivates them around worlds and even between them.  It's not uncommon to find a nomad far from their home plane, taking in every delight of an alien landscape through their enhanced senses.  If they set their mind on a destination, a nomad will inevitably get there - and often with paranormal speed.  But should the road offer distractions to one side or another, they are not adverse to taking the long way around.

Nomads cultivate a psychic connection to a shared world of sorts: a web of knowledge built between every sentient mind called the noosphere.  In this web exists all information perceived - a collection far too vast to see in its entirety across any lifespan.  Nomads browse the noosphere during their meditations, finding within it a taste, a sight, or a story that inspires them to their next destination.  While the traditions, memories, and sensations of all thinking minds are theirs to peruse at leisure, a nomad knows that there is simply no substitute for experiencing something for yourself.

3.name: Journey of Ten Thousand Steps
description: Starting at 3rd level, moving through time and space at an eccentric pace is second nature to you.  You learn the Misty Step spell, which you can cast by expending 2 ki points.  Your Psionic ability is your spellcasting ability for it, and it requires no components.
In addition, whenever you cast a spell through a mystic feature that teleports you or increases your movement speed as part of its effect, its ki point cost is reduced by 2.

3.name: Wandering Mind
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you are accustomed to visiting new places and picking up new skills.  You learn three languages of your choice, and the speed of your focus field increases by 10 feet.

Moreover, as an action, you can choose a skill related to a creature or object inside the space of your focus field.  You gain proficiency in the chosen skill if you don't already have it.  If you are already proficient in the skill, you double your proficiency bonus for ability checks you make that use the chosen skill.  You lose this bonus when you use this feature again, or when you complete a short or long rest.
You can use this action a number of times equal to your Psionic ability modifier (minimum of 1), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Psychic Souvenir
description: Starting at 6th level, whenever you move or teleport away from a creature within 5 feet of you, you can immediately use an action to force the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw against your Psionic save DC.  On a failed saving throw, you take a psychic souvenir with you: choose one skill, weapon, or saving throw the target is proficient in.  The target loses proficiency with the chosen skill, weapon, or saving throw for 8 hours.

You can hold a number of psychic souvenirs up to your Psionic ability modifier.  While you retain a souvenir, you can add half of your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to any roll you make using the skill, weapon, or saving throw the souvenir represents.  You can apply such a bonus only once to a roll.

You lose your psychic souvenirs if you are incapacitated.  If a target creature is within 5 feet of you, it can also use its action to repeat its saving throw, retrieving the souvenir and restoring its lost proficiency on a success

11.name: Meandering Step
description: Starting at 11th level, once on your turn, as long as your focus field is within 15 feet of you and its space is unoccupied, you can forfeit 10 feet of your movement to teleport to its space.

20.name: Planar Viator
description: At 20th level, you learn the Gate spell which you can cast by expending 16 ki points.  Whenever you cast the spell, it does not require the usual material component.  Your Psionic ability is your spellcasting abiltiy for it, and you do not require components when casting it in this way.  After casting the spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.
As an action while you are concentrating on the spell, you can spend an additional 10 ki points to change the destination of the gate.

subclasses.name: Nomad Discipline

description: The serpent that eats its own tail is a timeless symbol of infinity.  Mystics that bend their own perception of time are likened to it, for it is said that to them life becomes a seamless, sinuous loop.  An ouroboros can connect to both their past and future, nourishing or feeding from either as needed.  Their symbols evoke the concepts of regeneration and reincarnation that are widely studied by their peers.  Certain masters of this mysticism claim that most beings are destined to be reborn as themselves: bound into inanimate loops hanging in place upon the thread of time.  It is a privileged few who are given the chance and the means to recognize this pattern and take control of time's intricacies in motion.

3.name: Snaking Circle
description: Starting at 3rd level, your past, present, and future are simply different muscles within the same chronological body, waiting to be directed by your mind.  As an action, you can call up an apparition of your past or potential self through your focus field.  The apparition appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the field, and must remain within its maximum range.  It is identical to you, although you can decide if its place in your timeline confers small cosmetic changes.  It shares all of your features, armor class and hit points, but it cannot speak or take actions, bonus actions, or reactions.  In combat, the apparition moves on your turn (no action required).  It grants different benefits to you depending on where in your timeline you call it from.
An apparition lasts for 10 minutes.  If you call upon a new apparition, an existing one immediately vanishes.
You can use this action a number of times equal to your Psionic ability modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Past
description: The observations of your past self grant uncanny knowledge of the present.  While this apparition exists, any creatures, traps, or objects that it can see have disadvantage on attack rolls against you.  You also have advantage on any Dexterity saving throws against harmful effects that creatures, traps, or objects the apparition can see might inflict on you, as well as on attack rolls against those targets.  If your apparition takes damage, you take the same amount of damage, which cannot be reduced or prevented in any way, and the apparition immediately vanishes.

subFeatures.name: Potential
description: The reactions of a future version of yourself to events can help to predict and overcome obstacles.  While this apparition exists, its state changes to reflect decisions you contemplate, possibly granting new information.  For example, if you were considering investigating an alcove, your potential self might break out in acid burns, telling you that the alcove contains some alchemical trap.  The exact information shown is at the DM's discretion.  If you take damage, this apparition takes the same amount of damage, which cannot be reduced or prevented in any way.  In addition, you can use your reaction when you take damage to cause your potential self to vanish as you teleport to the space it occupied.

3.name: Tail's Offering
description: Also starting at 3rd level, you can borrow vitality from yourself by bending your timeline.  As an action, you can sacrifice any number of your own hit points to add to a pool of hit points that exists outside of present time.  The pool begins at 0 hit points, and can hold a maximum number of hit points equal to four times your mystic level.
Using your action, you can draw energy from the pool, reducing its total number of stored hit points by any amount you choose and regaining the same number of hit points.

6.name: Möbius Coil
description: Starting at 6th level, the looping forms of your personal timeline bend fluidly to your whims.  When a creature you are telepathically linked with or that is within 5 feet of your focus field makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force a replay of the last attack roll it made within the past minute.  The creature uses that roll instead.  You can choose to use this feature after it is determined whether the original roll succeeds or fails.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Psionic ability modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

11.name: Shed Self
description: At 11th level, like the serpent shrugs free of a skin that weathered another life, you can shrug off assault by briefly stepping out of sync with your typical time.  Once per turn when you are hit by an attack, you can roll your Psi Die.  If the result is a 7 or higher, the attack misses, as it instead strikes an alternate version of you that never was and never will be.

20.name: Escherian Hourglass
description: Starting at 20th level, as an action you can turn the coils of time through byzantine arcs around you.  Choose any number of creatures you are aware of within the maximum range of your focus field and roll your Psi Die.  Each chosen creature has its recent past rearranged: it is teleported to an unoccupied space of your choice within range of your field and immediately takes force damage or regains hit points (your choice for each creature) equal to the number rolled on your Psi Die + mystic level.

Creatures other than you affected by this action have no recollection of their previous state: as far as they are concerned, events played out exactly as necessary in order to get them to their new position.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Ouroboros Discipline

description: The humble sages of the mystic boast of no particularly esoteric powers, but they are highly respected nonetheless.  They are masters of meditative fundamentals: focused on training their minds and spirits for self-control and improvement.  When what seemed certain becomes clouded, or when doubt creeps in to undermine assurance, leaders, scholars, and even other mystics seek out the psages for their wisdom.

3.name: Adaptable Focus
description: Starting at 3rd level, your mental exercises enhance your mind's flexibility.  Your focus field gains the following properties:

• Damage dealt through the telekinetic attacks of the field can be bludgeoning, piercing, psychic, or slashing damage, as you manipulate the field's shape to your whim.
  • The range of attacks or effects delivered through or triggered by the field is extended by 5 feet.
Furthermore, at the end of a short or long rest, choose one of the following additional properties.  Your focus field gains the chosen property until the start of your next short or long rest:

• When you make a telekinetic attack through the field as part of the Attack action, you can target a second creature within 5 feet of your target with the same attack roll.
  • When a target is forcibly moved by an effect originating from your focus field or as the result of failing a saving throw against one of your effects, the target is moved by an additional 5 feet.
  • Your field's carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift is doubled.

3.name: Sage Philosopher
description: Also starting at 3rd level, to maintain mental balance, your mind is always open to exploring new ideas.  At the end of a long rest, you can replace one of the expressive mantras you know with a new one, provided you meet any prerequisites required to learn it.

6.name: Sage Advisor
description: Starting at 6th level, once per round when a creature other than you that you are telepathically linked to hits a target you can see with an attack, you can roll your Psi Die and add the number rolled to the damage of the attack.

11.name: Peaceful Existence
description: Starting at 11th level, once per round when you reroll a saving throw using your Quietude of the Soul feature, you can do so without expending a ki point.

20.name: Sage's Serenity
description: At 20th level, by meditating for a moment, you can enter a state of total psychic transcendence.  The air around you might grow hot or cold, be whipped into winds, or eerily calmed.
Using your action, you spend 10 ki points to undergo a transformation.  For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can hover.
  • At the start of each of your turns, you can roll your Psi Die, gaining a bonus to your Armor Class equal to the number rolled until the start of your next turn.
  • Whenever you spend ki points on a feature that requires an action, you can use that feature with a bonus action instead, or reduce the ki point cost of that feature by 1.

subclasses.name: Psychic Sage Discipline

description: Among your people, your gift has helped to cultivate spiritual peace, as it has done for generations.  You use it not only to examine the souls of individuals, but the soul of your community: looking beyond living minds and through the layers of life, time, and death to an ancestral multitude beyond.  Through intense focus, you have managed to draw forth the power of spirits from the ether to aid and advise your changes and yourself.  This connection sets a shaman apart from other mystics.  You invest your gift into the care of elder spirits: balancing the worlds of past and present, culture and nature, and trusting absolutely in their protection.

3.name: Spirit Guide
description: Starting at 3rd level, you direct your mind through the veil separating the departed from the living, and pull through an advisor and ally in the form of an ancestral spirit.
