Your focus field transforms permanently into a spirit guide.  It retains its maximum range, but it loses all of its other properties.  Any other features that refer to your focus field, including expressive mantras, now refer to your spirit guide instead.  If a mantra requires the use of an action other than the Cast a Spell action, a bonus action, or a reaction, it can use your spirit guide's action, bonus action, or reaction instead of your own.

The guide is friendly to your and your companions, and it obeys your commands.  See this creature's game statistics in the Spirit Guide stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.  You determine the creature's appearance.

In combat, the guide shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours.  It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action.  That action can be one in its stat block or some other action.  If you are incapacitated, the guide can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.
You can spend 2 ki points as an action to cause the spirit guide to regain hit points equal to two rolls of your Psi Die.

At the end of a short or long rest when you draw all of your expended ki back into yourself, you can summon a new spirit guide to you.  If you already have a spirit guide from this feature, the first one immediately vanishes.  The guide also vanishes if you die.

Spirit Guide
Medium undead
Armor Class: 11 + your Psionic ability modifier + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 2 + your Psionic ability modifier + five times your Mystic level
Speed: 40 ft. fly (hover)
STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA
12 (+1) 10 (0) 14 (+2) 12 (+1) 15 (+2) 10 (0)
Saving Throws: Wisdom +2 plus PB
Skills: Insight +2 plus PB, Medicine +2 plus PB
Damage Resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered
Damage Immunities: necrotic, poison
Condition Immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12
Languages: speaks, reads, and writes the languages you know, and is joined to your telepathic link
Challenge: —
Proficiency Bonus (PB): equals your bonus
Ethereal Sight. The guide can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane when it is on the Material Plane, and vice versa.
Incorporeal Movement. The guide can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Actions
Honored Weapon. Melee Weapon Attack: your Psionic attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d8 + PB necrotic, piercing, or radiant damage.
Death Rattle (1/Day). The guide shakes an instrument or calls out towards one target that can hear it within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Psionic save DC or become frightened for 1 minute. While frightened in this way, the target takes an additional 1d4 damage whenever it is hit with an attack. If the creature ends its turn in a location where it doesn't have line of sight to the guide, it can repeat its saving throw, ending the effect on a success.
Share Wisdom (3/Day). The guide passes its knowledge to a willing creature that can hear it within 120 feet. The creature gains advantage on the next History, Nature, Religion, Medicine, or Survival check it makes before the end of its next turn.

3.name: Totemic Teachings
description: Also starting at 3rd level, to anchor yourself to your spirit guide, you carve artful totems, fetishes, or similar spiritual foci representative of your cultural history.  A totem is a Tiny object made of natural material such as bone, stone, or wood.  You have a number of totems equal to your proficiency bonus.

At the end of a short or long rest while your totems are on your person, you can replace expressive mantras you know with unique benefits for your spirit guide, called Expressive Totems.  Each totem acts as the anchor for one such benefit, and each benefit can only be chosen once unless otherwise specified.
In addition, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Occult spell list.  Your Psionic ability is your spellcasting ability for them, and they do not require components when cast in this way.

6.name: Warding Presence
description: Starting at 6th level, your guide makes two Honored Weapon attacks, instead of one, when it takes that action on its turn.

11.name: Counsel of Spirits
description: Starting at 11th level, as an action, you can bring forth a haze of ethereal smoke or light that emits from your spirit guide for 10 feet in all directions for 1 minute.  The area is lightly obscured for the duration.  Creatures of your choice within the haze gain advantage on Wisdom saving throws and gain any resistances that your spirit guide currently has, as an ancestral advisors move through the haze to pass knowledge among them.

20.name: Bridge Between Worlds
description: At 20th level, you are a unifying force between past and present, the living and the dead.  Humanoids and undead have disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and you have advantage on saving throws against effects inflicted by creatures of those types.

In addition, you and your guide can cast the Warding Bond spell at will.  Your Psionic ability is your spellcasting ability for it, and the spell does not require components whne cast in this way.  When cast in this way, you and your spirit guide can only target one another.

subclasses.name: Shaman Discipline

description: Before you speak, listen.  This is the refrain of the Speakers: those who have meditated to attune themselves to the very language of the universe and its making.  Through this, they learn secrets of enlightenment, and can even speak directly into the world, translating thought into voice with effects that reverberate through it in ways great and subtle.

3.name: Voice of Veracity
description: Starting at 3rd level, speaking words of irrefutable truth, you gain the ability to communicate simple ideas with all living things.  Listeners can always understand the meaning of your words, though you have no special ability to understand them in return.  Moreover, you can choose for any creatures that hear your voice to know that you are telling the truth, if this is the case.

3.name: Voice of Making and Unmaking
description: Also starting at 3rd level, speaking words of creation itself, your tones have power over all things in it.  You gain the following benefits:

• You learn the Thaumaturgy cantrip and the Healing Word spell. Your psionic ability is your spellcasting ability for them, and they do not require components when cast in this way. You can expend 2 ki points to cast healing word.
  • Whenever you cast a spell through a mystic feature that normally has a verbal component, you can choose to speak the verbal component aloud to reduce its ki point cost by 1.
  • The telekinetic attacks of your focus field can deal thunder damage. If you know your target's true name, it takes an additional 1d8 damage on a hit.

6.name: Resonant Harmony
description: Starting at 6th level, the music of the spheres hums between your focus field and yourself as you speak: once on your turn after you speak aloud, you can deal 1d8 thunder damage to a creature that can hear you and that is between yourself and your focus field.  If you know the true name of your target, it takes an additional 1d8 thunder damage from this harmony.

11.name: True Listener
description: By 11th level, you have heard and understood more of the true nature of things than most ever shall.  You have advantage on saving throws against spells beloning to the enchantment and illusion schools of magic, as well as on Investigation, Insight, or Perception checks made to determine whether something is illusory, or if a creature is under the influence of an enchantment.

20.name: Choir Cosmic
description: At 20th level, when you speak, all listen.  You can no longer be silenced by any means while conscious, and you learn three of the following spells:

• Power Word: Glory
  • Power Word: Kill
  • Power Word: Heal
  • Power Word: Pain
  • Power Word: Resist
  • Power Word: Stun
  • Power Word: Vengeance
As an action, you can spend 20 ki points to cast each of the chosen spells simultaneously, targeting a separate creature with each spell.
Once you use this action, you gain one level of exhaustion.

subclasses.name: Speaker Discipline

description: Every nascent mystic opens their mind's eye to a new world of hidden thoughts.  For those with the talent, observing the unspoken can become second nature.  The great telepaths of the mystics bear witness to all things: every impulse, intent, and deed that crosses their expansive vision.  Their role is not to judge - but they cannot help but see.  Through their gifts, a witness also hones an oracle's analysis of cause and effect, knowing how a brief thought can translate into lasting action.

3.name: Greater Telepathy
description: Starting at 3rd level, your telepathic gift is so pronounced that other minds are never truly closed to yours.  You gain the following benefits:

• The maximum range of your Telepathy feature increases to 250 feet. This range becomes 500 feet at 6th level, 1 mile at 11th level, unlimited across the same plane of existence at 17th level, and unlimited across planes at 20th level.
  • Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of your focus field are added to your telepathic link. A creature linked in this way does not count towards your total number of linked creatures. The connection ends with a creature linked in this way if it moves more than 5 feet away from your focus field.
  • You learn the Detect Thoughts spell, which you can cast by expending 2 ki points. Your Psionic ability is your spellcasting ability for it, and it doesn't require components. In addition, whenever you cast a spell that allows you to access a creature's thoughts as part of its effect through a mystic feature, its ki point cost is reduced by 2.

3.name: Perennial Vision
description: Also starting at 3rd level, once on your turn (no action required) you can access the senses of a creature you are telepathically linked with.  You see through its eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, when you return to your own senses.  While perceiving through another creature's senses, you gain the benefits of any special senses possessed by that creature.  You are not blinded to your own surroundings so long as you can still see your own body through the borrowed senses.

6.name: Incisive Intuition
description: Starting at 6th level, once per turn, you can learn the intentions of a creature you deal damage to or force to make a saving throw by reading splinters of scattered thought.  Until the start of your next turn, that target has disadvantage on any attack roll that targets a creature that forms a part of your telepathic link.

11.name: Overseer
description: Starting at 11th level, your watchful mind keeps a vigil over your companions.  Whenever you or a creature of your choice you can currently communicate with via your telepathic link makes an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, the creature gains a bonus to the saving throw equal to your Psionic ability modifier (minimum of +1).  You must be conscious to grant this bonus.

20.name: Omniscient
description: At 20th level, through your mind's eye, you witness all.  You gain truesight out to the maximum range of your focus field.  Creatures within that range cannot have advantage on attacks against you or benefit from cover from you.  You are aware of where they are and their surface thoughts at all times.

subclasses.name: Witness Discipline

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Hunter's Prey
description: Starting at 1st level, you may use your bonus action to mark a single creature as your prey. You must be able to see or hear this creature, or succeed on a Wisdom (Survival) check to track it, the difficulty of which is determined by the Dungeon Master based on your access to tracks or other clues. You can also mark prey when you roll initiative, without expending a bonus action.

You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks to track your prey, as well as Wisdom (Perception) checks to find them. In addition, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to the target whenever you hit it with a weapon attack. This damage increases to 1d8 at 7th level, 1d10 at 13th level, and 1d12 at 19th level.
You can have only one creature marked as your prey at a time. This designation lasts until your next long rest, or until you mark a new creature as your prey.
At certain Nomad levels, the duration of your Hunter's Prey mark increases: at 6th level (8 hours), 10th level (24 hours), 14th level (1 week), and finally at 17th level (indefinite).

1.name: Favored Terrain
description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. At 1st level, choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark.

When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain or the creatures that dwell there, you have advantage on the check if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. When in that terrain, you can ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain, and all enemies that attempt to track you by non-magical means have disadvantage. You can also move stealthily at a normal pace.

1.name: Survivalist Knacks
description: In the wild, you have gathered bits of primal knowledge that bolster your exploration, hunting, and tracking skills, known as Survivalist Knacks. At 1st level, you learn two Knacks of your choice.
You learn additional Knacks as you gain Nomad levels, as shown in the Knacks Known column on the Nomad table.
Each time you gain a level in this class, you can choose one Survivalist Knack you know and replace it with another Knack of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites.

2.name: Fighting Style
description: At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

2.name: Wild Exploits
description: At 2nd level, you have picked up techniques in your travels to enhance your survival skills, both in the wild and in combat.

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: The Fighter table shows how many Exploit Dice you have to perform your Wild Exploits. To use an Exploit, you must expend one of these Dice. You can only use one Exploit per attack, ability check, or saving throw and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.
Your Exploit Dice begin as d4s, and increase in size as you gain levels in this class, as indicated in the Nomad table.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: At 2nd level, choose two Wild Exploits of 1st-degree. These become your Mastered Exploits. You gain more Mastered Exploits as you gain levels in this class, as shown on the Nomad table. When you gain new Mastered Exploits, they must be of a degree less than or equal to half of your Degree Limit (rounded up, minimum of 1st-degree). This limit can be seen in parentheses next to your Degree Limit on the Nomad table.

You can use each of your Mastered Exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can choose to exchange one of your Mastered Exploits with a different Wild Exploit for which you meet the requirements.

subFeatures.name: Exploits Prepared
description: At 2nd level, when you finish a long rest, you can prepare a number of Wild Exploits equal to your exploit modifier + half your Nomad level (minimum 1). To prepare an Exploit it must be of a degree less than or equal to your Degree Limit.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: If an Exploit requires a creature to make a saving throw, your Exploit saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

3.name: Natural Healer
description: Your experience surviving in the harsh wilderness has taught you how to identify and make use of medicinal plants. Starting at 2nd level, you may spend 1 hour a day searching a natural area for helpful herbs and fungi; this can count as part of a short or long rest. Roll a Wisdom (Survival) check against the DC corresponding to your environment. You have advantage on this check in your favored terrain.

Natural Healer DC
Environment DC
Forest, Grassland, Swamp 10
Mountain, Coast 15
Arctic, Desert, Underdark 20

On a success, you find enough herbs to produce a number of healing poultices equal to your Wisdom modifier. You must have an herbalism kit to produce these items, which must be done at the end of your search time as part of the same hour. On a failure, you can only produce a number equal to half your Wisdom modifier (rounded down).

Healing poultices are non-magical items which can be applied by any creature with Survival or Medicine proficiency to itself or an adjacent creature, using an action on their turn. The target creature regains hit points equal to 1d6 for every two levels you have in this class (rounded down, as shown in the Nomad table) and loses the poisoned condition. The healing poultice is consumed by this use. Healing poultices lose their potency 24 hours after being produced.

5.name: Martial Superiority
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Moreover, you can take the Dash or Disengage action in place of one of those attacks.

5.name: Martial Talent
description: At 5th level, you become further specialized in a form of combat characteristic of nomads. Choose one of the following options:
Double your ranged or thrown weapons' short and long ranges. (Attacking at long range still imposes disadvantage).
If you are wielding only one melee weapon and use it to hit your prey, you can choose to reroll your Hunter's Prey damage. You must take the new result.
When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can make two offhand attacks as part of the Attack action.

6.name: Roving
description: At 6th level, your walking speed increases by 5 feet, and you gain a climbing speed and swimming speed equal to your walking speed. Your speeds increase by an additional 5 feet while in your favored terrain.

7.name: Hunter's Instinct
description: Starting at 7th level, your sharply honed instincts allow you to act quickly in the face of danger. You add a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Wisdom modifier.

9.name: Favored Terrain Master
description: At 9th level, your mastery of your favored terrain grants you benefits even outside of it. You gain a benefit based on your favored terrain type. If you have multiple favored terrains, you gain the benefit associated with each type.
You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold.
Your swimming speed increases by 20 feet and you can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes.
You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme heat.
Your climbing speed increases by 20 feet and you ignore penalties to Dexterity (Stealth) checks from wearing medium armor.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
Your climbing speed increases by 20 feet and you have resistance to damage from falling.
You gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison.
You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, increase its range by 30 feet.
You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold.
Your swimming speed increases by 20 feet and you can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes.
You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme heat.

You gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison.
You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, increase its range by 30 feet.

10.name: Nature's Veil
description: At 10th level, you can add your proficiency bonus to Stealth checks made in natural terrain, or double your proficiency bonus instead if you were already proficient in Stealth, and you have advantage on Stealth checks made in your favored terrain. You can also Hide as a bonus action in any terrain. You cannot be tracked by non-magical means in any terrain, unless you wish to leave a trail.

13.name: Tireless Endurance
description: At 13th level, you persist through pain, exhaustion, and even near-death. As an action, you can give yourself a number of temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point). You can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Whenever you finish a short rest, your exhaustion level, if any, is decreased by 1.
In addition, you have advantage on death saving throws.

17.name: Split Focus
description: Starting at 17th level, you can focus on two foes at once, hunting both of them down. When you mark prey with Hunter's Prey, you can pick up to two creatures as your prey, and you can have two active prey simultaneously.

18.name: Killer Instinct
description: Beginning at 18th level, you can strike the most evasive of enemies, even those hiding behind obscured visibility or magical protection. Your attack rolls against creatures marked as your prey ignore disadvantage. You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't both blinded and deafened.

20.name: Apex Predator
description: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Add a bonus equal to your Wisdom modifier to all attack and damage rolls made against creatures marked as your prey.

The Beast Master creed embodies friendship between the civilized races and the beasts of the world. United in focus, beast and nomad work as one to fight the monstrous foes that threaten civilization and the wilderness alike. Emulating the Beast Master archetype means committing yourself to this ideal, working in partnership with an animal as its companion and friend.

3.name: Nomad's Companion
description: At 3rd level, you gain a beast companion that accompanies you on your adventures and is trained to fight alongside you. It is able to understand simple speech and commands. The beast grows along with you, using your proficiency bonus (PB) as its own. The beast can be created using the Beast Companion rules. Choose traits that fit the type of creature you wish to bond with, or use one of the example stat blocks.

In combat, the beast acts during your turn and moves at your command. It can use its reaction and bonus action (if applicable) on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. You can instead sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the beast to use an Attack, Dash, Disengage or Help action. If you are incapacitated, the beast can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

Like a player character, the beast becomes unconscious at 0 hit points and makes death saving throws. If the beast has died within the last hour, you can spend 10 minutes using a healing poultice to revive it with half the hit points normally provided by the healing poultice. You cannot revive the beast again in this way until you and your companion have completed a long rest.
The beast also follows all resting rules that apply to player characters, including the ability to roll Hit Dice to regain hit points on a short rest.
If your companion has an effect that requires a saving throw, its DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

subFeatures.name: Step 1: Size
description: Choose your companion's size from Tiny, Small, or Medium.

subFeatures.name: Step 2: Ability Scores
description: Choose your companion's ability score array from Bulky, Middling, or Light.  Your choice determines its ability Strength, Dexterity, and Constituion scores, its Armor Class, its hit points, and the size of its hit die.
Your companion's ability scores are as follows, and it has hit points equal to 6 + six times your nomad level.  Its hit dice are d10s.

subFeatures.name: Step 3: Speeds
description: Choose your companion's speed array from Amphibious, Aquatic, Burrower, Climber, Flyer, or Terrestrial.  Your choice determines its walking speed, as well as any additional speeds it may have.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a swimming speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 5 feet and a swimming speed of 60 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a burrowing speed of 10 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a climbing speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 10 feet and a flying speed of 60 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 40 feet and a swimming speed of 10 feet.

subFeatures.name: Step 4: Natural Weapons
description: Choose two of the following natural weapons for your companion to be capable of using.  Note that it must have the proper anatomy to perform an attack with a given natural weapon.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d8 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a bite attack, it can attempt to grapple the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing slashing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a claw attack, it can make another claw attack as a bonus action.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its claws' attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a pummel attack, it can attempt to shove the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If the target fails its saving throw against Envenom, it takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its stinger's attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 10 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a ranged attack with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 60 feet.  On a hit, the target is restrained by webbing.  As an action, the restrained target can make a Strength ability check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing has an AC of 10, 5 hit points, vulnerability to fire damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Step 5: Skills
description: Choose two skills from Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, and Survival for your companion to be proficient in.

subFeatures.name: Step 6: Special Features
description: Choose one of each of the following special features for your companion to have.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on hearing.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on sight.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on smell.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on its sense of touch.
Your companion has blindsight out to 60 feet as long as it isn't deafened or silenced.
Your companion can breathe water as well as air.
Your companion doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.
Your companion can hold its breath for up to 1 hour.
With a 10-foot running start, your companion can long jump up to 25 feet.
Your companion does not need limbs to walk, swim or climb.
Your companion can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Your companion's long jump is up to 10 feet and its high jump is up to 5 feet, with or without a running start.

Your companion's speeds all increase by 5 feet.
Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.

Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.
Your companion has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that has less than half its maximum hit points.

If your companion moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage, or an extra 2d6 piercing damage if your companion hit with a Gore attack. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion succeeds on an Athletics check to grapple, it deals additional bludgeoning damage to the target equal to its Strength modifier.

If your companion flies or swims at least 30 feet downward toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.
Your companion can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

If your companion succeeds on a Bite or Sting attack, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. An affected target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.
Your companion has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the beast's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

If your companion makes a long jump at least 10 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion takes damage less than 3 + your ranger level that would reduce it to 0 hit points, it can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.
Your companion can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your nomad level.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

Your companion can use a bonus action to give itself advantage on Constitution saving throws against being poisoned or paralyzed for 1 minute, and gain temporary hit points equal to half your nomad level (rounded up).
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

3.name: Animal Whisperer
description: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in Animal Handling. If you were already proficient in Animal Handling, double your proficiency bonus for any ability checks made using this skill.

7.name: Exceptional Training
description: Beginning at 7th level, your beast companion can use the Help action instead of the Dodge action on any turn in which you did not give it a command.

11.name: Bestial Fury
description: Starting at 11th level, when you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the beast can make two attacks.

15.name: Share Prey
description: Beginning at 15th level, your beast companion shares the benefits of Hunter's Prey when attacking or tracking any creature you have marked as your prey.

subclasses.name: Beast Master Creed

description: Known for their unequaled expertise with knots, binders prefer to capture their foes alive, but restrained. While they do not always land the killing blow, they are adept at hindering the movements of their foes. So long as they have their trusty rope, they can bind anything.

3.name: Knot Expert
description: By 3rd level, you are an expert with knots, nets, restraints, and rope of all kinds. Your training grants you the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency in Sleight of Hand and weaver's tools, and whenever you make a check related to tying a knot you add double your proficiency bonus to your roll.
  • Whenever you tie a knot, the DC to undo that knot equals your Nomad level + your Dexterity modifier.
  • When you use a net, its DC equals your Exploit save DC.
  • Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can transform 25-feet of rope into one net, a simple snare, or a trap from an Exploit you know.

3.name: Binding Restraints
description: At 3rd level, you are adept at restraining foes in combat. As a bonus action while you are holding at least 10 feet of rope or a net, you can attempt to restrain one creature within your reach. You force one creature you touch to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it is restrained by the rope or net.
Your Hunter's Prey has disadvantage on this saving throw, but for each size the creature is above Medium, it gains a +5 bonus to its Dexterity saving throw to resist this restraint.
A creature can make a Strength or Dexterity check as an action, escaping from the restraints on a successful check.

7.name: Quick Knots
description: At 7th level, you restrain your foes with ease. When you use your Binding Restraints feature on a creature that is currently grappled, it automatically fails its saving throw.
Moreover, your Hunter's Prey has disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws it makes to escape your nets, any trap you create with an Exploit, or your Binding Restraints feature.

7.name: Roper
description: Also at 7th level, you are always prepared to restrain foes. During the course of a long rest, you can spend 1 hour to craft a number of feet of rope equal to 10 times your Nomad level, so long as you have access to a knife and natural materials.

11.name: Cull the Bound
description: Starting at 11th level, once on your turn when you hit your Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack while it is grappled, restrained, or its speed is 0, you can choose for your attack to be an automatic critical hit.

15.name: Master of Ropes
description: By 15th level, you are an unequaled master of restraints. Whenever you could make an attack, you an use your Binding Restraints on a creature within reach, so long as you have enough nets or rope.
Additionally, creatures only gain a +5 bonus on their Dexterity saving throw to resist your Binding Restraints for each size they are above Large.

subclasses.name: Binder Creed

description: While you are as at home in the wilds as any nomad, your hunt has brought you into jungles of brick and mortar, where you stalk the most dangerous game: people. You have learned how to navigate cities and towns which have set themselves apart from the natural world; learned to blend in among its citizens and ferret out their secrets. You understand that civilization, after all, is simply another form of nature to master.

3.name: City Secrets
description: You know the secret patterns and flow to cities and can find passages through the urban sprawl that others would miss. When you are not in combat, you (and companions you lead) can travel between any two locations in the city twice as fast as your speed would normally allow.

3.name: Vagabond
description: At 3rd level, you gain a unique type of favored terrain: urban, characterized by artificial buildings and streets. This does not count against your maximum favored terrains.

Because of the dearth of native plant life, you cannot gather herbs for Natural Healer in this terrain; however, you can always find a local herbalist or apothecary who can sell you the necessary herbs to produce your healing poultices; once per day, you can produce up to your Wisdom modifier as part of a short rest, at the cost of 1 gp per healing poultice (the combined cost of the requisite herbs).
In addition, you gain the City Secrets feature from the urchin background in the Player's Handbook.

3.name: Gumshoe
description: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Investigation skill. If you were already proficient, your proficiency bonus is doubled for ability checks made with this skill. You also have proficiency with thieves' tools and disguise kits.

7.name: Paranoid Vigilance
description: Surrounded by potential threats in close quarters, you are constantly on alert and ready to fight. Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on initiative rolls, and you are never surprised in combat. You also have advantage on attack rolls against creatures that are surprised.

9.name: Favored Terrain Master: Urban
description: You can hide while only lightly obscured, such as by fog or shadows, and urban environments are considered natural terrain for you.

11.name: Sneak Attacker
description: You strike without warning, dispatching your quarry before they can even see your face. Starting at 11th level, once per turn, you can deal an additional 2d6 damage to a creature with a weapon attack if you have advantage on the attack roll, or if a conscious ally is adjacent to your target and you do not have disadvantage.

15.name: Eye for an Eye
description: At 15th level, experienced in street violence, you respond to injury in kind. If you are hit with a weapon attack by a creature you can see, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against that creature if it is within range of a weapon you are holding.

subclasses.name: Bounty Hunter Creed

description: Briar knights adopt the branching thicket of the wild as their armor, demonstrating without question that every strike against them will come at a cost. They serve as bulwarks for the natural world, fighting against those who would despoil it with industry or dark magic.

3.name: Bramble Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to modify your armor to be a living bramble. Over the course of an hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can use an herbalism kit to affix thorny vines and branches to a set of armor, turning it into Bramble Armor. Bramble Armor has the following properties when worn by you:

• It is as a martial melee weapon with a reach of 5 feet, and on hit, the Bramble Armor deals piercing damage equal to your Exploit Die + your Strength modifier.
  • When you use your action to use an Exploit, you can use a bonus action on your turn to make a single Bramble Armor attack.
  • When you successfully initiate a grapple, the grappled creature takes damage equal to your Exploit Die.

3.name: Thorny Grip
description: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in Athletics. Additionally, whenever a creature would provoke an attack of opportunity from you, you can attempt to grapple that creature.

7.name: Overgrowth
description: Starting at 7th level, while you are wearing Bramble Armor, when you move within 5 feet of a creature for the first time on a turn, you can choose to cause thorny branches to lash out at them, dealing piercing damage equal to your Exploit ability modifier.

11.name: Agonizing Thorns
description: Starting at 11th level, when you cause a creature to be grappled or restrained, that creature takes piercing damage equal to your Exploit Die at the start of each of its turns while it remains grappled or restrained.
Additionally, you ignore resistance to piercing damage.

15.name: Bramble Bulwark
description: Starting at 15th level, as an action, you can plant a thicket of brambles in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you that rapidly grows to fill a 10-foot cube. A creature that enters the cube for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there takes piercing damage equal to two rolls of your Exploit Die. Additionally, the thicket can be used as three-quarters cover, and ranged attacks made against creatures within the thicket or that pass through it automatically miss.
The thicket has 11 AC and 25 hit points, immunity to psychic damage, and vulnerability to fire damage. It lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again.
Additionally, any damage dealt by features of this subclass increases to two rolls of your Exploit Die.

subclasses.name: Briar Knight Creed

description: Gloom stalkers are at home in the darkest places: deep under the earth, in gloomy alleyways, in primeval forests, and wherever else the light dims. Most folk enter such places with trepidation, but a gloom stalker ventures boldly into the darkness, seeking to ambush threats before they can reach the broader world. Such nomads are often found in the Underdark, but they will go any place where evil lurks in the shadows.

3.name: Dread Ambusher
description: At 3rd level, you master the art of the ambush. At the start of your first turn of each combat, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, which lasts until the end of that turn. If you take the Attack action on that turn, you can make one additional weapon attack as part of that action. If that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d8 damage of the weapon's damage type.

3.name: Umbral Sight
description: At 3rd level, your eyes have become accustomed to heavy darkness. You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.
You are also adept at evading creatures that rely on darkvision. While in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on Stealth checks to hide from any creature that relies on darkvision to see you.

7.name: Shadow Sense
description: Your senses are finely attuned to detect nearby foes even when blinded or in magical darkness. At 7th level, you gain blindsight with a range of 10 feet, or an additional 10 feet if you already have blindsight.

In addition, you can stand still, focus, and extend your senses further, picking up on the subtlest vibrations, even through walls. As an action, you can grant yourself tremorsense within a 30 foot radius. Moving or taking damage causes you to lose this sense. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all uses upon completing a long rest.

11.name: Stalker's Flurry
description: At 11th level, you learn to attack with such unexpected speed that you can turn a miss into another strike. Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack, you can make another weapon attack as part of the same action.

15.name: Shadowy Dodge
description: Starting at 15th level, you can dodge in unforeseen ways, making expert use of the shadows around you. Whenever a creature makes an attack roll against you and doesn't have advantage on the roll, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on it. You must use this feature before you know the outcome of the attack roll.

subclasses.name: Gloom Stalker Creed

description: You have dedicated yourself to hunting down creatures of the night and wielders of grim magic. A grim warden seeks out vampires, dragons, evil fey, fiends, and other magical threats. Trained to resist such monsters' supernatural powers, slayers are experts at unearthing and defeating mighty, mystical foes.

3.name: Warden's Rite
description: By 3rd level, you have passed through the Warden's Rite, an unholy alchemical ritual that suffuses your blood with the sinister power of monsters. You change in the ways listed below, which cannot be reversed:

• You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies and in Arcana and Religion.
  • Your hit point maximum increases by 3, and increases by 1 again each time you gain a level in this class.

3.name: Crimson Mark
description: You can use your sinister blood magic to empower the mark on your foes. Starting at 3rd level, whenever you mark a creature as your quarry, you can make a blood sacrifice. When you do, you reduce your current and maximum hit points by one roll of your Hunter's Prey Die. Any reductions to your maximum hit points by this feature are undone at the end of your next long rest.
For the duration, you can choose for the bonus damage of Hunter's Prey to be necrotic. Necrotic damage dealt in this way ignores resistance and treats immunity as resistance.
Finally, when you deal necrotic damage to your quarry in this way, it cannot regain hit points for the next minute.

7.name: Dark Augmentation
description: By 7th level, the sinister magic in enhances your physical capabilities. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. Also, whenever you make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability check, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to one roll of your Exploit Die.

11.name: Sinister Resilience
description: Starting at 11th level, the dark magic that flows in your blood grants you defenses against evil magicks. You gain resistance to necrotic damage, and when you reduce your hit points with Crimson Mark, you roll your Hunter's Prey Die twice and use the lower result.

11.name: Greater Crimson Mark
description: Also at 11th level, powerful blood magic infuses all of your strikes. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can deal an additional 1d10 necrotic damage to it.

15.name: Sanguine Mastery
description: At 15th level, the magic of your Warden's Rite manifests its full potential. You cannot be frightened, and you are always under the effects of protection from evil and good while you are conscious.

subclasses.name: Grim Warden Creed

description: Herbalists are masters of foraging, able to quickly spot and identify useful plants and craft potent medicines from them.

3.name: Forager
description: At 3rd level, you halve the time needed to find herbs using Natural Healer to thirty minutes per day, and the Natural Healer DC of all terrain types is decreased for you by 5. The number of healing poultices you can produce per day increases to 2 + your Wisdom modifier, or half that number on a failed Survival check (rounded down).

3.name: Herbal Adept
description: Starting at 3rd level, add your Wisdom modifier to the healing provided by healing poultices you produce. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any skill check you make with an herbalist's kit, and you have proficiency in the Medicine skill if you did not already. If you were already proficient, double your proficiency bonus when you make a Medicine check.

7.name: Resilient Constitution
description: At 7th level, your experience surviving on wild forage in the wilderness has made you hardy. You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws, and have advantage on saving throws against disease and poison.

7.name: Poisoner
description: Starting at 7th level, you can use your herbalism kit to craft poisons, as though it were a poisoner's kit.

11.name: Combat Healer
description: You can heal and fight almost simultaneously. Starting at 11th level, when you use your action to apply a healing poultice, you can make one weapon attack as part of the same action.

15.name: Herbal Master
description: Your medicines have become more advanced and versatile, even soothing the mind as well as the body. Starting at 15th level, if your healing poultices are applied to a creature that is poisoned, paralyzed, blinded, deafened, frightened or charmed, any and all of those conditions immediately end on that creature.

subclasses.name: Herbalist Creed

description: You are first and foremost an explorer, never satisfied staying long in the same place, always seeking new experiences and challenges - even those beyond your world.

3.name: Adaptive Adventurer
description: Starting at 3rd level, you are able to adapt to new environments incredibly quickly. As a bonus action, you can change your favored terrain to any terrain type you have spent at least one day in, replacing an existing favored terrain.

You can also use your bonus action to change your favored enemy to any type of creature you have fought and marked as your prey with the Hunter's Prey feature within the last day, replacing an existing favored enemy.
You regain use of each feature after completing a long rest.

3.name: Exploit Weakness
description: You quickly become familiar with certain enemies' weak spots. At 3rd level, once per turn, you deal an additional 1d8 damage when you hit a favored enemy.

7.name: Planar Wanderer
description: At 7th level, you can even adapt to otherworldly environments. You gain an additional favored terrain, which does not count against your maximum, and access to planar terrain types: Upper Planes, Lower Planes, Feywild, Shadowfell, Mechanus, Limbo and the Elemental Chaos. As usual, you must have spent at least one day in one of these terrain types before designating it as your favored terrain.
The Natural Healer DC for all planar terrains is 25.
When you gain the Favored Terrain Master feature at 9th level, add the following to the list of potential benefits:

7.name: Planar Step
description: You learn to briefly shift through interplanar space. Starting at 7th level, you can cast the Misty Step spell a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
You gain resistance to one of the following damage types of your choice: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed.
You gain resistance to psychic damage.
You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
You gain proficiency with tinker's tools and thieves' tools, and you add double your proficiency bonus to your checks with these tools.
You gain resistance to necrotic damage.
You gain resistance to radiant damage.

11.name: Slayer
description: At 11th level, you may make an additional weapon attack when you take the Attack action against a favored enemy.

15.name: Key to the Cosmos
description: At 15th level, your planar travels have caused your soul to become attuned to the weave between worlds. You can cast Misty Step at will; additionally, you can cast Dimension Door once per long rest, and either Teleport or Plane Shift once every seven long rests. You still need to provide all necessary spell components.

subclasses.name: Horizon Walker Creed

description: The hunter is the most classic of nomadic creeds. Whether you stand as a self-sufficient outlander or as the bulwark between civilization and the terrors of the wild, you excel in specialized techniques for taking down your prey.

3.name: Hunter's Eye
description: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Perception skill. If you were already proficient in Perception, double your proficiency bonus for any ability checks made using this skill.

3.name: Hunter's Quarry
description: At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.

Your tenacity can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature.

Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.

7.name: Defensive Tactics
description: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage.
When a creature hits you with an attack, you gain a +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.
You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

11.name: Multiattack
description: At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
When you only attack one creature on your turn, you can make one additional weapon attack as a bonus action.

Once per turn, when you make a ranged weapon attack, you can make one additional ranged weapon attack against a creature within 10 feet of your target. Additionally, you can apply your Hunter's Prey damage when you hit any creature within 10 feet of your prey with a ranged weapon attack, as long as you also attack your prey on that turn.

Once per turn, when you make a melee weapon attack, you can use your momentum to sweep through multiple creatures. Make one additional melee weapon attack against every creature within 5 feet, aside from your original target.

15.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
description: At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.

When you are subjected to an effect, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or a lightning bolt spell, that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature (other than itself) of your choice.
When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.

subclasses.name: Hunter Creed

description: Many nomads disdain the idea of riding an animal companion, but for some this is the ultimate expression of the bond between nomad and beast. Whether charging over a hillside or riding wild and free across the plains, outriders and their mounts fight and live as one.

3.name: Bonded Mount
description: At 3rd level, you gain a Medium or Large beast companion, typically but not exclusively a horse. Use the Beast Companion rules to create it. The companion must not use the Light array or Flyer speed. Your companion is trained to understand and obey your commands and uses your proficiency bonus (PB).

Your companion acts on your turn and moves at your command. It can use its reaction and bonus action (if applicable) on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action, unless you use a bonus action on your turn to command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage or Help action; you must be mounted to command it in this way. If you are incapacitated, the beast can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

Like a player character, the beast becomes unconscious at 0 hit points and makes death saving throws. If the beast has died within the last hour, you can spend 10 minutes using a healing poultice to revive it with half the hit points normally provided by the healing poultice. You cannot revive the beast again in this way until you and your companion have completed a long rest.
The beast also follows all resting rules that apply to player characters, including the ability to roll Hit Dice to regain hit points on a short rest.
If your companion has an effect that requires a saving throw, its DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier.

subFeatures.name: Step 1: Size
description: Choose your companion's size from Medium or Large.

subFeatures.name: Step 2: Ability Scores
description: Choose your companion's ability score array from Bulky or Middling.  Your choice determines its ability Strength, Dexterity, and Constituion scores, its Armor Class, its hit points, and the size of its hit die.
Your companion's ability scores are as follows, and it has hit points equal to 6 + six times your nomad level.  Its hit dice are d10s.
<table><thead><tr><th>STR</th><th>DEX</th><th>CON</th><th>INT

YYour companion's ability scores are as follows, and it has hit points equal to 5 + five times your nomad level.  Its hit dice are d8s.
