WISCHA14 + PB12 + PB12 + PB612 + PB11

subFeatures.name: Step 3: Speeds
description: Choose your companion's speed array from Amphibious, Aquatic, Burrower, Climber, or Terrestrial.  Your choice determines its walking speed, as well as any additional speeds it may have.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a swimming speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 5 feet and a swimming speed of 60 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a burrowing speed of 10 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a climbing speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 40 feet and a swimming speed of 10 feet.

subFeatures.name: Step 4: Natural Weapons
description: Choose two of the following natural weapons for your companion to be capable of using.  Note that it must have the proper anatomy to perform an attack with a given natural weapon.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d8 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a bite attack, it can attempt to grapple the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing slashing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a claw attack, it can make another claw attack as a bonus action.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its claws' attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a pummel attack, it can attempt to shove the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If the target fails its saving throw against Envenom, it takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its stinger's attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 10 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a ranged attack with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 60 feet.  On a hit, the target is restrained by webbing.  As an action, the restrained target can make a Strength ability check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing has an AC of 10, 5 hit points, vulnerability to fire damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d8 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a bite attack, it can attempt to grapple the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing slashing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a claw attack, it can make another claw attack as a bonus action.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its claws' attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a pummel attack, it can attempt to shove the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If the target fails its saving throw against Envenom, it takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its stinger's attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 10 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a ranged attack with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 60 feet.  On a hit, the target is restrained by webbing.  As an action, the restrained target can make a Strength ability check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing has an AC of 10, 5 hit points, vulnerability to fire damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Step 5: Skills
description: Choose two skills from Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, and Survival for your companion to be proficient in.

subFeatures.name: Step 6: Special Features
description: Choose one of each of the following special features for your companion to have.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on hearing.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on sight.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on smell.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on its sense of touch.
Your companion has blindsight out to 60 feet as long as it isn't deafened or silenced.
Your companion can breathe water as well as air.
Your companion can hold its breath for up to 1 hour.
With a 10-foot running start, your companion can long jump up to 25 feet.
Your companion does not need limbs to walk, swim or climb.
Your companion can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Your companion's long jump is up to 10 feet and its high jump is up to 5 feet, with or without a running start.
Your companion has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it prone.
Your companion's speeds all increase by 5 feet.
Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on hearing.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on sight.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on smell.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on its sense of touch.
Your companion has blindsight out to 60 feet as long as it isn't deafened or silenced.
Your companion can breathe water as well as air.
Your companion can hold its breath for up to 1 hour.
With a 10-foot running start, your companion can long jump up to 25 feet.
Your companion does not need limbs to walk, swim or climb.
Your companion can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Your companion's long jump is up to 10 feet and its high jump is up to 5 feet, with or without a running start.
Your companion has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it prone.
Your companion's speeds all increase by 5 feet.
Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.
Your companion has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that has less than half its maximum hit points.

If your companion moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage, or an extra 2d6 piercing damage if your companion hit with a Gore attack. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion succeeds on an Athletics check to grapple, it deals additional bludgeoning damage to the target equal to its Strength modifier.

If your companion flies or swims at least 30 feet downward toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.
Your companion can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

If your companion succeeds on a Bite or Sting attack, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. An affected target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.
Your companion has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the beast's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

If your companion makes a long jump at least 10 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion takes damage less than 3 + your nomad level that would reduce it to 0 hit points, it can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.
Your companion can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your nomad level.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

Your companion can use a bonus action to give itself advantage on Constitution saving throws against being poisoned or paralyzed for 1 minute, and gain temporary hit points equal to half your nomad level (rounded up).
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

3.name: Born to Ride
description: Starting at 3rd level, your mastery as a rider becomes apparent. You gain proficiency with the Animal Handling skill, and you can double your proficiency bonus for this skill if you were already proficient. You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. If you fall off your mount and descend no more than 10 feet, you can land on your feet if you're not incapacitated.
Finally, mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed.

7.name: Nomad's Charge
description: Starting at 7th level, you use your mount's momentum to deadly effect. If your mount moves at least 20 feet uninterrupted while you are riding it and you take the Attack action, the first of your attacks to hit that turn deals an additional 1d8 damage.

11.name: Trampling Charge
description: Starting at 11th level, you can spur your mount to plow through whole groups of enemies. Use your action to command your mount to move in a straight line up to its speed. It can move through occupied spaces, which count as difficult terrain. All creatures in its path must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + its Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus) or take 6d6 bludgeoning damage, or half as much on a successful save. A Huge or larger enemy blocks the path of the charge but still takes damage. This movement does not trigger attacks of opportunity.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all uses after you and your mount complete a long rest.

15.name: Legendary Bond
description: At 15th level, the bond between you and your mount has grown so strong that you instinctively understand each other. Once per turn, you can command your mount to Attack, Dash, Disengage or Help as part of your action, instead of using your bonus action.

subclasses.name: Outrider Creed

description: Some nomads prefer to let their quarry come to them, setting cunning traps for unsuspecting prey. Trappers use snares not only to catch prey, but also to track them, and to alert themselves to approaching danger. Skilled trappers can even rig together a half-readied snare in combat, turning a simple melee into a minefield.

3.name: Snarecrafter
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can efficiently craft simple traps. When you use Set Minor Trap, you can roll a d4 and add it to your roll instead of expending an Exploit Die. At 11th level in this class, this bonus becomes a d6.

3.name: Trap Finder
description: Your expertise in making traps makes them easy to spot for you. Starting at 3rd level, you have advantage on Perception or Investigation checks to find hidden traps.

7.name: Ensnaring Weapons
description: Starting at 7th level, you can make an attack with a net as a bonus action. You also gain proficiency with bolas. The escape DC for bolas and nets becomes your snare DC.

7.name: Quick Snares
description: Also at 7th level, when you use Set Minor Trap, Set Greater Trap, or Set Advanced Trap, you can set the trap as part of the same action you use to create it.

11.name: Advanced Snarecrafter
description: Starting at 11th level, you can craft better traps easily. When you use Set Greater Trap, you can roll a d4 and add it to your roll instead of expending an Exploit Die. At 17th level in this class, this bonus becomes a d6.
You also learn Set Expert Trap, but it doesn't count against your total number of Exploits Prepared.

15.name: Snare Master
description: Starting at 15th level, once per turn when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a use of Set Minor Trap or Set Greater Trap.

subclasses.name: Trapper Creed

description: All nomads have a deep connection to the wilderness, but wardens delve even further, into the realm of primal mysticism. Wardens are often trained by a druidic circle, in order to serve as the first line of defense between the civilized world and the mysteries of the wild.

3.name: Spellcasting
description: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: You learn three cantrips from the Primal spell list: Shillelagh and two other cantrips of your choice. You learn another Primal cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Warden Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You know three 1st-level spells of your choice from the Primal spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Warden Spellcasting table shows when you learn more Primal spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be a transmutation or conjuration spell of your choice, and must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The spells you learn at 8th, 14th, and 20th level can come from any school of magic.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the spells you know with another spell of your choice from the Primal spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, and it must be a transmutation or conjuration spell, unless you're replacing the spell you gained at 3rd, 8th, 14th, or 20th level from any school of magic.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Primal spells, since they are derived from your instinctive connection to primal magic.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a primal focus as a spellcasting focus for your Primal spells.

3.name: Druidic Warrior
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast the Shillelagh cantrip, you can target up to two quarterstaves or clubs that you are holding. The duration of the spell increases to 1 hour. If you are holding a quarterstaff affected by shillelagh in two hands, the damage die increases to a d12.
In addition, when you hit your marked prey with a spell attack roll from a warden spell, add your Hunter's Prey damage as you would with a weapon attack.

7.name: Primeval Awareness
description: Beginning at 7th level, you can use your action to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute, you can sense whether the following types of creatures are present within 1 mile of you (or within up to 6 miles if you are in your favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, undead, and your favored enemy if it's not already on the list; how many there are; and roughly how close they are, though not their exact location.

In addition, you learn Beast Sense and Speak with Animals, and can cast either without expending a spell slot. Once you cast either spell with this feature, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest.

11.name: Vanish
description: Starting at 11th level, you can draw on the powers of nature to hide yourself from view briefly. As a bonus action, you can magically become invisible, along with any equipment you are wearing or carrying, for 1 minute in non-natural terrain, 10 minutes in natural terrain, or one hour in your favored terrain. The effect ends if you take damage or make an attack.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

15.name: Primal Communion
description: Beginning at 15th level, you learn Speak with Plants, Locate Creature, and Commune with Nature, and you can cast each one once without expending a spell slot. Once you cast one of these spells with this feature, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Warden Creed

description: While most nomads have some skill with animals, those who pursue the life of a Wrangler are true masters at taming wild beasts. Drawing upon their intimate understanding of animal behavior, they tame and guide all sorts of fantastical animals. Rugged and wild, Wranglers are always on the hunt for ever more strange and exotic creatures to tame and befriend.

3.name: Beast Tamer
description: Starting at 3rd level, your intimate understanding of animal behaviours and habits grants you insight into how they will act.  You gain the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency in the Athletics and Animal Handling skills, and you double your proficiency bonus for checks made with them.
  • Whenever you make an ability check to grapple, climb, wrestle, or subdue your quarry, you have advantage on the roll.
  • As an action, you can attempt to soothe a beast you can see within 30 feet of you that is your quarry. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or become charmed by you for 1 minute. You must maintain concentration on this effect, as if concentrating on a spell. The target can repeat its saving throw whenever it takes damage, ending the effect on itself on a success. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

7.name: Bring to Heel
description: Starting at 7th level, you can bend creatures of the wild to your will.  Whenever a beast charmed by you that can see or hear you makes a saving throw to end the condition, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on their saving throw.

You can also command the monsters you tame. Any beast charmed by you acts during your turn for the duration of that charm effect. If you are within 30 feet of the charmed creature and it can hear you, you can use an action to command it to take one of the actions from its stat block.

11.name: Monster Tamer
description: Starting at 11th level, your ability to tame and train creatures is near-supernatural in scope.  You can use your Beast Tamer feature to attempt to charm a celestial, draogn, fey, fiend, giant, plant, or ooze that has an Intelligence score less than or equal to your Nomad level.
Also, you can command any creature that is charmed by you to take an action from its stat block with a bonus action, so long as that creature is within 30 feet and can hear you.

15.name: Wrangler of Legends
description: Starting at 15th level, once you charm a creature, there is little it can do to escape your influence.  When you use your Beast Tamer feature, your concentration cannot become broken as a result of taking damage.

Moreover, creatures that are charmed by you gain the benefits of your Hunter's Prey feature and any Knacks you know, and whenever such a creature makes a saving throw, you can use your reaction to grant advantage on the saving throw if the target can see or hear you.

subclasses.name: Wrangler Creed

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Oathbound
description: Each Sovereign Oath has a set of three Tenets which paladins of that Oath swear to uphold.  Should a paladin knowingly and willingly violate a Tenet of their Oath, they lose access to all paladin class features until they spend 1 hour making reparations appropirate to their oath.  This time can coincide with a short or long rest.

If a paladin consistently violates the Tenets of their Oath, they risk breaking their Oath completely.  Paladins that break their Oath in this way become Blackguards, Graceseekers, or Oathless, depending on the nature and severity of their transgressions.  Good paladins who turn evil become Blackguards, evil paladins who turn good become Graceseekers, and all others simply become Oathless.

subFeatures.name: Fervor
description: The power of your Sovereign Oath is represented by a pool of Fervor used to fuel various Paladin and Oath features. You have an amount of Fervor equal to your Paladin level + your Oath ability modifier (minimum of 0). You regain expended Fervor when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Oath Ability
description: Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) is your oath ability for your paladin features, since your power derives from the strength of your convictions.
Oath save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your oath ability modifier
Oath attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your oath ability modifier

1.name: Fighting Style
description: At 1st level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

2.name: Spellcasting
description: Starting at 2nd level, you learn to augment your martial prowess with spellcasting. Choose whether you are an Antipaladin, a Champion, a Hierophant, or a Warden.

traits.name: Antipaladin
description: You are a dark knight who serves an evil master or purpose. You seek only to bring destruction, pain, and sorrow to the world around you. Paladins who swear oaths of Conquest, Shadows, or Vengeance are often antipaladins, as are all Blackguards.

traits.name: Spellcasting
description: You have learned to draw on occult magic through ritual to cast spells as a warlock does.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Occult spells. To cast one of your Occult spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Occult spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the Occult spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Occult spells equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Occult spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: You use your oath ability for your spellcasting ability.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a occult focus as a spellcasting focus for your Occult spells.

traits.name: Champion
description: You are a strong knight who serves your people and your communities. You seek to bring happiness, freedom, or justice. Champiosn rarely serve any specific master, being more loyal to an ideal, a cause, or a group of people. Paladins who swear oaths of Freedom, Friendship, Glory, or the Unbreakable are often champions.

traits.name: Spellcasting
description: You have learned to draw on divine magic through prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Divine spells. To cast one of your Divine spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Divine spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the Divine spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Divine spells equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Divine spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: You use your oath ability for your spellcasting ability.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a divine focus as a spellcasting focus for your Divine spells.

traits.name: Hierophant
description: You are a white knight who serves a holy master, such as a deity, high priest, or nature spirit. Hierophants are often the most strictly oathbound of paladins. Paladins who swear oaths of the Ancients, Devotion, or Inquisition are often hierophants, as are all Graceseekers.

traits.name: Spellcasting
description: You have learned to draw on divine magic through prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Divine spells. To cast one of your Divine spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Divine spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the Divine spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Divine spells equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Divine spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: You use your oath ability for your spellcasting ability.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a divine focus as a spellcasting focus for your Divine spells.

traits.name: Warden
description: You are an esoteric knight who serves a to guard against the forces of the planes. Wardens are mysterious paladins who hold a variety of beliefs. Paladins who swear oaths of the Grim Hunt or the Watchers are often wardens.

traits.name: Spellcasting
description: You have learned to draw on divine magic through prayer to cast spells as a cleric does.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Paladin table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Divine spells. To cast one of your Divine spells of 1st level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Divine spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the Divine spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Divine spells equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + half your paladin level, rounded down (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Divine spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: You use your oath ability for your spellcasting ability.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use an arcane or divine focus as a spellcasting focus for your Divine spells.

2.name: Smite
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can imbue your strikes with the power of your conviction.  Choose one of the following features:

traits.name: Profane Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra necrotic damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

traits.name: Booming Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra thunder damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

traits.name: Divine Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra radiant damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

traits.name: Arcane Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can expend one spell slot to deal extra force damage to the target, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is 2d8 for a 1st-level spell slot, plus 1d8 for each spell level higher than 1st.

3.name: Oathbound Health
description: By 3rd level, the magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease. In addition, you cannot become intoxicated by consuming alcohol or narcotics.

3.name: Divine Regeneration
description: Also starting at 3rd level, during a short rest, you can recover spell slots of a combined level equal to your Charisma modifier. Once you use this feature you must complete a long rest before you can use this feature again

5.name: Aura Sense
description: Starting at 5th level, you can use an action to open your senses to powerful extraplanar good and evil.  For the next 10 minutes, you know the exact location and creature type of any aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, fiend, shapechanger, or undead within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover or hidden from divination magic.
Once you use your Aura Sense, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses left, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to use this feature again.

6.name: Aura of Protection
description: Starting at 6th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you are considered proficient in all saving throws so long as you are not incapacitated.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

9.name: Improved Oathbound Health
description: By 9th level, your health improves further.  You gain resistance to poison damage and immunity to the poisoned condition.

10.name: Aura of Courage
description: Starting at 10th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be frightened while you are conscious.  If a frightened creature enters your aura, the effect is suspended while they remain within it.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

11.name: Enhanced Smite
description: By 11th level, you are so in-tune with your oath that all your melee weapon strikes carry power with them.  Choose one of the following features:

traits.name: Improved Profane Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage.

traits.name: Improved Booming Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage.

traits.name: Improved Divine Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage.

traits.name: Improved Arcane Smite
description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d8 force damage.

14.name: Spellbreaking Touch
description: Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your oath ability modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

18.name: Aura of Conviction
description: Your legendary conviction for your oath infuses your aura with wondrous power.  Starting at 18th level, when you or a creature within your aura fails a saving throw, you can use your reaciton to cause it to succeed instead.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use this reaction again. When you have no uses left, you can expend 5 points of Fervor to use this reaction again.

The Oath of the Ancients is as old as the race of elves and the rituals of the druids. Sometimes called fey knights, green knights, or horned knights, paladins who swear this oath cast their lot with the side of the light in the cosmic struggle against darkness because they love the beautiful and life-giving things of the world, not necessarily because they believe in principles of honor, courage, and justice. They adorn their armor and clothing with images of growing things-leaves, antlers, or flowers-to reflect their commitment to preserving life and light in the world.

subFeatures.name: Kindle the Light
description: Through your acts of mercy, kindness, and forgiveness, kindle the light of hope in the world, beating back despair.

subFeatures.name: Preserve the Light
description: Delight in song and laughter, in beauty and art. If you allow the light to die in your own heart, you can't preserve it in the world.

subFeatures.name: Shelter the Light
description: Where there is good, beauty, love, and laughter in the world, stand against the wickedness that would swallow it. Where life flourishes, stand against the forces that would render it barren.

1.name: Emissary of the Wilds
description: Starting at 1st level, you have been marked as a friend and defender of the ancient and wild places.  You learn to speak, read, and write Druidic.  If you speak Druidic, you can communicate with animals as if you were under the effects of Speak with Animals.

You can also infuse  others with the primal resilience of your Oath. As an action, you can touch one creature and expend 1 point of Fervor to grant it temporary hit points equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1).

3.name: Elder Shield
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can shield your allies from the natural elements. When you or another creature within 10 feet takes cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder damage, you can use a reaction to expend 1 point of Fervor and reduce that damage by your Paladin level + your oath ability modifier.

3.name: Verdant Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it is restrained by mystical vines for up to 1 minute.

A restrained creature, or another creature within 5 feet of it, can use an action on its turn to make Strength check against your oath save DC. On a success, the creature is no longer restrained by these mystical vines.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Warding
description: Beginning at 7th level, ancient magic lies so heavily upon you that it forms an eldritch ward. You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to damage from spells, and any creature within your aura is a valid target for your Elder Shield feature.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

In addition, you can speak Druidic to communicate with plants as if you were under the effects of Speak with Plants.  When using this feature, you are only able to communicate with plants, not command, move, or control them.

15.name: Undying Sentinel
description: Starting at 15th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points and are not killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.
Additionally, you suffer none of the drawbacks of old age, and you can't be aged magically.

20.name: Elder Champion
description: At 20th level, you can assume the form of an ancient force of nature, taking on an appearance you choose. For example, your skin might turn green or take on a bark-like texture, your hair might become leafy or moss-like, or you might sprout antlers or a lion-like mane.
As a bonus action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• At the start of each of your turns, you regain 10 hit points.
  • You can use your Elder Shield feature at will, without expending a use of the feature or a spell slot.
  • The area within your aura becomes overgrown and is difficult terrain for creatures of your choice.
  • Creatures within your aura have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and Verdant Smite.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Ancients

description: Paladins who swear the Oath of the Blade dedicate their lives to becoming masters of combat. Often given the title of Blade Master, these paragons of battle strive for mastery with the armaments of war. Some serve as mercenaries, and others as guardians or bodyguards. However, no matter their station Paladins of the Blade always look to test their martial skills.

subFeatures.name: Fair Play
description: True warriors will fight on a level playing field. Do not stoop to crushing enemies and adversaries who are beneath you unless you first level the playing field.

subFeatures.name: Honesty
description: Let your word be as unbending as your blade, and as true as steel.

subFeatures.name: Respect
description: Those who hold to the Tenets of the Blade, and all warriors who prove themselves in combat, deserve your respect as a fellow combatant, no matter their alignment.

1.name: Martial Ace
description: At 1st level, you have trained with many kinds of weapons and can pick up new ones rapidly.  As an action while you are holding a weapon, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain proficiency with that type of weapon for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

Alternatively, you can use this feature to allow yourself to ignore any penalties that would come from using a weapon that is too large for you, so long as the weapon was intended for use by a creature no more than two sizes larger than you.

1.name: Knight's Exploits
description: At 1st level, you have gained advanced martial training and gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: You have two d4 Exploit Dice. To use an Exploit you must expend one of these dice, and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: You know the Commander's Presence and Martial Focus exploits.  You can use each of these exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die.  Starting at 17th level, you also gain the Warrior's Challenge exploit as a Mastered Exploit.

subFeatures.name: Exploits Known
description: You know two Martial Exploits of your choice. You learn two additional exploits at 6th level and again at 17th level. When you gain a level, you can choose one Exploit you know and replace it with another Exploit of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: If an Exploit requires a creature to make a saving throw, your Exploit saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)

3.name: Stand and Fight
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 point of Fervor to inspire your allies to fight on despite their ailments.  Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you can immediatley make a saving throw against an effect that would normally allow them to make a saving throw at the end of each of their turns.

3.name: Skillful Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to use a 1st-degree exploit you know that can be used as a part of an attack without expending an exploit die.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Honor
description: At 7th level, when a creature of your choice starts its turn within 10 feet of you or moves there for the first time on a turn, you can force them to make a Charisma saving throw against your oath save DC.  On a failed saving throw, the target cannot knowingly and willingly tell a lie or use poison until the start of their next turn.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Counterattack
description: At 15th level, you learn to strike back at those who strike you. As a reaction when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can make a melee weapon attack against that creature, with advantage on your attack roll.

In addition, when you use your Stand and Fight feature, the targets can make a saving throw even if the effect wouldn't normally allow them to make one at the end of each of their turns, so long as the effect is not permanent.

20.name: Warrior of Legend
description: At 20th level, you can you can use a bonus action to enter a trance that enhances your combat skills to legendary levels. For the next minute, you do not expend exploit dice when you use exploits, have proficiency with all weapons, and do not suffer penalties from using a weapon too large for you, so long as the weapon was intended for a creature no more than three sizes larger than you.

This feature ends early if you are incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again, unless you spend a spell slot of 5th-level or higher to use it an additional time.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Blade

description: The Oath of Conquest calls to paladins who seek glory in battle and the subjugation of their enemies. It isn't enough for these paladins to establish order. They must crush the forces of chaos. Sometimes called knight tyrants or iron mongers, those who swear this oath gather into grim orders that serve gods or philosophies of war and well-ordered might.

Some of these paladins go so far as to consort with the powers of the Nine Hells, valuing the rule of law over the balm of mercy. The archdevil Bel, warlord of Avernus, counts many of these paladins - called hell knights - as his most ardent supporters. Hell knights cover their armor with trophies taken from fallen enemies, a grim warning to any who dare oppose them and the decrees of their lords. These knights are often most fiercely resisted by other paladins of this oath, who believe that the hell knights have wandered too far into darkness.

subFeatures.name: Douse the Flame of Hope
description: It is not enough to merely defeat an enemy in battle. Your victory must be so overwhelming that your enemies' will to fight is shattered forever. A blade can end a life. Fear can end an empire.

subFeatures.name: Rule With an Iron Fist
description: Once you have conquered, tolerate no dissent. Your word is law. Those who obey it shall be favored. Those who defy it shall be punished as an example to all who might follow.

subFeatures.name: Strength Above All
description: You shall rule until a stronger one arises. Then you must grow mightier and meet the challenge, or fall to your own ruin.

1.name: Subjugator's Voice
description: Starting at 1st level, your voice inspires command and causes others to quaver.  You gain proficiency in Intimidation, and whenever you make an Intimidation check, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain a bonus to the roll equal to your oath ability modifier.
In addition, attacks made against you before you have taken a turn in combat have disadvantage.

3.name: Conquering Presence
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to exude a terrifying presence. As an action, you force each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature becomes frightened of you for until the end of your next turn.

3.name: Oppressing Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to deliver a one-word command to the target that is not directly harmful to it.  The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be forced to carry out your command on its following turn.
A target that is frightened of you has disadvantage on this saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Conquest
description: Starting at 7th level, you constantly emanate a menacing aura while you're not incapacitated. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover.
If a creature is frightened of you, its speed is reduced to 0 while in the aura, and that creature takes psychic damage equal to half your paladin level if it starts its turn there.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Scornful Rebuke
description: Starting at 15th level, those who dare to strike you are psychically punished for their audacity. Whenever a creature hits you with an attack, that creature takes psychic damage equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1) if you're not incapacitated.

20.name: Invincible Conqueror
description: At 20th level, you gain the ability to harness extraordinary martial prowess. As a bonus action, you can magically become an avatar of conquest, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You have resistance to all damage.
  • When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as part of that action.
  • Your melee weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Conquest

description: The Oath of the Crown is sworn to the ideals of civilization, be it the spirit of a nation, fealty to a sovereign, or service to a deity of law and rulership. The paladins who swear this oath dedicate themselves to serving society and, in particular, the just laws that hold society together. These paladins are the watchful guardians on the walls, standing against the chaotic tides of barbarism that threaten to tear down all that civilization has built, and are commonly known as guardians, exemplars, or sentinels. Often, paladins who swear this oath are members of an order of knighthood in service to a nation or a sovereign, and undergo their oath as part of their admission to the order's ranks.

subFeatures.name: Courage
description: You must be willing to do what needs to be done for the sake of order, even in the face of overwhelming odds. If you don't act, then who will?

subFeatures.name: Law
description: The law is paramount. It is the mortar that holds the stones of civilization together, and it must be respected.

subFeatures.name: Loyalty
description: Your word is your bond. Without loyalty, oaths and laws are meaningless.

1.name: Court Culture
description: Starting at 1st level, you know how to present yourself around royalty and nobility.  You gain proficiency in Persuasion and Society, you learn to speak, read, and write an additional language of your choice, and whenever you make a Society check, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain a bonus to the roll equal to your oath ability modifier.
In addition, royalty and nobles recognize your knightly status, and may act more courteous to you, and more willing to help you.

3.name: Champion Challenge
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to issue a challenge that compels other creatures to do battle with you. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can't willingly move more than 30 feet away from you. This effect ends on the creature if you are incapacitated or die or if the creature is more than 30 feet away from you.

3.name: Challenger's Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw.  On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on any attack roll that does not target you for the next minute.  The target can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
A creature under the effects of your Champion Challenge feature has disadvantage on their saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Allegiance
description: Starting at 7th level, when a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to magically substitute your own health for that of the target creature, causing that creature to not take damage.  Instead, you take the damage, after your resistances and immunities.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Unyielding Spirit
description: Starting at 15th level, you have advantage on saving throws to avoid becoming paralyzed or stunned.

20.name: Exalted Champion
description: At 20th level, your presence on the field of battle is an inspiration to those dedicated to your cause. You can use a bonus action to gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

• You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.
  • Your allies have advantage on death saving throws while within 30 feet of you.
  • You have advantage on Wisdom saving throws, as do your allies within 30 feet of you.
This effect ends early if you are incapacitated or die. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Crown

description: The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to the loftiest ideals of justice, virtue, and order. Sometimes called cavaliers, white knights, or holy warriors, these paladins meet the ideal of the knight in shining armor, acting with honor in pursuit of justice and the greater good. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some, for better or worse, hold the rest of the world to the same standards. Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of their devotion. They hold angels - the perfect servants of good - as their ideals, and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.

subFeatures.name: Compassion
description: Aid others, protect the weak, and punish those who threaten them. Show mercy to your foes, but temper it with wisdom.

subFeatures.name: Honesty
description: Don't lie or cheat. Let your word be your promise.

subFeatures.name: Honor
description: Treat others with fairness, and let your honorable deeds be an example to them. Do as much good as possible while causing the least amount of harm.

1.name: Lay on Hands
description: At 1st level, your consecrated touch heals wounds. As an action, you can touch a creature and expend any number of Fervor points and restore five hit points per point of Fervor spent. This feature has no effect on constructs or undead.

3.name: Sacred Weapon
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to imbue one weapon that you are holding with the power of your oath, causing it to radiate with divine light. For the next minute, your weapon emits bright light in a 20 foot radius, it deals radiant damage instead of its normal damage type, and you can add your oath ability modifier to its attack and damage rolls.

3.name: Righteous Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.
Fiends, undead, and creatures of evil alignment have disadvantage on this Wisdom saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Devotion
description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.  If a charmed creature enters your aura, the effect is suspended while they remain within it.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

In addition, you gain an additional way to use your Lay on Hands feature.  You can expend 1 point of Fervor to cure the target of one disease or neutralize one poison affecting it. You can cure multiple diseases and neutralize multiple poisons with a single use of Lay on Hands, expending Fervor separately for each one.

15.name: Purity of Spirit
description: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a Protection From Evil and Good spell.

20.name: Holy Nimbus
description: At 20th level, as a bonus action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For the next minute, you gain the following benefits:

• Weapons you hold automatically become Sacred Weapons.
  • You manifest angelic wings, gaining a 60 foot flying speed.
  • You radiate bright light within a range equal to your aura's range. The light is sunlight.
  • Creatures of your choice that start their turn within your aura take 10 radiant damage. This radiant damage is doubled against fiends and undead.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Devotion

description: Paladins who swear this Sacred Oath are often craftsmen in some sense of the word. Whether they are artisans working over the forge, or activists working to build a better society, all Forge Paladins work toward progress and order in their chosen craft. For some Paladins, they will even hold their Oath fulfilled when they achieve perfection in their craft.

subFeatures.name: Form the Shape
description: Share the knowledfe of the hammer and the anvil with those around you so that they may forge their own path.  Strengthen bonds among the weak so that they become mighty in their own works.

subFeatures.name: Temper the Steel
description: The working of any craft is an act of worship, for in every weaver's fingers or cooper's tongs lie the echo of primordial creation heard once again in the material world.  Take pride in your work and submit to a lifetime of patient growth in your own skills.

subFeatures.name: Warm the Furnace
description: Offer relief to the suffering by standing among them and sharing in their burdens.  Stoke the heat of courage through compassion and perserverance, and commit yourself completely to defending the weak and the defenseless.

1.name: Ironworks
description: By 1st level, you have experience at the forge, gaining the following benefits:

• You gain proficiency with blacksmith's tools and in the Endurance skill.
  • You gain resistance to fire damage.
  • As an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor and touch a Small or smaller metal object, instantly transfiguring it into a shape of your choosing. You cannot change the object into any object that would require skill or training using this feature.

3.name: Molten Weapon
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor and hold aloft a melee weapon to imbue it with the power of the forge, causing it to glow red-hot and emit wisps of smoke. For the next minute, your weapon emits bright light in a 20 foot radius, it deals fire damage instead of its normal damage type, and you can add your oath ability modifier to its attack and damage rolls.

3.name: Smog-Choked Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to create a cloud of thick black smoke in a 15-foot cube adjacent to you.  The area is heavily obscured.  The smoke remains for 1 minute or until dispersed.
In addition, when you use your Smite feature, you can choose for the extra damage to be fire damage.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of the Blacksmith
description: Beginning at 7th level, the power of your Oath imbues metal weapons and armor of your choice within 10 feet with a supernatural quality. Armor grants its wearer at +1 bonus to their Armor Class. Weapons count as magical for the sake of overcoming resistances and gain a +1 bonus to their attack and damage rolls.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Unyielding Steel
description: Starting at 15th level, your arms and armor have been infused with the power of your Oath. Once per turn when you take damage while you are wearing heavy armor, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to halve the amount of damage that you would take.

20.name: Flame of the Forge
description: Starting at 20th level, as a bonus action, you can transform into a spirit of forge and fire. While transformed you gain the following benefits:

• Weapons you hold automatically become Molten Weapons.
  • Creatures of your choice within your Aura of the Blacksmith gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
  • You can use your Unyielding Steel reaction on each of your turns without expending a use of the feature.
  • Whenever you deal fire damage you can ignore resistance to fire damage and treat immunity to fire as resistance.

This transformation lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you are incapacitated. Once you use this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. If you have no uses left you can expend a 5th-level spell slot to transform again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Forge

description: Most paladins place great emphasis on duty, honesty, order and justice, believing that an orderly approach to life is the best way to keep their tenets and accomplish their objectives. The Paladins of Freedom, however, reject this approach. Instead, they stress that personal liberty is the most important thing an individual can have.

The Oath of Freedom ties paladins to the ideals of liberty and personal agency above all else. Paladins of this oath resemble skirmishers more than they do knights in shining armor. They use their skills to free the oppressed and defend them from oppressors. For this reason, kings, queens, and other rulers are often suspicious of Freedom paladins - for where these paladins go, revolution may soon follow.

subFeatures.name: Equity
description: Respect the autonomy and desires of others. Hierarchy only leads to injustice.

subFeatures.name: Liberty
description: Tyranny must be opposed. Chains imposed by unjust authority are meant to be broken.

subFeatures.name: Revolution
description: Change is only brought through sudden transformational struggle.

1.name: Freedom from Chains
description: Starting at 1st level, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 point of Fervor and inspire others to rise against their oppressors. All friendly creatures other than yourself within 30 feet of you can use their reaction to stand if they are prone or to make an ability check or saving throw to attempt to escape from being grappled, swallowed, or restrained.

3.name: Turn the Bourgeoisie
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to utter an indictment against those who would trample rights, inspiring the same terror on them that they impose on their lessers. Each non-chaotic evil humanoid, non-chaotic fiend, or dragon that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your oath save DC. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

3.name: Uprising Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to give a bonus equal your oath ability modifier in the next attack roll to all friendly creatures within 10 feet of you make.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Mobility
description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you are unaffected by magical and nonmagical difficult terrain while you are conscious.
The range of this aura, and of your Uprising Smite, increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Free Spirited
description: At 15th level, when you use your action to Dash or Disengage, you can make a single weapon attack as a bonus action.

20.name: Hero of the Revolution
description: At 20th level, you break free of all bonds and restrictions. Using a bonus action action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• You gain a flying speed of 90 feet.
  • You and creatures within your aura are under the effects of the Freedom of Movement spell.
  • You and creatures within your aura are immune to enchantment spells you do not choose to be affected by.
  • When you inflict damage on a creature, you ignore its damage resistances.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Freedom

description: Paladins take on many types of oaths, and not always towards a king or higher power. Some choose to be loyal to the people around them instead, swearing to uphold the force that binds people together in friendship. Those sworn to the Oath of Friendship dedicate themselves to their relationships, friendships, and even lifelong rivalries. These knights understand that sometimes the strongest thing one can do is ask for help. Transcending race and creed, the Oath of Friendship can be upheld as long as people are willing to stand by each other's side.

subFeatures.name: Die for Your People
description: If it comes down to it, you must lay your life on the line to keep your friends safe.

subFeatures.name: Help Your People
description: Lend a helping hand when in need to keep your friends feeling strong and ready for battle.

subFeatures.name: Stand with Your People
description: Never betray your friends. Stand with them no matter what.

1.name: Help From Friends
description: Starting at 1st level, you can help your friends whenever they need aid.  You can expend 1 point of Fervor to take the Help action as a bonus action on your turn.

3.name: Power of Sharing
description: Starting at 3rd level, whenever you cast a spell that has a range of Self, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to additionally target another willing creature within your reach.

3.name: Distributed Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to grant a measure of its power to a friendly creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The next time that creature hits a target with a melee weapon attack, their target takes an additional 1d8 damage of the same type as your Smite feature.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Fealty
description: At 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.  If a charmed creature enters your aura, the effect is suspended while they remain within it.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Unwavering Loyalty
description: Starting at 15th level, if you would drop to zero hit points while at least one allied creature is within 60 feet, you can make a Charisma saving throw with a DC equal to the amount of damage taken. On success, you instead drop to 1 hit point.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. The DC resets when you finish a long rest.

20.name: Best of Friends
description: At 20th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest your loyalty and friendship, gaining the following benefits for 1 hour:

• When you use your Power of Sharing feature, it can target any number of creatures within 10 feet of you.
  • At the start of each of your turns, you and friendly creatures within your aura of you gain temporary hit points equal to your oath ability modifier.
  • If a friendly creature within your aura is reduced to 0 hit points by another creature, you can use your reaction to move up to your speed towards them and make an attack against that creature.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Friendship

description: Paladins who take the Oath of Glory believe they and their companions are destined to achieve glory through deeds of heroism. They train diligently and encourage their companions so they're all ready when destiny calls.

subFeatures.name: Actions Over Words
description: Strive to be known by glorious deeds, not words.

subFeatures.name: Challenges are But Tests
description: Face hardships with courage, and encourage your allies to face them with you.

subFeatures.name: Hone the Body
description: Like raw stone, your body must be worked so its potential can be realized.

1.name: Peerless Athlete
description: Starting at 1st level, your athletic abilities are the stuff of legend. You gain the following benefits:

• You have proficiency in Athletics.
  • Whenever you make an Athletics check, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain a bonus to the roll equal to your oath ability modifier.
  • You count as one size larger for the purposes of determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, and lift.
  • The distance of your long and high jumps increases by 10 feet (this extra distance costs movement as normal).

3.name: Legendary Contest
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as an action to begin a contest of strength with a creature within your reach.  The target must make a Strength saving throw against your passive Strength (Athletics) or become grappled by you, regardless of its size.  While grappled in this way, the target is considered restrained if it is Large or smaller. The target can use an action on each of their turns to repeat the saving throw, breaking free and ending the contest on a success.

3.name: Inspiring Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to distribute temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt to creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you.

7.name: Aura of Alacrity
description: Starting at 7th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet.  In addition, if you aren't incapacitated, the walking speed of a creature of your choice who starts their turn within 10 feet of you increases by 5 feet until the end of their turn.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.
In addition, your Legendary Contest feature can now restrain Huge creatures.

15.name: Glorious Defense
description: When you reach 15th level, you can turn defense into a sudden strike. When you or another creature you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to grant a bonus to the target's AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. The bonus equals your oath ability modifier (minimum of +1). If the attack misses, you can make one weapon attack against the attacker as part of this reaction, provided the attacker is within your weapon's range.

20.name: Living Legend
description: At 20th level, you can empower yourself with the legends - whether true or exaggerated - of your great deeds. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You are blessed with an otherworldly presence, gaining advantage on all Charisma checks.
  • Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack and miss, you can cause that attack to hit instead.
  • If you fail a saving throw, you can use your reaction to reroll it. You must use this new roll.
  • Your Legendary Contest feature can restrain a creature of any size.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Glory

description: The oath of the grim hunt is a calling that requires its followers to seek out and destroy the many evils the stalk the mortal realms. Often called Grim knights, or Knight Slayers, these hunters dedicate themselves, body and soul, to hunting down the monstrous, the wicked, and the mutated, destroying them with a burning, merciless prejudice.

subFeatures.name: Burn the Witch
description: End the mortals who betray their kind for the powers of horrid monsters.

subFeatures.name: Hunt the Biggest Game
description: When presented with the choice between a great monster and a lesser threat, fight the greater threat without hesitation.

subFeatures.name: Kill the Monster
description: Destroy that which would rule the land with tooth and claw and spell.

1.name: Hunter of the Shadows
description: At 1st level, you gain proficiency in either Nature, Religion, or Survival.

Whenever you make an Intelligence (Nature), Intelligence (Religion), or Wisdom (Survival) check related to fiends, shapechangers, or undead, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain a bonus to the roll equal to your oath ability modifier.

3.name: Merciless Crippling
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to horribly cripple a creature with divine power. Choose a creature within 60 feet of you. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have their burrowing and flying speeds are reduced to 0, and their other speeds halved, until the end of your next turn.

3.name: Slaying Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to cause the damage dice to increase to d10s. If the target is a fiend, shapechanger, or undead, the dice further increase to d12s.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Cleansing
description: Beginning at 7th level, whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you is under the effects of a spell or other effect that allows it to repeat a saving throw at the end of each of its turns, it can repeat the saving throw at the start of its turn instead, possibly ending the effect early.
In addition, you can perceive the true form of any creature within this range that you can see.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Living Inevitable
description: Starting at 15th level, You can no longer be charmed or paralyzed, and you can't be sensed or scryed upon by divination magics unless you want to be.

20.name: Chosen Slayer
description: At 20th level, you can use a bonus action to take a monstrous form of your own for 1 minute.

• Your size becomes Large, unless you were larger.
  • Your Strength score becomes 26, unless it was already higher.
  • You are immune to being grappled, paralyzed, and stunned.
  • You can grapple a creature of any size.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Grim Hunt

description: Truth. All dedicated paladins who become Inquisitors have the same goal: reveal what is hidden, and purge the planes of those who obscure the truth. Those who swear this Oath will stop at nothing to accomplish their goals, and no matter how ruthless their actions, they believe they are justified.

Above all else they despise creatures that hide their true intentions or forms. Fiend, celestial, or fey; it matters not to the Inquisitor paladin. Any creature, no matter its goals, that uses its power to deceive mortals, has forfeited their life.

subFeatures.name: Absolute Truth
description: The truth is out there, and you must do whatever it takes to bring it to light. Those who obscure the truth deserve punishment, and you will deliver that justice.

subFeatures.name: Immutable Forms
description: All creatures of the multiverse have a natural form. Those that would seek to physically alter their form or obscure it with magic must be reprimanded.

subFeatures.name: Swift Retribution
description: Those who break the laws of the multiverse deserve a punishment to fit their crime. A thief may lose a hand, but an oathbreaker may forfeit their life.

1.name: Unexpected Inquisition
description: Starting at 1st level, on your first turn after rolling initiative, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a bonus action to hold aloft your symbol and force a number of creatures of your choice equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1) within 60 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, creatures that have not yet taken a turn since rolling initiative are surprised. A creature who you know the true name of has disadvantage on their saving throw.

3.name: Divine Interrogation
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor and grasp your symbol, forcing a creature you can see within 10 feet, to make an Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, you learn the true name of the creature and it has disadvantage on the first Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw you force it to make within the next minute.

3.name: Revealing Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Charisma saving throw against your oath save DC.  On a failed save, the target can't cast enchantment or illusion spells or maintain concentration on such spells, and can't benefit from being invisible, until the start of your next turn.
A creature who you know the true name of has disadvantage on their saving throw.
