7.name: Aura of Inquisition
description: Beginning at 7th level, you do not tolerate those who would stand in the way of your quest for truth. Once per turn, when you or a creature within 10 feet of you hits a Large or smaller creature with a melee attack, you can force them to make a Strength saving throw. A creature who you know the true name of has disadvantage on this saving throw. On a failure, they are knocked prone, in addition to the normal damage. A creature who you know the true name of has disadvantage on their saving throw.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Iron Will
description: You have honed your mind to resist any effects that would restrict your agency or obscure the truth for you. Starting at 15th level, you are immune to any effect that would force you to act against your will.
In addition, your Aura of Inquisition can affect Huge or smaller creatures.

20.name: Grand Inquisitor
description: Upon reaching 20th level, you can use a bonus action to become a divine embodiment of absolute Truth and Law. When you do so, you gain the benefits listed below for one minute:

• You gain truesight out to a 120-foot radius.
  • All of your attacks trigger your Aura of Inquisition feature, and it can affect creatures of any size.
  • Any shapechanger hit by one of your attacks reverts to its original form and takes an additional 2d8 damage of the same type as your Smite.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Inquisition

description: The Oath of the Open Sea calls to sea-faring warriors, swashbuckling sailors, and journeying guardians who seek the thrill of an endless horizon. Driven to seek the adventure and mystery across and beneath every endless oceanic expanse, paladins who swear this oath stand against those who would deny the liberties afforded to likeminded travelers, rooting out the tyrannical and corrupt that claim any shore. Such guardians believe in the natural beauty of the sea, often making offerings and prayers to entities or deities like the Wild Mother or Storm Lord that influence safe passage, while often feeling called to hunt those monstrosities that seek to terrorize and spoil the waters with wanton violence and ill intent.

subFeatures.name: Adapt Like the Water
description: The waters of the ocean can shift around any obstacle or become an impassable one. They can carve around and reveal the secrets of the past or swallow the truth and hide it forever. To embrace this fluidity is to be ready for any challenge.

subFeatures.name: Explore the Uncharted
description: The world is filled with much mystery. Through the pursuit of these enigmatic ends, one can both uncover those who hide their dark deeds in shadow to be judged, and find the path to becoming something great.

subFeatures.name: No Greater Life Than a Life Lived Free
description: One should be free to chart their own path without oppression. Those who would exert their power to dominate others shall be smote.

1.name: Seafaring Guardian
description: Starting at 1st level, you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and you can breathe water as well as air.  In addition, your vision cannot be obscured by fog.

1.name: Marine Layer
description: Also at 1st level, when you are hit with an attack, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to create a cloud of fog in a 5-foot sphere centered on yourself.  The fog heavily obscures the area, and lasts until the end of your next turn.

3.name: All Hands on Deck
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to bellow an order to your allies. A number of creatures of your choice up to your oath ability modifier within 30 feet that can see or hear you can use their reaction to move up to their full speed. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

3.name: Tidal Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Strength saving throw.  On a failed save, the target is pushed away from you a distance equal to 5 × your proficiency bonus, and is knocked prone.
In addition, when you use your Smite feature, you can choose for the extra damage to be cold, lightning, or thunder damage.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Liberation
description: Starting at 7th level, you emanate an aura while you're not incapacitated. You and any creature of your choice within 10 feet of you cannot be attached to, grappled, restrained, or swallowed, as well as ignore penalties on movement or attacks while underwater. Creatures that are already attached to, grappled, restrained, or swallowed when they enter the aura can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape nonmagical restraints.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Stormy Waters
description: At 15th level, you can call crashing waters around you as a reaction whenever a creature enters or exits your melee range. The creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to your oath abiltiy modifier and must succeed a Strength saving throw against your oath save DC or be knocked prone.

20.name: Mythic Admiral
description: At 20th level, you learn to channel the spirits of historic sea captains to briefly become a paragon of heroic adventure. As a bonus action, you embrace these spirits of the sea, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You are immune to cold, lightning, and thunder damage.
  • You can cast Command at 1st-level as a bonus action on each of your turns without expending a spell slot.
  • Whenever you hit a Huge or smaller creature with a melee attack, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your oath save DC or be knocked prone.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Open Sea

description: Sometimes, piety is not the only reason for a paladin to receive power from a deity. Sometimes it's devotion to an idea such as mercy, protection, or smiting evil. Others, however, are devoted to one single idea: perfection.

Commonly known as mirror knights, knight radiants, or knights of the vain table, these warriors' bodies are perfect, and their actions are performed with absolute grace and skill. This has caused many entities to offer these bastions of vanity a place at their side in return for giving them the power to take their perfection above and beyond what is possible with mortal powers.

subFeatures.name: Humiliate Those Who Threaten
description: Your perfefction will earn you enemies, let them know who you are.

subFeatures.name: Perfection of Body
description: Your body should never be marred with scars or blemishes, and your physique should never falter under any circumstances.

subFeatures.name: Stand Above the Wastrel
description: Your perfection means nothing if you stand among the sheep who sully your image with their presence.

1.name: Constant Improvement
description: Starting at 1st level, you always continue to improve in every aspect of life.  When you fail an ability check, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to reroll it.  You must use the new roll.

3.name: Peek of Perfection
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to reveal your radiant physical form to all who can see. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that can see you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become blinded until the start of your next turn.

3.name: Vainglorious Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain the benefits of the Sanctuary spell until the end of your next turn or until you miss with an attack roll or fail an ability check or saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of the Peerless
description: Starting at 7th level, failure becomes difficult when you are around. Whenever you or a creature of your choice within 10 feet of you makes an attack roll or ability check, they can roll a d6 and add it to the roll. They can't do so again until the start of your next turn.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Grand Reflection
description: Starting at 15th level, your perfect form wavers like a mirage until you are struck. Creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against you. If you take damage, the feature ceases to function until the start of your next turn. This feature is suppressed while you are incapacitated, restrained, or otherwise unable to move.

20.name: Nimbus of Perfection
description: At 20th level, you can assume a form of absolute perfection that only the gods themselves are capable of achieving. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

• Whenever you or a creature of your choice within 30 feet of you make a skill check, treat any roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
  • The die used by your Aura of the Peerless changes to a d10.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Perfection

description: Clad in grime-soaked armor and wielding rusting weapons, the Oath of Pestilence paladin spreads corruption, disease, and filth. Bound by an oath which infests their bodies with all manner of plagues, these heralds of decay lumber forward with unholy toughness and grim resolve.

subFeatures.name: Contamination
description: Spread disease and decay wherever you go.  Taint that which is untainted.

subFeatures.name: Cull the Meek
description: Many must die for the strong to prosper.  Those who cannot survive the plague must be left to their wretched fates or put on the sword.

subFeatures.name: Survival of the Fittest
description: Only those of strong body and spirit can survive horrible disease.  Respect those who survive against all odds.

1.name: Eroding Presence
description: Starting at 1st level, your mere presence corrodes metal and rots flesh.  If you are hit by a melee attack, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to impose a penalty on the attacker's next attack roll equal to your oath ability modifier.

3.name: Turn the Undying
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to weaken those who deny the natural order of death. Each construct or undead, as well as each creature that is immune to disease, that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your oath save DC. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

3.name: Debilitating Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, your touch inflicts disease. When you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw.  On a failed save, the target is poisoned until the start of your next turn.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Rampant Sickness
description: Starting at 7th level, you emit an aura of contagion and virulence to a range of 10 feet. When a creature within your aura makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw you can give that roll disadvantage as a reaction.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Disgusting Resilience
description: At 15th level, when you take damage which would reduce you to 0 hit points, you can choose to expend any number of Hit Dice. Roll those dice and subtract the result from the damage taken. If this reduces the damage to 0, you don't take any damage.
In addition, if you are killed your corpse violently explodes in a shower of pus and gore, dealing 8d6 necrotic damage to creatures within 20 feet of you that fail a Constitution saving throw.

20.name: Plaguebringer
description: At 20th level, you become an avatar of plague, which gives you the following benefits:

• You have resistance to necrotic damage and are immune to poison damage.
  • Your hit point maximum can't be reduced.
  • Creatures of your choice who start their turn within 5 feet of you, or who move within 5 feet of you on their turn, take necrotic damage equal to your oath ability modifier. Once a creature takes damage from this ability, it can't take damage from it again until the start of its next turn.

subclasses.name: Oath of Pestilence

description: Wealth is the availability of goods and services, and thus is a representation of both power and opportunity. A wealthy benefactor can save a civilization, while a wealthy tyrant can turn the world on its head. The Oath of Prosperity merges the spiritual with the materialistic, benevolence with self-interest, and temperance with a hunger for power. Through these seemingly opposites, you've sworn to let nothing stand between you and the accumulation of wealth, as any goal you have can be accomplished with the prudent use of overwhelming financial might.

subFeatures.name: Benefit
description: Before acting, analyze any benefits you may gain, whether in wealth or favors.

subFeatures.name: Investment
description: Every action is an investment that should pay off for you in the future. Debt is a powerful force to wield over another.

subFeatures.name: Profit
description: Never enter a bad deal. Each agreement you take part in must eventually increase your power, influence, or wealth.

1.name: Distilled Fortune
description: Starting at 1st level, as an action, you can touch a Large or smaller non-magical object that is not worn or carried and expend 1 point of Fervor, transforming it into a Tiny gemstone with the same monetary worth as the item. If the object is a container, you transmute the object along with every object inside of it, causing creatures to be ejected to the nearest open space. As an action, you can touch the gemstone and transform it back into the original object. You can have a maximum number of such gems equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of one), and if you relinquish one of these gems it reverts to its original shape in 1 hour.
In addition, you have proficiency with jeweler's tools and you have advantage on checks made to determine the value of gemstones, artwork, or magic items.

3.name: Hired Help
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to summon a simple magical construct for 1 hour. This construct has the statistics of a commoner, though it is a construct instead of its normal type. It cannot attack, cast spells, or activate magic items. If it dies or the duration expires, it fades into mist.

3.name: Greedy Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Strength saving throw.  On a failed save, you steal an object or weapon of your choice from the target.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Investment
description: Starting at 7th level, you are surrounded by a 10-foot aura of mutual benefit. You and all friendly creatures within 10 feet of you gain temporary hit points equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.
In addition, you can now transmute a Huge or smaller object into a gemstone using your Distilled Fortune feature.

15.name: Fortunate Defense
description: Starting at 15th level, you can liquidate your investments to protect you from harm. When you take damage from a creature you can see, you can use your reaction to destroy a gemstone gained from Distilled Fortune and reduce the incoming damage by 1d10 for every 100 gp the Distilled Fortune gemstone is worth.

20.name: Golden Idol
description: At 20th level, as a bonus action, you can call upon the debts that you are owed and empower yourself. For 1 minute, the rustling of your armor sounds strangely like the clinking of coins. You gain the following benefits.

• You gain 20 temporary hit points at the start of each of your turns that last for the duration of this feature.
  • Whenever you steal a weapon using your Greedy Smite feature, you can immediately make a weapon attack using it as part of the same action.
  • When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can choose to unleash a blast of golden light. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your oath save DC. If they fail, they are blinded until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Prosperity

description: The Oath of Redemption sets a paladin on a difficult path, one that requires a holy warrior to use violence only as a last resort. Paladins who dedicate themselves to this oath believe that any person can be redeemed and that the path of benevolence and justice is one that anyone can walk. These paladins face evil creatures in the hope of turning them to the light, and the paladins slay them only when such a deed will clearly save other lives. Paladins who follow this path are known as redeemers.

While redeemers are idealists, they are no fools. Redeemers know that undead, demons, devils, and other supernatural threats can be inherently evil. Against such foes, the paladins bring the full wrath of their weapons and spells to bear. Yet the redeemers still pray that, one day, even creatures of wickedness will invite their own redemption.

subFeatures.name: Innocence
description: All people begin life in an innocent state, and it is their environment or the influence of dark forces that drives them to evil. By setting the proper example, and working to heal the wounds of a deeply flawed world, you can set anyone on a righteous path.

subFeatures.name: Patience
description: Change takes time. Those who have walked the path of the wicked must be given reminders to keep them honest and true. Once you have planted the seed of righteousness in a creature, you must work day after day to allow it to survive and then flourish.

subFeatures.name: Peace
description: Violence is a weapon of last resort. Diplomacy and understanding are the paths to long-lasting peace.

1.name: Emissary of Peace
description: Starting at 1st level, when you speak, you are listened to. You gain proficiency in the Persuasion skill, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks made with it.

Additionally, if a creature can understand at least one language, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to allow them to understand your speech for the next hour, regardless of whether you share a language.

3.name: Rebuke the Violent
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can rebuke those who use violence. Immediately after an attacker within 30 feet of you deals damage with an attack against a creature other than you, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker takes radiant damage equal to the damage it just dealt. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

3.name: Marking Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to cause the target to become Marked.  The next time a Marked target deals damage to a creature other than you, they take damage of the same type as your Smite feature equal to half of the initial damage.

5.name: Protector's Strike
description: Starting at 5th level, you can punish those who attack your allies. When a creature within 5 feet of you other than you is attacked, if the attacker is within your reach, you can use your reaction to make a single melee weapon attack against them.

7.name: Aura of the Guardian
description: Starting at 7th level, you can shield your allies from harm at the cost of your own health. When a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to magically take that damage, instead of that creature taking it. This feature doesn't transfer any other effects that might accompany the damage, and this damage can't be reduced in any way.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Protective Spirit
description: Starting at 15th level, a holy presence mends your wounds in combat. You regain hit points equal to 1d6 + half your paladin level if you end your turn in combat with fewer than half of your hit points remaining and you aren't incapacitated.

20.name: Emissary of Redemption
description: At 20th level, you become an avatar of peace, which gives you the following benefits.

• You have resistance to all damage dealt by other creatures (their attacks, spells, and other effects).
  • Whenever a creature damages you, it takes radiant damage equal to half the amount it dealt to you.

If you attack a creature by any means but your Protector's Strike feature, cast a spell on it, or deal damage to it by any means but this feature or your Rebuke the Violent, Marking Smite, or Protector's Strike features, neither benefit works against that creature until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Oath of Redemption

description: The Oath of Shadows is a pledge to serve as the weapon of a dark patron that eschews the light of day. It is said the first paladins to swear this Oath swore it to the night itself, to defend night travelers from those that would prey on them.

Paladins of Shadows universally wear shades of brown, grey, and black, and are equally at home in leathers as they are in plate. Always a foreboding sight, paladins of this Oath sometimes find themselves the target of fear, suspicion, and prejudice from those afraid of who, or what they represent.

subFeatures.name: Calculation
description: Stumbling into situations is an easy way to die. Plan thoroughly for all contingencies, but do not be afraid to modify your plans should the situation change.

subFeatures.name: Obfuscation
description: Whether your deeds are noble or nefarious, little good comes from drawing undue attention to oneself. Do not let your name or face be known; those that remain unrecognized live to fight another day.

subFeatures.name: Silence
description: Words carry power, and the wrong ones can end a life. Take great care in what you say and, when in doubt, say nothing at all.

1.name: Shadow Sense
description: Starting at 1st level, you can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet, and you have proficiency in Stealth.
In addition, you are immune to being blinded or deafened.
Finally, whenever you make a Stealth check, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain a bonus to the roll equal to your oath ability modifier.

3.name: Night Cloak
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action you can expend 1 point of Fervor to weave your power around you and hide yourself from view. For up to 1 hour or until you attack or cast a spell, you are invisible, inaudible, and your armor does not give you disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. You are also silent and incapable of speaking for the duration.  You must concentrate on this effect as if concentrating on a spell.

3.name: Silencing Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw.  On a failed save, the target is silenced until the end of your next turn, and loses concentration on any spells they are currently concentrating on.
Celestials and creatures concentrating on spells that create magical light have disadvantage on their saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Midnight
description: Beginning at 7th level, the darkness grants you a boon, which you may pass on to those around you. For you and creatures you choose within 10 feet of you, armor does not impose disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and creatures within this radius gain darkvision out to 60 feet. If they already have darkvision, they increase their current darkvision by 60 feet. Further, any affected creature within the radius may telepathically send a message that can be heard only by other affected creatures within the radius.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Umbral Jaunt
description: Starting at 15th level, you can slide through darkness to strike in retribution at those who threaten your allies. When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack against you or a creature friendly to you, you may expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to teleport yourself through your shadow to a point within 5 feet of the attacking creature. You may then make one attack against the creature, resolving it after the creature resolves its attacks. You can teleport up to 60 feet if the attacking creature is standing in an area of dim light or darkness.

20.name: Living Nightmare
description: At 20th level, you grow ever closer to becoming one with the night. As a bonus action on your turn, you can allow the shadow energy within you to overtake your physical form, turning you into a shifting, pitch dark humanoid horror. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• Your attacks deal an additional 1d8 psychic damage, and a creature hit by one or more of your attacks on your turn must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your oath save DC or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
  • You are invisible to all creatures except the creature you have most recently attacked. This invisibility persists even after you attack or cast a spell.
  • You can move through a space as narrow as one inch in diameter without squeezing.
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons that are not silver.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Shadows

description: Spiders are beings of incredible creativity and ingenuinty for their small size. Though their appearance wouldn't obviously betray it, all mundane spiders are distantly descended from the great, demonic Demonweb Spiders of Lolth's domain - the Demonweb Pits. Paladins who swear this oath are almost always devout followers of the Spider Queen, and often drow. Their fealty to her grants them powerful spider-like abilities, though the cost of this power is unclear given their patron's madness.

subFeatures.name: Have a Plan
description: Spiders delight in managing their intricate webs. Likewise, you should always form a plan to take what you want and say, do, and sacrifice whatever necessary.

subFeatures.name: Might Makes Right
description: In the bug world, only power is respected. There is no greater goal and no emotion or attachment that should prevent you from your upward progress.

subFeatures.name: Sow Discord
description: If power is the greatest virtue, then you can only help the world by throwing it into chaos and conflict. This provides opportunity for the strong to rise over the weak.

1.name: Spider Walk
description: Starting at 1st level, as a bonus action you can expend a point of Fervor to transform your legs into eight spider-like limbs for 10 minutes. While you have spider legs, you have a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, you can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings and across webs, without penalty, and you have advantage on saving throws against being knocked prone.

3.name: Dark Mother's Design
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you roll initiative, you can choose to not roll initiative. If you do so, during the current combat encounter, if you have not taken a turn yet in a given round, you can take your turn directly after any other creature's turn.

3.name: Venomous Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your oath save DC.  On a failed save, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
A poisoned creature has disadvantage on their saving throw. If a poisoned creature fails its saving throw, it takes additional poison damage equal to half the initial damage.

7.name: Aura of the Demonweb
description: Beginning at 7th level, a bit of the Demonweb seeps into the world around, obscuring secrets and lies. When a creature within your aura makes a Wisdom ability check or saving throw, you can choose to impose a penalty equal to your oath ability modifier.
Additionally, creatures within your aura of your choice have advantage on checks made to hide, and can move across webs without penalty.

15.name: Spinner of Webs
description: At 15th level, your connection to the Demonweb allows you to pull in sections of its silk to coat your surroundings in webs. As an action, you can expend 2 points of Fervor to fill a 5-foot cube within 5 feet of you with spectral, demonic webs for 1 hour.

Each creature that starts its turn in the webs or that enters them for the first time on a turn must make a Dexterity saving throw against your oath save DC. On a failed save, a creature is restrained as long as it remains in the webs or until it breaks free. A creature restrained by the webs can use its action to make a Strength check against your oath save DC. If it succeeds, it is no longer restrained.
Additionally, you are immune to being grappled or restrained.

20.name: Spider Queen's Decree
description: Upon reaching 20th level, you can use an action to allow the Spider Queen to twist your form into that of a monstrous spider. When you do so, you gain the benefits listed below for one minute:

• Your weapons are incorporated into your new form, and you cannot be disarmed of them.
  • Your size becomes Huge, unless it was larger.
  • Your type changes to Fiend (demon), you cannot speak, and you are considered hostile to all creatures.
  • Your Strength score becomes 26, unless it was already higher.
  • Your movement speed increases by 10 feet, and you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed. You can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings and across webs, without penalty.
  • You can use your Spinner of Webs feature without expending any points of Fervor and as a bonus action.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Spider

description: Unbreakable Paladins are soldiers who dedicate themselves to defending the ideals of freedom and prosperity and fighting those who would use strength and violence to subdue and rule the weak. Commonly called bulwark knights, mountain knights, and The Unbroken, these soldiers stride into battle with defensive magics alight, making them mobile fortresses that can withstand the wrath of kings, emperors, and gods.

subFeatures.name: Defend the Weak
description: You must challenge the strong with your own strength so that the weak might prepare or flee.

subFeatures.name: Kindle Hope
description: When there is doubt, you must be an anchor for the courage and will of those around you.

subFeatures.name: Never Back Down
description: You are unbreakable, show no fear, and take little caution.  You must be where others cannot.

1.name: Adamantine Bulwark
description: Starting at 1st level, when you take damage, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your paladin level.

3.name: Unstoppable Tilt
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as an action to charge forwards. You may move up to twice your speed in a straight line. You can move through the spaces of other creatures, and each creature you come into contact with must make a Strength saving throw against your oath save DC, or they take bludgeoning damage equal to your oath ability modifier and are forcefully moved with you until you finish your charge, taking no damage, not being moved with you, and being knocked prone on a successful save.

3.name: Surgebreaker Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to halt the target's advance.  The target cannot willingly move out of your reach until the start of your next turn.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Iron
description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you reduce all damage by an amount equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum 1).
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Living Bulwark
description: Beginning at 15th level, you can no longer be grappled, restrained, knocked prone, or forcefully moved. Allies of your size or smaller may also use you to gain the benefits of three-quarters cover.

20.name: Armor of the Gods
description: At 20th level, as a bonus action, you can create an additional layer of armor made of solidified arcane energy over your existing armor. For the next minute, you gain the following benefits:

• If you would take 15 or less damage, you instead take no damage, and ignore any additional effects of the damage's source.
  • Whenever a creature within your aura takes damage, you can choose to take the damage in place of that creature.
  • Creatures of your choice within your aura always gain the benefits of half cover.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Unbreakable

description: The Oath of Vengeance is a solemn commitment to punish those who have committed a grievous sin. When evil forces slaughter helpless villagers, when an entire people turns against the will of the gods, when a thieves' guild grows too violent and powerful, when a dragon rampages through the countryside - at times like these, paladins arise and swear an Oath of Vengeance to set right that which has gone wrong. To these paladins - sometimes called avengers or dark knights - their own purity is not as important as delivering justice.

subFeatures.name: By Any Means Necessary
description: Your qualms can't get in the way of exterminating your foes.

subFeatures.name: No Mercy For the Wicked
description: Ordinary foes might win your mercy, but your sworn enemies do not.

subFeatures.name: Fight the Greater Evil
description: Faced with a choice of fighting your sworn foes or combating a lesser evil, choose the greater evil.

1.name: Vow of Enmity
description: Starting at 1st level, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to make a vow to destroy one target. As a bonus action, you can utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. You gain advantage on attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious.
In addition, you gain proficiency in Insight, Investigation, or Survival.

3.name: Vengeful Pursuit
description: Starting at 3rd level, your supernatural focus helps you close off a foe's retreat. When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, you can move up to half your speed immediately after the attack and as part of the same reaction.

3.name: Vengeful Smite
description: Also at 3rd level,when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is frightened of you, and its speed becomes 0 for 1 minute, or until it takes any damage.
Any creature marked by your Vow of Enmity has disadvantage on this saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Vengeance
description: Starting at 7th level, when you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you is forced to make an ability check or saving throw by a creature marked by your Vow of Emnity, they gain a bonus 1d6 to the roll.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Relentless Avenger
description: Starting at 15th level, your supernatural focus helps you menace your sworn foes.  When a creature marked by your Vow of Emnity attacks or forces a creature other than you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to move up to your speed towards that creature and make one melee attack against it.
If you are hit by an opportunity attack as part of this movement, your attack is made at advantage.

20.name: Avenging Angel
description: At 20th level, you can assume the form of an angelic avenger. Using a bonus action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• Wings sprout from your back and grant you a flying speed of 60 feet.
  • You can cast Misty Step at will. If you teleport within 5 feet of a creature, you can make a melee weapon attack against it.
  • Whenever you make a weapon attack roll with advantage, you can forgo advantage on your attack roll to make one additional attack against the target.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of Vengeance

description: The Oath of the Watchers binds paladins to protect mortal realms from the predations of extraplanar creatures, many of which can lay waste to mortal soldiers. Thus, the Watchers hone their minds, spirits, and bodies to be the ultimate weapons against such threats.

Paladins who follow the Watchers' oath are ever vigilant in spotting the influence of extraplanar forces, often establishing a network of spies and informants to gather information on suspected cults. To a Watcher, keeping a healthy suspicion and awareness about one's surroundings is as natural as wearing armor in battle.

subFeatures.name: Discipline
description: You are the shield against the endless terrors that lie beyond the stars. Your blade must be forever sharp and your mind keen to survive what lies beyond.

subFeatures.name: Loyalty
description: Never accept gifts or favors from fiends or those who truck with them. Stay true to your order, your comrades, and your duty.

subFeatures.name: Vigilance
description: The threats you face are cunning, powerful, and subversive. Be ever alert for their corruption.

1.name: Watcher's Will
description: Starting at 1st level, your will is unbreakable. When you or a creature within 30 feet of you makes an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to grant them a bonus to their role equal to your oath ability modifier.

3.name: Turn the Extraplanar
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor and say a prayer to castigate nearby extraplanar foes. Each aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your oath save DC. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

3.name: Binding Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Charisma saving throw.  On a failed save, the target is frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.  While frightened in this way, the target is unable to use any spell or feature that would allow them to teleport or plane shift.
An aberration, celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend has disadvantage on this saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of the Sentinel
description: At 7th level, you emit an aura of alertness while you aren't incapacitated. When you and any creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you roll initiative, you all gain a bonus to initiative equal to your proficiency bonus.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Vigilant Rebuke
description: At 15th level, you've learned how to chastise anyone who dares wield beguilements against you and your wards. Whenever you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you succeeds on an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw, you can use your reaction to deal 2d8 + your oath casting ability modifier force damage to the creature that forced the saving throw.

20.name: Mortal Bulwark
description: At 20th level, you manifest a spark of divine power in defense of the mortal realms. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You gain truesight with a range of 120 feet.
  • You have advantage on attack rolls against aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, and fiends.
  • When you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can also force it to make a Charisma saving throw against your oath save DC. On a failed save, the creature is magically banished to its native plane of existence if it's currently not there. On a successful save, the creature can't be banished by this feature for 24 hours.
Once you use this bonus action, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oath of the Watchers

description: A Blackguard is a paladin who breaks their sacred oaths to pursue some dark ambition or serve an evil power. Whatever light burned in the paladin's heart been extinguished. Only darkness remains.

1.name: Skullspeech
description: Starting at 1st level, your speech is so corrupted that even the dead pause to listen.  You learn to speak, read, and write Dark Speech, the language of evil gods.
In addition, you can cast Murmers of the Restless at will, without expending a spell slot.
Finally, when you hit a hostile creature with a weapon attack, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain temporary hit points equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1).

3.name: Marshall of Darkness
description: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can expend 1 point of Fervor and focus your will at one fiend or undead you can see within 30 feet, forcing it to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the creature must obey your commands for the next 24 hours, or until you use this feature on another target.
This feature has no effect on fiends and undead who have a Challenge Rating equal to or greater than your Paladin level.

3.name: Corrupting Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Charisma saving throw against your oath save DC. On a failed save, the target must immediately use its reaction to make an attack against a creature friendly to them that is within range of one of their attacks (target's choice). If there are no valid targets, the affected creature makes an attack against itself.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Hate
description: Starting at 7th level you, as well any fiends and undead within 10 feet of you, gain a bonus to damage rolls equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of +1).
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.
In addition, you can speak Dark Speech to communicate with corpses as if they were under the effects of Speak with Dead.

15.name: Supernatural Resistance
description: At 15th level, you gain resistance to cold, fire, and lightning damage.

20.name: Dread Lord
description: At 20th level, as a bonus action, you can transform into an avatar of dark hatred. While transformed you gain the following benefits:

• Any bright light within 30 feet of you becomes dim light.
  • When you deal necrotic damage to a creature you gain temporary hit points equal to half the damage dealt.
  • When a creature frightened of you starts its turn within your Aura of Protection it takes 4d10 necrotic damage.
  • As a bonus action, you can force one creature within 30 feet of you to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 4d10 necrotic damage.

This transformation ends early if you become unconscious or you end it as a bonus action. Once you use transform, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again. If you have no uses left, you can expend a 5th-level spell slot to use this transformation again.

subclasses.name: Blackguard

description: A Graceseeker is a paladin who once served a dark master and an evil purpose. Through their service, they may have done unspeakable acts, but now they seek to replace the darkness within themselves with light.

1.name: Sunlight Orb
description: Starting at 1st level, as an action, you expend any number of Fervor points to hurl a ball of searing radiance that explodes at a point within 120 feet of you.  Creatures within 5 feet of the explosion must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, taking fire damage and radiant damage each equal to 1d8 per point of Fervor spent, or half as much on a success.
The area of effect of this feature increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

3.name: Burning Light
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a bonus action to begin shining with burning radiance that threatens to consume everyone around you. For the next minute, you shed bright light in a 20 foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that.

In addition, at the end of each of your turns, you and other creatures within the bright light take radiant damage equal to your oath ability modifier (minimum of 1). You can end this effect early at any time (no action required).

3.name: Sunlit Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to force the target to make a Constitution saving throw.  On a failed saving throw, the target is blinded until the end of your next turn.
A target that is weak to sunlight, such as through the Sunlight Sensitivity trait, has disadvantage on this saving throw.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Brilliance
description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made against illusion spells, and creatures can't benefit from being invisible while within this aura.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.
In addition, any light you create through your spells or paladin features is considered sunlight.

15.name: Blazing Rebuke
description: Starting at 15th level, you can cause your inner light to flash to protect yourself from harm. When a creature within 5 feet of you makes a melee attack against you, you can expend a point of Fervor as a reaction to force them to make the attack at disadvantage. When you use this feature, the target takes radiant damage equal to 2d8 + your oath ability modifier.

20.name: Radiant Form
description: At 20th level, you can temporarily transform yourself and your equipment into pure radiance. Using a bonus action, you undergo a transformation. For 1 minute, you gain the following benefits:

• You have a flying speed of 60 feet and can hover.
  • You can move through spaces as wide as 1 inch without squeezing.
  • You radiate bright light in a 60 foot radius and dim light 60 feet beyond that. Creatures of your choice that enter the bright light for the first time on a turn or start their turn there take radiant damage equal to your paladin level. The light is sunlight. If any of this light's area overlaps with an area of darkness created by a magical effect, the effect that created the darkness is dispelled.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Graceseeker

description: An Oathless is a paladin who once held an oath, good or bad. They now owe allegiance to no one, holding no tenets and being loyal to nothing but themselves.  Oathless are often selfish, with their own safety and power being their only concern.

1.name: Shattered Oath
description: Starting at 1st level, you have no qualms fighting without honor or ignoring the rules of war. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack and there is another hostile creature within 5 feet of your target, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to mark it.
Whenever you damage this marked target with a weapon attack, including the attack used to mark it, you can add your oath ability modifier (minimum of +1) to your damage roll.
However, your duplictious nature is plain to see, and creatures will be less likely to trust you.

3.name: Illusory Escape
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you take damage from a source you can see, you can expend 1 point of Fervor as a reaction to turn invisible and move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. You remain invisible until the beginning of your next turn, or until you attack or force a saving throw.

3.name: Draining Smite
description: Also at 3rd level, when you use your Smite feature, you can expend 1 point of Fervor to gain temporary hit points equal to half the additional damage dealt.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Aura of Deception
description: Starting at 7th level, when you use your Illusory Escape feature, you can force a creature within 10 feet of you to make a Charisma saving throw.  On a failed save, you and the creature instantly switch places, and it takes the triggering damage in your place. You then gain the normal benefits of Illusory Escape starting from the space that you reappear in.
The range of this aura increases as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the Paladin table.

15.name: Forceful Will
description: At 15th level, whenever you force a creature within your aura to make a saving throw to resist the effects of an enchantment or illusion spell, it has disadvantage on its saving throw.

20.name: Icon of Deceit
description: At 20th level, you gain the ability to emanate feelings of treachery. As a bonus action, you can magically become an avatar of deceit, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:

• You are invisible.
  • You can take the Dash or Hide action as a bonus action.
  • When a creature misses you with an attack, you can force it to repeat its attack roll against another creature of your choice within range.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Oathless

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Spellcasting
description: As a student of necromantic magic, you have obtained a grimoire containing spells dealing with the dark arts. At first, your ability to understand the scripture in this tome is limited.
However, you are told that through devoted study and practice you will be able to decipher more of the pages, and the potency of the spells available to you will become formidable.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the Occult spell list. You learn additional pale master cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Pale Master table.

subFeatures.name: Grimoire
description: At 1st level, you have a grimoire containing six 1st-level Occult spells of your choice. Your grimoire is the repository of the Occult spells you know, except your cantrips, which are fixed in your mind.

The spells that you add to your grimoire as you gain levels reflect the occult research you conduct on your own, as well as intellectual breakthroughs you have had about the nature of life and death. You might find other spells during your adventures. You could discover a spell recorded on a scroll in an evil wizard's chest, for example, or in a dusty tome in an ancient library.

subFeatures.name: Copying a Spell Into the Book
description: When you find an Occult spell of 1st level or higher, you can add it to your grimoire if it is of a spell level you can prepare and if you can spare the time to decipher and copy it.

Copying a spell into your grimoire involves reproducing the basic form of the spell, then deciphering the unique system of notation used by the wizard who wrote it. You must practice the spell until you understand the sounds or gestures required, then transcribe it into your grimoire using your own notation.

For each level of the spell, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp.  If the spell belongs to the school of necromancy, it requires only 1 hour and 25 gp per level, instead of the normal cost. The cost represents material components you expend as you experiment with the spell to master it, as well as the fine inks you need to record it. Once you have spent this time and money, you can prepare the spell just like your other spells.

subFeatures.name: Replacing the Book
description: You can copy a spell from your own grimoire into another book-for example, if you want to make a backup copy of your grimoire. This is just like copying a new spell into your grimoire, but faster and easier, since you understand your own notation and already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 gp for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your grimoire, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the spells that you have prepared into a new grimoire. Filling out the remainder of your grimoire requires you to find new spells to do so, as normal. For this reason, many wizards keep backup grimoire in a safe place.

subFeatures.name: The Book's Appearance
description: Your grimoire is a unique compilation of spells, with its own decorative flourishes and margin notes. It might be a plain, functional leather volume that you received as a gift from your master, a finely bound gilt-edged tome you found in an ancient library or even a loose collection of notes scrounged together after you lost your previous grimoire in a mishap.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Pale Master table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Occult spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Occult spells that are available for you to cast. To do so, choose a number of Occult spells from your spellbook equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + your pale master level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of Occult spells requires time spent studying your spellbook and memorizing the incantations and gestures you must make to cast the spell: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Intelligence or Wisdom (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Occult spells.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

subFeatures.name: Ritual Casting
description: You can cast an Occult spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell in your grimoire. You don't need to have the spell prepared.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use an occult focus as a spellcasting focus for your Occult spells.

subFeatures.name: Learning Spells of 1st-Level and Higher
description: Each time you gain a pale master level, you can add two Occult spells of your choice to your grimoire. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown on the Pale Master table. On your adventures, you might find other spells that you can add to your grimoire.

1.name: Undead Servant
description: At 1st level, you forge a bond with a creature of the night, allowing you to use your magic to animate dead flesh into a servile being.
With 8 hours of work and an occult component, you complete a ritual that imbues a material component with a foul mimicry of life, raising it as an undead creature to become your faithful servant.

In combat, the undead servant acts during your turn and moves at your command. It can use its reaction and bonus action (if applicable) on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. You can instead sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the servant to use an Attack, Dash, Disengage or Help action. If you are incapacitated, the servant can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge. If you have an additional creature under your control, such as with the animate dead spell, you can command your servant with the same bonus action you use to command other creatures.

Like a player character, the servant becomes unconscious at 0 hit points and makes death saving throws. If the servant has died within the last hour, you can spend 10 minutes making a sacrifice to revive it with half of its maximum hit points. You cannot revive the servant again in this way until you and your servant have completed a long rest.
The servant also follows all resting rules that apply to player characters, including the ability to roll Hit Dice to regain hit points on a short rest.
The specific nature of your servant, as well as its game statistics and the material component needed to create it, are determined by your requiem.

Requiem of SoulsServantMaterial Component
Requiem of the AshenDust Skeletonthe skull of a humanoid that died violently
Requiem of the BoundAncient Mummya strand of mummy wrappings recovered from an ancient tomb
Requiem of the FrigidFrozen Ghostan icicle that has been used to draw blood
Requiem of the HauntedTenebrous Shadowa block of incense bearing the scent of death
Requiem of the LegionClaw Swarma cluster of fish roe
Requiem of the SanguineVampiric Ghoula vial of your own blood, drawn with a sacrificial dagger
Requiem of the TorporificRotting Zombiea piece of rotted flesh from a humanoid corpse
Requiem of WrathVengeful Wraitha small pouch of gunpowder

2.name: Dark Mending
description: Beginning at 2nd level, you are able heal your wounds and the wounds of undead creations you have created by channeling forbidden necromantic energies. When you or an undead creature under your control that you can see within 60 feet of you is hit with an attack but before the damage is rolled, you can use your reaction to heal the target for an amount equal to one Dark Mending die, a d6. If the target creature is your undead servant, it is healed for double the amount.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier (a minimum of once). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Your Dark Mending die changes when you reach certain levels in this class. The die becomes a d8 at 5th level, a d10 at 10th level, and a d12 at 15th level.

2.name: Death's Whisper
description: Starting at 2nd level, you gain the ability to cast Speak with Dead as a ritual.

Also, the undead who lurk in the dark begin to lose their mystery. You gain darkvision out to 60 feet (if you already have darkvision, its effective distance is increased by 30 feet), you become proficient with the Religion skill if you are not already and you have advantage on all Religion skill checks if they are related to the undead.

6.name: Greater Undead Servant
description: Starting at 6th level, your undead servant's attacks are considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical damage.

10.name: Thrall's Boon
description: Starting at 10th level, when you cast a spell with a range of touch, your undead servant can deliver the spell as if it had cast the spell.
Your servant must be within 100 feet of you, and it must use its reaction to deliver the spell when you cast it. If the spell requires an attack roll, you use your attack modifier for the roll.

18.name: Necromastery
description: At 18th level, you have gained mastery over certain pale master spells, allowing you to cast them at will.

Choose a 1st-level Occult spell and a 1st or 2nd-level Occult spell that are in your grimoire. Those spells are always considered prepared, and they don't count against your maximum number of prepared spells.  In addition, you can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

20.name: Rebuke the Grave
description: At 20th level, you have learned the secrets of undeath, allowing you to become partially undead yourself to gain certain benefits:

• You do not need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep, and you do not age.
  • You are immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition, you are immune to disease, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.
  • You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, or stunned, and you have advantage on saving throws made to avoid exhaustion.
  • You have resistance to necrotic damage.
  • If you are ever killed, you return to life 24 hours later. If your body was destroyed, a new body is created at a point within 1 mile of where you died.

Ashen pale masters focus on the ebbs and flows of life and death. They feel most comfortable surrounded by armies made of bone, and have expanded their prowess to utilize rudimentary flame magic to aid in the process of turning creatures to ash, feeding the regrowth process.

1.name: Ossien Armor
description: When you choose this requiem at 1st level, your skin becomes hard as bone in response to attacks to grant you some natural protection. While you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your Armor Class equals 13 + your Constitution modifier.

1.name: Dust Skeleton Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a dust skeleton, which uses the following statistics. Your servant is proficient with light armor and all simple weapons. When the skeleton makes an attack with a weapon, it uses your spell attack modifier.

Dust Skeleton
Medium undead
Armor Class: 13 + PB (leather)
Hit Points: 5 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 5 times your pale master level
Speed: 30 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
9 (-1)15 (+2)13 (+1)7 (-2)8 (-1)6 (-2)
Saving Throws: DEX +2 plus PB, CON +1 plus PB
Skills Acrobatics +2 plus PB, Stealth +2 plus PB
Damage Vulnerabilities: bludgeoning
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Skeletal Camouflage.While the dust skeleton remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal humanoid's skeleton.
Actions
Slam. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d4 + PB bludgeoning damage.

3.name: Skeletal Grasp
description: At 3rd level, you inscribe a rune into one of your arms that causes the flesh to evaporate off of it, leaving you with only bones.

Your skeletal arm can be used as a spellcasting focus for your Occult spells, and it is considered a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient, dealing 1d8 necrotic damage on a hit. You can use your spellcasting ability modifier, rather than Strength, for attack and damage rolls with it.

When you hit a creature with your skeletal grasp, you can force them to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed saving throw, the creature is incapacitated until the start of their next turn or until they take any damage. You can force this saving throw a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Dust Mastery
description: At 6th level, your skeleton gains control over the dust covering itself, granting it the ability to use the following actions. The skeleton can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Dredged Breath
description: As an action, the skeleton exhales a 15-foot cone of blinding dust. Each creature in that area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be Blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subFeatures.name: Dust Devil
description: As a reaction when targeted with an attack, the skeleton can create a small dust storm around itself that lasts until the start of its next turn. While active, the dust storm imposes disadvantage on attacks made against the skeleton for the duration.

10.name: Reanimation
description: Starting at 10th level, if your undead servant has been destroyed, you can expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher as an action to instantly revive it with half of its maximum hit points.

14.name: Shell of Bone
description: Starting at 14th level, when you would be hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the damage dealt by the attack.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Ashen

description: Bound pale masters prefer to keep their enemies in place and slowly kill them through use of agonizing necromantic magic that makes each moment a living nightmare.

1.name: Clutching Rot
description: Starting at 1st level, you know how best to bind up a creature. You have proficiency in the Athletics skill, and have advantage on ability checks made to tie knots.
In addition, when you make a Strength (Athletics) check to grapple a creature, you can use your spellcasting ability modifier in place of your Strength modifier.

1.name: Ancient Mummy Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of an ancient mummy, which uses the following statistics.

Ancient Mummy
Medium undead
Armor Class: 11 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 6 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 6 times your pale master level
Speed: 30 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
14 (+2)8 (-1)17 (+3)6 (-2)9 (-1)7 (-2)
Saving Throws: STR +2 plus PB, CON +3 plus PB
Skills: Athletics +2 plus PB, Survival -1 plus PB
Damage Vulnerabilities: fire
Damage Immunities: necrotic, poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Mummy Rot. When the mummy deals necrotic damage to a creature, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its maximum hit points reduced by an equal amount.
Actions
Decaying Grasp. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d4 + PB necrotic damage.

3.name: Spectral Wrappings
description: Starting at 3rd level, you gain control over spectral wrappings that bind and ensnare your enemies. As a bonus action, you or your servant can attempt to grapple a Large or smaller creature within 10 feet of you with your wrappings.
You and your servant each have two such wrappings, each of which can grapple a single creature.

6.name: Curse of Rot
description: Starting at 6th level, your mummy servant's rotting curse grows more powerful, granting it the following actions. The mummy can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Rotting Grasp
description: As an action, the mummy makes a melee attack (your spell attack modifier to hit) against a creature within 5 feet of it, dealing 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit. In addition, if the target fails their saving throw against the mummy's Mummy Rot trait, it must repeat the saving throw at the start of each of its turns, having its hit point maximum reduced by 1d4 if it fails its saving throw, and ending the effect if it succeeds. If this effect reduces the target's hit point maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. A remove curse spell can end this effect.

subFeatures.name: Rejuvenation
description: As a reaction when it takes damage, the mummy can gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier + your proficiency bonus. These temporary hit points are gained before the damage is taken.

10.name: Withering Wrap
description: Starting at 10th level, you can channel necromantic magic through your mummy wrappings to drain the life of a wrapped target. As a bonus action, you can deal necrotic damage equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier to a creature grappled by your mummy wrappings.
In addition, you gain a third wrapping that can grapple an additional creature, and your wrappings can grapple Huge or smaller creatures.

14.name: Sepulcher
description: Starting at 14th level, as an action, you can fully encase a wrapped creature using all of your mummy wrappings. While a creature is encased, you cannot grapple any other creatures using your mummy wrappings.

An encased creature is considered paralyzed, and takes necrotic damage equal to your pale master level at the start of each of their turns. An encased creature can make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your spell save DC at the end of each of their turns, breaking free on a success.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
In addition, you gain a fourth wrapping that can grapple an additional creature.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Bound

description: Frigid pale masters bring a cold gripping death to their foes. Harnessing the chill of winter, they are able conjure ice and snow on a whim.

1.name: Icy Soul
description: Starting at 1st level when you choose this requiem, you are considered acclimated to extreme cold.
In addition, you learn the frostbite cantrip. It is considered an Occult spell for you.

1.name: Frozen Ghost Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a frigid ghost, which uses the following statistics.

Frigid Ghost
Medium undead
Armor Class: 12 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 4 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 4 times your pale master level
Speed: fly 40 ft. (hover)
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
1 (-5)15 (+2)11 (0)10 (0)12 (+1)14 (+2)
Saving Throws: DEX +2 plus PB, CHA +2 plus PB
Skills: Intimidation +2 plus PB, Stealth +2 plus PB
Damage Vulnerabilities: fire
Damage Resistances: acid, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
Damage Immunities: cold, necrotic, poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 11
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Soul Phasing. The ghost can pass through enemy spaces as though they were difficult terrain, but cannot end its turn in a space occupied by another creature.
Actions
Ice Shard. Melee or Ranged Spell Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, range 30/120, one target you can see. Hit: 1d4 + PB cold damage.

3.name: Winter's Bite
description: Starting at 3rd level, your icy magic can further hobble a creature. Once per turn when you deal cold damage to a creature with a spell of 1st-level or higher, you can impose one of the following additional effects of your choice:

• Its speeds are reduced by 10 feet until the end of your next turn.
  • It has disadvantage on the next ability check it makes before the end of your next turn.
  • It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
In addition, you gain resistance to cold damage.

6.name: Blizzard Spirit
description: At 6th level, your ghost's form drops dramatically in temperature, granting it the following actions. The ghost can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Freezing Drain
description: As an action, the shadow makes a melee spell attack (your spell attack modifier to hit) against a creature within 5 feet of it, dealing 2d6 cold damage on a hit and regaining hit points equal to the damage dealt.

subFeatures.name: Tendancy
description: As a reaction when targeted with an attack, the ghost can briefly possess the target's mind. The attacker must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be unable to attack the ghost until after the end of the ghost's next turn; the attacker must choose a new target or else lose the attack.

10.name: Frozen Over
description: Starting at 10th level, when you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a spell or pale master feature that deals cold damage, they are frozen into an ice sculpture, killing them instantly.

A frozen creature radiates extreme cold for 1 minute after they are killed, and creatures that start their turns within 5 feet of the frozen creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take cold damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

14.name: Sheer Cold
description: Starting at 14th level, your spells and pale master features ignore resistance to cold damage, and treat immunity as resistance. This feature does not apply to your frigid ghost servant.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Frigid

description: Haunted pale masters live in the shadows. They are able to spread their influence to snuff out light and enjoy terrifying their foes with thoughts of the unknown.

1.name: One With Darkness
description: When you choose this requiem at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Stealth skill, and you can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

1.name: Tenebrous Shadow Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a tenebrous shadow, which uses the following statistics.

Tenebrous Shadow
Medium undead
Armor Class: 12 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 4 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 4 times your pale master level
Speed: fly 40 ft. (hover)
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
