4 (-3)15 (+2)8 (-1)8 (-1)13 (+1)7 (-1)
Saving Throws: DEX +2 plus PB, WIS +1 plus PB
Skills: Insight +1 plus PB, Stealth +2 plus PB
Damage Vulnerabilities: radiant
Damage Resistances: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
Damage Immunities: necrotic, poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 11
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Amorphous. The shadow can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.
Actions
Dark Embrace. Melee Spell Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d4 + PB necrotic damage.

3.name: Occult Sight
description: Starting at 3rd level, no darkness can hide things from you. You can see normally in darkness and dim light, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.

6.name: Duplicitous Shadows
description: Starting at 6th level, the confusion of shadows can allow you to easily surround and disorient your enemies. Your tenebrous shadow gains the following actions. The shadow can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Blinding Embrace
description: As an action, the shadow makes a melee spell attack (your spell attack modifier to hit) against a creature within 5 feet of it, dealing 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit and forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be blinded until the end of the target's next turn.

subFeatures.name: Shadow Stride
description: As a reaction when the shadow is hit by an attack that deals damage, the shadow can engulf itself in darkness and teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that it can see.

10.name: Nyctophobia
description: Starting at 10th level, your darkness can cause irrational fear in your victims. If a creature is unable to see or within an area of magical darkness as a result of a spell you cast or one of your pale master features, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC at the start of each of their turns. On a failed saving throw, the creature is frightened until the start of their next turn or until they can see again, whichever comes first.

14.name: Secrecy of the Night
description: Starting at 14th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn. If the spell is cast using your Thrall's Boon feature, only you need to be hidden from the target, not your servant.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Haunted

description: Why only hold one creature under your command when you can fight with many?  Pale masters of the Requiem of the Legion are masters of using a swarm of undead monstrosities to overwhelm their enemies with sheer numbers.

1.name: Swarm's Grasp
description: Also at 1st level, you learn the Mage Hand cantrip if you don't already know it. When you cast it, the hand takes the form of your claw swarm.

1.name: Claw Swarm Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a swarm of undead claws, which use the following statistics.

Claw Swarm
Medium swarm of Tiny undead
Armor Class: 10 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 7 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 7 times your pale master level
Speed: 40 ft., climb 40 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
16 (+3)12 (+1)11 (0)5 (-3)10 (0)4 (-3)
Saving Throws: STR +3 plus PB, DEX +1 plus PB
Skills Athletics +3 plus PB, Sleight of Hand +1 plus PB
Damage Resistances: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, stunned
Senses: blindsight 30 ft. (blind beyond this radius), passive Perception 10
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Swarm.The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny crawling claw.
Actions
Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm's space. Hit: 2d4 + PB slashing damage or 1d4 + PB slashing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer.

3.name: Profane Army
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have a mastery of commanding your undead forces in battle, gaining the following benefits:

• If you have multiple undead creatures you can command using your bonus action, you can command all of them using a single bonus action.
  • When you are targeted by an attack, if there is an undead creature you control within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to switch spaces with them, causing them to become the new target of the attack.

6.name: Swarm Interference
description: At 6th level, your swarm gains expertise in causing interference, granting it the ability to use the following actions. The swarm can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Claw's Grasp
description: As an action, the swarm forces a creature in its space to make a Strength saving throw.  On a failed saving throw, the target is restrained by the swarm, and the swarm can't move or target another creature until the condition ends.  An affected creature can repeat its saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effects on a successful save.

subFeatures.name: Swarming Interception
description: As a reaction when a creature in the swarm's space makes an attack, the swarm can interrupt them to impose disadvantage on their attack roll.

10.name: Dexterous Swarm
description: Starting at 10th level, your control of your swarm grows in finesse.  When you cast Mage Hand, you can perform the following additional actions with it:

• You can stow one object the hand is holding in a container worn or carried by another creature.
  • You can retrieve an object in a container worn or carried by another creature.
  • It can use any set of tools that you are proficient with.
  • You can perform one of these tasks without being noticed by a creature if you succeed on a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by the creature's Wisdom (Perception) check.

10.name: Skittering Horror
description: Also at 10th level, your undead servant's walking speed and climbing speed increase to 60 feet.

14.name: Call the Legion
description: By 14th level, you never need to engage in combat yourself, and only need to command your unholy legions.  When you roll initiative, you can cast a spell that creates undead creatures under your control and has a casting time of 1 action, such as the Army of the Dead or Danse Macabre spells.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Legion

description: Sanguine pale masters make use of vampiric abilities to drain the life force of their enemies.

1.name: Bloodsense
description: Starting when you choose this requiem at 1st level, you can innately sense things about the life forces of creatures. As a bonus action, you can lock your senses onto a creature with blood that you can see within 30 feet of you, learning the following things about it:

• Current and maximum hit points
  • Damage resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities
  • Active conditions, diseases, and curses
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

1.name: Vampiric Ghoul Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a vampiric ghoul, which uses the following statistics.  Your servant is proficient with all simple weapons.  When the ghoul makes an attack with a weapon, it uses your spell attack modifier.

Vampiric Ghoul
Medium undead
Armor Class: 11 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 6 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 6 times your pale master level
Speed: 30 ft., climb 20 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
17 (+2)8 (-1)14 (+2)6 (-2)11 (0)7 (-2)
Saving Throws: STR +3 plus PB, CON +2 plus PB
Skills Acrobatics -1 plus PB, Perception +0 plus PB
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10 + PB
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Spider Climb. The ghoul can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Actions
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d6 + PB piercing damage and the ghoul gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.

3.name: Scarlet Drain
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the life force of other creatures to fuel your blood magic. When you cast a spell that requires you to expend hit dice, you can instead force a creature that has blood within 30 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature can choose to fail this saving throw.

On a failed saving throw, the creature loses the requisite number of hit dice needed to cast the spell, and you do not need to expend any hit dice. If the creature does not have enough remaining hit dice to cast the spell, it loses all remaining hit dice, and you must expend hit dice to make up the difference.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Ghastly Horror
description: Starting at 6th level, your ghoul companion becomes a ghast, gaining the following actions. The ghoul can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Stench
description: As an action, the ghoul exudes the stench of death. Creatures within 5 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be poisoned for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

subFeatures.name: Feeding Frenzy
description: As a reaction when it is hit by an attack, the ghoul can make a Bite attack against a random creature within 5 feet of it.

10.name: Enhanced Bloodsense
description: Starting at 10th level, your bloodsense increases in power, and you gain the ability to learn the following additional things about a creature when you use it:

• Total level
  • Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores
  • Number of remaining hit dice
In addition, you can now use your bloodsense on a creature up to 60 feet away.

14.name: Wings of the Night
description: Starting at 14th level, you can call upon a vampire's ability to fly. As a bonus action, you can sprout a pair of leathery bat wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your walking speed. The wings last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Sanguine

description: Torporific pale masters spread disease and decay across the battlefield.

1.name: Diseasing Spells
description: Starting when you choose this requiem at 1st level, all of your spells carry disease with them. When you deal damage to a creature with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can additionally force the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, becoming poisoned until the start of your next turn on a failed saving throw.
You can use this a feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

1.name: Rotting Zombie Servant
description: Your undead servant takes the form of a rotting zombie, which uses the following statistics. Your servant is proficient with light armor, medium armor, and all simple weapons. When the zombie makes an attack with a weapon, it uses your spell attack modifier.

Rotting Zombie
Medium undead
Armor Class: 10 + PB (nattural armor)
Hit Points: 7 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 7 times your pale master level
Speed: 20 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
14 (+2)8 (-1)17 (+3)6 (-2)9 (-1)7 (-2)
Saving Throws: STR +2 plus PB, CON +3 plus PB
Skills Athletics +2 plus PB, Survival -1 plus PB
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 9
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Undead Fortitude. If damage reduces the zombie to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, the zombie drops to 1 hit point instead.
Actions
Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d6 + PB slashing damage.
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 2d4 + PB piercing damage.

3.name: Decaying Touch
description: At 3rd level, you inscribe a rune into one of your arms that causes the flesh on it to rot and fester.

Your skeletal arm can be used as a spellcasting focus for your Occult spells, and it is considered a simple melee weapon with which you are proficient, dealing 1d8 necrotic damage on a hit. You can use your spellcasting ability modifier, rather than Strength, for attack and damage rolls with it.

When you hit a creature with your decaying touch, you can force them to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed saving throw, the target is poisoned until the end of their next turn. You can force this saving throw a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Rage of Undeath
description: At 6th level, your zombie becomes more ferocious in its opposition of your enemies, granting it the following actions. The zombie can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Vile Smash
description: As an action, the zombie makes a melee attack (your spell attack modifier to hit) against a creature within 5 feet of it, dealing 2d6 poison damage on a hit and forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be poisoned until the end of the target's next turn.

subFeatures.name: Disparaging Retaliation
description: As a reaction when the zombie is hit by an attack, it can make a Claw attack against the attacker if the attacker is within 5 feet of the zombie.

10.name: Enduring Flesh
description: Starting at 10th level, your undead servant is much harder to actually destroy. Whenever your servant takes at least 5 bludgeoning or slashing damage from a single source, roll a d20 to determine what else happens to it:

d20Effect
1 - 8One leg is severed from the zombie if it has any legs left. A severed leg is unable to attack and has a speed of 5 feet. The zombie's speed is halved if it's missing a leg. If it loses both legs, it falls prone. If it has both arms, it can crawl. With only one arm, it can still crawl, but its speed is halved. With no arms or legs, its speed is 0 feet, and it can't benefit from bonuses to speed.
9 - 16One arm is severed from the zombie if it has any arms left. A severed arm has a speed of 5 feet and can make one Claw attack on its turn, with disadvantage on the attack roll. The zombie cannot use its Vile Smash action if it is missing either arm.
17 - 20The zombie is decapitated. If its head is severed, the zombie loses its bite attack and its body is blinded unless the head can see it. The severed head has a speed of 0 feet. It can make a Bite attack, but only against a target in its space. The zombie cannot use its Vile Smash action if it is missing its head.

If the zombie is reduced to 0 hit points, all parts of it die. Until then, a severed part acts on the zombie's initiative and has its own action and movement. A severed part has AC 8. Any damage it takes is subtracted from the zombie's hit points.
If the zombie is alive, you can use an action to re-attach any separated parts.

14.name: Billowing Decay
description: At 14th level, if you kill a humanoid creature with a spell that you cast, you can choose to raise them as a zombie under your control at the end of your next turn (no action required). Zombies created by this feature are friendly to you and obey your verbal commands to the best of their ability.
The only action they can take is the Attack action. The zombies last for 1 minute, after which time they collapse and die.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended hit points when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Requiem of the Torporific

description: Pale masters who use the requiem of wrath prefer to manipulate the emotions of their enemies, often tricking them into fleeing in terror or fighting against one another.

1.name: Voice of Wrath
description: Starting when you choose this requiem at 1st level, others feel the vengeful rage in your voice when you speak. You gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill. In addition, when you speak, creatures that can understand at least one language can always understand what you say.

1.name: Vengeful Wraith Servant
description: Pale masters who use the requiem of wrath prefer to manipulate the emotions of their enemies, often tricking them into fleeing in terror or fighting against one another.

Vengeful Wraith
Medium undead
Armor Class: 12 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 3 + your spellcasting ability modifier + 3 times your pale master level
Speed: fly 30 ft. (hover)
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
4 (-3)15 (+2)8 (-1)8 (-1)7 (-1)13 (+1)
Saving Throws: DEX +2 plus PB, CHA +1 plus PB
Skills: Intimidation +1 plus PB, Stealth +2 plus PB
Damage Vulnerabilities: radiant
Damage Resistances: acid, cold, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks
Damage Immunities: necrotic, poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 11
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Incorporeal Movement. The wraith can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Actions
Vengeful Grasp. Melee Spell Attack: your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one target you can see. Hit: 1d6 + PB psychic damage.

3.name: Invoke Wrath
description: Starting at 3rd level, your touch can invoke feelings of incredible fury. As an action, you can force a creature within 5 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed saving throw, on their next turn, the target must move up to their speed towards a creature of your choice and use their action to attack the creature if they end their movement within 5 feet of the creature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Outrage
description: At 6th level, your wraith's thirst for vengeance grows, granting it the following actions. The wraith can use each of the actions a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Life Drain
description: As an action, the wraith makes a melee spell attack (your spell attack modifier to hit) against a creature within 5 feet of it, dealing 2d6 necrotic damage on a hit. In addition, the target cannot regain hit points by any means short of the wish spell until the end of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Vengeful Strike
description: As a reaction when you are hit by an attack, if the wraith is within 5 feet of the attacker, the wraith can make a Vengeful Grasp attack against the attacker.

10.name: Ire of Death
description: Starting at 10th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you reduces another creature to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to force the killing creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed saving throw, the target feels the pain that their target felt upon death, and is considered stunned until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

14.name: Spirit of Vengeance
description: Starting at 14th level, if you kill a humanoid creature with a spell that you cast, you can choose to raise them as a specter under your control at the end of your next turn (no action required). Specters created by this feature are friendly to you and obey your commands to the best of their ability.
The only action they can take is the Attack action, making one melee attack. The specters last for 1 minute, after which time they fade away and die.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Requiem of Wrath

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Survivalist Knacks
description: In the wild, you have gathered bits of primal knowledge that bolster your exploration, hunting, and tracking skills, known as Survivalist Knacks. At 1st level, you learn two Knacks of your choice.
You learn additional Knacks as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Knacks Known column on the Ranger table.
Each time you gain a level in this class, you can choose one Survivalist Knack you know and replace it with another Knack of your choice for which you meet the prerequisites.

1.name: Favored Terrain
description: You are particularly familiar with one type of natural environment and are adept at traveling and surviving in such regions. At 1st level, choose one type of favored terrain: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or the Underdark.

When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain or the creatures that dwell there, you have advantage on the check if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. When in that terrain, you can ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain, and all enemies that attempt to track you by non-magical means have disadvantage. You can also move stealthily at a normal pace.

1.name: Hunter's Prey
description: Starting at 1st level, you may use your bonus action to mark a single creature as your prey. You must be able to see or hear this creature, or succeed on a Wisdom (Survival) check to track it, the difficulty of which is determined by the Dungeon Master based on your access to tracks or other clues. You can also mark prey when you roll initiative, without expending a bonus action.

You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks to track your prey, as well as Wisdom (Perception) checks to find them. In addition, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to the target whenever you hit it with a weapon attack. This damage increases to 1d8 at 7th level, 1d10 at 13th level, and 1d12 at 19th level.
You can have only one creature marked as your prey at a time. This designation lasts until your next long rest, or until you mark a new creature as your prey.
At certain Ranger levels, the duration of your Hunter's Prey mark increases: at 6th level (8 hours), 10th level (24 hours), 14th level (1 week), and finally at 17th level (indefinite).

2.name: Fighting Style
description: At 2nd level you choose a Fighting Style that best reflects your training. You cannot select a Fighting Style more than once, even if a feature allows you to select another Fighting Style.

2.name: Spellcasting
description: Also at 2nd level, you learn to draw upon the primal magic of the natural world to enhance your survival and combat skills.

subFeatures.name: Preparing and Casting Spells
description: The Ranger table above shows how many spell slots you have to cast spells. To cast a Primal spell of 1st-level or higher, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all of your expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

At the end of each long rest, you prepare a list of spells that are available for you to cast. Choose a number of spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + half your Ranger level, rounded down. The spells must all be from the Primal spell list, and be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for Primal spells as you draw magic from your connection to nature. You use your Wisdom when a Primal spell refers to your spellcasting ability, and you use your Wisdom modifier whenever you set the saving throw DC or make a spell attack roll for one of your Primal spells.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your Primal spells. See the Player's Handbook for examples.

subFeatures.name: Ritual Casting
description: Your knowledge of the natural world allows you to draw out its innate magic. You can cast any Primal spell that you have prepared as a ritual so long as that spell has the ritual tag.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

6.name: Roving
description: At 6th level, your walking speed increases by 5 feet, and you gain a climbing speed and swimming speed equal to your walking speed. Your speeds increase by an additional 5 feet while in your favored terrain.

7.name: Hunter's Instinct
description: Starting at 7th level, your sharply honed instincts allow you to act quickly in the face of danger. You add a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Wisdom modifier.

9.name: Favored Terrain Master
description: At 9th level, your mastery of your favored terrain grants you benefits even outside of it. You gain a benefit based on your favored terrain type. If you have multiple favored terrains, you gain the benefit associated with each type.
You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold.
Your swimming speed increases by 20 feet and you can hold your breath for up to 15 minutes.
You gain resistance to fire damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme heat.
Your climbing speed increases by 20 feet and you ignore penalties to Dexterity (Stealth) checks from wearing medium armor.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
Your climbing speed increases by 20 feet and you have resistance to damage from falling.
You gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison.
You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, increase its range by 30 feet.
You gain resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold.

You gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against poison.
You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, increase its range by 30 feet.

10.name: Nature's Veil
description: At 10th level, you can add your proficiency bonus to Stealth checks made in natural terrain, or double your proficiency bonus instead if you were already proficient in Stealth, and you have advantage on Stealth checks made in your favored terrain. You can also Hide as a bonus action in any terrain. You cannot be tracked by non-magical means in any terrain, unless you wish to leave a trail.

11.name: Adaptable
description: Your time in the wilderness has taught you that anything that doesn't change dies. Starting at 11th level, when you finish a long rest, you can replace one Knack you know with another Knack of your choice, so long as you meet its prerequisites.

18.name: Feral Senses
description: You hunt as an apex predator, never losing track of your prey. Starting at 18th level, you cannot have disadvantage on any attack roll you make that targets a creature within 30 feet of you or a creature that is marked as your Hunter's Prey.

20.name: Foe Slayer
description: You are a Ranger of mythic skill, rivaling the great huntsmen of legend. At 20th level, when you hit your Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack, you can immediately end the mark and cause that attack to deal maximum damage instead of rolling.
If the damage from this attack reduces the target to 50 hit points or fewer, it is instantly reduced to 0 hit points.
Once you use this feature you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

The Beast Master conclave embodies a friendship between the civilized races and the beasts of the world. United in focus, beast and ranger work as one to fight the monstrous foes that threaten civilization and the wilderness alike. Emulating the Beast Master conclave means committing yourself to this ideal, working in partnership with an animal as its companion and friend.

3.name: Beast Companion
description: At 3rd level, you gain a beast companion that accompanies you on your adventures and is trained to fight alongside you. It is able to understand simple speech and commands. The beast grows along with you, using your proficiency bonus (PB) as its own. The beast can be created using the Beast Companion rules. Choose traits that fit the type of creature you wish to bond with, or use one of the example stat blocks.

In combat, the beast acts during your turn and moves at your command. It can use its reaction and bonus action (if applicable) on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. You can instead sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the beast to use an Attack, Dash, Disengage or Help action. If you are incapacitated, the beast can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

Like a player character, the beast becomes unconscious at 0 hit points and makes death saving throws. If the beast has died within the last hour, you can use an action and expend a spell slot to revive it.
The beast also follows all resting rules that apply to player characters, including the ability to roll Hit Dice to regain hit points on a short rest.
If your companion has an effect that requires a saving throw, its DC is equal to your spell save DC.

subFeatures.name: Step 1: Size
description: Choose your companion's size from Tiny, Small, or Medium.

subFeatures.name: Step 2: Ability Scores
description: Choose your companion's ability score array from Bulky, Middling, or Light.  Your choice determines its ability Strength, Dexterity, and Constituion scores, its Armor Class, its hit points, and the size of its hit die.
Your companion's ability scores are as follows, and it has hit points equal to 6 + six times your ranger level.  Its hit dice are d10s.

subFeatures.name: Step 3: Speeds
description: Choose your companion's speed array from Amphibious, Aquatic, Burrower, Climber, Flyer, or Terrestrial.  Your choice determines its walking speed, as well as any additional speeds it may have.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a swimming speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 5 feet and a swimming speed of 60 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a burrowing speed of 10 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 30 feet and a climbing speed of 30 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 10 feet and a flying speed of 60 feet.
Your companion has a walking speed of 40 feet and a swimming speed of 10 feet.

subFeatures.name: Step 4: Natural Weapons
description: Choose two of the following natural weapons for your companion to be capable of using.  Note that it must have the proper anatomy to perform an attack with a given natural weapon.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d8 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a bite attack, it can attempt to grapple the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing slashing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a claw attack, it can make another claw attack as a bonus action.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its claws' attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If your companion hits with a pummel attack, it can attempt to shove the target as a bonus action.

Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 5 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d4 + its Strength modifier on a hit.  If the target fails its saving throw against Envenom, it takes an additional 1d8 poison damage.  Your companion can use its Dexterity modifier in place of its Strength modifier for its stinger's attack and damage rolls.
Your companion makes a melee attack against a target within 10 feet of it, dealing piercing damage equal to 1d6 + its Strength modifier on a hit.

Your companion makes a ranged attack with a normal range of 30 feet and a long range of 60 feet.  On a hit, the target is restrained by webbing.  As an action, the restrained target can make a Strength ability check, bursting the webbing on a success. The webbing has an AC of 10, 5 hit points, vulnerability to fire damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Step 5: Skills
description: Choose two skills from Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, and Survival for your companion to be proficient in.

subFeatures.name: Step 6: Special Features
description: Choose one of each of the following special features for your companion to have.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on hearing.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on sight.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on smell.
Your companion has advantage on checks that rely on its sense of touch.
Your companion has blindsight out to 60 feet as long as it isn't deafened or silenced.
Your companion can breathe water as well as air.
Your companion doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.
Your companion can hold its breath for up to 1 hour.
With a 10-foot running start, your companion can long jump up to 25 feet.
Your companion does not need limbs to walk, swim or climb.
Your companion can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Your companion's long jump is up to 10 feet and its high jump is up to 5 feet, with or without a running start.
Your companion has advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made against effects that would knock it prone.
Your companion's speeds all increase by 5 feet.
Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.

Your companion can only breathe underwater. It has advantage on Stealth checks while underwater.
Your companion has advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature that has less than half its maximum hit points.

If your companion moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage, or an extra 2d6 piercing damage if your companion hit with a Gore attack. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion succeeds on an Athletics check to grapple, it deals additional bludgeoning damage to the target equal to its Strength modifier.

If your companion flies or swims at least 30 feet downward toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be stunned until the end of its next turn.
Your companion can use this action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.

If your companion succeeds on a Bite or Sting attack, the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed saving throw, the target is poisoned for 1 minute. An affected target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Your companion can use this attack a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a long rest.
Your companion has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the beast's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

If your companion makes a long jump at least 10 feet straight toward a target and then hits it with a natural weapon attack on the same turn, the target takes an extra 1d6 bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
If your companion takes damage less than 3 + your ranger level that would reduce it to 0 hit points, it can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.
Your companion can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d6 + your ranger level.
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

Your companion can use a bonus action to give itself advantage on Constitution saving throws against being poisoned or paralyzed for 1 minute, and gain temporary hit points equal to half your ranger level (rounded up).
Your companion can use this feature once, and regains the ability to do so when it finishes a short or long rest.

7.name: Exceptional Training
description: Beginning at 7th level, as a reaction, you and your Beast Companion can grant the other advantage on any saving throw they are forced to make, so long as you can see and are within 30 feet of each other.
Also, your Beast's attacks count as magical for the sake of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks.

11.name: Bestial Fury
description: Starting at 11th level, when you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the beast can make two attacks.

15.name: Primal Bond
description: Beginning at 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.

subclasses.name: Beast Master Conclave

description: Briar knights adopt the branching thicket of the wild as their armor, demonstrating without question that every strike against them will come at a cost. They serve as bulwarks for the natural world, fighting against those who would despoil it with industry or dark magic.

3.name: Bramble Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, while you are concentrating on a spell or other effect, magical thorns sprout from your body. When a creature hits you with a melee attack while you are covered in thorns, the attacker takes 1d4 piercing damage. This damage increases to 2d4 when you reach 7th level.

3.name: Briar Strike
description: Also at 3rd level, you learn the Thorn Whip cantrip. When a hostile creature's movement provokes an attack of opportunity from you, you can use your reaction to cast Thorn Whip, targeting that creature. If you hit, the target's speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.

7.name: Overgrowth
description: Starting at 7th level, while you are under the effects of your Bramble Armor feature, when you move within 5 feet of a creature for the first time on a turn, you can choose to cause thorny branches to lash out at them, dealing 2d4 piercing damage.

11.name: Agonizing Thorns
description: Starting at 11th level, when a spell you cast causes a creature to be grappled or restrained, that creature takes 2d4 piercing damage at the start of each of its turns while it remains grappled or restrained.
Additionally, you ignore resistance to piercing damage.

15.name: Bramble Bulwark
description: Starting at 15th level, you can cast Wall of Thorns without expending a spell slot. When you cast Wall of Thorns in this way, it does not require concentration, and whenever you attempt to move through the wall, you can spend 5 feet of movement to emerge at any other point within 5 feet of the wall.
You can use this feature once, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Briar Knight Conclave

description: Combining their survival skills, an affinity for nature magic, and passion for the high seas, Buccaneers are Rangers who feel more at home on the water than on solid ground. Serving as sailors, pirates, marines, or privateers, they are often one of the most valuable crew members on board their vessels. How did you come to sail the seas? Were you pressed into the service of a pirate captain, or have you sworn to kill a certain sea monster?

3.name: Mariner's Eye
description: Starting at 3rd level, your sight has become especially keen. Whenever you make a Wisdom (Perception) check that relies on your sense of sight, you can treat a roll of 7 or lower on the d20 as an 8.
Also, when you make a weapon attack against a Hunter's Prey that is swimming, you have advantage on your attack roll.

3.name: Sea Legs
description: Also at 3rd level, the time you have spent at sea has granted you abilities that land-locked Rangers lack. You gain the following benefits:

• You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.
  • You can hold your breath underwater for a number of minutes equal to 10 + your Constitution modifier.

7.name: Windswept Hide
description: Starting at 7th level, your experience has granted you increased resistance to the dangers of the sea.  You gain resistance to cold, lightning, and thunder damage.
In addition, you have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid being knocked prone or moved against your will.

11.name: Wrath of the Waves
description: Starting at 11th level, you carry the magic of the high seas whether you are on sea or land. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can imbue your strike with watery magic. When you do, the creature takes additional cold damage equal to one roll of your Hunter's Prey die, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Spell Save DC or be knocked back from you 10 feet in a straight line.  Any creature that is at least one size larger than you has advantage on its Strength saving throw.

15.name: Watery Resilience
description: Starting at 15th level, when a creature you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to temporarily take on a watery form, halving the damage you would take from the triggering attack.
As a part of this reaction, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking attacks of opportunity.

subclasses.name: Buccaneer Conclave

description: Your connection to the natural world takes the form of a draconic spirit, which can manifest in physical form as a drake. As your powers grow, your drake grows as well, blossoming from a small four-legged companion to a majestic winged creature large and strong enough for you to ride. Along the way, you gain an increasing share of the awe-inspiring power of dragons.
Consider the source of the draconic spirit you have bonded with. The Drakewarden Origin table offers examples.

Drakewarden Origin
d6Origin
1You studied a dragon's scale or claw, or a trinket from a dragon's hoard, creating your bond through that token's lingering draconic magic.
2A secret order of rangers who collect and guard draconic lore taught you their ways.
3A dragon gave you a geode or gemstone to care for. To your surprise, the drake hatched from that stone.
4You ingested a few drops of dragon blood, forever infusing your nature magic with draconic power.
5An ancient Draconic inscription on a standing stone empowered you when you read it aloud.
6You had a vivid dream of a mysterious figure accompanied by seven yellow canaries, who warned you of impending doom. When you awoke, your drake was there, watching you.

3.name: Draconic Gift
description: At 3rd level, the bond you share with your drake creates a connection to dragonkind, granting you understanding and empowering your presence.
You learn the Thaumaturgy cantrip, which is a Primal spell for you, and you learn to speak, read, and write Draconic.

3.name: Drake Companion
description: At 3rd level, as an action, you can magically summon the drake that is bound to you. It appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you.

The drake is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the accompanying Drake Companion stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. Whenever you summon the drake, choose a damage type listed in its Draconic Essence trait. You can determine the cosmetic characteristics of the drake, such as its color, its scale texture, or any visible effect of its Draconic Essence; your choice has no effect on its game statistics.

In combat, the drake shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the drake can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.

The drake remains until it is reduced to 0 hit points, until you use this feature to summon the drake again, or until you die. Anything the drake was wearing or carrying is left behind when the drake vanishes.
Once you summon the drake, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to summon it.

Drake Companion
Small dragon
Armor Class: 14 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 5 + five times your ranger level (the drake has a number of hit dice [d10s] equal to your ranger level)
Speed: 40 ft.
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
16 (+3)12 (+1)15 (+2)8 (-1)14 (+2)8 (-1)
Saving Throws: Dex +1 plus PB, Wis +2 plus PB
Damage Immunities: determined by the drake's Draconic Essence trait
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 12
Languages: Draconic
Challenge: Proficiency Bonus (PB) equals your bonus
Draconic Essence. When you summon the drake, choose a damage type: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. The chosen type determines the drake's damage immunity and the damage of its Infused Strikes trait.
Actions
Bite. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 plus PB to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d6 plus PB piercing damage.
Reactions
Infused Strikes. When another creature within 30 feet of the drake that it can see hits a target with a weapon attack, the drake infuses the strike with its essence, causing the target to take an extra 1d6 damage of the type determined by its Draconic Essence.

7.name: Bond of Fang and Scale
description: At 7th level the bond you share with your drake intensifies, protecting you and stoking the drake's fury. When you summon your drake, it grows wings on its back and gains a flying speed equal to its walking speed.
In addition, while your drake is summoned, you and the drake gain the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Dragonrider
description: The drake grows to Medium size. Reflecting your special bond, you can use the drake as a mount if your size is Medium or smaller.

subFeatures.name: Magic Fang
description: The drake's Bite attack deals an extra 1d6 damage of the type chosen for the drake's Draconic Essence.

subFeatures.name: Resistance
description: You gain resistance to the damage type chosen for the drake's Draconic Essence.

11.name: Drake's Breath
description: At 11th level, as an action, you can exhale a 30-foot cone of damaging breath or cause your drake to exhale it. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison damage (your choice doesn't have to match your drake's Draconic Essence). Each creature in the cone must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 8d6 damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
This damage increases to 10d6 when you reach 15th level in this class.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to use it again.

15.name: Perfected Bond
description: At 15th level, your bond to your drake reaches the pinnacle of its power. While your drake is summoned, you and the drake gain the following benefits:

subFeatures.name: Draconic Growth
description: The drake grows to Large size.

subFeatures.name: Empowered Bite
description: The drake's Bite attack deals an extra 1d6 damage of the type chosen for its Draconic Essence (for a total of 2d6 extra damage).

subFeatures.name: Reflexive Resistance
description: When either you or the drake takes damage while you're within 30 feet of each other, you can use your reaction to give yourself or the drake resistance to that instance of damage. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Drakewarden Conclave

description: A fey mystique surrounds you, thanks to the boon of an archfey, the shining fruit you ate from a talking tree, the magic spring you swam in, or some other auspicious event. However you acquired your fey magic, you are now a Fey Wanderer, a ranger who represents both the mortal and the fey realms. As you wander the multiverse, your joyful laughter brightens the hearts of the downtrodden, and your martial prowess strikes terror in your foes, for great is the mirth of the fey and dreadful is their fury. You also possess a preternatural blessing from a fey ally or a place of fey power. Choose your blessing from the Feywild Gifts table or determine it randomly.

Feywild Gifts
d6Gift
1Illusory butterflies flutter around you while you take a short or long rest.
2Fresh, seasonal flowers sprout from your hair each dawn.
3You faintly smell of cinnamon, lavender, nutmeg, or another comforting herb or spice.
4Your shadow dances while no one is looking directly at it.
5Horns or antlers sprout from your head.
6Your skin and hair change color to match the season at each dawn.

3.name: Dreadful Strikes
description: Starting at 3rd level, once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal additional psychic damage to the target equal to one roll of your Hunter's Prey die.
Moreover, when you mark a creature as your Hunter's Prey, you can choose for the bonus damage to by psychic damage.

3.name: Otherworldly Glamour
description: Additionally at 3rd level, your fey qualities give you a supernatural charm. As a result, whenever you make a Charisma check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
In addition, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Performance, or Persuasion.

7.name: Beguiling Twist
description: Beginning at 7th level, the magic of the Feywild guards your mind. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw against being charmed or frightened, you can use your reaction to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If the save fails, the target is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a successful save.

11.name: Fey Reinforcements
description: At 11th level, the royal courts of the Feywild have blessed you with the assistance of fey beings: you know the Summon Fey spell. It doesn't count against the number of Primal spells you know, and you can cast it without a material component. You can also cast it once without using a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.
Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require concentration. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

15.name: Misty Wanderer
description: When you reach 15th level, you can slip in and out of the Feywild to move in a blink of an eye: you can cast Misty Step without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

In addition, whenever you cast Misty Step, you can bring along one willing creature you can see within 5 feet of you. That creature teleports to an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of your destination space.

subclasses.name: Fey Wanderer Conclave

description: Gloom stalkers are at home in the darkest places: deep under the earth, in gloomy alleyways, in primeval forests, and wherever else the light dims. Most folk enter such places with trepidation, but a gloom stalker ventures boldly into the darkness, seeking to ambush threats before they can reach the broader world. Such rangers are often found in the Underdark, but they will go any place where evil lurks in the shadows.

3.name: Dread Ambusher
description: Starting at 3rd level, during the first turn you take in combat, your walking speed increases by 10 feet, which lasts until the end of that turn. If you take the Attack action on that turn, you can make an additional weapon attack as part of that action. If it hits, the target takes bonus damage equal to one roll of your Hunter's Prey die.
In addition, when you roll initiative and aren't surprised, you roll your Hunter's Prey die and add it to your initiative roll.

3.name: Umbral Sight
description: At 3rd level, you gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision from your race, its range increases by 30 feet.
You are also adept at evading creatures that rely on darkvision. While in darkness, you are invisible to any creature that relies on darkvision to see you in that darkness.

7.name: Iron Mind
description: By 7th level, you have honed your ability to resist the mind-altering powers of your prey. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

11.name: Stalker's Flurry
description: At 11th level, you learn to attack with such unexpected speed that you can turn a miss into another strike. Once on each of your turns when you miss with a weapon attack, you can make another weapon attack as part of the same action.

15.name: Shadowy Dodge
description: Starting at 15th level, you can dodge in unforeseen ways, with wisps of supernatural shadow around you. Whenever a creature makes an attack roll against you and doesn't have advantage on the roll, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on it. You must use this feature before you know the outcome of the attack roll.

subclasses.name: Gloom Stalker Conclave

description: Horizon walkers guard the world against threats that originate from other planes or that seek to ravage the mortal realm with otherworldly magic. They seek out planar portals and keep watch over them, venturing to the Inner Planes and the Outer Planes as needed to pursue their foes. These rangers are also friends to any forces in the multiverse - especially benevolent dragons, fey, and elementals - that work to preserve life and the order of the planes.

3.name: Detect Portal
description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal. As an action, you detect the distance and direction to the closest planar portal within 1 mile of you.

3.name: Planar Warrior
description: Starting at 3rd level, as a bonus action, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet. The next time you hit that creature on this turn with a weapon attack, all damage dealt by the attack becomes force damage, and the creature takes additional force damage equal to two rolls of your Hunter's Prey die.

7.name: Ethereal Step
description: At 7th level, you learn to step through the Ethereal Plane. As a bonus action on your turn, you can cast the Etherealness spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the spell ends at the end of the current turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

11.name: Distant Strike
description: At 11th level, you gain the ability to pass between the planes in a blink of an eye. When you use the Attack action, you can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see.
If you attack at least two different creatures with the action, you can make one additional attack with it against a third creature.

15.name: Spectral Defense
description: At 15th level, your ability to move between planes enables you to slip through the planar boundaries to lessen the harm done to you during battle. When you take damage from an attack, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to all of that attack's damage on this turn.

subclasses.name: Horizon Walker Conclave

description: Some rangers seek to master weapons to better protect civilization from the terrors of the wilderness. Members of the Hunter Conclave learn specialized fighting techniques for use against the most dire threats, from rampaging ogres and hordes of orcs to towering giants and terrifying dragons.

3.name: Hunter's Prey
description: At 3rd level, you are ruthless in pursuing your chosen prey. You gain the features below, but once you use one of these features you cannot use another until the beginning of your next turn:

subFeatures.name: Cripple
description: When you hit a Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack, you can force it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, its speed is reduced to 0 until the beginning of your next turn.

subFeatures.name: Flurry
description: When you hit your Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack, you can make an additional weapon attack with the same weapon against another creature within 5 feet of your Hunter's Prey and within the weapon's range.

subFeatures.name: Focus
description: When you hit your Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack and it has fewer then its maximum hit points, you can double your Hunter's Prey damage bonus against it.

7.name: Defensive Tactics
description: At 7th level, you have trained to defend yourself against your prey. You gain one of the features below of your choice:
When a creature that is at least one size larger than you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use a reaction to make one weapon attack against it.
Opportunity attacks against you are made at disadvantage, and if your Hunter's Prey makes an opportunity attack against you it misses unless they roll a critical hit.
When you are forced to make a saving throw to resist being charmed, frightened, or stunned, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to one roll of your Hunter's Prey die.

11.name: Flexible Hunter
description: Starting at 11th level, at the end of a long rest you can do one of the following:

• Replace your Fighting Style with another Fighting Style, choosing from those available to the Ranger class.
  • Replace your Defensive Tactics feature with another feature of your choice from Defensive Tactics.

11.name: Multiattack
description: At 11th level, you are adept at destroying your prey and any creatures that would stand with them. You gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Volley
description: As an action, you can make a ranged attack against your Hunter's Prey and any number of creatures within 10 feet of it, so long as the targets are also within the range of your weapon. You must roll a separate attack roll for each target, and you must have ammunition for each individual attack.

subFeatures.name: Whirlwind Attack
description: As an action, you make a melee attack against your Hunter's Prey and any number of other creatures within range. Make a separate attack roll for each target.

15.name: Superior Defense
description: At 15th level, you have mastered defending yourself from those that you have marked as your prey. You gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Evasion
description: When your Hunter's Prey subjects you to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take half damage, such as you instead take no damage if you succeed on a saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

subFeatures.name: Uncanny Dodge
description: When your Hunter's Prey hits you with an attack, you can use a reaction to halve the damage you take.

subclasses.name: Hunter Conclave

description: You have dedicated yourself to hunting down creatures of the night and wielders of grim magic. A monster slayer seeks out vampires, dragons, evil fey, fiends, and other magical threats. Trained in supernatural techniques to overcome such monsters, slayers are experts at unearthing and defeating mighty, mystical foes.

3.name: Slayer's Insight
description: At 3rd level, you have a keen eye for the weak points of foes. When you roll initiative, so long as you are not surprised, you can use your reaction to mark one creature that you can see as your Hunter's Prey.

Moreover, when you mark a creature as your Hunter's Prey you immediately learn if it has any damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities and what they are. If it is hidden from divination magic, such as by a nondetection spell you sense that the creature has no immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities.

7.name: Iron Will
description: At 7th level, you gain extra resilience against your prey's assaults on your mind and body. Whenever your Hunter's Prey forces you to make a saving throw and whenever you make an ability check to escape that target's grapple, you gain a bonus to your roll equal to your Hunter's Prey die.

11.name: Bane of Darkness
description: At 11th level, your hatred for evil empowers your weapons. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal additional radiant damage equal to your Hunter's Prey die.

15.name: Ruthless Counter
description: At 15th level, if your Hunter's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, casts a spell, or attempts to teleport, you can use your reaction to make a single weapon attack against it using a weapon you are holding. On a hit, you automatically succeed on the saving throw, or its spell or teleport automatically fails.

subclasses.name: Monster Slayer Conclave

description: While most Rangers stand with a foot in the wild and one in the civilized world, some side firmly with nature. Where cities and industry threaten ancient groves and sacred woods, the Rangers known as Primeval Guardians stand as defenders of the natural world. Wielding the primeval magic of creation, these warriors can take on a terrible form, reminiscent of the flora and fauna that they have sworn to defend.

3.name: Guardian Form
description: Starting at 3rd level, The primordial forests you protect lend you their power. You can use your bonus action to take on your Guardian Form. In Guardian Form, you retain your game statistics, you take on tree-like appearance, and you gain the benefits below:

• Your skin becomes bark-like and resilient. Your Armor Class is equal to 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Wisdom modifier, unless it was already higher. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.
  • At the start of each of your turns, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).
  • The reach of your melee attacks increases by 5 feet.
  • Your unarmed strikes deal 1d10 bludgeoning damage on a hit,and you can use your Wisdom modifier for attack and damage rolls with them.
  • When you would make a Strength (Athletics) check, you can instead make a Wisdom (Athletics) check.

Your transformation lasts for 10 minutes.  It ends early if you are reduced to 0 hit points, or if you choose to dismiss it (no action required).  Once you transform, you must finish a short or long rest before you can do so again.  When you have no uses of this feature remaining, you can expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to transform again.

3.name: Piercing Thorns
description: Also at 3rd level, your attacks are enhanced by primal thorns.  Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal additional piercing damage equal to your Hunter's Prey die.

7.name: Ancient Fortitude
description: At 7th level, you gain the endurance of ancient forests.  While you are in your Guardian form, you gain the following additional benefits:

• Your size category is increased by one.
  • When you enter your Guardian form, you gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Ranger level.
In addition, you learn to speak, read, and write Druidic.

11.name: Vengeful Thorns
description: Starting at 11th level, the magic of your primal thorns hinders the movement of those who would descrate your charge.  When you use your Piercing Thorns feature, the target additionally has its speeds reduced by half until the start of your next turn.

15.name: Shepherd of the Forest
description: At 15th level, you can extend the vibrant primal magic of the forest to those who would protect it with you.  When you gain temporary hit points while in your Guardian form, creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you also gain an equal number of temporary hit points.

subclasses.name: Primeval Guardian Conclave

description: While all Rangers have a unique bond with the wilds, those who join the Conclave of Shifters take this bond to its extreme. Using the ancient and powerful magic of Druids, these Rangers are able to change their physical form and take on the shape of the beasts they defend. They use this primal power to stand as guardians of all wildlife and the natural world.

3.name: Limited Wild Shape
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can draw on primal nature magic to take the shape of beasts, much like a Druid does. You gain the ability to Wild Shape. As a bonus action on your turn, you can assume the form of any beast that you have physically touched.
Your Ranger level determines the maximum CR of beasts that you can transform into, as shown in the table below.

Ranger LevelMax CRLimitations
3rd0No flying or swimming speed
7th1/4No flying speed
11th1/2-
15th1-
While you are in Wild Shape, the following rules apply:

• Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics of the beast, but you retain your alignment, personality, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of the creature. If the creature has the same proficiency as you and the bonus in its stat block is higher than yours, use the creature's bonus instead of yours. If the creature has any legendary or lair actions, you can't use them.
  • When you transform, you assume the beast's hit points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form, For example, if you take 10 damage in animal form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked unconscious.
  • You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your beast form. Transforming doesn't break your concentration on a spell you've already cast, however, or prevent you from taking actions that are part of a spell, such as Call Lightning, that you've already cast.
  • You retain the benefit of any features from your class, race, or other source and can use them if the new form is physically capable of doing so. However, you can't use any of your special senses, such as darkvision, unless your new form also has that sense.
  • You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

You can stay in Wild Shape for up to one hour, at which point you revert to your normal form. You can revert to your normal form earlier if you use a bonus action to do so, or if you fall unconscious, you drop to 0 hit points, or you die.
Once you use your Wild Shape you must complete a short or long rest before you can use it again, unless you expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to use Wild Shape again.

7.name: Wild Bound
description: At 7th level, the Druidic magic you wield has permeated body and spirit. You learn Druidic, the secret language of druids. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages. While speaking Druidic, you gain the benefits of the Speak with Animals spell.
Also, your attacks in your Wild Shape beast forms count as magical for overcoming any resistances or immunities to non-magical attacks and damage.

11.name: Empowered Shapes
description: Starting at 11th level, you have learned to empower your Wild Shape with the Druidic magic you wield. When you use Wild Shape, you can expend a spell slot of 1st-level or higher to transform into a beast with a CR equal to or lower than the level of the spell slot you expended to transform.
Once you use this feature you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it to empower your Wild Shape again.

15.name: Thousand Forms
description: At 15th level, you are so in tune with your abilities that you can change your form in subtle ways at will. You can cast Alter Self at will, targeting only yourself, without expending a spell slot.

subclasses.name: Shifter Conclave

description: You are the first, and often last, line of defense against the terrors of the wilderness. Joining the Skirmisher Conclave requires a cool mind and steady hand. You are the stalker of prey, honing your skills in the methods of tracking and finding. The land itself is your teacher and the beasts that call it home, your allies.

You might be driven by the necessity of triumph over some great injustice or ongoing threat. Perhaps a corrupt noble extorts the countryside, a hag coven kidnaps local children on moonless nights, or a horde of gnolls threatens to destroy an ancient forest. Whatever it is that drives you, you single-mindedly put your skills, magics, tools, and techniques to the task of defeating your foe.

3.name: Spotter
description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you learn to track, detect, and perform deadly strikes against fleeing targets. You can take the Search action as a bonus action, and when you hit a creature with an attack of opportunity, you can add your Hunter's Prey die to the damage dealt.

3.name: Herbal Remedies
description: Also at 3rd level, you learn to use your knowledge of herbal remedies and the natural healing of the body to treat a creature's wounds. During a short rest, choose a number of willing creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). For this short rest, whenever one of those creatures spends one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points, it treats any roll of less than half the maximum value on the die, as half the maximum value of the die.

7.name: Martial Instincts
description: Beginning at 7th level, your trained senses allow you to react quickly to the movement of enemies around you. When a creature moves within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to move up to half your speed. You must be able to see or otherwise sense the creature to use this reaction.

11.name: Felling Blow
description: Starting at 11th level, your knowledge of your enemies gives you insight into disrupting their movement and abilities. Choose a creature within your weapon's range. You can use your action to make a single powerful weapon attack against that creature. You gain advantage on this attack if the creature is at least one size larger than you. If you hit, the attack deals additional damage equal to two rolls of your Hunter's Prey die, and the creature must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or fall prone.

15.name: Ambuscade
description: When you reach 15th level, you have learned to master the tactics of ambush. On initiative count 20 on the first round of combat you take an extra turn in addition to the turn taken on your normal initiative count.

subclasses.name: Skirmisher Conclave

description: While most Rangers are masters of the terrestrial wilderness those known as Skysworn defend the great open skies. Often organized in small fraternities, this order of Rangers master a style of elemental magic that grants power over air. These aerial Rangers use this elemental air magic to empower their attacks, enhance their skills, and even to take flight.

3.name: Skysworn Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, you have enchanted your armor with the power of elemental air. Over the course of 1 hour, which can be during a short or long rest, you can enchant a set of light armor that you touch, transforming into a set of Skysworn Armor.

You can only have one set of Skysworn Armor at a time. Enchanting another set immediately dispels the benefits for any previous set. Only you can wear and benefit from a set of Skysworn Armor, and it grants you the following benefits:

• The Armor has a number of Charges equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 2), and it regains all of its expended charges when you finish a short or long rest.
  • As a bonus action, you can expend 1 Charge to fly in a straight line up to 30-feet. Creatures in your flight path must make a Dexterity saving throw. They take thunder damage equal to three rolls of your Hunter's Prey die on a failed save, and half as much damage on a success. This flight does not count against your total movement.
  • You can cast Feather Fall without expending a spell slot.
  • You can add your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) to any Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks you make.

When your Skysworn Armor has no Charges remaining, you can use an action to touch the Armor and expend a spell slot, and it regains a number of Charges equal to the level of the spell slot you expended, up to its maximum Charges.

3.name: Storm Strike
description: Also at 3rd level, you can empower your weapon strikes with the thunderous elemental magic you wield. When you hit your Hunter's Prey with a weapon attack you can expend a Charge from your Skysworn Armor to deal additional thunder damage to your target equal to three rolls of your Hunter's Prey die.

7.name: Tempestuous Magic
description: Starting at 7th level, you have enchanted your Skysworn Armor with tempestuous magic. While your Skysworn Armor has at least 1 Charge, it grants you a 40-foot flying speed, and you add your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1) to your Dexterity saving throws.

11.name: Thunderous Flight
description: Starting at 11th level, you can channel the thunderous might of the greatest storms. When you expend a Charge of your Skysworn Armor to fly in a straight line, you add your Wisdom modifier to the thunder damage you deal to targets. Moreover, any Large or smaller creature that fails its Dexterity saving throw falls prone.
In addition, when you are flying with your Skysworn Armor, any opportunity attacks made against you have disadvantage.

15.name: Sonic Eruption
description: Starting at 15th level, you can erupt with a burst of thunderous force.
