description: As a bonus action, you can place your Summoner's Mark on a beast or plant that is Large or smaller and has a CR of ½ or less.  This CR increases as you gain levels, as shown in the Summon CR column of the Summoner table.
Whenever a marked creature within 60 feet of you dies, you can use your reaction to turn the creature's body in to a summoning stone.  You do not need to deliver the killing blow.
You can have a maximum number of summoning stones equal to your Wisdom modifier.

subFeatures.name: Using Summoning Stones
description: As an action, you can focus on a summoning stone and summon the creature inside. When summoned, it appears with full hit points, and materializes in an unoccupied space of your choice within 10 feet of you. The creature you summon is friendly towards you and your companions, and obeys your commands.

In combat, a summoned creature acts during your turn. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but it only uses the Dodge action on its turn unless you use your bonus action to order it to take an action in its stat block, or another action. If you are incapacitated, a summoned creature acts on its own.

The summoned creature is a reconstruction of the original creature that was used to make the summoning stone and has all of the same features and abilities that the original had in life, with the exception of legendary actions.

A summong creature disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points and can't be summoned again until you finish a long rest. You can dismiss a summoned creature at any time (no action required) and return it to its summoning stone, but it does not regain any hit points or features until you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Starting Stone
description: At 1st level, you start with one summoning stone, holding a Small or Medium beast of CR ¼ or lower.

1.name: Artificial Evolution
description: Also starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to enhance your summons by altering their forms and abilities.

subFeatures.name: Evolutions Known
description: You know two evolutions, which you can choose from when you apply evolutions to a creature.  You learn additional evolutions as you gain levels in this class, as shown in the Evolutions Known column of the Summoner table.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the evolutions you know and replace it with another evolution of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Evolution Points
description: You have a number of evolution points equal to your Summoner level, which you can spend on artificial evolutions.  You regain any expended evolution points whenever you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Evolving a Summon
description: When you summon a creature using a summoning stone, you can expend evolution points to apply up to three evolutions to the summoned creature.  Each evolution has a cost, which is the number of evolution points you must expend to apply that evolution.
Once you apply an evolution to a creature, the evolution remains on that summoned creature until you finish a long rest.

2.name: Spellcasting
description: Also at 2nd level, you learn to draw upon the primal magic of spirits to accompany your summoning skills.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: At 2nd level, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Primal spell list. You learn an additional Primal cantrip of your choice when you reach 4th level and again at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Primal spell list.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Primal spells you know and replace it with another spell from the Primal spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for Primal spells as you draw magic from your connection to nature spirits. You use your Wisdom when a Primal spell refers to your spellcasting ability, and you use your Wisdom modifier whenever you set the saving throw DC or make a spell attack roll for one of your Primal spells.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for your Primal spells.

2.name: Natural Evolution
description: Also starting at 2nd level, you learn to enhance your summons in tandem with your own abilities.  Any creature you summon has a number of hit dice equal to your number of Summoner hit dice, and has a proficiency bonus equal to your own, unless its proficiency bonus was already higher.

5.name: Summoner's Bond
description: Starting at 5th level, when you are targeted by an attack, you can force a summoned creature within 10 feet of you to become the target of the attack in your place.

6.name: Rending Strikes
description: At 6th level, the damage of a summoned creature's natural weapons increases by 1d6. At 11th level, the extra damage increases to 2d6, and again to 3d6 at 17th level.
Additionally, your a summoned creature's attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

9.name: Spiritual Recovery
description: Starting at 9th level, your summons recover more readily than normal creatures.  When you finish a short rest, each of your summoned creatures gains temporary hit points equal to your Summoner level.

10.name: Improved Summons
description: At 10th level, your skills of summoning and capturing monsters has improved.  You can now mark, summon, and capture any type of creature so long as it is not a humanoid, and the maximum size of creatures from which you can make summoning stones is Huge.
In addition, you can have two creatures summoned at once.  You can command both creatures using the same bonus action.

20.name: Sacrificial Pawn
description: At 20th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points and have at least one creature currently summoned, you can destroy the summoning stone and regain hit points equal to the creature's CR (minimum of 1 hit point).

Alternatively, if a summoned creature is reduced to 0 hit points, you can reduce your current and maximum hit points by an amount equal to its CR (minimum of 1 damage) to allow it to regain an equal number of hit points.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Chimera
description: Summoners who forge a Bond of the Chimera use their magics to unnaturally fuse their summons together.  These grotesque abominations are seen by most summoners as an affront to the natural order, and summoners of this bond are usually hunted by all others except Mongrels and their fellow summoners of this bond.

3.name: Chimerism
description: Starting at 3rd level, each of your summoned creatures bears a little bit of the essence of the others.  When you command a summoned creature to take an action, you can choose for the creature to take an action from a different creature's stat block for which you also have a summoning stone, provided that the other creature's summoning stone is not currently in use.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

3.name: Anatomical Knowledge
description: Also at 3rd level, your brutal experiments have granted you knowledge of how creatures work inside.  You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill.  Additionally, if you make a Wisdom (Medicine) check regarding a creature for which you have a summoning stone for a creature of the same type, you gain advantage on the check.

7.name: Artificial Splicing
description: At 7th level, your expertise with creating chimeras grants you additional insights into providing unique abilities to your creations.  You gain an additional number of Evolution Points equal to your Wisdom modifier, and you can apply up to four evolutions to each creature.

14.name: Unnatural Horror
description: Starting at 14th level, the chimeric effects wrought upon your summons makes them truly horrible to behold.  Each of your summons gains the Horrifying Presence action below.  If a creature has the Multiattack action, it can use this action as a part of its Multiattack.

subFeatures.name: Horrifying Presence
description: The summoned creature reveals its chimeric nature and lets out a mangled scream.  Creatures that can see it within 60 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or become frightened of you and the creature until the start of your next turn.  A creature that succeeds on its saving throw is immune to the Horrifying Presence of your summons for 24 hours.

18.name: True Chimerism
description: At 18th level, you can permanently and inexorably fuse your creatures together.  Over the course of a long rest, you can fuse two summoning stones into a single stone.  The resulting creature has the following properties:

• Its creature type is Aberration and any creature types that the component creatures have other than Beast.
  • Its maximum hit points is equal to the sum of the maximum hit points of both creatures.
  • It has access to all of the actions of both creatures.
  • It has all of the vulnerabilities, resistances, immunities, save proficiencies, and skill proficiencies of both creatures.
  • For all other attributes, such as size category, ability scores, or Armor Class, it uses whichever creature's attribute you choose.
You can have one such fused stone at a time.  You must destroy the existing fused stone in order to create another.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Elements
description: On the edge of existence lies worlds made of the primal energy of the universe.  Those who forge a Bond of the Elements specialize in the overwhelming powers of these realms and the primal titans within them.  They combine the elements with the power of their summons to create the most dangerous threats on the battlefield.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can speak, read, and write Primordial, and you gain proficiency in the Nature skill.

3.name: Elemental Strike
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your summons gain the ability to infuse their strikes with elemental energy.  Once per turn when a summoned creature hits a creature with a melee attack, they deal an extra 1d8 damage to the target.  You choose the damage type from acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

7.name: Primal Sacrifice
description: At 7th level, when a summoned creature dies, it creates an explosion of elemental energy.  All creatures within 10 feet of it must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC.  On a failed save, they take damage equal to 3d6 + your Wisdom modifier, or half as much damage on a success.  You choose the damage type from acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
At 18th level, the range of this feature increases to 30 feet, and the damage increases to 6d6 + your Wisdom modifier.

14.name: Elemental Resistance
description: At 14th level, your summons have adapted to the use of the elements in their attacks.  You and your summoned creatures gain resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage.  You can change which damage type you and your summons have resistance to when you finish a long rest.

18.name: Final Bow
description: At 18th level, when you dismiss a summon, you can use your Primal Sacrifice feature, even if the summoned creature had hit points remaining.
You can use this feature once, and regain the abiliy to do so when you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Guardian
description: Guardians defend the weak from threats too dangerous to defend themselves from.  Summoners who forge a Bond of the Guardian turn their summons into such beings, using them as towers of defense for themselves and their allies.

3.name: Spiritual Armor
description: Starting at 3rd level, while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.
In addition, your summoned creature's AC is equal to 13 + your Wisdom modifier, unless it was already higher.

3.name: Bestial Bulwark
description: Also starting at 3rd level, your summons are designed to defend you.  Your summoned creatures gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws, and their Constitution score is increased by an amount equal to your Wisdom modifier.

7.name: Aura of the Tower
description: At 7th level, your summoned creatures exude an aura of protection which you and your allies benefit from.  Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of one of your summoned creatures have advantage on Constitution saving throws.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 10 feet.

14.name: Shield of Scales
description: At 14th level, your summons are more skilled at protecting those around them.  Attacks targeting a creature within a summon's aura that do not target the summon are made at disadvantage.

18.name: Titan's Might
description: Starting at 18th level, your summons' ability to proken you and others has manifested as immense resilience.  Your summoned creatures gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Horde
description: Summoners who forge a Bond of the Horde wield an array of summoning stones to aid themseles with a vast host of summons.  They rarely need to get into the fight themselves, just stay back and command their summons.

3.name: Dual Summon
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you summon a creature, you can choose to split it into two beings. Each of these split summons has half of its maximum hit points, and deals half the amount of damage. When you gain the Improved Summons feature at 10th level, you can split only one of your summoned creatures.
In addition, you can command any number of creatures you have summoned using summoning stones with a single bonus action.

7.name: Pack Tactics
description: At 7th level, if one of your summoned creatures is within 5 feet of another summoned creature, it gains advantage on its attack rolls.

14.name: Wall of Summons
description: At 14th level, if a hostile creature is within 5 feet of at least two of your summons, its walking speed is reduced to 0 if both of the summons are no more than two sizes smaller than it. An affected creature can make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC as a bonus action, gaining the ability to move at half speed until the end of its current turn on a success.

18.name: Summoned Army
description: At 18th level, you can have three creatures summoned at once.
In addition, you can use your Dual Summon feature to split all three of your summoned creatures.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Mongrel
description: Summoners who forge a Bond of the Mongrel use dark magic to merge themselves with their summons, gaining their powers instead of creating a separate creature.  They are seen by most of their contemperaries as abominations.

3.name: Hybridization
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you would summon a creature, you can instead choose to merge with it for 1 minute or until you dismiss it (no action required). You can't have a creature summoned if you are merged with a creature.  When you gain the Improved Summoning feature at 10th level, you can have a single creature summoned while you are merged.

While merged, you gain the benefit of the summoned creature's senses, speeds, and special traits, except for any flying speed the summon has. You cannot use Artificial Evolutions on yourself while using this feature. If the summon is larger than you, you grow to its size. Anything you are wearing or carrying grows with you. None of your other statistics change, and you retain the ability to speak, cast spells, and use any features from your class, race, or other source.

For the duration, you can use your action to take one of the actions in the summon's stat block. You are proficient with the summon's natural weapons. You can use your spellcasting ability, instead of the summon's attack modifier, for the attack and damage rolls of attacks you make with them, and can use your Primal spell save DC instead of any of the summon's DCs. In addition, whenever you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use the summon's statistics or your own (your choice).
Once you merge with a creature, you can't merge with or summon that creature until you finish a long rest.

3.name: Tainted Blood
description: Also at 3rd level, your fusions have touched your blood, strengthening your body through its corruption. Your maximum hit points increases by 3, and you gain an additional hit point every time you gain a Summoner level.

7.name: Self Mutation
description: Starting at 7th level, you can enhance yourself as you would your summons.  When you use your Hybridization feature, you can apply up to three Artificial Evolutions to yourself for the duration.
In addition, you now gain the flying speed of creatures while under the effects of your Hybridization feature.

14.name: Crossbreed Hybrid
description: Starting at 14th level, you can merge with two creatures at the same time.  If you are merged with two creatures, you can't have any creatures summoned.

You gain the benefit of both creature's senses, speeds, and special traits. If both creatures have the same type of speed, use whichever is higher. If both creatures have flying speed, you also gain the faster of the two flying speeds. If either creature is larger than you, you become the size of the largest creature. You can take the actions in either creature's stat block, and you can make ability checks and saving throws using either creature's statistics.

18.name: Abomination
description: At 18th level, you manage to stabilize your hybridization magic. Choose one of your summons. You are permanently under the effects of your Hybridization feature with that creature, and it doesn't count against the number of creatures you are merged with for the purposes of your Crossbreed Hybrid feature. While you are permanently merged, you cannot summon the creature you are merged with.
Whenever you finish a long rest, you can change which creature you are permanently merged with.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Observer
description: The Bond of the Observer uses their summons to aid them in spying, stealing, and sneaking.  They specialize in intrigue and stealth and use their summons to aid them in these ventures.

3.name: Tread Cautiously
description: At 3rd level, your summons can hide themselves for spying.  As an action, a summoned creature can turn invisible until it rolls initiative, attacks, or targets a creature with a harmful effect.

3.name: Third Eye
description: Also starting at 3rd level, as long as a summoned creature is within 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically and see through its senses.  You gain the benefits of any special senses the summon possesses.
In addition, you gain proficiency in the Perception skill.

7.name: Trackless
description: Starting at 7th level, you and your summons leave no trace.  You and your summoned creatures gain proficiency in the Stealth skill, and have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to move silently.

14.name: Surprise Attack
description: At 14th level, your summons are adept at surprising their enemies.  Whenever a summoned creature has advantage on its attack roll, it deals an additional 2d6 damage.

18.name: Total Silence
description: At 18th level, when a summoned creature turns invisible using your Tread Cautiously feature, it does not become visible when it rolls initiative or misses with an attack roll.

subclasses.name: Bond of the Wildheart
description: Summoners who forge a Bond of the Wildheart meld their minds with the primal spirits of their summons.  They fight like wild beasts, their summoned creatures more the members of their pack than their servants.

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: Starting at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons.

3.name: Wildheart's Exploits
description: Your bond with your summons increases your brutality in combat. At 3rd level, you gain the following features:

subFeatures.name: Exploit Dice
description: You have two d4 Exploit Dice. To use an Exploit you must expend one of these dice, and you regain all expended Exploit Dice when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Mastered Exploits
description: You know the Primal Intuition and Wild Strike exploits.  You can use each of these exploits once per turn without expending an Exploit Die.  Starting at 17th level, you also gain the Trampling Rush exploit as a Mastered Exploit.

subFeatures.name: Savage Exploits
description: You learn two Exploits of your choice from the list of Savage Exploits. You can only use one Exploit per ability check or attack. Your summoned creatures can use Savage Exploits the same as you. When you gain a level, you can replace an Exploit you know with another of your choice.

subFeatures.name: Saving Throws
description: Some of your Exploits require your target to make a saving throw to resist your Savage Exploit's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Exploit save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

7.name: Extra Attack
description: At 7th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. You can command one of your summoned creatures to make a single attack from its stat block in place of one of these attacks.

14.name: Primal Revenge
description: At 14th level, when you or one of your summoned creatures is hit by a melee attack, the target can make a single melee attack against the attacker as a reaction.

18.name: Primordial Rage
description: At 18th level, your ferocity only grows as your are injured.  While you or a summoned creature is below half of its maximum hit points, it deals additional damage equal to your Summoner level with each of its atatcks.

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Expert Performer
description: At 1st level, you gain proficiency in Performance. Additionally, choose two skills. You gain proficiency in these skills.  If you already have proficiency, your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks made with them.

Additionally, you are deft at managing musical instruments, even in stressful situations. You can stow or unstow a musical instrument with the same movement as drawing or sheathing a weapon, and a hand holding a musical instrument counts as free for reloading and operating ranged weapons.

1.name: Corcondance
description: Starting at 1st level, you can empower your allies with your song. When you take the Attack action, in place of making an attack you may grant a concordant note to a creature within 30 feet. The next time they make an attack roll before the end of your next turn, they add 1d4 to the roll and deal additional thunder damage to one target. You must sing and play an instrument to grant an ally a concordant note; you cannot do so if you are deafened, silenced, or unable to use your instrument.

The additional thunder damage dealt by your concordant notes starts at 1d4 and increases as shown in the Troubadour table, at 5th level (1d6), 9th level (1d8), 13th level (1d10), and 17th level (1d12).

2.name: Spellcasting
description: Also at 2nd level, your music is capable of picking apart the very fabric of reality, singing new patterns into the weave of magic. Your spells help you adapt to new situations and extend magical support to your allies.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Troubadour table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Melodic spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Melodic spell list.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Melodic spells you know and replace it with another spell from the Melodic spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Wisdom or Charisma (your choice) is your spellcasting ability for your Melodic spells. Your magic comes from the heart and soul you pour into the performance of your music or oration.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Focus
description: You can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus for your Melodic spells.

2.name: Mystic Songs
description: At 2nd level, you may sing mystic songs that embolden and empower your allies. You may begin singing a Mystic Song as a bonus action, and it affects a number of creatures of your choice within 30 feet up to your Charisma modifier. You start out knowing two Mystic Songs of your choice, which are listed at the end of this class. You learn an additional Mystic Song at 7th level, and again at 12th level.

Initially you can sing two Mystic Songs per long rest, with your uses increasing as shown in the Troubadour class table. Your Mystic Songs last for 1 minute, though you can stop singing at any time (no action required). If a Mystic Song has effects that last an entire round, they are reset at the start of your turn. If targeted creatures leave the area of your Mystic Song or become ineligible as targets, you may designate new ones at the start of your turn.

You automatically stop singing a Mystic Song if you become incapacitated or silenced. If you are deafened or become so while singing a Mystic Song, you must make a DC 10 Charisma (Performance) check at the start of each round to continue singing.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Honeyed Words
description: At 7th level, your music is able to shift the hardest hearts. You have advantage on the next Persuasion or Deception check you make to influence any creature who has listened to you perform for at least one minute continuously.

Additionally, you are adept at salvaging bad situations. When you or an ally within 30 feet fails a Charisma skill check, you may butt in and attempt to save face, adding a d4 to the result and potentially changing the outcome. If you have already used this ability to influence a creature, you cannot influence that creature again until after a long rest.

7.name: Sooting Song
description: Also at 7th level, your melodies can relax your allies and invigorate their hearts. As part of a long or short rest, you sing this soothing song. Targeted creatures may reroll 1's or 2's rolled on any Hit Dice spent as part of the rest, and gain advantage on the next ability check they make.

11.name: Powerful Concordance
description: At 11th level, your concordant notes deal an additional die of concordance damage.

11.name: Shattering Song
description: Additionally at 11th level, you learn to channel your music with extraordinary flexibility and power. As an action, you can sing, shout, or otherwise perform a special note of power. When you do so, select one or two of the following effects.  You may invoke each of these effects one time, regaining all uses after a long rest.

subFeatures.name: Dispel Silence
description: You may attempt to dispel all magical silence within 60 feet. If it is a result of a leveled spell, you may attempt a Charisma (Performance) check with a DC of 10 + the spell's level, dispelling the effect on a success. If it does not originate from a leveled spell, you automatically succeed.

subFeatures.name: Shatter Objects
description: You may shatter all non-wielded or worn objects of your choice within 30 feet. Each affected object takes 12d8 thunder damage.

subFeatures.name: Thunderous Blast
description: You may blast all creatures of your choice within 30 feet with a shattering echo. Each affected creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. If they fail, they suffer 6d8 thunder damage and are deafened and have their movement speed reduced by half. If they fail by 5 or more, they are stunned until the end of their next turn. If they succeed, they take half damage and suffer no additional effects. They may reattempt the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, recovering on a success.

14.name: Improved Mystic Songs
description: At 14th level, you have effortless command of your Mystic Songs. Your Mystic Song range increases to 60 feet, and if you have no Mystic Song uses at the end of a short rest, you regain one.

18.name: Impossible Song
description: At 18th level, your musical magic resonates so strongly that you can bend the very passage of time. On your turn, you may grant your action to an ally affected by your Mystic Song. You lose your action, and the next time that ally takes a turn, they may take two actions.
You may grant an action in this way once, regaining the ability to do so after a short or long rest.

Troubadours of the Bloodcaller tradition put their music to a more sinister purpose - their melodies resonate directly with the blood of the living, and even sometimes the dead. Some Bloodcallers simply find a sanguine resonance to their songs; others may have learned their art from blood mages, or in benighted vampiric courts.

Bloodcallers still serve their allies with their song, though. A bloodcaller can help restore injured teammates, sap the vitality of enemies, and unleash devastating blood magic on the battlefield. They are among the most versatile of troubadours, but pay for their skills with an unsavory reputation.

3.name: Scarlet Songs
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, your music is able to speak directly to the blood of both your allies and enemies. You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient. You can add your spellcasting ability modifier to any Medicine checks involving wounds or blood diseases, and to any Survival checks to examine or track blood stains.

3.name: Music in the Blood
description: Additionally at 3rd level, you find that your own vitality is the key to unlocking new reserves of power. While you are singing a Mystic Song, anytime you fall below half your maximum hit points, you may begin singing a second song simultaneously without expending a use of your Mystic Songs feature. This song has the same targets as the first, and ends immediately if you go above half your maximum hit points.
In addition, you learn the Sanguine Sarabande Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Crimson Concordance
description: At 6th level, when an ally deals damage with one of your concordant notes, they may heal for half the concordance damage dealt. In addition, your concordant notes can deal necrotic damage instead of thunder (you choose when you grant them).

10.name: Reap the Harvest
description: At 10th level, while you are singing a Mystic Song, you may use your reaction to harvest the life of any creature that dies within its area. Before the end of your next turn, you can use this harvested life to cast one of your tradition spells without expending a spell slot.
You can cast spells in this way with a combined level total equal to your proficiency bonus. This total resets after a short rest.

15.name: Blood Bond
description: At 15th level, you are able to reveal to your allies the latent power in their own blood. After performing for one minute, you may choose a number of listening creatures equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. Each of those creatures receives two of the following three boons, of their choice. These boons last for one hour or until you use this feature again.

• They gain resistance to necrotic damage.
  • They gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Troubadour level.
  • Once per turn when they receive healing, they may add your spellcasting ability modifier.

20.name: Power in the Blood
description: At 20th level, if you are singing a Mystic Song and you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to instead drop to 1 hit point.

subclasses.name: Bloodcaller's Tradition

description: Gravewakers are feared and shunned, maligned practitioners of necromancy who are rarely tolerated and never trusted. Their music is, in fact, able to wake the dead - summoning spirits from beyond and tearing corpses from their rest.

Gravewakers, perhaps unsurprisingly, are relatively self-sufficient troubadours - they can make their own allies, after all. Their music and their minions enable fearsome control of a battlefield, as skeletal hands clutch their foes and rotting corpses assault them.

3.name: Lore of the Beyond
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you develop an affinity for death and corpses. You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient. You can use your Charisma modifier in place of Wisdom when attempting to determine a corpse's cause or time of death, or other facts about its decomposition.

3.name: Wake the Dead
description: Also at 3rd level, your songs have the power to wrench the dead from their very graves. Over the course of 10 minutes, you can raise a Small or Medium beast or humanoid corpse under your control. Your woken dead is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the accompanying Woken Dead stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. It has the same size and general body configuration (number of limbs, etc.) as the corpse it originated from. You can have one woken dead at a time.

In combat, your woken dead shares your initiative count, taking its turn immediately after yours. It can move on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, and it cannot take reactions normally. When you take the Attack action, you may forego one attack to allow the woken dead to choose an action on its turn instead.

That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. It cannot spend its own Hit Dice during a short rest to regain hit points, but when you roll Hit Dice, it regains hit points equal the number rolled + its Constitution modifier.

Your woken dead remains until it is reduced to 0 hit points or until you die. Anything it was wearing or carrying is left behind when it vanishes. If it dies, you can revive it via a 10-minute ritual, which requires expending a spell slot of any level. It revives with 1 hit point, but you may expend a number of your Hit Dice equal to the slot level expended, rolling them and adding your Constitution modifier to each die, giving it a number of hit points equal to the result (up to its maximum). It regains all its hit points after you complete a long rest.
In addition, you learn the Skeletons' Seungmu Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

Woken Dead
Medium or Small undead
Armor Class: 10 + PB (natural armor)
Hit Points: 5 + five times your troubadour level
Speed: 25 ft. (hover)
STRDEXCONINTWISCHA
16 (+3)12 (+1)16 (+3)6 (-2)10 (0)8 (-1)
Saving Throws: Strength +3 plus PB, Constitution +3 plus PB
Damage Immunities: poison
Condition Immunities: exhaustion, poisoned
Senses: darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10 plus PB
Languages: understands the languages you speak
Undead Fortitude. If damage reduces the woken dead to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, it drops to 1 hit point instead.
Animated by Song. If the woken dead is targeted by your mystic song, its movement speed increases by 10 feet, its armor class increases by 2, and it becomes able to take reactions.
Actions
Slam. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 plus PB to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 1d6 + 3 + PB bludgeoning damage.

6.name: Deathly Echoes
description: At 6th level, when an undead under your control deals damage with one of your concordant notes, they may add your spellcasting ability modifier to the damage dealt. In addition, your concordant notes can deal necrotic damage instead of thunder (you choose when you grant them).

6.name: Empowered Dead
description: Also at 6th level, you may select one of the following traits for your woken dead when you raise it or after a long rest:
Any creature who hits the woken dead with a melee attack suffers acid damage equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.
Creatures of your choice who start their turns within 15 feet of the woken dead have their movement speed reduced by 10 feet.
The woken dead gains proficiency in Athletics, using your proficiency bonus for its own. As a bonus action after it attacks, it may attempt to grapple the target of its attack.

10.name: Soulsong
description: At 10th level, you learn one 1st-, 2nd-, and 3rd- level spell of your choice from the necromancy school. These count as tradition spells for you.

Additionally, when inspecting a corpse, you can use your action to sing a brief melody and commune with its spirit. You can ask a single question as if you had cast speak with dead. You can do this a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, regaining all uses after a long rest.

15.name: Grave Blessing
description: At 15th level, you can call up a font of necromantic power to strengthen your allies. After performing for one minute, you can wreathe a number of listening creatures up to your spellcasting ability modifier in deathly power. Each target gains temporary hit points equal to your troubadour level, and has resistance to necrotic damage as long as they possess these temporary hit points. Undead creatures have advantage on all attacks while they possess these temporary hit points.

20.name: Undying Song
description: At 20th level, your song summons up mighty waves of necromantic energy. Friendly creatures targeted by your mystic songs gain the Undead Fortitude trait from the Woken Dead stat block.

Creatures of slain by your concordant notes rise as additional Woken Dead under your command, entering initiative immediately after you. They keep their prior size and have hit points equal to 5 times their Challenge Rating. They become lifeless again after 1 minute.

subclasses.name: Gravewaker's Tradition

description: The tradition of the Hellcantor is disfavored for a reason. Hellcantors tap into the power of the Nine Hells, threading fiendish melodies into their music. Their songs may be discordant or uncannily beautiful, as the situation calls. While some Hellcantors pass along their art through forbidden texts or secret tutelage, others are rumored to cavort with fiendish powers directly, selling their souls in exchange for profane music.

Hellcantors are offensive troubadours, standing behind their allies and unleashing infernal fires across the battlefield. Their abilities will wrap their allies in hellfire, curse their enemies' attacks, and eventually bend their foes to their devilish will.

3.name: Unholy Skill
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you learn the Infernal language. Additionally, anytime you make a Charisma (Performance) check, you may choose to give yourself advantage on the check. If so, you emit a faintly sulfurous odor for the next hour, and you register as a fiend for purposes of abilities or spells that detect them.

3.name: Infernal Melodies
description: Also at 3rd level, your songs can carry devilish influence to control your foes. When you begin singing a mystic song, and again as a bonus action while you sing it, you may turn the luck of one creature within the song's area. When that creature makes its next attack roll before the end of its next turn, it must roll a die equal to your Concordance Damage die and subtract that from the result. If the die roll is higher than the d20 roll for the attack, it takes fire damage equal to the number rolled.
In addition, you learn the Hellfire Hora Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Fiendish Flames
description: At 6th level, your fire burns with devilish intensity. When you deal fire damage with a spell or your Infernal Melodies, you may add your proficiency bonus to the damage dealt. Also, your concordant notes can deal fire damage instead of thunder (you choose when you grant them).

10.name: Infernal Hide
description: At 10th level, you receive an ever-shifting boon. After you complete a long rest, select one damage type out of acid, cold, fire, poison, or lightning. You receive resistance to that damage until you select a different type. In addition, you gain advantage on saving throws to avoid being charmed.

15.name: Devil's Bargain
description: At 15th level, you can offer your allies a small slice of the fiendish power you enjoy. After performing for one minute, a number of listening creatures up to your spellcasting ability modifier can choose to make a fiendish deal. If so, their hit point maximum is reduced by a number equal to your troubadour level, but they gain temporary hit points equal to twice that amount. If they fail a saving throw while they have any temporary hit points from this ability, they may sacrifice all remaining temporary hit points and add the amount lost to the number rolled, potentially changing the result. This maximum hit point reduction disappears at the end of a long rest.
You can perform in this way once, regaining the ability after a long rest.

20.name: Hell's Temptations
description: At 20th level, you can extend your infernal power to your enemies as well. When a creature takes damage from one of your concordant notes, you can use your reaction to attempt to charm them. They must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they are charmed by you until the end of your next turn.

While a creature is charmed by you in this way, you can use your bonus action to issue them a command to move up to 30 feet and make one attack against a target of your choice. The target will not move into obviously dangerous terrain or attack itself.

subclasses.name: Hellcantor's Tradition

description: The melodist is easily as devoted to their music as any wizard to their spellbook. A specialized performer, a melodist is one who discovered their talent for magic music, and opted to explore every possible avenue within this unusual power.

Melodists keep close to their comrades in battle, but rarely put themselves on the front lines - their talents are better kept out of immediate danger. Their focus is on enabling their allies, not swinging a sword of their own. But a melodist's songs are capable of awe-inspiring power, as they perfect their craft and become magical musicians without peer.

3.name: Dedicated Performer
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check that uses your Performance proficiency. If you already selected Performance as one of the choices for your Expert Performer feature, you may choose another skill with which you are proficient.

3.name: Inspired Song
description: Starting at 3rd level, when you sing one of your Mystic Songs, you may choose one target to be affected by a second mystic song you know. In addition, you learn the Mesmerizing Melody Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Persuasive Performance
description: Starting at 6th level, When an ally deals damage with one of your concordant notes, they may add your spellcasting ability modifier to the damage dealt.

10.name: Ever Adaptable
description: At 10th level, when you are singing a Mystic Song, you can change which Mystic Song you are singing as a bonus action without expending a use of your Mystic Songs feature.
Additionally, after a long rest, you may select one skill with which you are not proficient. You gain proficiency in that skill until you complete a long rest.

15.name: Revered Performer
description: At 15th level, you have advantage on all Performance checks using an instrument with which you are proficient.
Additionally, if you attempt a Persuasion or Deception check to influence a creature who has heard you perform within the last week, you can replace the die result with your Troubadour level.

20.name: Legendary Melodies
description: At 20th level, your Mystic Songs echo through the very bonds of reality. Any time a Troudabour feature uses your proficiency bonus, spellcasting ability modifier, or any written number for your Mystic Songs feature, you may double it.

subclasses.name: Melodist's Tradition

description: The Mindwhisper tradition is secretive and little-known, for its adherents dabble with mysterious and fearsome powers. They possess innate mental powers, and a talent for reading thoughts and influencing the minds of others. An identified Mindwhisper is rarely trusted, but they are often able to quietly worm their way into positions of power.

The Mindwhisper prefers to stay at the back of the fight, manipulating from the shadows. Their spells and abilities let them strike fear into enemies' hearts, breaking their confidence and causing psychic pain. That their allies might be at least as uncomfortable is a mere detail.

3.name: Innate Psionics
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you can communicate telepathically with any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. If you and the target don't share any languages, you can communicate only in simple images and emotions. The target must know at least one language.

3.name: Mental Music
description: Also at 3rd level, you are able to pipe your music directly into other creatures' minds. When you begin singing a Mystic Song, you can do so silently and without any visible action at all. You can also force one creature targeted by your Mystic Song to make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn.
In addition, you learn the Disquiet Dirge Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Blossoming Telepath
description: At 6th level, you gain access to the Telepathic Intrusion psionic power. You gain a number of psi points equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining them on a short or long rest. You can use these points to empower your Telepathic Intrusion or cast spells granted by the subclass, spending 1 psi point per level of the spell in place of a spell slot.
When you use your Telepathic Intrusion power, you can use your Concordance feature as a bonus action.
Additionally, when you grant a concordant note, you can choose for it to deal psychic damage instead of thunder.

subFeatures.name: Telepathic Intrusion
description: As an action, you assault the mind of a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or take 1d8 psychic damage. If the target fails the saving throw, it has disadvantage on attacks made against you until the start of your next turn. You can choose to deal no damage to the creature when it fails its saving throw.
You can spend psi points to add the following modifiers (you can add multiple modifiers). The points must be spent when choosing the target of the power.

subFeatures.name: Rending
description: You spend 1 or more psi points, and the target takes 1d8 psychic damage for each additional point spent on a failed save.

subFeatures.name: Terrifying
description: You spend 1 psi point, and the target is frightened of you until the end of your next turn if it fails its saving throw.

subFeatures.name: Meddling
description: You spend 2 psi points, and you make one creature invisible to the target creature or cause the creature to see something that is not there with the effect of minor illusion until the start of your next turn if it fails its saving throw.

subFeatures.name: Overwhelming
description: You spend 3 psi points, and the target is stunned until the end of its next turn if it fails its saving throw.

10.name: Psychic Fortitude
description: At 10th level, you gain resistance to psychic damage. While you are singing a Mystic Song, you can select a number of targets up to your spellcasting ability modifier to gain resistance to psychic damage.

15.name: Empty the Soul
description: At 15th level, you learn a song that can wrap a creature's mind away, sealing it off from the world. After you project a performance into a single creature's mind for one minute, that creature gains the benefits of the mind blank spell for one hour. You can perform in this way once, regaining the ability after a long rest.

20.name: Mind Sear
description: At 20th level, your mind is a fortress, even as your songs rend the minds of your foes. While you are singing a Mystic Song, you gain the following benefits:

• You are immune to psychic damage, and to the charmed and frightened conditions.
  • When an enemy is damaged by your concordant notes, they must make a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
  • When an enemy is frightened of you, they take bonus damage equal to two rolls of your concordance damage die from your Telepathic Intrusion and your concordant notes.

subclasses.name: Mindwhisper's Tradition

description: The skald is a battle troubadour, singing in the thick of the fight alongside their comrades. To sit in the back lines would be an act of cowardice, for a skald. Skalds are not only welcome at the warriors' table but celebrated, for every old veteran can tell of a time when a skald's music deflected a mortal blow.

Skalds are eager and willing to join the front line, swinging axes with crashing force. Their songs can amplify the party's damage directly, and their concordant notes are as likely to bless their own axes as an ally's. And skalds are unafraid to take a few blows themselves; they may not be able to trade with an enemy champion, but they can certainly provide few rounds' bulwark.

3.name: Battle Bard
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in heavy armor.

3.name: Songs of War
description: Starting at 3rd level, your Mystic Songs allow you to enter a battle trance, focused on the thrill of combat. Once per round while you are singing a Mystic Song, when you take damage from a weapon attack, you can reduce the damage taken by one roll of your concordance die.
In addition, you learn the Dirge of Devastation Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Concordant Strikes
description: Starting at 6th level, when you use your Concordance feature, you can grant a concordant note to yourself instead of an ally.
When you target yourself with your Concordance feature, you may do so as a bonus action.

10.name: Thunderous Defense
description: Starting at 10th level, when a character with one of your concordant notes is damaged with a melee weapon, they may explode the concordant note in response. As a reaction, they may roll your concordance die, subtracting the result from the damage they suffer and dealing the result as thunder damage to the attacking creature.

15.name: Rousing Performance
description: At 15th level, you are able to inspire your allies before a battle, by delivering a special performance over the course of 1 minute. The next time you roll initiative, you automatically cast the Heroism spell on all friendly creatures within 60 feet, up to a maximum of five times your spellcasting ability modifier. While under the effect of this spell, creatures additionally gain advantage on all Strength ability checks. The spell does not require concentration when cast in this way.
You can cast the spell in this way once per long rest.

20.name: Soul of Battle
description: At 20th level, you become an unstoppable herald of battle. While you are singing a Mystic Song, you gain resistance to thunder, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. Additionally, you gain resistance to one more damage type out of fire, cold, lightning, and acid damage. You select this damage type every time you begin singing a Mystic Song.

subclasses.name: Skald's Tradition

description: Spellsingers are troubadours fascinated by the interplay between music and magic - wandering performers intent on using their skills to explore the world's magical secrets. They share a wizard's fascination with knowledge, though the spellsinger still filters their understanding through the prism of song.

Spellsingers are most certainly not front-line combatants; their heavy reliance on spells makes them too vulnerable to head-ringing strikes. They prefer to focus on enhancing their allies' spells, and harnessing the leftover energy to bolster their own magical reserves.

3.name: Arcana Artist
description: When you select this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Arcana skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient. In addition, when you make an Arcana check to examine an item, perceive a phenomenon, or understand a magical effect, you can do so by singing softly to the weave itself. When you do so, you can use your spellcasting ability modifier in place of Intelligence.
In addition, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Arcane spell list.

3.name: Songs of Sorcery
description: Starting at 3rd level, your song can pull tattered threads of the weave back into usable forms. Anytime an ally affected by one of your Mystic Songs casts a spell, you may recover one spent spell slot of a lower level as a reaction. You may recover total spell levels in this way equal to your proficiency bonus plus one-third your Troubadour level.
In addition, you learn the Sorcerous Shanty Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Concordant Casting
description: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a leveled spell, you may use your Concordance feature as a bonus action.

10.name: Scroll and Song
description: At 10th level, your understanding of the arcane, while intuitive, is advanced enough that you can translate magical scrolls into song. When you find an Arcane spell of 1st level or higher, you can learn it if it is of a level you can prepare. Learning the spell takes you 4 hours per level of the spell but requires no ink or parchment, since the final form is a memorized tune rather than arcane pages.

You can learn up to 5 Arcane spells in this way. This increases to 6 at 13th level, 7 at 16th level, 8 at 19th level, and 10 at 20th level. When you level up, you may forget one spell to make space for learning new ones.

15.name: Enchanting Rest
description: At 15th level, you can conjure uncanny peace and a tranquil atmosphere upon your allies. If you take ten minutes to perform as part of a short or long rest, creatures of your choice who hear this song gain advantage on saving throws against fear and charm effects for the next hour. Additionally, they gain resistance to the next instance of damage they suffer from any spell.
You can perform in this way once per long rest.

20.name: Spellbinding Song
description: At 20th level, your music causes the weave to vibrate with power. While you are singing a Mystic Song, any spell of 6th level or lower cast by a friendly creature within its area takes effect as if cast at one level higher. Anytime you roll a saving throw to maintain concentration, you may choose to roll an Arcana check instead.

subclasses.name: Spellsinger's Tradition

description: The stormcrow is an outlier among troubadours, an eccentric who is as likely to perform on a barren tor as in a packed feast hall. A stormcrow specializes in the music of desolate places, taming the wind and the rain as it lashes the landscape. Some historians believe the tradition dates to rogue storm giants, who taught lesser beings how to sing to the skies. Others think stormcrows are divinely inspired, eccentrics touched by the whims of thunder gods or elemental princes. In either case, stormcrows tend to be wanderers and drifters, and a village only knows they have seen one when a tornado passes by unexpectedly - or, if the village was unwelcoming, touches down.

Stormcrows flit about the battlefield, darting around on summoned winds. They often stay just at the edges of the melee, relying on their mobility to keep them safe as they sing terrible blasts of lightning and thunder.

3.name: Call to the Wind
description: When you select this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Nature skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient. Anytime you are outdoors, you may sing to the wind and use spellcasting ability in place of Intelligence on Nature checks. You gain advantage on all checks to understand, identify, or predict storms, weather, and other similar phenomena.

3.name: Song of the Storm
description: At 3rd level your songs are able to command the very winds. When you begin singing a mystic song, and again as a bonus action while you sing it, you may move any creature within the song's area 15 feet in a direction of your choice. Unwilling creatures may make a Strength saving throw against your spellcasting DC to resist the effect.
In addition, you learn the Lightning Lied Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Thunderous Blasts
description: At 6th level, your concordant notes explode with the force of the storm. When a creature deals damage with your Concordance feature, you can create a blast of thunder or lightning as a reaction. If you do so, all other creatures 5 feet of their target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they suffer thunder damage equal to one roll of your concordance die.

10.name: Tempestuous Song
description: At 10th level, you gain resistance to both lightning and thunder damage, and when you select targets for a mystic song, you may choose to grant each target resistance to lightning or thunder damage. Additionally, when you move a creature with Song of the Storm, it no longer requires a bonus action (you can still only do so once per round).

15.name: Melody of the Mountain
description: At 15th level, your songs of barren places and distant crags inspire wanderlust. You learn the Longstrider spell, and you can cast it at will, without expending a spell slot.

20.name: Wings of the Storm
description: At 20th level, your mastery of storm magic is without peer. As a bonus action, you may transform yourself, becoming one with the storm. This lasts for 10 minutes, and grants the following benefits:

• You gain a 60 foot fly speed. If you already have a fly speed, it increases by 30 feet.
  • Your Thunderous Blasts now affect a 15-foot radius.
  • You are immune to lightning and thunder damage.
  • Once per round, if a creature within your Mystic Song would suffer lightning or thunder damage, you may reflect it back at its origin. If the effect required an attack roll, you make the attack roll with your spellcasting attack modifier. If it required a saving throw, the reflection target makes that saving throw against your spellcasting DC. You can transmute the damage from lightning to thunder or vice versa.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it again.

subclasses.name: Stormcrow's Tradition

description: Sunchanters are troubadours strongly tied to clerical faiths and divine magic. Their magic invokes the power of the gods, calling listeners to acts of faith and service. Some Sunchanters are affiliated with a specific deity, and serve that deity's temple; other sunchanters call on many or even all the gods, their songs harnessing ambient faith as often as strands of the weave.

Sunchanters do not leave their allies to face the darkness alone, but prefer to surround themselves with stout hearts while singing glad music to hold back the tide. A Sunchanter's skills work fine from the back lines, but it would be unrighteous to ask others to face dangers a Sunchanter themselves would not.

3.name: Voice of the Gods
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Religion skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient. You gain advantage on any Charisma (Performance) checks when performing religious or liturgical material. In addition, you learn the Guidance cantrip.

3.name: Building Chant
description: At 3rd level, your Mystic Songs build a reserve of holy power over time. Anytime you sustain a Mystic Song for three rounds, you may cast one of your tradition spells without expending a spell slot. It must be of a level you are able to cast, but casts at the highest level you can cast as a troubadour.
In addition, you learn the Cleaning Canticle Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Holy Guidance
description: At 6th level, your concordant notes grant a d6 bonus to hit, instead of a d4. In addition, your concordant notes can deal radiant damage instead of thunder (you choose when you grant them).

10.name: Divine Chant
description: At 10th level, you learn one 1st-, 2nd-, and 3rd- level spell of your choice from the Divine spell list. These count as tradition spells for you.
You also learn the Legend Lore spell, which you can cast once per long rest without expending a spell slot.

15.name: Sacred Benediction
description: At 15th level, you learn a blessed chant to protect your companions, which requires one minute of sustained performance. Select a number of listeners up to your spellcasting ability modifier. Each target immediately gains the benefits of one of the Lesser Restoration, Remove Curse, or Freedom of Movement spells, and regains hit points equal to double your troubadour level.
You may grant this benediction once per long rest.

20.name: Holy Thunder
description: At 20th level, any creature that takes damage from your Concordance feature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they become frightened of you and become vulnerable to the next instance of radiant damage they suffer before the end of their next turn.

subclasses.name: Sunchanter's Tradition

description: Where the Stormcallers wander jagged ridges and lonely mountains, Wildheart troubadours prefer more lively landscapes. Their concern is less for the barren and windswept places, and more for lands where animals and plants thrive. Some Wildhearts keep to themselves in the deep woods or jungles, while others travel between small farming communities, cultivating harmony between civilization and nature.
Wildhearts excel at controlling the battlefield, locking down enemies as others deal damage. They wish to bolster their allies, but do not prefer to expose themselves to needless danger.

3.name: Wild Wanderer
description: When you adopt this tradition at 3rd level, you focus on channeling the music of the forest. You gain proficiency in the Survival skill or Nature skill, or another skill of your choice if you are already proficient in both.
In addition, you learn the Speak with Animals spell, at will without expending a spell slot.

3.name: Beast Singer
description: At 3rd level, your Mystic Songs are able to speak directly to the independence and wildness in creatures' hearts. You learn the find familiar spell, and can cast it as a ritual.

When you begin singing a Mystic Song, you can channel your song through any creature you have summoned which you can see, centering its effect on that creature instead of on yourself. You can also use your Concordance feature on your summoned creatures, which may transfer the Concordant note to an ally when they take the Help action.
In addition, you learn the Greenwood Gavotte Mystic Song, which does not count against your total.

6.name: Rootcaller
description: At 6th level, you may command the roots and vines with your song. As a reaction when an ally deals damage with one of your concordant notes, you may summon magical roots to bind the target, as if they were affected by the entangle spell.
You can summon roots in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses after a long rest.

10.name: Greensong
description: At 10th level, you learn one 1st-, 2nd-, and 3rd- level spell of your choice from the Primal spell list. These count as tradition spells for you.
When you cast any of your tradition spells while singing a Mystic Song, one creature affected by your song regains 1d4 hit points.

15.name: Paean to the Elements
description: At 15th level, you learn a song which is able to invoke a blessing from nature itself and shield your allies like a cloak. Select a number of listeners up to your spellcasting ability modifier. You can sustain a performance for one minute, after which each target immediately gains resistance to one damage type out of acid, cold, fire, lightning, and poison.
This resistance lasts 1 hour, and you may grant it once per long rest.

20.name: Glory of the Greenwood
description: At 20th level, creatures of your choice who are targeted by your Mystic Songs gain the following benefits:

• They regain 1 hit point at the start of each of their turns.
  • They may ignore natural difficult terrain, and are each surrounded by a circle of grasping roots which is difficult terrain for creatures hostile to you.
In addition, while you are singing a Mystic Song, you gain resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning, and poison damage.

subclasses.name: Wildheart's Tradition

4.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 4th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

8.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 8th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

12.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 12th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

16.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 16th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

19.name: Ability Score Improvement
description: When you reach 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Alternatively, you gain one feat of your choice.
You can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
You gain one feat of your choice for which you meet the prerequisities.

1.name: Spiritual Defense
description: Starting at 1st level, you can innately draw on your Sealed Spirit's instinct for self-preservation to shield yourself with its power. So long as you are not wearing armor or a shield your Armor Class is equal to 10 + your Constitution modifier + your Charisma modifier.

1.name: Iridescent Strike
description: Each Sealed Spirit has a Strike feature, which is referred to by other features as your Iridescent Strike feature.

1.name: Unsealed Aspects
description: You are able to exert limited control over the Spirit bound to your soul and can partially release its power. At 1st level, you master one Unsealed Aspect of your choice from the list at the end of this class. When you gain certain Vessel levels, you master additional Aspects of your choice, as indicated in the Unsealed Aspects column of the Vessel table. If an Aspect has a prerequisite, like another Unsealed Aspect or a certain Vessel level, you must meet those prerequisites to master it.

2.name: Vessel Magic
description: Beginning at 2nd level, you can draw on the immense power of the Sealed Spirit bound within you to produce spells.

subFeatures.name: Cantrips
description: At 2nd level, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the Occult spell list. You learn an additional Occult cantrip of your choice when you reach 4th level and again at 10th level.

subFeatures.name: Spell Slots
description: The Vessel table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Vessel spells, and the level of those spell slots. All of your spell slots are the same level. To cast a Vessel spell of 1st-level or higher, you must expend a spell slot. You regain all of your spell slots when you finish a short or long rest.

subFeatures.name: Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher
description: At 2nd level, you learn two 1st-level spells of your choice from the Vessel Spell List at the end of this class description.

The Spells Known column of the Vessel table shows when you learn additional Vessel spells of 1st-level and higher. Any spell you choose must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your Vessel level.

Additionally, whenever you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Vessel spells you know and replace it with another spell of your choice from the Vessel spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subFeatures.name: Spellcasting Ability
description: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Vessel spells, as you are using your will to draw on the power of the Spirit that dwells within you. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability, when you set the saving throw DC for a spell, and when you make a spell attack roll.

subFeatures.name: Spirit Focus
description: Since your magic is drawn from the Spirit sealed within you, your body is the spellcasting focus for your Vessel spells. You must have at least one free hand to cast spells that require somatic or material components, and you must still provide material components that are consumed or have a gold cost.

3.name: Archon Form
description: Beginning at 3rd level, you can transform into a creature that resembles the true form of the Spirit within you. As a bonus action, you can transform into your Archon Form, which uses the Archon stat block in your Sealed Spirit description. This stat block uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places and uses your Vessel Spellcasting modifier and save DC.

You can maintain your Archon Form for 1 minute. You then revert to your normal form unless you use a bonus action to expend a Vessel Magic spell slot to extend the transformation by 1 minute. You also revert to your normal form if you fall unconscious, or use a bonus action on your turn to do so.
While in your Archon Form, the following rules apply:

• Your game statistics are replaced by the statistics in the Archon Form stat block, but you retain your alignment, personality, ability scores, and hit points. You also retain all of your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining those of your Archon. If your Archon has the same proficiency as you, use the higher bonus.
  • When you transform, you gain temporary hit points equal to your twice your Vessel level. Any temporary hit points you gain during this transformation are instantly dispelled if you revert to your normal form.
  • You retain the benefits of any features from the Vessel class, your race, and any other source, and you can use them if your Archon Form is capable of doing so, including casting spells with Vessel Magic.
  • When you transform, you choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your Archon Form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but your DM can decide whether it is practical for your Archon to use it. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match your Archon Form, and any equipment that your Archon can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with your Archon has no effect until you leave the Form.

You can transform into your Archon Form once, and you regain the ability to transform again when you finish a short or long rest. If you have no uses left, you can expend a Vessel Magic spell slot to transform into your Archon Form again.
In addition, you are now considered a shapechanger.

5.name: Extra Attack
description: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

7.name: Controlled Transformation
description: You have gained a deep understanding of your Sealed Spirit and greater control over your Archon Form. Beginning at 7th level, your Archon Form transformation lasts for 10 minutes, and it only ends early if you are reduced to 0 hit points, or if you use a bonus action to revert to your normal form.
Finally, you can transform into your Archon Form twice without expending a Vessel Magic spell slot, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

10.name: Twin Consciousness
description: Upon reaching 10th level, the Spirit bound to you grants you a portion of its ancient and vast mental fortitude. When you are forced to make an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, or a Constitution saving throw to maintain your concentration on a Vessel spell, you can add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to the result of your saving throw.
You can do so a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of this feature when you complete a long rest.

11.name: Unchained Power
description: You can unleash a greater amount of your Sealed Spirit's true power. Beginning at 11th level, when you transform into your Archon Form, you can cast a Vessel Spell you know that has a casting time of one action or one bonus action, as part of the same bonus action without expending a spell slot.
If you are the only target of the spell and it has a duration of 1 minute or longer, it instead lasts until you revert to your normal form, and your concentration cannot be broken on it.

20.name: Twin Soul
description: You and the Spirit bound to your soul merge and become an entirely new and distinct creature. At 20th level, your Archon Form transformation lasts indefinitely and only ends if you are killed or if you use a bonus action to end it.

When mortals attain heights of arcane power that allow them to ascend beyond their physical forms, they make themselves vulnerable to being sealed away. Often, these great sorcerers and archmages are punished by the deities of magic, and are imprisoned where they can no longer violate arcane laws.
Familiar Types: Any

1.name: Ancient Knowledge
description: Starting at 1st level, the ascended mage bound to your soul grants you access to its esoteric knowledge. You gain the following benefits:

• You learn the Prestidigitation cantrip.
  • When your Vessel Magic feature lets you learn an occult spell of 1st level or higher, you can choose the new spell from the Arcane spell list or the Occult spell list. You must otherwise obey all the restrictions for selecting the spell, and it becomes an occult spell for you.
